source_documents.title: Wix Site and Content Ownership
source_documents.content:
Wix Site and Content Ownership
Wix provides you with a platform to create websites to reach your online audience. As a Wix user, you waive any claims that you may have against Wix with regards to your site being used in marketing or promotional material.Note:See section 2.2.5 of our Terms of Use for more information.In the event of a dispute between several parties, Wix will determine site ownership by using established guidelines. We reserve the right to determine and/or grant ownership to an account or site based on our reasonable judgment, whether or not an independent investigation has been conducted by us. Among others, we may consider the principles set forth below:
For free sites: The owner of any sites or content is the owner of the Wix account under which the content was created. In most cases, the owner of the account is considered to be the person or entity who has access to the email address listed in Wix's records.For premium sites connected to a domain: If a site is/was connected to a domain whose registration information is publicly available via the WHOIS database, the owner of the site is considered to be the person or entity registered as the owner of this domain.If a domain is not connected or we are unable to verify the registration information in the WHOIS database, we may use any relevant billing information to determine the account or site owner. If any paid services were purchased via the account, the owner of this account or any site or content created there, is considered to be the person or entity whose billing details were used to purchase these paid services.Note:See section 1.3 of our Terms of Use for more information.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Adding and Setting Up the Wix Checkout Requirements App
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Adding and Setting Up the Wix Checkout Requirements App
With the Checkout Requirements app, you can take control over what requirements need to be fulfilled before a customer can complete checkout. You can use the app to create 3 different types of requirements:
Add a minimum quantity of products requirement: Prevent customers from purchasing too few of a specific item (e.g. minimum purchase is 3 vanilla candles). Add a maximum quantity of products requirement: Prevent customers from purchasing too many of a specific item (e.g. Purchase of vases is limited to one per order). Add a minimum order subtotal requirement: Orders must reach a minimum of $100.Check out some examples of how the checkout requirement can be used in the FAQs below.After creating one or more checkout requirements, you can easily activate or deactivate them with a click.Step 1 | Add the Checkout Requirements appTo get started, go to the Wix App Market and add the Checkout Requirements app.Wix EditorEditor XStudio EditorDashboard
Go to your editor. Click Add Apps  on the left side of the editor. Search for the Wix Checkout Requirements app in the search bar. Click Add to Site. Click Go to Dashboard. 
Go to your editor. Click App Market  at the top of the editor. Search for the Wix Checkout Requirements app in the search bar. Click Add to Site. Click Go to Dashboard. 
Go to your editor. Click App Market  on the left side of the editor. Click App Market. Search for the Wix Checkout Requirements app in the search bar. Click Add to Site. Click Go to Dashboard. 
Go to the Wix App Market in your site's dashboard. Search for the Wix Checkout Requirements app in the search bar. Click Add to Site.Step 2 | Create a checkout requirementNow that you've added the app, go to your site's dashboard and create your first requirement.You can create a single requirement or multiple ones. For example, you can create a requirement that ensures that customers must buy at least 2 candles and another requirement limiting the purchase of candles to 10 per order.To create a checkout requirement:
Go to Checkout Requirements in your site's dashboard. Click Add Requirement. Enter a requirement name (e.g. 2-candle minimum).
Note: Customers won't see this name. Select the type of requirement you want to create:
    
Minimum quantity of products Maximum quantity of products Minimum order subtotal   Enter the required quantity/subtotal. If you selected, minimum or maximum quantity of products, select what the requirement applies to:
    
Specific products: Only specific product(s) count towards the minimum or maximum (e.g. if you set a 2-product minimum, customers must buy 2 of each of the specific products you select). All products: The requirement applies separately to each product (e.g. if you set a 2-product minimum, customers must buy 2 of each product they buy, not 2 products from your shop).   If you selected Specific products in step 6, select those products.
Tip: Start typing the product name and select it from the list. Choose what happens if customers don't meet the requirement:
    
Yes, enable checkout but show a warning message: Customers see your message explaining the requirement, but can still complete a purchase.
 No, disable checkout and show error message: Customers see your message explaining why they can't complete the purchase and cannot complete a purchase.
   Enter the message text you want your customers to see.
Tip: Make sure the message is clear and specific so that customers know what to do (see FAQ below).FAQsClick a question below to learn more about the app.Where do customers see indications that they haven't met a requirement?Customers see an indication that they haven't met a requirement on the Cart Page. If the customer gets to the Checkout Page (e.g. by using the "Buy Now" button or because you haven't disabled checkout) they see an additional message there.
What kind of message should I display to my customers?Make sure your message conveys to customers what they need to do - especially if you disabled the checkout option. For example:
Order must total $100 or more. You must purchase a minimum of 100 items. Sale of this special-release item is limited to one per customer. Add an additional hat to the cart to checkout.Tip: After setting up your minimum requirements and composing your message, go to your live site and try adding relevant products to your cart as though you were a customer to check if your messages are clear.How can I activate or deactivate a requirementGo to the Checkout Requirements page and click the Status toggle to active or deactivate it.Can I make changes to a requirement I already created?Yes. Go to the Checkout Requirements page, click the More Actions icon  and click Edit. Tip: If you change a requirement, make sure to update the message text so customers know what to expect.What are some examples of how checkout requirements are applied?Here are some examples of checkout requirements and how they affect customers.Minimum 2 Candles example:This merchant wanted to make sure that any customer purchasing a candle bought at least 2 of that candle. They created a 2-candle minimum and added all their candles as specific products during setup.When a customer adds 1 Bergamot candle and 1 Beeswax candle to the cart, they'll see your message that they need to purchase 2 of each of these to proceed.
Note: Checkout will either be blocked or not, depending on what you selected when creating the requirement.
Maximum 1 per customer example:This merchant wanted to make sure customers limited the purchase of a specific sale rug to 1 per order. Customers can still purchase multiple rugs. However, they can only purchase one of the rug for which a maximum quantity was set.Note: Checkout will either be blocked or not, depending on what you selected when creating the requirement.

source_documents.title: ADI: Adding Alt Text to Your Images and Galleries
source_documents.content:
ADI: Adding Alt Text to Your Images and Galleries
It is important to add Alt text to your images as it provides search engines with information about your image and helps them to "read" them. Tip:Alt text is also important for accessibility purposes. Some of your site visitors might be using screen readers, which read out the alt text to describe the media on your site. Learn MoreThe recommended and free Wix images automatically have Alt Text on them, however, it is important to check that the text is suitable for your needs.Note:Adding Alt text is only available when your Media Layout is set to either Crop or Full Image. To add Alt text to your imagesHover over the section inside ADI that includes the image you want to add Alt text to.Click Edit.Hover over the image thumbnail and click Edit & Replace.In the Title (Alt Text) field, enter the title of your image. It should be a short description (just a few words) of the image. This title is used as the image's Alt text.                ﻿﻿To add Alt text to your gallery imagesHover over the section that includes the gallery you want to add Alt text to.Click Settings.Click Manage Media.Click the desired image.In the Title field, enter the title of your image. It should be a short description of the image. This title is used as the image's Alt text.

Add a stunning slideshow to showcase images on your site. It can include your own images, free Wix images or stock images. You can also add text and a different button to each slide. Each slide in the slideshow is displayed one at a time:Step 1 | Add a slideshow:Adding a slideshowClik Add on the top bar.Click Section to Page.Choose a section that contains multiple images (like Services for example).Scroll through the different layouts to find one with the Slideshow label.﻿﻿Step 2 | Edit your slideshow:Editing a slideHover over the slideshow on your site and click Edit.Hover over the relevant slide and click the Edit icon ﻿﻿ under the Slideshow items list.In the edit panel, edit the text or replace the image. Click the ﻿﻿ icon to show or hide an element. Click on the arrow at the bottom of the panel to move to the next slide.Click the Reorder﻿﻿ icon and drag the slide to the new location. Adding a slideHover over the slideshow on your site and click Edit.Click + Add Slide under the Slideshow items list to add a new slide.                   ﻿﻿Click the Reorder﻿﻿ icon and drag the slide to the new location. Check the Show icon to show or hide a slide:The ﻿﻿ icon indicates that the slide or field is shown. The ﻿﻿ icon indicates that the slide or field is hidden.Setting up your slideshow transitionHover over your slideshow. Click Design. Click Customize Section Design. Click Animation. Choose a transition effect.Drag the Duration slider to adjust the time a slide is displayed.Tip: Preview your site to see your slideshow animation.Deleting a slideHover over the slideshow on your site and click Edit.Click the Settings icon﻿﻿next to the relevant slide under the Slideshow items list.Click Delete. Click Delete to confirm.﻿﻿

source_documents.title: Branded App: Troubleshooting
source_documents.content:
Branded App: Troubleshooting
We've compiled a list of some general issues related to the branded app. For questions about how the branded app works, and the submission process see our FAQs here. Click the issue you're experiencing below to learn how to solve it.Troubleshooting general issuesGo to your site in the Wix app and follow the relevant steps below to solve general issues with your branded app. I'm not seeing push notifications If you aren't receiving push notifications about activity in your branded app, try the following steps:
Make sure you have enabled push notifications for the Wix app in the general notification settings of your phone. This differs from one device to another. Check your site notification settings in the Wix app:
    
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap your profile at the top. Tap Notification settings.
 Select your site from the list (if you have more than one). Enable the Allow Push Notifications toggle to allow site notifications to your mobile device. (Optional) Manage the notification settings for the apps on your site by enabling or disabling the toggle next to the relevant notification.  I'm not getting notified about live site visitorsIf you aren't getting notified about site visitors, first make sure you've added Wix Chat to your site. You won't be able to see live visitors without the Wix Chat app.
Note: Publish your site after adding Wix Chat.Once Wix Chat is added, go your Inbox activity settings:
Open the Wix App. Tap Inbox at the bottom. Tap the More Actions icon  at the top right. Tap Settings. Tap Notification settings under General Settings. Tap the Allow Notifications toggle if not already enabled. Under Inbox, enable the New visitor on site toggle to turn on notifications every time a new visitor is on your site.

I'm not able to find my branded app's site
Open the Wix app. Tap the site drop-down on the top right.
 Tap the site where you're building a branded app. Troubleshooting local issuesClick the relevant issue below to learn how to solve it. Check that your branded app is up to date
Go to the Apple App Store (on iPhone) or Google Play (on Android). Search for your branded app. (If available) Click Update.
Note: If there's no option to update it means you're running the most up-to-date version of the app.Check that you're using a supported deviceBranded app by Wix is supported on:
iPhone: iOS 11 and above Android: 6.0 and aboveLog out of your branded app and log back in
Open your branded app. Tap your profile icon at the top left. Tap the Settings icon . Tap Log Out. Log back in using your account credentials. (If the issue isn't resolved) Restart your mobile device.Clear Cache on Android Devices:
Long press the app icon on your device's home screen. Tap App Info. Tap Storage. Tap Clear Data. Open your branded app and log back in.Uninstall and re-download your appIf logging out and back in doesn't work, try completely uninstalling and then downloading your app again.

source_documents.title: Branded App: FAQs
source_documents.content:
Branded App: FAQs
Here are some commonly asked questions about Branded App by Wix:General FAQsWhat's the process of creating my own branded app with Wix?First you'll design your app (including its name, logo, look and feel) from the Branded App dashboard in your Wix account. Once your app is designed you can preview it for free on your mobile device. If you like the way it works, purchase a Branded App plan and follow the steps to publish your app on the Google Play and App Store.Is this app a native app or a web app?Branded App by Wix is a native app, which means it's built with the native language of the device it's installed on. This allows for a smoother user experience.Does a branded app replace the existing mobile version of my site?No, your branded app will be available in addition to the mobile version of your website. Branded App by Wix is a fully native mobile app that can be downloaded from app stores. Members accessing your site from a mobile browser can still view the mobile version.When I make changes to my Wix site, does my app automatically update?Your app is linked to your site dashboard. That means any changes or edits you make on the dashboard are reflected in your branded app. This includes adding items to your online store, new bookings or services, or creating new blog posts. However, any content or design changes you make directly from the Editor won't affect your app's design.How do I access the Branded App dashboard?The Branded App dashboard is located in your Wix account. Click the Start Now button to start creating your app. Go to the Branded App dashboard now.How do I publish my Branded App?After you've designed your app in the Branded App dashboard, you'll follow the steps to open both an Apple and Google developer account. This process is done on Apple and Google's side and can take a few business days to be approved.Once your account is approved, you'll finish registering your app from the Branded App dashboard and submit your app to Wix for approval. Once that's submitted, we'll submit it to the relevant app stores.Can my app be viewed in multiple languages?You can change the default language of your branded app. Your members can still choose their preferred language from their member profiles. Learn how to change your app's language in Step 2 of this article. Note: Branded App by Wix does not currently support multilingual.Can I migrate my existing members from my member app to my branded app?If you're using an existing Wix member app to communicate with your members (Spaces by Wix, Fit by Wix or Dine by Wix), there's no migration required.Your members will get a notification in their app asking them to download your new branded app. Learn how to switch your preferred member app.Can I only publish my app in one app store (e.g. only Apple's App Store and not Google Play?)Currently you must register your app in both stores.What is the difference between Branded App by Wix and Spaces by Wix?The main difference between your branded app and Spaces by Wix is that a branded app has no Wix branding and is only for your business and community. Your members download your app directly from the App Store and Google Play rather than downloading a Wix app and engaging with your site from there.What are the available languages for Branded App by Wix? Branded App by Wix is available in the following languages:Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Ukrainian. Can my app members/I use my branded app offline?No, Branded App by Wix requires an online connection. Currently it is not possible to use the app offline and then have the content sync once the device is online again.Purchasing a Branded App planWhat is included in a Branded App plan?Learn more about what's included in a Branded App plan. Does my Branded App plan include membership fees to Apple's App Store and Google Play?No, the plan does not include the registration fees and you must pay those separately. Apple's App Store membership fees start at $99 USD a year, and Google Play is a $25 USD one-time fee.What happens to my app if I cancel my Branded App subscription?You can get a full refund within the first 30 days of purchasing a subscription.After your app is live, if you decide to cancel your subscription Wix automatically removes your app from the app stores. If your members try to use the app they will be notified that the app is no longer available for use.Can I assign my Branded App plan to a different site in my account?Yes. After you purchase a Branded App plan, it is possible to assign it to another site in your account.
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the Show More icon  next to your branded app plan. Click Assign to a Different Site. Select the checkbox next to the relevant site. Click Next.  Click Assign to confirm. Can I transfer my Branded App plan from one Wix account to another Wix account?Yes. Since your branded app is connected to a Wix site, you can change ownership by transferring the premium site associated with your branded app to another Wix account. Learn how to transfer a premium site to another account. Submitting your Branded App for reviewWhat happens after I submit my app?
We will review your application to make sure it follows Apple and Google's compliance guidelines. If we see something that needs changing, we'll notify you within 7 business days. Once your app passes our internal review, we submit the app to Apple and Google on your behalf. Once Apple and Google approve the app, it will be released to app stores. The upload process can take up to 3 days.
Note: Your branded app is subject to Apple and Google's approval. Wix has no control over whether it will be approved or rejected by Apple and Google.How long does it take for Apple and Google to approve my app?The approval process varies from platform to platform and Wix has no control over the timeline.
Learn more about Apple's approval process. Learn more about Google's approval process.What happens if I get emails from Apple and Google?As part of the Branded App plan, Wix takes care of your app's submission to the stores as well as the app's maintenance and compliance with any new policies. During this process you may receive emails from Apple and Google. These emails require no action from you.Learn more about the emails you receive from Apple and Google.What if my app is not approved by Apple and/or Google?If your application does not pass Apple or Google's review, Wix gets notified. We'll then inform you why your app has not been approved and ask you to make the necessary changes.Once you've made the changes, you will have to resubmit your app to Wix for approval, and then again to Apple and Google. Learn how to resubmit your app.How do app updates work once my app is live in the app stores?Once your app is live, we make sure it stays current by updating it when necessary.Canceling your Branded App planHow do I cancel my Branded App plan?
Go to Subscriptions in your Wix account. Scroll down to the site with the branded app and click the More Actions icon  next to Branded App. Click Cancel Branded App. Click Cancel Now in the pop-up to confirm.When I cancel my Branded App plan, will it still appear in the app stores? After your app is live, if you decide to cancel your subscription, Wix automatically removes your app from the app store listings. If you want to build another Branded App, purchase a Branded App plan and follow the steps to publish your app on the Google Play and App Store.How will canceling my Branded App affect my members? If your members try to use the app they will be notified that the app is no longer available for use.How do I get a refund for my Branded App plan? You can get a full refund within the first 30 days of purchasing a subscription. To get the refund, cancel your plan from Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Learn more about the Wix refund policy.Do I need to do anything with my Apple Developer Account or Google Developer Account? Your Apple Developer Account or Google Developer Account information will be saved in case you want to relist your Branded App at any stage. If you wish to relist your Branded App, you can re-purchase a Branded App plan to get it back in the app stores. What can I do if I canceled my Branded App by mistake? If you change your mind about canceling your Branded App, or canceled it in error, you can contact customer care for support and they can help you relist it. Note: Branded Apps remain listed for 2-3 days after cancelation.

source_documents.title: Editor X: Working With Layers on Your Page
source_documents.content:
Editor X: Working With Layers on Your Page
Editor X has a wide range of tools allowing you to select and manage your layers. If your page has overlapping layers, it's important to control their stacking order so that all relevant information is visible to your visitors. Learn how to:
Set a layer selection preference Arrange layers on your canvas Use the Layers panelSetting a Layer Selection PreferenceUsing Editor X, you can choose a default pathway for grabbing layers on your canvas. Decide which element gets "selected" when you click a parent container that has child elements.  
Parent Container First: The parent container (e.g., container box, stack, etc.) is selected when you click it. Then, you can click again on any element inside to edit it.  Child Element First: The specific child element you click on is selected, not its parent container.  You can set this preference from the top bar in your Editor. Show me how
Click View on the top left of Editor X.  Hover over Layer Selection. Select the pathway you prefer: Parent first or child element first. Arranging Layers on Your CanvasWhen working with many different elements, layers could overlap in an order that doesn't fit your original design. Right-click on any element to move its layer forward or backward. You can also bring the layer to the front or send it to the back, making it the foreground for your design.Show me how
Select the element you want to re-position and click the Show More icon .  Select Arrange. Choose one of the following options:
    
Move Forward: Bring the element one layer forward. Bring to Front: Place the element in front of all other layers. Move Backward: Send the element one layer back. Send to Back: Place the element behind all other layers.

  Tip:You can also use the Layers panel to re-arrange your layers. Click the Show More icon  next to the relevant layer and select Arrange.Using the Layers PanelThe Layers panel in Editor X lets you manage your page's layers in one place. It displays all the elements on your page, from the top to the bottom, and allows you to select layers, change their order, hide them, and more. Learn More

source_documents.title: Email Marketing: Customizing the Footer of Your Campaign
source_documents.content:
Email Marketing: Customizing the Footer of Your Campaign
Personalize the footer of your email campaign to showcase your business information and branding. Add your address, phone number, social networks, and invite people on mobile join your member app.In this article, learn more about:
Customizing the footer of your campaign Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Customizing the footer of your campaignModify the footer of your email campaign to show your address, phone number, social networks and more. To customize your campaign's footer: 
Go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Edit next to an existing campaign or create a new one. Click the footer at the bottom of your campaign.  Select the tab you want to customize:Content Enable the toggle next to each element you want to display:
Show Wix branding: A Wix branding banner appears at the bottom of the footer. Upgrade to an email marketing plan to remove Wix branding from emails. Show address: Enter your street address in the field. Show phone number: Enter your phone number in the field. Add social links: Enable the toggle to give people the option to either share your campaign on social media, or reach your social accounts. 

Sharing this email: Enter an informative title and select the social network(s) you want people to share your campaign on. Linking to social accounts: Enter an engaging title, select the relevant social network(s) and enter your account link(s).   Add a link to your site: Include a link to your site. Enter the link text and the URL you want the text to link to. Invite mobile members: Add a link to your members app and grow your mobile community. Enter the invitation text and link text.Design Customize your footer using the design options available: 
Font: Select a font from the drop-down.  Font color: Select a color that matches your brand.  Icon color: Choose the color of your social icons.  Separator color: Choose the color of the divider that separates the content of your footer. 5. Click Apply. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about customizing your footer. Can I edit the option to unsubscribe message?No. You cannot edit the option to unsubscribe message, which is automatically added to the bottom of your campaign when you publish. The language of this unsubscribe message matches the language of your Wix account. You can change the language of your Wix account to change the language of your unsubscribe message. Keep in mind that changing your account's language affects the unsubscribe text for future campaigns only. The language of previously published campaigns does not change. Learn more about the unsubscribe link that appears at the bottom of your campaigns.Can I update my footer for all future campaigns?Yes. Changes you apply to the footer of a campaign automatically appear in future campaigns you create. This way, you don't have to adjust the footer every time you create a new campaign. Future campaigns sent via Wix Automations will also use your updated campaign footer. This applies to campaigns for a particular site. If you have more than one site in your Wix account, changes you make to the footer of one site's campaign do not apply to another site's campaign. How do I remove the Wix branding from my campaign?You can upgrade to an email marketing plan to remove Wix branding from your campaign emails. Once you upgrade, you will need to disable the Show Wix branding toggle from your email composer. Learn more about upgrading your email marketing plan.  Why is the footer in my campaign cropped? If automatic picture downloads in Outlook are blocked, information in the footer of your email campaigns can appear cropped.﻿Learn more about how to block and unblock automatic picture downloads in Microsoft Outlook.

source_documents.title: Preparing Your Wix Site for the LGPD
source_documents.content:
Preparing Your Wix Site for the LGPD
About the LGPDThe Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD) - which came into force in August, 2020 - aims to protect the fundamental right to privacy and the protection of the personal data of Brazilian citizens.This regulation affects any entity (including websites) that processes Brazilian citizens' personal data. Whether or not you, or your business, is located in Brazil; if you have Brazilian site-visitors or, if your marketing campaigns target Brazilian citizens, this affects you.Important:As stated in our Terms of Use, it is your responsibility to ensure that Wix services are permitted and abiding by local laws. Any information contained herein is not legal advice and you should not rely upon it as such. The LGPD can require several actions from site owners, depending on how you plan to use site-visitors’ data. If you are uncertain about your responsibilities, it is always wise to get legal advice from an expert.Building an LGPD-Compliant Website with WixYou can build a stunning LGPD-compliant website at Wix. Be aware that there are steps you must take to ensure your site is LGPD-compliant.Wix is a DIY (do-it-yourself) platform. We aim to make it easy to use our platform to comply with privacy and data protection laws like the LGPD. Wix provides you with specific tools to help you give your site-visitors control over their personal data. These tools implement technical and security measures to ensure that your customers’ personal data is protected as it crosses borders.Learn more about your role as a site owner
As a site owner, you are considered the Controller of your site-visitors’ data. This means that you are the one who is choosing what data to collect from your site-visitors and you decide how it will be handled. Wix.com is a Processor for your site-visitors’ data. This means that Wix will only process your site-visitors’ data following your instructions and on your behalf. Wix.com will not process your site-visitors’ data for our own benefit. For more information about Wix’s obligations as a data processor for your customer data, see our Data Processing Agreement Wix.com gives you tools to be LGPD compliant. However, there are multiple and essential steps you will need to take on your side. Compliance with the LGPD is the responsibility of each site owner. You are the one who is deciding what data will be collected and how it is handled.Helping Your Wix Site Meet LGPD RequirementsUse the following information and recommendations to prepare your site for the LGPD:Create a Privacy PolicyTransparency and communication with your site visitors are key elements of the LGPD. As part of the regulation, you must let your site visitors know how you collect, store and use their data - in a clear and transparent way. In addition, you must comply with your site-visitors' requests to receive a copy of their data that is processed on your site.A privacy policy is a statement that discloses the ways in which your website gathers, uses, discloses and manages your site visitors' data. Wix cannot provide you with legal advice on how to write a privacy policy. However, we do recommend that you maintain a clear and comprehensive privacy policy for your website, in accordance with both the LGPD and local privacy regulations. Learn how to create a Privacy Policy.For information on how Wix handles your site visitors' data, please review sections 4, 12, and 13 of Wix's Privacy Policy.About Data Storage and Data TransfersWix can store your site visitors' data in a number of locations.Your site visitors ́ personal information may be stored in data centers located in the United States of America, Ireland, South Korea, Taiwan and Israel. We may use other jurisdictions as necessary for the proper delivery of our services and/or as may be required by law. Wix is a global company that respects the laws of the jurisdictions it operates within.The security of sensitive data is of extreme importance to Wix and we are 100% committed to data protection. See all the security certifications received by Wix.com.About Cookies and Cookie BannersThe LGPD does not explicitly require that you get affirmative consent from site visitors before placing cookies (and similar technologies) on their device.However, you are required to provide complete information about which cookies you are using (you can use your privacy policy to provide such information to your visitors)  Learn more about which cookies are placed on your site-visitors' browsers.You can use the Wix Privacy Center to add a cookie banner to your site. With a cookie banner, your visitors can give their consent to non-essential cookies to be placed on their device. Learn more about Privacy and Cookies.Request Consent to Process Your Site Visitors’ DataThe LGPD establishes ways in which you can lawfully process your site visitors’ data. Requesting your site visitors’ consent is just one of the ways to lawfully process data. Sometimes consent will not be the best method for your business.Learn more about the principal bases for processing data Under the LGPD, you may process data:
With the consent of the data subject To comply with a legal or regulatory obligation of the controller To execute public policies provided in laws or regulations, or based on contracts, agreements, or similar instruments To carry out studies by research entities that ensure, whenever possible, the anonymization of personal data To execute a contract or preliminary procedures related to a contract of which the data subject is a party, at the request of the data subject To exercise rights in judicial, administrative or arbitration procedures To protect the life or physical safety of the data subject or a third party To protect health, in a procedure carried out by health professionals or by health entities To fulfill the legitimate interests of the controller or a third party To protect credit (referring to a credit score)Choose the best and most appropriate data processing method for your business. If you want to receive affirmative consent from your site visitors before processing their data, you can do so by:
Displaying a Cookie Banner on Your Site Using Wix Forms to Receive Explicit Consent  Creating a Custom Form and Connect it to a Database using Velo by Wix Adding a Policy Checkbox to Your Wix Stores Checkout Page Customizing Your Booking Form’s Fields in Wix BookingsTo ensure regulatory compliance, we recommend reviewing details of the regulation, as well as seeking legal advice.Use Wix Tools to Access and Delete Your Site Visitors' DataIn accordance with the LGPD, site visitors have the right to access their data or to be permanently deleted from your databases. Wix has developed two main tools to assist you in becoming LGPD compliant:
The right to access.  The right to be deleted.

source_documents.content:
Site Members: Offering Exclusive Content to Your Members
As the Members Area is login protected, you can use it to share exclusive content with members only, and also allow your members to share their own content with other members. This is a great way to keep your customers loyal and make them feel part of a community. Can I restrict access to any site page?Yes, you can limit any site page so only logged-in members are able to access it. You can make the page even more exclusive by restricting it to members with a specific role or pricing plan. This page does not have to be part of your Members Area. The built-in member pages in your Members Area (e.g. My Account, Profile) are private by default, as well as any custom member pages you create.In this article, learn more about:
Restricting pages to specific member roles Restricting pages to paying members Restricting pages to members with Badges Allowing customers to access their private informationRestricting pages to specific member rolesAllow certain members to have access to specific member pages. For example, you may run a yoga studio and want to create pages just for the students, and also pages just for the teachers. Before you begin:Create member roles and assign them to different members. To restrict pages to specific member roles:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Site Members under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Enable the Members with roles toggle. Click Manage Roles and select the relevant role(s). Click Apply.
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Members only under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Select Members with roles.  Click Manage Roles and select the relevant role(s). Click Apply.Restricting pages to members with pricing plansRestrict site pages to members who have purchased specific pricing plans. For example, if you're a teacher offering online courses, you can restrict the pages with the course material to members who have purchased the relevant pricing plan.Before you begin:Make sure you've added the Pricing Plans app and created plans.To restrict pages to members with a pricing plan:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Site Members under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Enable the Members with plan subscriptions toggle.  Click Manage Plans and select the relevant plan(s). Click Apply.
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Members only under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Enable the Members with plan subscriptions toggle. Click Manage Plans and select the relevant plan(s). Click Apply.Restricting pages to members with badgesUsing badges to reward your members and make them stand out? Create exclusive pages for them. For example, if you have a blog with premium content, you can set permissions so it's only accessible by members with a 'Blog VIP' badge.Before you begin:Make sure you've enabled badge permissions in your site's dashboard for the relevant badge. If you do not enable them, the option to restrict page permissions by badge type will not appear. To restrict pages to members with badges:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Site members under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Enable the Members with badges toggle.  Click Manage Badges and select the relevant badge(s).  Click Apply.
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the relevant page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select Members only under Who can access this page? Select Specific members under Which members can access this page? Enable the Members with badges toggle.  Click Manage Badges and select the relevant badge(s). Click Apply.Allowing customers to access their private informationThe Members Area interacts with many different business solutions, like Wix Stores or Wix Bookings. By signing up to your site, members get access to pages with all their previous info so they're encouraged to keep engaging. If you're using Wix Stores, for example, a My Orders page is automatically added to your Member's Area so customers can keep track of their previous purchases. Another example is the My Wallet page where members can view and update their credit cards.

source_documents.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Creating Your Wix Site and Online Business
source_documents.content:
Step-by-Step Guide to Creating Your Wix Site and Online Business
Having all the right tools and features to help you build your own fantastic website and online business are the key to success. With Wix, you get a robust platform with all the built-ins you need to create the website you want.In this article, you'll find an easy-to-follow checklist that guides you through the main steps of creating a site and setting up your online business. We will focus on creating a site with Wix Editor.Step 1 | Establish your purpose and goalsEvery site and business is unique and has a different purpose or goal. Start by clearly defining the purpose of your website. What do you want to achieve with it? Are you looking to showcase your work, sell products, provide information, or promote a cause? Understanding your goals will help you make informed decisions throughout the planning and design process. Step 2 | Define your target audienceUnderstanding your target audience is key to creating a website and business that resonates with them. Start by defining their demographics, such as age, gender, location, and income level. This information helps you tailor your content and design to their preferences. Next, identify your audience's interests and needs. How will they reach your site and what are they going to look for once they get there? This allows you to create content that is relevant and engaging for them.Step 3 | Research, research, researchEven if you have a clear vision for how your site should look and how your business should be presented, take time to research other sites for inspiration. It's a great idea to check out competitors' sites, as well as sites of businesses outside of your industry. You never know where you'll find inspiration.When building your website, our template gallery is a great place to start. There you'll find there hundreds of site templates showcasing a wealth of styles and designs. You can also visit our Explore page to view inspirational sites built with Wix. Step 4 | Set up your business dashboardOnce you have decided on your business, you need to create your Wix account and set up your business dashboard. You can use our AI tool to help you, or you can do it yourself. If you choose to use AI, write a little about yourself or business in the chat, and you will get personalized tools and a dashboard completely ready for you.If you choose to set up your business manually, follow the steps and add all your details.Ready to get started?
Set up your business dashboard. If you're an agency or enterprise building sites for clients, head to Wix Studio.Step 5 | Create your siteWhen your dashboard is all set up, you can start creating your site. Just click Design Site to get started.To get started designing your site, you can either use our AI tool, or you can customize one of our professionally designed templates.With both options, you can customize every part of your site according to your needs using the Wix Editor. With an intuitive drag-and-drop interface, building and customizing your site is a breeze, and the best part is, you don't need to write a single line of code!Using AI If you choose AI, you can customize the prompt or regenerate the design as much as you want until your site looks just as you imagined. Don't worry, you can still customize every part of your site later in the Wix Editor.Go straight to our AI site generator.Using a site templateWix offers 800+ website templates that have been carefully researched and curated by our own designers, to make sure they best fit current trends and industry needs.Make sure to choose a template that reflects your style preferences. Do you prefer a sparse, minimalist look? Going for a full-of-life, colorful design? We recommend selecting a template that already has the color palette and vibe you're aiming for, rather than one with the apps you need. You can add apps to any template in seconds. Check out our guide to outstanding web design.Step 6 | Customize your site in the Wix EditorHead to the Wix Editor to customize all aspects of your site and really make it your own. You can change every part including the text, media, layout etc. Here are some ideas to get you started customizing your site:Add and edit textRemove the default text and add your own. If you're unsure what to write, use our AI text creator tool to help you. You should also think about where you want to place the text on your site's pages. For example, you might want an introductory paragraph, or place text next to an image to describe it. Add media or upload your ownAdd images to your site that reflect your business. You can use free Wix media, Unsplash, or upload your own. If you want to get creative, use our image AI tools to design stunning graphics and animations that bring your vision to life.  Add animationsUse animations to bring your site to life. Add effects such as "Float-in" and "Expand-in" to create imaginative, striking pages and draw visitors' attention to your content. Learn more about adding animations.Step 7 | Publish your siteNow for the really exciting part. After taking the time to build your site and adding the essential elements, it’s time to publish. Once you’re happy, go ahead and click that Publish button. Learn more about publishing your site.Connecting a domain:Upgrade your site to connect your own domain for a more professional touch. Think about your site name and incorporate that into a domain. Learn more about domainsStep 8 | Optimize your site's SEOAfter you publish your site, it's time to get it appearing on search engines such as Google. Being visible in search results for relevant searches can help you build brand awareness and generate revenue. Each Wix website comes with an SEO Setup Checklist to give you a step-by-step guide to getting your homepage ready for Google Search. Your checklist also gives you suggestions for improving your site's search engine optimization (SEO) so that your site ranks higher.Ready to get seen online?Go to your SEO Setup Checklist

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Using the Members Area
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Using the Members Area
A Members Area is the ideal platform to turn site visitors into loyal customers. Every member gets their own account where they can see their information and manage their activity. For example, members can check on their latest store order or reschedule a session they've booked. 
Go to our Wix Studio Academy to check out additional Wix Studio webinars, tutorials, and courses.In this article, learn how to:
Add the Members Area to a site Choose which tabs to display Customize the tabs Show exclusive content for members View and manage the member listAdding the Members AreaAdd the Members Area app to your client's site directly from the editor. This automatically adds the Member Page and a Login Bar element, allowing people to sign up and log in. Before you begin:If you see the Member Page in the Pages panel, the Members Area is already installed. Some templates already include the Members Area app, and certain Wix apps (e.g. Wix Stores, Wix Forum) automatically install the Members Area.  To add the Members Area:
Click App Market  on the left side of the Editor. Click App Market. Enter "Wix Members Area" in the search bar.  Click Wix Members Area. Click Add to Site.What's next?Customize the Members Area to fit your client's design and purposes. For example, you can switch to a different layout. Choosing which tabs to displayThe Members Area is made up of different tabs, centralized under one site page – the Member Page. You can choose which tabs to show on the Member Menu, depending on the capabilities your client wants members to have. The available tabs depend on the Wix apps that are currently installed. For example, Wix Stores adds tabs like "My Wallet" and "My Orders", for members to easily manage their purchases.When using Members Area with other social Wix apps (e.g. Wix Blog), every member also gets a Profile tab, encouraging interaction between members. If you're not using a social app, you can always add this tab from the Member Menu.To choose which tabs to display:
Go to the Member Page in the editor. Select the Member Menu. Click Manage and Navigate. Choose what to do next:Add more tabsClick + Add or Remove Tabs at the bottom to see what's available. If no tabs appear, it means the Members Area already includes all relevant tabs (depending on the Wix apps that are currently installed).Note about the Followers / Following tab:This tab does not appear on the Member Menu. Members can access this tab by clicking the Following / Followers counter on every member's profile card. Reorder tabsHold the Reorder icon  next to a tab and drag it to the desired position. Rename a tab
Hover over the relevant tab and click the More Actions icon . Select Edit Tab Name. Enter the new name and click Done.Remove a tab
Hover over the relevant tab and click the More Actions icon .  Select Delete Tab.
Note: This option is not available for the my account tab.Changed your mind? You can always re-add the tab to the menu by clicking + Add More Tabs. Add any link to the Login Bar menu:While the Member Menu only shows the default tabs, you can add any link to the Login Bar menu. Customizing tabs in the Members AreaYou can personalize each tab of the Members Area so it fits your client's brief. Edit the texts that appear on the tab and adjust the design, choosing the colors and fonts you need.To access and customize a tab:
Go to the Member Page in the editor. Select the Member Menu. Click Manage and Navigate. Click the relevant tab to access it. Customize the tab to your liking:
    
Select the tab.
Tip: Usually, the content of the tab is displayed in a single widget. This widget is what you need to select. Click Settings. Use the available settings to customize the tab's texts, design and layout.  The Members Area includes both private and public tabs. Private tabs (e.g. Account Settings) usually include a member's personal info, whereas public tabs (e.g. Profile) are visible to any site member.Showing exclusive member-only content Add custom pages to the Members Area, on top of the built-in tabs. This is a great way to make announcements and market exclusive promotions. You can design these custom pages from scratch, based on the content your client wants to show their members.The page is already private when you add it.To add a private member page:
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click + Add New Page at the bottom. Click Add under Members Area Page. (Optional) Customize the page's name and permissions:
    
Rename the page: Double-click the page and enter the new name.
Tip: This automatically changes the page's name in the Login Bar menu.  Limit the page to specific roles or pricing plans: 

Hover over the page and click the More Actions icon . Click Settings. Click the Permissions tab. Select the relevant option under Which members can access this page?.    What's next?Once you create a custom page, it's automatically added to the Login Bar menu. Viewing and managing site membersOnce you make the Members Area live, visitors can sign up by clicking the Login Bar. Head over to the site's dashboard to see and manage the member list. The list is divided into current members, members who are waiting to be approved, as well as members who were reported or blocked.To view the member list:
Go to the relevant site dashboard. Click Contacts on the left. Click the More Actions icon  at the top right. Select Site members. Click a tab at the top to view members and their details:
    
Site Members: All current members of the Members Area. Pending: View any member requests if you have chosen to require approval for potential members. Reported: View any members who have been reported by other members.  Blocked: View any members you've blocked from your Members Area.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Understanding Your Blog Pages
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Understanding Your Blog Pages
When you add Wix Blog to your site, you automatically get 2 new pages on your site – a Post page and a Blog page. The Post page displays a single blog post and your Blog page is a feed of all your blog posts on one page. The Wix Blog app also offers the option to add a Members Area to your site. This is a section of your site dedicated to all your site visitors that signup and become members of your site. In this article, learn more about:
The Blog page The Post page The Members Area Frequently asked questions (FAQs)The Blog pageThe Blog page contains your main blog feed, which is all of your blog posts. By default, this page is called "Blog" but you can rename it. If you have created categories in your blog, then your readers can filter your posts by category.All Posts feedWhen a reader clicks All Posts, they can view every post in your blog.Category feedIf you have created categories, they are displayed at the top of your blog pages. When a reader clicks a category in your category menu, they can view all the posts that are part of that category. Once you have created categories for your blog, you can assign them to posts. You can also use tags and hashtags to assign posts to categories.Customizing your Blog pageYou can completely customize the Blog page, including the All Posts feed and the Category feed to look exactly how you want. For example, you can change the layout, choose what information is displayed, and design them using a huge range of customization options. Tip:Click Settings on the Blog element to get started. Learn more about customizing your Blog pageNote:The Category feed design is also used for the tags, hashtags and archive results pages.The Post pageWhen a reader clicks a post on your Blog page, they are taken to the Post page. This is a dynamic page that displays your individual blog posts. This means that the content changes depending on the blog post your reader is viewing. Customizing your Post pageYou can change the design of the Post page to look just how you want. You only need to customize the Post page once, and your design is displayed for every blog post. To access the customization options, click Settings on the Post page element. Learn more about customizing your Post pageThe Members pageWhen you add a Members Area to your site, you get a Members page. This page lets your site members see who else is part of your blog community, follow each other, comment on other members' posts, and see other members' activities (such as likes). Adding a Members Area also gives your site visitors access to other benefits if you have Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, or other Wix apps installed. Learn more about the Members Area.Tip:If you want to have a Members Area on your site, but without this page, you can hide it. FAQsClick a question below to find out more information.  How can I structure my blog by category or topic?If you have a lot of posts on your blog, it can be helpful to add some categories for certain posts or topics. Your readers can click on a topic and find posts related to that topic. Can I display blog posts on other parts of my site, or just my blog pages?Posts are mainly found in your post pages, however, you can add a Post List element to any page on your site, and give your site visitors a peak at your blog content. For example, adding a Post List to your site's homepage, is a great way to pull traffic into your blog. If I make changes to my main blog feed, does it show on my blog post page?No, the settings for your main blog feed and Post page are all separate settings. When you make changes to one of these the changes are only reflected on that specific page.

Wix Editor: Adding and Setting Up a Twitter Follow Button
Let your site visitors follow you on Twitter. Just add your username and get more people following your Tweets.Step 1 | Add a Twitter Follow buttonStart by adding a Twitter Follow button to your site. You can add this directly from your Editor. To add a Twitter Follow button:
Click Add  on the left side of the Editor. Click Social. Click the Twitter Follow button under Twitter, or drag the button to the relevant location.Step 2 | Add your username and languageOnce you've added your Twitter Follow button, you can add your username and select your preferred language. To add your user name and language:
Click the button in your Editor. Click Set Username. Enter your Twitter username. Press Enter on your keyboard. What language is your button in?: Select the relevant language from the drop-down.Step 3 | Make your account publicIn order for your tweets to appear on your site, you need to ensure your Twitter account is public. To make your account public:
Go to your Twitter account and log in.  Click More. Click Settings and Support. Click Settings and Privacy.  Click Privacy and Safety.  Click Your Tweets.  Deselect the Mark media you Tweet as having material that maybe sensitive box.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor Request: Choosing the Display of Your Hover Box on Mobile
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor Request: Choosing the Display of Your Hover Box on Mobile
When adding a Hover Box to your site, any changes made in hover mode are automatically hidden on mobile. By default, visitors see the regular view of the Hover Box. Currently, it is not possible to choose which Hover Box view (regular, hover) to display on your mobile-friendly site. However, you can re-add elements from hover interactions from the Hidden Elements panel.To re-add elements from hover interactions:
Open the page that contains the Hover Box in the mobile Editor. Click the Hidden Elements icon  on the left side. Locate the elements under From Hover Interactions. Click Show next to the relevant element to re-add it to your Hover Box.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor Request: Creating Style Presets for Your Elements
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor Request: Creating Style Presets for Your Elements
Currently, it is not possible to create style classes that let you define the same design settings for all relevant elements. For example, applying the same design to every image or button on your site as they belong to that specific class.  Instead, you can use the following features to make your design process quicker and more efficient: 
You can copy and paste the design of an element.  You can save single or grouped elements to your library and reuse them on your site, or a different site on your Wix account. We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor Request: Maintaining One Repeater List for Multiple Sites
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor Request: Maintaining One Repeater List for Multiple Sites
Currently, it is not possible to use the same list library for two different sites, even if those sites are in the same account.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is hugely appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor Request: Randomize Gallery Images when the Page is Refreshed

Wix Editor Request: Randomize Gallery Images when the Page is Refreshed

source_documents.title: Wix Retail POS: Creating Product Categories
source_documents.content:
Wix Retail POS: Creating Product Categories
Important:
This article is about Wix Retail POS tablet for brick & mortar businesses.  For info on using POS on a mobile device, click here.Using product categories, you can organize your store products to help you locate them more quickly at your point of sale.Note:Product categories were previously called product collections.All your products are automatically added to the "All Products" category. You can also add products to other categories so that they appear in more than one category. For example, if you have a pet shop, you can create a "Dog" category and a "Cat" category, that contain dog and cat food respectively. You can also create a general "Pet Food" category that includes the same products that are in the other categories. Note:Any product categories you create on the POS tablet also appear in your dashboard on desktop and vice versa. You can use categories in your live site to display different types of products on different pages.To create a product category:
Open the POS tablet.  Tap the Menu icon  at the bottom left.  Tap Catalog. Tap Categories.  Tap + New Category. Enter a name for your category and tap Save. Add products to your new category:
    
Tap Add Products. Select the checkboxes next to the products you want to add.
Note: You can use the search bar to find specific products.  Tap Add.   Notes:
To delete a product category, select the category and tap Delete at the top right. Deleting a category does not delete the products. To remove a product from a category, tap the Remove iconnext to the product.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Creating a Facebook Shop Using the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed App
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Creating a Facebook Shop Using the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed App
Important:Wix's previous method of creating a Facebook and Instagram shop will soon no longer be available. We suggest you create Meta shops using our partner app, Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed app.Display your Wix store products on Facebook and Instagram to get more exposure and drum up sales. After you integrate Wix with Facebook / Instagram, you can manage the orders you receive in the GoDataFeed dashboard. In this article, learn how to:
Add the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed app Set up your Facebook and Instagram shops Disconnect your old Facebook and Instagram shopsAdding the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed appHead over to the Wix App Market to add the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed app.To add the app:
Go to the Wix App Market in your Editor:
    
Wix Editor: Click Add Apps  on the left side of the Editor. Wix Studio: Click App Market  on the left side of the Editor. Editor X: Click App Market  at the top of Editor X.   Start typing "Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed" in the search bar and select Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed from the drop-down . Click Add to Site.  Review permissions and click Agree & Add. Select an option:
    
Create a new GoDataFeed account and click Start my Trial.
Tip: GoDataFeed offers a 14-day trial period for new accounts. Sign in to an existing GoDataFeed account.   Setting up Facebook and Instagram shopsAfter adding the Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed app and connecting your account, you can set up your Facebook and Instagram shops. To do so, you need to submit your feed and then sync your orders.Tip:You can set up a Facebook shop or both Facebook and Instagram shops. You can't, however, set up an Instagram shop without Facebook.Learn how to set up your Meta shops with Facebook Shops by GoDataFeed or watch the video below.
Disconnecting old shopsIf you previously connected Facebook and Instagram shops in the Wix dashboard, disconnect your old shops. By disconnecting your Facebook shop, you will also disconnect your Instagram shop, if you have one.To disconnect your existing shops:
Go to Facebook shop in your site's dashboard.  Click the More Actions icon . Select Disconnect Account. Click Disconnect Account to confirm.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Creating Invoices for Store Orders
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Creating Invoices for Store Orders
You can create invoices to request payment for store orders or to create a record for you and your customers. Before you start sending invoices, make sure your company details are displayed at the top of the invoice.In this article, learn how to:
Set up invoices Automatically create invoices for each store order Manually create an invoice for one or more paid orders Request payment via invoice for an unpaid order Create an invoice from scratch (not from a store order) View invoices you createdSetting up invoicesAdd your company logo and business details so they appear at the top of your invoices. You can also add other elements such as a due date field or legal terms.To set up your invoices:
Go to Invoices in your site's dashboard. Click Get Started. Enter your basic business information: 
    
Enter your Business Name. Enter your Business Email Address.  
(Optional) Add a business logo:
    
Click the Plus icon . Upload a logo and click Add to Page. Click Add & Continue.   Add additional customizations:
    
Go to Invoice Settings in your site's dashboard. Personalize your invoices to show your business info, notes and more.   Don't have a business logo yet?Use the Wix Logo Maker to create a logo for your business.Automatically creating invoices for each orderYou can set your store to automatically create an invoice every time an order is paid online. These invoices have a balance of $0.00 because the order has already been paid.Invoices are only created for:
Orders paid online through your site (not with the manual payment method) Orders for which you have the buyer's email address Orders for which you have not yet created an invoiceTo automatically generate an invoice for every order:
Go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard. Click Payments. Select the Invoices checkbox.Note:If you issue a partial or complete refund on a store order, the invoice doesn't update to reflect the refund amount.Manually creating an invoice for paid ordersCreate invoices for store orders that have the "paid' status so you or your customers have an official record of the purchase. You can create an invoice for a single order, or select multiple orders and create invoices for all of them at once. To manually generate an invoice for paid orders:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant paid order. Click the More Actions drop-down. Select Create Invoice. Click Create Invoice to confirm.   (Optional) Share, print, or email the invoice using the links at the top.Tip:You can also create invoices for multiple orders at once:
Select the checkboxes next to the relevant orders or click the top checkbox to select all.  Click Create Invoice. Click Create Invoice to confirm.Requesting payment via invoice for an unpaid orderYou can create an invoice for an unpaid order to request payment from your customer. If you send the invoice to your customer by email or as a shared link, they can click to pay for it online using any of your payment methods.To manually generate an invoice for an unpaid order:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Select the relevant unpaid order.  Click the Collect Payment drop-down and select Charge with invoice. Click Create Invoice.
Tip: This creates a saved draft of your invoice. Select how to send the invoice to your customer:
    
Share using a link:

Click Share link at the top.  Click Click Here to Create a Link. Click Copy Link. Click Done. Send the link to your customer.   Print a copy of the invoice:

Click Print at the top. Print a PDF or hard copy of the invoice. Send the invoice to your customer.   Send by email:

Click Send via email at the top.   (Optional) Edit the email's subject line or message. Click Send.    Updating the payment status:
If your customer pays online, the status updates automatically.  You can also accept payment by manually entering the customer's credit card details. If you receive offline payment, you can go to the Orders tab and mark the order as "Paid".  If you receive partial payment, you can go to Invoices in your site's dashboard and record the amount. Learn more about requesting partial payment as a deposit.Creating an invoice from scratchUsing Wix Invoices, you can create an invoice and a new store order in one go.This can come in handy when you want to add other charges to the invoice (e.g. charging billable hours) along with Wix Stores products.  Tips:
Out of stock items can be added to the invoice. You cannot create a manual order for a product subscription. You can add store products to an invoice - without creating a store order - by following the instructions below, but select Invoice in step 3. To create a manual order through Wix Invoices:
Go to Invoices in your site's dashboard. Click New Invoice. Select Invoice & Order. (Optional) Edit the Issue Date for your invoice.  (Optional) Edit the Due Date.  Enter your customer's details:
Note: Details must include phone number, shipping and billing addresses.
    
Click Customer and select an option:
        
Select an existing contact from the drop-down. Click + New Customer to add a new contact.     Enter an invoice title. Add a store product to your invoice:
    
Click the Product or Service drop-down and select a store product.  If relevant, select product variants and click Add to Invoice.
Note: The product price and description are added automatically and can be edited.


 (Optional) Select an existing tax from the drop-down menu or create a new one.    (Optional) Add a line item to your invoice (e.g. billable hours):
Tip: You can select this line item next time you send an invoice.
    
Click the Product or Service drop-down. Select an option:
        
Add a new invoice item:

Click +Add New. Enter a name (e.g. Dressmaking Services). Enter a description (e.g. Alterations on blue jacked). Enter a price. Click Save & Add.   Select an existing invoice item: Select the item from the drop-down.   (Optional) Select an existing tax rate from the drop-down menu or create a new one.     (Optional) Click Add Discount and enter a discount. (Optional) Scroll down and enter or edit the text in the Notes and Legal Terms fields. Click Preview to view your invoice. Click Send Invoice.What's next?After your customer pays the invoice online, the order appears in the Orders tab.Viewing invoices you createdYou can view a specific invoice by going to the relevant order in the Orders tab and clicking View Invoice. You can also print the invoice, resend it by email, or share it as a link.Tip:To view a list of all your invoices, go to the Invoices tab in your site's dashboard.To view your invoices:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant order. Click the More Actions button. Select View Invoice. (Optional) Share, print, or email the invoice using the links at the top.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Displaying an 'Out of Stock' Notice on a Product
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Displaying an 'Out of Stock' Notice on a Product
When one of your products is out of stock, an Out of Stock message automatically appears in the Product Gallery and in the Product Page.Tip:Instead of the "Out of Stock" message, you can set up back-in-stock notifications. This way, when an item is out of stock, customers see a "Notify When Available" message and can sign up to get an email letting them know when the item is available. Learn moreIn this article, learn how to:
Customize the "Out of stock" notice in Product Galleries Customize the notice in the Product PageCustomizing the message in Product GalleriesIf you display a button in your product gallery, it changes automatically to an "Out of Stock" message when needed. You can customize the text of the "Out of stock" message.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Go to the page with the gallery you want to customize.  Click the gallery on your page.  Click Settings . Edit the text:
    
Click the Text tab. Edit the "Out of Stock" text.  
Go to your editor. Go to the page with the gallery you want to customize.  Click the gallery on your page.  Click Settings. Edit the text:
    
Click the Text tab. Edit the "Out of Stock" text.  Customizing the message in the Product PageWhen a product is out of stock, the Add to Cart button in the Product Page automatically changes to an Out of Stock button. The color and font of this button cannot be edited, but you can edit the message text. To customize the "Out of stock" message in the Product Page:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Go to your Product page:
    
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click Store Pages. Click Product Page.   Click the Product Page element on your page. Click the Text tab. Edit the "Out of Stock Message" text.
Go to your editor. Go to your Product page:
    
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click your Product page under Store Pages.   Click the Product Page element on your page. Click the Text tab. Edit the "Out of Stock Message" text.Want to learn more?Check out the full course in Wix Learn on building your store or skip to the video on back in stock notifications.

source_documents.title: Wix Video: Adding a YouTube Playlist
source_documents.content:
Wix Video: Adding a YouTube Playlist
Add a YouTube playlist to your site to allow visitors to browse your videos. For example, if you are a personal trainer, you can display a series of fitness videos to motivate your audience.  To add your playlist, first copy your URL from YouTube. Then paste the URL into Wix Video. Note: YouTube videos set to private are not supported and may not display properly in Wix Video. Make sure the videos you want to add are set to "public".Step 1 | Find your playlist URL on YouTubeGo to YouTube and locate the playlist you want to add to your site. Copy the playlist URL. You can choose any public YouTube playlist, as long as the playlist has 50 videos or less. To find your playlist URL on YouTube:
Go to YouTube.com and access the relevant YouTube profile.  Click the Playlists tab.  Click View full playlist under the relevant playlist.
Copy the playlist URL at the top of the page.
Note: Make sure to copy the full playlist URL not an individual video URL. Step 2 | Create a new channel and paste the playlist URLOnce you've copied your playlist URL, create a new YouTube Feed. Then paste your playlist URL into Wix Video. Once you connect, visitors can then view the playlist on your site. To create a channel and paste the playlist URL: 
Go to Channels in your site's dashboard. Click the New Channel drop-down on the top right.  Select YouTube Feed. 
Paste your YouTube playlist URL into the field provided.  Click Connect. Visitors to your site will now be able to view and browse your playlist. Note:It may take several hours for your embedded YouTube playlist on Wix to sync with the latest uploads on your YouTube channel.

source_documents.title: Wix Multilingual Request: Changing the Font Color of Translated Product Descriptions

Wix Multilingual Request: Changing the Font Color of Translated Product Descriptions

The translated description remains all one color in the Multilingual Dashboard - black. source_documents.title: Wix Multilingual: Troubleshooting a Missing Language Menu
source_documents.content:
Wix Multilingual: Troubleshooting a Missing Language Menu
Can't see the Language Menu? No problem, you can always add it again. Below are some common reasons why your Language Menu could be missing, and the way to solve every issue. The language menu is missing from your live siteIf the Language Menu doesn't appear on your live site but is still visible in your editor, your secondary language might be hidden. When your main language is the only visible language, the Language Menu is not displayed to visitors.  Any time you add a secondary language to your site, it's hidden by default. When your translation is ready to go live, you need to make the secondary language visible. DashboardWix EditorStudio Editor
Go to Multilingual in your site's dashboard. Ensure the secondary language is visible:
    
Click the Status drop-down next to the relevant secondary language. Select Visible.   (In the editor) Click Publish at the top right to publish your site.
Go to your editor. Click Settings at the top and select Multilingual.  Ensure the secondary language is visible:
    
Click the Status drop-down next to the relevant secondary language. Select Visible.   (In the editor) Click Publish at the top right to publish your site.
Go to your editor. Click the Switch languages drop-down menu at the top of the editor. Click Manage Languages.
Ensure the secondary language is visible:
    
Click the Status drop-down next to the relevant secondary language. Select Visible.   (In the editor) Click Publish at the top right to publish your site.The Language Menu is missing from your editorIf you're unable to see the Language Menu in your editor, there are several reasons to look into. Another element is hiding the Language MenuIf your Language Menu is hidden behind, or overlapped, by another element, you might not see it on your live site. You can use the layers panel to locate the Language Menu and then bring it to the front so it is visible.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click Tools  at the top of the editor. Select the Layers checkbox. Select the  Language Menu in the Layers panel. 
Tip: You can find the language menu by click Header / Page / Footer to view the layers of each section, or the Arrow icon  next to a specific layer. Click and drag the Language Menu up to reorder it. When it appears as the first element on the list, it also visually appears as the top layer in your editor.  Click Save or Publish. 
Go to your editor. Click Layers  on the left side of the editor. Hover over the Language Menu and click the More Actions icon . Hover over Arrange. Select Bring to Front.  Click Save or Publish.The Language Menu was deletedIf you accidentally deleted the Language Menu, don't worry, you can always re-add it, just like other elements. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Menu & Anchor. Click Language Menus. Click a menu or drag the menu to the relevant location. Click Save or Publish. 
Go to your editor. Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Multilingual. Click a menu or drag the menu to the relevant location. Click Save or Publish.Still having trouble?If you are still experiencing this issue, please contact us providing the steps you have taken to troubleshoot the issue and we'll be happy to investigate further.

source_documents.title: Wix Restaurants: About the Wix App for your Restaurant
source_documents.content:
Wix Restaurants: About the Wix App for your Restaurant

This article is about the original Restaurants Orders app.  We're in the process of releasing a new restaurants orders app.Stay on top of what's going on in your restaurant, even when you are not there.
