source_documents.title: Claiming and Applying Vouchers After Upgrading Your Site
source_documents.content:
Claiming and Applying Vouchers After Upgrading Your Site
As a promotional gift, you may receive complimentary vouchers with the initial purchase of any yearly or multi-year site plan. For example, select plans include a 1 year free domain voucher.In this article, learn more about:
Claiming a voucher Applying a voucher Checking the expiration date of a voucher Frequently asked questions (FAQs) Claiming a voucherTo use a voucher, you'll need to first claim it within 2 months of purchasing your plan. You can then apply it to your site.To claim a voucher: 
Go to Premium Vouchers in your Wix account. Click Claim Voucher or Get Your Domain next to the voucher you want to claim.Applying a voucherOnce you've claimed your voucher, follow the on-screen instructions to apply it. Make sure to apply your voucher by the Valid until date listed on the voucher. To apply a voucher:
Go to Premium Vouchers in your Wix account. Click Go to (Company) under Claimed next to the voucher you want to apply. Follow the on-screen instructions to redeem it. Checking the expiration date of a voucherYou can view the expiration dates of your vouchers to the right of each voucher listed. The Valid until date is the date by which you must claim your voucher before it expires. If you have already claimed your voucher but haven't applied it yet, this is the date by which you must apply your voucher before it expires. To check the expiration date of a voucher:
Go to Premium Vouchers in your Wix account. View the expiration date to the right of the relevant voucher.FAQsHere are some common questions about claiming and applying vouchers.When do I receive vouchers? You receive vouchers after purchasing a new yearly or multi-year Premium plan or Studio plan. Vouchers are limited to the initial purchase of a plan.Can I get vouchers if I am on a monthly billing cycle for my Premium plan? No. Vouchers are only offered for yearly and multi-year plans, and are not included with plans on a monthly billing cycle. Learn more about Wix billing cycles for site plans.Why is the expiration date different before and after I click 'claim'?Before you claim the voucher, the expiration date you see is the 2-month claim window. After you claim the voucher, the expiration date changes. It now shows you how long you have to apply the voucher.I got different vouchers from what I was expecting. Why is this? Voucher availability may depend on your location. Vouchers may not be offered in all countries. How long before the domain voucher expires?  You have two months from the date you purchased your plan to claim the free domain voucher. You can check the expiration date of the domain voucher on the Premium Vouchers page in your Wix account. Learn more about the Wix free domain voucher.I'm a collaborator on someone else's site and I need to purchase a domain. Can I apply a voucher?Yes. Billing Managers can apply a domain voucher on behalf of the site owner. Learn more about domain voucher roles and permissions.

source_documents.content:
Connecting GMO-Epsilon as a Payment Provider
Accept credit/debit card payments from your customers using GMO-Epsilon as a payment provider.General InfoSupported countriesJapanSupported payment methodsCredit / Debit CardsTransaction fees3.5% per transactionAccount activation timeUp to 1 monthSupported currenciesJPYNotesThe currency used in your Wix account must match the currency in your Epsilon account. If the currencies do not match, the transactions may be declined. Learn how to change your currencyManaging your accountFor information on topics such as payout schedules, refunding a customer, chargeback disputes, and more, visit EpsilonIn this article, learn about:
Connecting GMO-Epsilon Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Connecting GMO-Epsilon
Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard.
Tip: Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it. Click See More Payment Options. Click See Options next to Third-Party Credit / Debit Card Providers. Click Connect next to GMO-Epsilon. 
Depending on whether you are creating a new GMO-Epsilon account or have an existing account, follow the instructions:Existing GMO-Epsilon account
Enter your Contract Code.
Note: The contract code is the same one you use to log in to your GMO-Epsilon account.  Click Connect. New GMO-Epsilon account
Click an option: 
    
Create Sole Proprietorship Account. Create Corporate Business Account.    Follow the instructions on the GMO-Epsilon website to complete your account setup. Once your new account is approved and valid, look for an email from GMO-Epsilon and copy your Contract Code. Return to this window (repeat steps 1-4) and follow the steps under Existing account to connect your account.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about accepting payments.How can I tell if a payment method is active?In order to accept online payments, you must connect a payment provider. Once connected, your checkout will be active for your chosen payment method(s).

You need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.Is my currency supported?Be aware that payments will fail If you are using an unsupported currency.
The currency used in your payment provider account must match the currency that you set in your Wix account. If you need to change the currency set in your provider account, please contact your payment provider.If your current payment provider does not support your desired currency, Wix hosts a wide range of alternative payment providers. Learn how to change your payment provider.What is a minimum payment amount?Some payment providers have a minimum payment threshold (e.g. $1.01). Payments below this amount will not be processed.Make sure that all of your products or services are priced over the minimum threshold. This includes discounted items or Pricing Plans. Please contact your payment provider to get the most up-to-date information about their minimum payment threshold. Can I offer recurring payments?To offer recurring payments, you must connect a payment provider that supports recurring payments.How do I get my payouts? Payouts are managed by your payment provider. If your provider is a third-party provider, contact them directly. 
If your provider is Wix Payments, learn about receiving payouts from Wix Payments. My customers' payments are being declined. What can I do?If your customers are experiencing payment failures, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting issues for accepting payments.Why can’t I connect my desired payment provider?If you’re having trouble connecting your payment provider, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting common connection issues.

source_documents.title: Editor X: Previewing Your Site
source_documents.content:
Editor X: Previewing Your Site
Use Preview mode to view your site as though it was live, across all breakpoints. By default, the preview is adjusted to your current screen size, but you can change the width and height to see your site in other viewports. This is especially useful when testing the responsiveness of different elements on your page.In this article, learn how to preview your site:
While working inside Editor X In your browserPreviewing your site inside Editor XThere are two ways to get a preview of your site from inside the Editor, whether it's already published or still work in progress:Dragging the handles on the CanvasUsing Editor X, you can preview your site in different screen sizes as you're working. This makes the process much more efficient since you can make the necessary adjustments on the spot. Drag the handles on the sides of the page to increase or decrease the width and see how your elements are arranged. This is especially useful when you need to check elements with fluid measurements (e.g., vh, vw, %).Tip:You can also add custom breakpoints to edit your site for a specific screen size.Clicking the Preview buttonYou can always access your site's Preview Mode by clicking the Preview button at the top right. See how your site looks in different breakpoints to ensure the elements look good in every screen size.You can select a specific device (e.g., Laptop, iPad, Galaxy S7) from the drop-down menu at the top, or enter custom width and height values if your breakpoint isn't on the list. To access Preview Mode:
Click Preview at the top right of the Editor. View your site in different screen sizes by doing the following:
    
Click the drop-down menu at the top to select a device. Drag the handles to increase or decrease the width.  Define the width and height of the screen in pixels.    Click Edit Site to continue editing, or Publish to make your changes live.      Want to view your site in landscape mode?"Landscape mode" is the horizontal orientation of your page, meaning that the screen has more width to accommodate your content. Simply drag the handles to increase the width of the page and see how it looks like in landscape orientation. Previewing your site in your browserIf needed, you can see how a site looks in your browser without having to access the Editor at all. The "All Sites" area of your account offers this quick action, among many others. Tip:This option is always available, regardless of whether you've published your site or not.To preview from your account:
Go to the All Sites page in your account. Hover over the site you want to preview and click Site Actions. Click Preview Site / View Live Site.
Note: The specific option you see depends on if your site is published or not.

source_documents.title: Email Marketing: Using Personalized Content in Your Campaigns
source_documents.content:
Email Marketing: Using Personalized Content in Your Campaigns
Personalize your email campaigns by using dynamic values. Dynamic values are placeholders in your email that will insert your recipient's personalized information, like a first or last name. Adding this personal touch to a campaign significantly increases interest in your email.Use personalized content in both the campaign's text and subject line to best engage your recipients. You can also add fallback text so your recipient won't see a blank space if the data is not available.In this article learn more about:
Adding personalized content to your campaign's text Adding personalized content to your campaign's subject line Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Note:Personalized content doesn't appear in test email campaigns. Your recipients will still see them when you send the campaign. Adding personalized content to your campaign's textYou can include personalized content in any of your email campaign's text elements. Add your recipient's name, email address and/or your site's URL to make the content personal and exciting to read. To add personalized content to your campaign text:
Go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Edit next to an existing campaign, select a template, or create a new one. Click any text element or add a new one.  Click where you want to add the dynamic value. Click + Add Personalized Content under Styles.  Select the value from the drop-down (e.g. contact last name, contact birthday, etc.) (Optional) Write a fallback text in the text box.Adding personalized content to your campaign's subject lineWhen you're ready to send your campaign, draw your recipients' attention to your email by including their details in the subject line or preview text. To add personalized content to the subject line or preview text:
Go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Edit next to an existing campaign, select a template, or create a new one. When you're done editing, click Next. Add at least one recipient and click Next. Click Edit next to Subject line. Click where you want to add the dynamic value. Click + Personalize under the subject line and/or preview text.  Select the value from the drop-down (e.g. contact last name, contact birthday, etc.) (Optional) Write a fallback text in the text box.FAQsClick a question to learn more about using dynamic values.What is an example of using personalized content in an email?Some common examples of personalized content include the recipient's name or address. For example, insert the content [Contact First Name] in the email text 'Thanks for subscribing [Contact First Name]' to personalize the text to the name of the recipient.What is fallback text?If data for the personalized content is not available, the fallback text you enter appears in its place. For example, if you include your recipient's first name in the email title, you can add fallback text like "dear customer" so the title still makes sense if their first name isn't in the system.Can I add personalized content to emails using the mobile app?No. You can only choose variables from a list when using desktop.

Embedding a Yandex Map on Your Wix Site
Important:The Yandex Maps app has been retired from the Wix App Market. You can still add a Yandex map to your site by using the Yandex map constructor to build the map and pasting the code into your site. Add a custom Yandex map to your site to let your customers know where they can find your business. Step 1 | Create a map using the Yandex Map constructorThe Yandex Map constructor lets you create your own map, where you can design routes and highlight locations. Select Embed on site.  Customize the size of your map.  Click Get map code.  Copy the code in the box. Step 2 | Embed the code on your siteAfter you've copied the code from the Yandex Map constructor, return to your site's editor to embed it.To embed code on your site:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the Editor. Click Embed Code. Click Embed HTML. Paste the code you copied from Yandex into the Add your code here (HTTPS only) field.  Click Update.  (Optional) Enter alt text that describes what you're embedding in the What's in the embed? source_documents.title: ICANN: Reactivating Your Domain
source_documents.content:
ICANN: Reactivating Your Domain
The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names & Numbers (ICANN) requires all domain owners to confirm their domain contact information.If you do not confirm your domain contact information within 14 days of purchase, your domain is deactivated, and a parking page replaces your site on your domain.You can reactivate your domain from your Wix account or the parking page on your domain. Important:Once you confirm your domain contact info, it may take up to 48 hours for your domain to propagate and display your site again. Note: If you don't see this option, you do not need to confirm your domain's contact email. Confirm your domain's contact information:Access the mailbox for your domain's contact email address. Learn HowOpen the email titled Confirm Your Domain Contact Information (sent from wix-team@notifications.wix.com).Click Confirm in the email.To reactivate your domain from the parking page:Enter your domain in your browser's address bar.Click Reactivate Domain on the parking page.Note: If a parking page does not appear on your domain, you must reactivate your domain from your Wix account.Confirm your domain's contact information:Access the mailbox for your domain's contact email address. source_documents.title: Turning the Auto Renewal Off for a Wix Premium Subscription
source_documents.content:
Turning the Auto Renewal Off for a Wix Premium Subscription
To prevent any disruption of service to your site, subscriptions for Wix services are set to renew automatically at the end of the subscription period. To prevent a subscription from renewing, you can turn the auto-renewal function off. Select a service below to learn more:Premium or Studio site plan
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant plan. Click Cancel Plan. Click Cancel Now in the pop-up to confirm.
Note: This does not cancel your plan immediately. Instead your plan does not renew at the end of the subscription period.Domain
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon next to the relevant domain. Click Cancel domain. Select Cancel auto renew and click Submit.Business email
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant business email. Click Cancel subscription. Select the I still want to cancel checkbox and click Cancel mailbox.Premium App
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant app. Click Cancel App. Select Cancel auto renew and click Cancel now.Changed your mind?You can simply turn auto-renew back on again before the end of the subscription period.

source_documents.title: Understanding the Differences Between Contacts, Members, and Subscribers
source_documents.content:
Understanding the Differences Between Contacts, Members, and Subscribers
﻿Learn the differences between Contacts, Members, and Subscribers to better manage your Contacts. Anyone who submits info via your site is classified as a Contact, while Subscribers and Members are specific types of Contacts.In this article, learn more about:
Contacts Members SubscribersContactsContacts are visitors to your site who are on your Contacts List. Visitors are automatically added to your list when they contact you through your site (e.g., through a contact form) along with the information they provided. You can also manually add new contacts, import contacts from Gmail, or import contacts from a CSV file in your site's dashboard. You can manage your contacts from the Contacts section of your site's dashboard. Learn more about managing your contactsMembersMembers are any visitors to your site who have signed up as members through the Member Signup form. Members have their own profiles in the Members Area and can interact with other members of the community.Members can also take on specific roles in your site, and you can assign badges to them to highlight their roles (e.g., Blog Writer).You can manage your members from the Site Members section of your site's dashboard. Learn more about managing your membersTip:You can also manually turn a contact into a member without them needing to go through the signup process. Learn more about setting contacts as membersSubscribersSubscribers are site visitors who have subscribed to your newsletter (e.g., through the Get Subscribers form). They are also any contact who has given you permission to send them marketing emails, newsletters, or updates from your site.You can manage your subscribers from the Contacts section of your site's dashboard. Learn more about managing subscribers

source_documents.title: Wix Blog Request: Increasing the Excerpt Character Count
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog Request: Increasing the Excerpt Character Count
Currently, excerpts for blog posts are capped at 140 characters. It is not possible to go over this limit.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Viewing Your Blog Analytics in the Wix App
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Viewing Your Blog Analytics in the Wix App
Catch a glimpse of your blog's statistics using the Wix app. You can find useful information like the amount of views and shares your posts got in a selected timeframe. To access Blog Analytics:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage at the bottom right. Tap Blog.  Tap Analytics. See an overview of your blog's statistics for the selected time period (7 days, 4 weeks, or 3 months):  
    
Posts Views: Shows the overall number of views for all posts. Unique Posts Views: Shows the number of different people who visited your blog. Each visitor is counted once, even if they've seen your blog multiple times during the selected timeframe.  Shares: Shows the number of times your posts were shared in the selected time period. Site Visits: Shows the total amount of visits made to your site. The same visitor can be counted multiple times if they visit your site more than once.    Check how your most recent post is doing:
    
Views: Shows the total number of post views, including multiple views by the same reader. Unique views: Shows how many people have viewed your post. A reader who views your post multiple times in the defined time period is counted once. Likes: The number of times a reader clicked "like" on the post Shares: The number of times the post was shared.   See your three most popular posts and tap Post Analytics for in-depth information about each one.Tip:Tap the drop-down at the top to change the selected time frame.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings Request: Offering Longer Intervals Between Recurring Classes
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings Request: Offering Longer Intervals Between Recurring Classes
Currently, you can offer a maximum interval of 4 weeks in between recurring classes. Therefore, it is not possible to schedule recurring class sessions months, quarters, or even years apart. We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Apps in the Mobile View
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Apps in the Mobile View
When moving from your desktop editor to your mobile editor, third-party apps that are not mobile-ready are automatically hidden, or may not display correctly. These apps are not optimized for mobile and therefore are not displayed as they are on the desktop version of your site.However, you can choose to show the apps on the mobile version of your site if you wish.To display apps on your mobile site:
Click Hidden on Mobile  on the left side of the mobile editor. Click the Show Element icon   next to the relevant app.Want to hide the app on your mobile site again? Simply click the app in the mobile editor and press Delete on your keyboard.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Creating a Drop-Down Menu
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Creating a Drop-Down Menu
Place pages under other pages to create a drop-down menu on your site. Visitors can see the drop-down when they hover over the main page on the menu.To turn a page into a drop-down:
Go to your editor. Click Pages & Menu    on the left side of the editor. Click the relevant page. Click the More Actions icon . Click Subpage .Tip:You can easily turn the drop-down back into a main page at any time. Click the More Actions icon  next to the drop-down and click Main page.Note:If the drop-down in your menu open behind other elements, move your menu forward.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Sharing Documents on Your Site
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Sharing Documents on Your Site
Allow visitors to download documents from your site with ease. There are a number of ways of sharing documents on your site. The options range from a variety of apps, to document buttons and linkable elements. In this article, learn more about:
Adding a document button Linking a document to an element Displaying PDF files Displaying Google Drive documents Creating a sharing libraryAdding a document buttonLet visitors download documents from your site in one click by adding a document button. Once you choose your button, you can connect your document file, change your button's icon and choose whether to display the document's title or not.To add a document button:
Go to your editor. Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Button. Select a button under Document Buttons, or drag it the relevant location on your page. Click the button. Click Change File. Select a file. Click Choose File to connect it to your button. (Optional) Customize the button using the available options.Linking a document to an elementLink your element to a document of your choice. When your visitors click the element, a new browser tab opens with the document. To link a document to an element:
Click the relevant element. Click the Link icon . Select the checkbox beside Document. Click Choose File. Click Upload Media and upload your document to the Media Manager. Click Add to Page. Click Done.Displaying PDF files on your siteBy adding the PDF Viewer app, you can upload and display PDF documents directly on your site. Choose from a variety of display options and make the links inside your PDF accessible to all users.To display PDF files:
Click Add Apps    on the left side of the editor. Type "PDF Viewer" in the search bar. Select PDF Viewer from the drop-down menu. Click Add to Site. If you have more than one site, you'll get an option to select the site you want to add it to. Click Add to Site.  
Tip: You can cut and paste the app to move it to another page on your site. Upload a PDF to the app. Customize the app's layout and design. Adjust the app's settings.Tip:Uploaded PDF files create their browser tab title based on the metadata in the file. You can configure this title with tools like PDF Candy. You should complete this before uploading your PDF to Wix, so that it displays properly once you add the PDF to your site.Displaying Google Drive documents on your siteWith the Google Drive app, you can display any file or folder you have on your Google Drive. Just connect the app to your Google Drive and select what you want to display.To display Google Drive documents:
Click Add Apps    on the left side of the editor. Type "Google Drive" in the search bar and select Google Drive from the drop-down menu. Click Add to Site. Click OK. Set up your app.Tip:To learn how to limit who can access your site's Google Drive page, click hereCreating a sharing libraryWith the File Share app, you can create a file sharing library where people can exchange ideas and collaborate on projects. Whether you manage a school, business, or community, the File Share app is a great way to upload and share documents securely. To create a sharing library:
Click Add Apps    on the left side of the editor. Type "Wix File Share" in the search bar and select Wix File Share from the drop-down menu. Click Add to Site.  Click OK.  Customize the app's permissions and member settings. Personalize the app's design.

source_documents.title: Wix Member Apps: Adding and Managing Buttons in Your App
source_documents.content:
Wix Member Apps: Adding and Managing Buttons in Your App
Buttons are elements in your app that enhance user interaction. Buttons can be linked to various areas within your app, external websites, and more. For example, add a "Call Us" phone number button to allow members to contact you directly through the app.Ensure your buttons offer clear calls to action, to encourage users to explore what you and your brand offers.In this article, learn more about:
Adding and managing buttons in your app Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Adding and managing buttons in your appCustomize your Wix Members app with buttons. You can customize the button layout, size, the action, which devices the buttons will be visible on and more. Add and edit up to two buttons at a time and choose how you want your buttons to look in your app.DashboardWix appWix Studio app
Go to Mobile App in your site's dashboard. Select the relevant tab (e.g. Spaces by Wix app, Branded Mobile App).  Click Edit Mobile App.  Click the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Click Elements on the left.  Select Button under Basic items.  Customize your button using the options below:
    
Layout: Select the number of buttons you want to add (e.g. one or two buttons). Then choose the size, width, and alignment of the button(s). Behavior: Click the Select button action drop-down and choose what you want the button(s) to do. For example, link the button to take members directly to another screen on your app, chat directly through your app, open an external link and more.
Note: Different actions may appear depending on the type of apps you have on your site. Design: Choose a button design.  Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Click the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Click General Settings and under Element visibility, choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android, or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.      Click Save & Publish.
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Mobile App.  Tap Edit under your site name or the name of your branded app.  Tap the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Tap + Add Element in the relevant location. Select Button under Basic items.   Customize your button using the options below:
    
Layout: Select the number of buttons you want to add (e.g. one or two buttons). Then choose the size, width, and alignment of the button(s). Behavior: Tap the Select button action drop-down and choose what you want the button(s) to do. For example, link the button to take members directly to another screen on your app, contact you through your app, open an external link and more.
Note: Different actions may appear depending on the type of apps you have on your site. Design: Choose a button design.  Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Tap the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Choose which screen and device you want this button to appear on:
        
Visibility: Choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.  Location: Select which screen you want the button displayed on.     Tap Add. ﻿
Go to your site in the Wix Studio app. Tap Mobile App.  Tap Edit under your site name or the name of your branded app.  Tap the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Tap + Add Element in the relevant location. Tap the Button element under Basic items. Customize your button using the options below:
    
Layout: Select the number of buttons you want to add (e.g. one or two buttons). Then choose the size, width, and alignment of the button(s). Behavior: Tap the Select button action drop-down and choose what you want the button(s) to do. For example, link the button to take members directly to another screen on your app, contact you through your app, open an external link and more.
Note: Different actions may appear depending on the type of apps you have on your site. Design: Choose a button design.  Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Tap the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Choose which screen and device you want this button to appear on:
        
Visibility: Choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.  Location: Select which screen you want the button displayed on.     Tap Add. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about adding and managing buttons in your app.How do I edit the color of my button?You can edit the color of your button by changing the theme color of your Wix Members App. Learn more about editing the color themes of your app.How do I link a button to an external URL?To link your button to an external URL to bring members to an external site, follow the steps below.
Choose Open URL from the Select button action drop-down. Enter the link in the Button URL section.  (Optional) Enter the text you want displayed on your button under Button text.How do I link a button to direct members to another screen?To link a button to another screen on your app, follow the steps below.
Choose Open screen from the Select button action drop-down. Select a screen from the Select screen drop-down. (Optional) Enter the text you want to display on the button in the Button text section.Can members call me directly through the app?Yes, members can contact you directly through the app with a Call phone number button. 
Choose Call phone number from the Select button action drop-down. Enter your phone number in the Add phone number section. (Optional) Edit the Button text to what you want displayed on the button.Can members email me directly through the app?Yes, connect a button to your email address, so members can contact you directly from their device. You can choose which email address the emails are directed to.
Choose Send email from the Select button action drop-down. Enter your email address in the Add email section. (Optional) Edit the Button text to what you want displayed on the button.Can I delete a button?Yes, you can. Learn more about managing your app elements.

source_documents.content:
Privacy: Retrieving Your Wix Account Data
Here at Wix, we respect your privacy and are fully committed to the protection of your personal information. We collect data from our customers so that we can create the best and safest products. source_documents.title: Switching Your Site Template
source_documents.content:
Switching Your Site Template
While creating a website, we understand that you might have a change of heart and want to switch to another template. While it's not possible to switch to a different template for a site you already created, you can create as many sites as you want in your account. This means you can start over with a new template at any point. Once you have chosen your new template, you can import elements, pages and media from your old site, and transfer your plan and domain to it.Step 1: Choose your new templateGet started by selecting a new template from our huge range of professionally designed templates. There are a variety of options and categories available including portfolio sites, business services, eCommerce templates and more, so you can choose the best style for your brand needs. 
View our Editor templates View our Studio Editor templatesStep 2: Copy elements and pages from your old siteTo make the process much easier when starting again with a new template, you can copy and paste elements and pages from your old site, or save and re-use design assets, depending on which Editor you are using.Learn more about:Copying elements from an Editor siteIn the Editor, you can copy specific elements from your old site, and paste them on to your new site. You can also copy and paste entire pages to make the process of starting on a new a template a breeze! Learn how to copy and paste elements and pages to a new site.You can also right-click on any element or section and save it to My Designs. They will be saved in a design library that you can use on any Editor site in your account. Copying elements from an Editor X siteIn Editor X, you can save and  re-use design assets in a library that you can use on any of your Editor X sites. This saves you time as you don't need to create elements, groups of elements, or sections from scratch.Note: While you can't copy entire pages from Editor X, you can save entire sections as design assets that you can use on your new site.Copying elements from a Studio Editor siteIn Studio Editor, you can save and re-use design assets in a library that you can use on any of your Studio Editor sites. This saves you time as you don't need to create elements, groups of elements, or sections from scratch.Note: While you can't copy entire pages from the Studio Editor, you can save entire sections as design assets that you can use on your new site.Are there parts of other templates you want to use?You can also copy or save designs (using My Designs or Design Assets) from any template you like, and then add them to your site.Step 3: Import media from your old siteAll the media from your existing site is saved under Site Files in your Media Manager. Site Files folders can be accessed from the Media Manager from all the sites in your account. If you want to add any file from your existing site to your new site, just import it from the Site Files folder. Can't find a file you are looking for?Search your Media Manager to find the file you need.Step 4: Transfer additional featuresWhen starting over with a new template, it's important to note that there are some features that you can transfer over to the new site and some that you can't. What other features can I transfer to a new template?You can transfer the following features from one Wix site to another. 
Business email Ascend Plan and features Wix BlogWhat features can't I transfer to a new template?You cannot transfer the following features from one Wix site to another. However, we really want to hear from you. Click the features you want to be able to transfer below to add your vote and view possible workarounds:
Site Theme, Design and Layout Premium Apps Contacts Site Members Wix Inbox messages Wix Invoices Wix Stores Wix Video Wix Bookings Wix Photography apps Wix Hotels Email Marketing Marketing IntegrationsStep 5: Transfer your plan and domainOnce your new site is ready, you can transfer your plan which you used to upgrade your site, and the domain from your old site to your new one. This ensures that your site will be fully functioning and live on the internet with your unique domain name, just as it used to be. The process takes just a couple of minutes.Learn how to transfer your plan and domain to your new site.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about switching to a new site template..What will happen to my site's SEO if I start with a new template?Changing to a new site template can affect your site's SEO. You can learn more about site redesign and SEO with our dedicated blog post.What happens to my uploaded fonts?If you uploaded fonts to your old site, they will also be available in the Font drop-down in the new site. How can I vote for the feature to switch templates?If you would like to vote for the ability to switch your site's template, go to this article and click Vote for this feature at the bottom.

source_documents.title: Troubleshooting Rich Results Eligibility Issues
source_documents.content:
Troubleshooting Rich Results Eligibility Issues
You can use Google's Rich Results test tool to check if a specific page on your site is optimized for rich results. The test checks if Google can access your page, see the rich result code, and confirm the validity of the rich result code.Sometimes, you may see an error that tells you your page is not eligible for rich results. Try the steps below if a rich result you expect to see does not appear in the report.Step 1 | Check that the rich result type is supportedNot all rich result types are supported by Google. You can check the list of supported rich result types to see if it's currently supported in the report.Step 2 | Make sure the page is indexedRich results can only be shown for pages that can be crawled and indexed. The pages on your site might not be crawled for various reasons. For example, very large sites can have a significant difference between the number of pages with structured data on them and the number of rich results actually shown in the report. If you see a sharp drop in the number of rich results on your site, see if you can find a corresponding dip in your indexed pages. You can use the URL Inspection tool to check if a page is indexed and if Google can access it. Test the live version of the page as well to confirm that Google can access it.﻿Step 3 | Ask Google to recrawl your pagesIt can take some time for Google to crawl new or updated pages. If you've recently added new pages or made updates to your site, you can ask Google to recrawl your URLs. Note:It can take up to a week for Google to index your pages after you submit a request.Step 4 | Make sure Google can access your pageGoogle can only create rich results for pages it can access. For example, if you have a password protected page on your site, Google won't be able to create rich results for it.You can use the URL Inspection tool to check whether Google can access your page.Step 5 | Make sure your structured data markup is validIf your page's markup is invalid, Google may not be able to recognize it as a rich result. If the test can find your markup but it can't parse it, it should appear in the Unparsable structured data report.Step 6 | Check that rich results are supported for your locationCertain rich result types might not be supported for your location yet. Check the features guides section of Google's structured data documentation to see if your location is supported.Still need help? If the problem persists, contact us with the information below: Information to add to your support ticket
The name or URL of your Wix site.  The name and version of the web browser you're using.   The name and version of your computer's operating system. A screenshot of your console view using the steps below:
    
Open an incognito window in Google Chrome (Ctrl + Shift + N). Sign in to Wix and try to open your Editor.  Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + J (on PC) or Cmd + Option + J (on Mac). Click the Console tab at the top of the panel and refresh the page (F5). Take a screenshot of this tab.

source_documents.title: Using Shutterstock Media Purchased Through Wix
source_documents.content:
Using Shutterstock Media Purchased Through Wix
Adding Shutterstock images and videos can give your site a high-quality, unique and professional look. There are millions of files to choose from. Read below for the conditions of using Shutterstock media on your Wix site.Shutterstock media guidelines:
You can use Shutterstock images and videos you've purchased on any site in the same Wix account. Learn how to import them to another site. Images are for digital use within Wix only and may not be used for printing. Shutterstock files are not downloadable. You may not use the media as a trademark for a business. You may not portray a person in a way that may be offensive, including:
    
in connection with adult-oriented services or ads for dating services;  in connection with political endorsements;  with pornographic, defamatory, unlawful, offensive or immoral content; and  as suffering from, or being treated for, a physical or mental ailment.   You may only use the media in websites and content on Wix, and not with other website or content services.

source_documents.title: Wix App: Inviting and Managing Collaborators
source_documents.content:
Wix App: Inviting and Managing Collaborators
Assign roles and permissions to collaborators, so they can help you manage your site and business through the Wix app. Granting collaborators the right level of access gives them the flexibility to manage and collaborate on your site on the go.  In this article, learn how to: 
Invite people to collaborate Change collaborator roles and permissions Remove collaborators FAQsInviting people to collaborateInvite collaborators and assign them one or more roles, depending on what you want them to do. You can add, view, and edit roles for your site from here. Important: Some roles and permissions can only be accessed via the Wix app or the dashboard specifically. Learn more about roles and permissions that are specific to the dashboard.  Tell me about the roles in the Wix appCustom roles: Choose a custom role with the permissions you want the collaborator to have based on the areas they should help you with. Custom roles are currently created on the dashboard and can be assigned through the Wix app. Learn more about creating custom roles for your site. System roles: 
Admin (Co-Owner): 

Site: Can manage, edit and publish your site. People with this role have access to billing, domains and inviting others. People with this role can't delete or transfer a site. App: Can manage, edit and publish your site. People with this role can't delete or transfer the app.   Customer Relations Manager: Can manage contacts, forms, tasks, workflows, automations, and communicate in chat. People with this role can't export contacts.  Website Viewer: Can view all pages inside Editor X, but can't edit the site.  Website Commenter: Can add comments and tag people inside Editor X. People with this role can't edit the site.  Website Manager: Can help you manage all aspects of your business from the Wix app. People with this role can access to manage, edit and publish your site, but they can't work with billing, delete or duplicate, or transfer the site.  Website Designer: Can edit your site on the Wix app. People with this role can change settings and how your site appears in the member app, but they can't access inbox, contacts, or other sensitive information. Back Office Manager: Can access the dashboard to manage site settings and apps. People with this role can't edit the site. Billing Manager: Can help you manage and organize the financial side of your business. People with this role have permission to make purchases, manage subscriptions, add payment methods and connect a domain to a site.  Domain Manager: Can connect and manage domains. People with this role can't make purchases.  Payments Manger: Can view and manage customer payments. People with this role have access to your site's payments and account information, but they can't purchase domains or subscriptions.  Blog Writer: Can help you manage your blog. People with this role can write and manage posts and comments, but can't create or manage categories. Blog Editor: Can fully manage the blog, but not other areas of your site. Guest Writer: Can write posts, but can't publish them.  Bookings Admin: Has full access to your bookings calendar and contacts page. People with this role can't edit other areas of your site. Events Check-In Assistant: Can see the guest list, check-in guests and scan tickets. Marketing Manager: Can manage all marketing tools, contacts, automation, and view site analytics. Content Collection Manager: Can add and modify content for all collections. People with this role can't edit other areas of your site. To invite collaborators:
Go to your site in the Wix app.﻿ Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down to Settings and tap Roles & Permissions.  Tap Collaborators. Tap + Invite Others under Collaborators. Enter the email address of the person you're inviting. Choose the role you want to assign them under Choose Roles. Tap Send.What happens next?: When you invite someone to work on your site, they receive an invitation email. If they already have an account, they can simply log in to accept the invitation. If they don't, they can create a free Wix account to get started. Collaborators have to enter the right credentials, and follow the correct SSO login process, to collaborate on your site via the Wix app. Your collaborators need to:
Open the Wix app.  Sign up in via Google, Facebook or email. Tap Sign Up.Changing collaborator roles and permissionsA collaborator's role gives them different permissions to help manage your site. You can edit a collaborator's role at anytime right from the Wix app to change what information they can view and what actions they can perform.Note:When you update the role of a collaborator, their permissions change in the app and dashboard.To change permissions of a collaborator:
Go to your site in the Wix app.﻿ Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down to Settings and tap Roles & Permissions.  Tap Collaborators. Tap the More Actions icon  next to the relevant collaborator. Tap Change Role. Select one or more roles for your invitee.  Tap Save.Removing a collaborator Remove a collaborator if you no longer want them to contribute to your site. Collaborators do not receive a notification when they are removed, but they won't be able to access your site through the dashboard or the app.To remove a collaborator:
Go to your site in the Wix app.﻿ Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down to Settings and tap Roles & Permissions.  Tap Collaborators. Tap the More Actions icon next to the relevant collaborator. Tap Remove. Tap Remove to confirm.FAQsCan I view detailed information on each of the available roles? Yes. Learn more about the specific roles and permissions..Will changes I make on the Wix app reflect in the dashboard? Yes. Any role changes you make from the Wix app take effect in dashboard too. E.g. When you change the role of a collaborator, permissions change in both the Wix app and dashboard.Will permissions granted through the app give collaborators access to the dashboard?Yes. When you assign roles and permissions, your collaborators gain the access you've granted them to manage your site through the dashboard and the app.

Wix Blog: Searching for a Specific Blog Post

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Adding and Setting Up a PayPal Buy Now Button
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Adding and Setting Up a PayPal Buy Now Button
PayPal Buy Now buttons allow you to sell products on your site, without needing to add an online store. The button links to your PayPal account and product, so it's quick and easy for visitors to make purchases.Add the button to your page, and set it up by linking it to your PayPal account. You can also choose its layout, currency, and language. Important:
This article is about PayPal buttons in the Wix Editor, which is separate to adding PayPal as a payment method for use with Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, and other business solutions. To use the PayPal button, you must have a PayPal Business or Premier account.Step 1 | Add a Buy Now buttonAdd a Buy Now button to sell a product through your PayPal account. You can link one item per button, and add as many buttons as you need to sell different products across your site.To add a Buy Now button to your site:
Click Add Elements  in your Editor. Click Button. Click PayPal Buttons. Click and drag the Buy Now button to add it to your site.Step 2 | Set up your buttonAfter adding the Buy Now button, link it to your Paypal account and set the product details (e.g. item name, price, etc.). When visitors click the button, they're directed to PayPal to complete the purchase.To set up your PayPal Buy Now button:
Click the PayPal button in the Editor. Click Add PayPal Info. Select Selling under What's this button for?. Set up the buttons with the below options:
    
What's your PayPal email?: Enter the email address you want to link into the field. What's the product's name?: Enter the name of the product or item into the field. Want to add an ID number?: Add the ID number of the product into the field (optional). What's the price?: Enter the price of the product into the field. What's the currency?: Click the drop-down menu to select the currency for the button. How does PayPal open?: Click the drop-down menu to select whether Paypal opens in the same window, or a new window.  What language is the button in?: Click the drop-down menu to select the button's language.  Note:Due to changes in the PayPal API, you must fill the PayPal email field in order to complete your button's set up. We also recommend entering the product's name, and confirming its price. Learn more about changes to PayPal buttonsStep 3 | Choose your button's layoutSet how you want the button to look on your site. You can choose between a button that shows accepted cards, or a button without them.To choose the layout of your PayPal button:
Click the button in your Editor. Click the Layout icon . Select a layout preset from the options.Note:You do not get notifications on your Wix account for purchases made through PayPal buttons. This is because the payments are made to the PayPal account, and not your Wix account.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor Request: Editing Your Site from a Mobile Web Browser
source_documents.content:

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: About Shipping Labels
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: About Shipping Labels
Get store orders delivered to your customers as quickly and easily as possible by connecting to a shipping label solution that works for your business.  Before you begin:Make sure you enter your business's address in the Business Info page. In this article, learn how to:
Choose a print label solution Track packagesChoosing a print label solution for your businessWix has partnered with Shippo to create Wix Shipping - an integrated print label solution. In addition, you can choose from a variety of third-party shipping apps (including Shippo). Wix ShippingUse the Wix Shipping integrated shipping label solution to purchase and print labels right in your Wix dashboard. Wix Shipping is currently available for merchants in the following locations:
Canada France Germany Spain UK USLearn more about Wix Shipping.Third-party shipping label appsAfter setting up any of the shipping label apps, your orders automatically appear in the dashboard of the app. You can go ahead and purchase and print your labels there. Check out any of the options below, or go to the Wix App Market to look for additional third-party shipping label apps.
Shippo ShipStation Boxtal (Available only in France) Melhor Envio (Available only in Brazil) Envia (Available only in parts of North and South America)Tracking packagesThe unique code that appears on a label's barcode is its tracking number. The number is automatically added to the order you fulfilled.  If you send your customer a shipping confirmation email, they receive the tracking number as well and can use it to track the progress of their package. Want to learn more?Check out the full course in Wix Learn on building your store or skip to the video on streamlining logistics with apps.

source_documents.title: ADI: Adding a Map to Your Site
source_documents.content:
ADI: Adding a Map to Your Site
Display a Google Map on your site so that your site visitors can easily visualize your business location. To add a map, you must add a Contact section. You can change your address at anytime and choose a color scheme that suits your site's design.In this article, learn more about:
Adding a map to your site Changing the location on your map Changing the color of your mapAdding a map to your siteTo add a map to your site, you must add a contact section. Then select the checkbox next to Map to make it visible.To add a map:
﻿Hover ﻿over Add at the top of ADI. Click Section to Page. (If you want a whole contact page, click Page.) Click Contact. (If necessary) Select the checkbox next to Map to make the map visible. Changing the location on your mapWhen you add a map to your site, a standard address is displayed. You can change this to your own address in a just a couple of clicks.To change the location on your map:
Click the Contact section on your site. Type your address in the Map field.Tip:If your Google Map does not show the correct address, we recommend pasting the coordinates of your location in the Map field, instead of the address.Changing the color of your mapChoose a color template that best suits your site's style and apply it to your map.To change the color of your map:
Click the Contact section on your site. Hover over the map and click Edit.  Select one of the map coloration options.Note:You can add several maps to your site in ADI, but they are all synced, and display the same address. When you change the location on one map, the location on the rest of the maps on your site also change. If you want to add multiple maps to your site with different addresses, then you need to head to the Editor.

source_documents.title: ADI: Customizing Your Store Pages
source_documents.content:
ADI: Customizing Your Store Pages
Adding Wix Stores automatically adds a new page, called Shop, to your site and 3 hidden pages:
The Product page: This page is displayed when a customer clicks a product in your product gallery. It contains all the details of the product they are viewing. The Cart page: Displayed when a customer clicks the Cart icon at the top, or the Add to Cart button on a product page. The Thank You page: Displayed when a customer makes a purchase.You can customize each of these pages to suit your needs.In this article, learn how to:
Customize your Product page Customize your Cart page Customize your Thank You pageCustomizing your Product pageCustomize the Product page for your store. This Product page is a dynamic page which displays different content depending on the product your customer is viewing.To customize your product page:
Click the Pages menu on the top bar inside ADI. Click Product Page.  Click your Product page in ADI. Customize your page using the options:
    
Display elements: Select or deselect the Show/Hide icon to show or hide parts of the Product page. Image scaling: Click the drop-down to choose how you want to display your product images. Button: Select or deselect the Show/Hide icon to show or hide the Add to Cart button. Sharing options: Select or deselect the Show/Hide icon to show or hide the social share icons.  Tip:Preview your site to see what it's like to purchase a product on your site!Customizing your Cart pageCustomize your Cart page and encourage your customers to check out.To customize your cart page:
Click the Pages menu on the top bar inside ADI. Click Cart. 
 Click the Cart page in ADI. Customize your page using the options:
    
Title: Edit the title text "My Cart".  
Empty Cart: Edit the text customers see when the cart is empty. Continue shopping link: Edit the "Continue Shopping" link. Add note link: Edit the link customers click to leave you a note on their order. Add promo code link: Edit the link customers click to enter a coupon. Add note instructions: Edit the note instructions text. Button text: Edit the text on the checkout button.  Customizing your Thank You pageCustomize the Thank You page to let your customers know that you appreciate them.To customize your Thank You page:
Click the Pages menu on the top bar inside ADI. Click Thank You Page. 
 Click the Thank You page in ADI. Customize your page using the options:
    
Title: Edit the title text. Subtitle: Edit the text customers see. Order number label: Edit the text under the order number field. Total cost label: Edit the text under the total cost field. Shipping address label: Edit the text under the shipping address field.

source_documents.title: Business Phone Number: Assigning Incoming Calls to Your Agents
source_documents.content:
Business Phone Number: Assigning Incoming Calls to Your Agents
Build a team of call agents to help manage your customer relationships. You can forward your incoming business calls directly to agents and decide the order in which they receive calls.Before you begin:To forward incoming calls to call agents, make sure to add call agents to your team.Step 1 | Set up call forwarding to your agentsGet started by setting up call forwarding so that incoming business calls are routed to the relevant numbers. You can add call agents anytime and set the order you want your agents to receive incoming calls.To set up call forwarding:DashboardWix app
Go to Business Phone Number in your site's dashboard. Click + Add Forwarding Number in the General tab. Select the desired call agent from the Select a call agent dropdown.
Note: Click Add Call Agent to add more agents to your team. 


 (Optional) Click and drag the Reorder icon  next to the relevant number(s) to set the order in which calls are forwarded to agents.
No longer want to forward incoming calls to an agent?
On the General tab, hover over the relevant agent under Call Forwarding. Click Remove and Confirm the change.When removing a call agent from your call forwarding list, that person can still make outgoing calls and they remain a call agent. Learn how to remove existing agents completely. 
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Marketing and select Business Phone Number. Tap General under Line Settings. Tap Call Forwarding. Tap Set Forwarding Numbers. Select the numbers to have calls forwarded to them.
Note: To add more agents, go to your site's dashboard on desktop. (Optional) On the Call Forwarding page, tap and drag the Reorder icon  next to the relevant number(s) to set the order in which calls are forwarded to agents.No longer want to forward incoming calls to an agent?On the Call Forwarding page, deselect the relevant agent. The line owner will always remain selected and cannot be deselected.
When removing a call agent from your call forwarding list, that person can still make outgoing calls and they remain a call agent. Learn how to remove existing agents completely. Step 2 | Manage ring order and durationNext, decide how long the call rings and which agents get it first. Choose to forward calls to all agents at once, or in the order of your list. Then set the number of seconds in which calls ring before going to voicemail or get forwarded to the next agent.To manage ring order and duration:DashboardWix app
Go to Business Phone Number in your site's dashboard. Scroll down to Ring order & duration in the General tab. Choose what happens when you get an incoming call:
    
Call all forwarding numbers together: All your call agents are called simultaneously. When the first agent picks up, all the other phones stop ringing. Click the dropdown to select how long incoming calls ring before sending callers to voicemail. Call forwarding numbers in order: All your call agents are called in the order you choose. Click the dropdown to select how long calls ring before forwarding to the next number.  
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Marketing and select Business Phone Number. Tap General under Line Settings. Tap Ring Order & Duration. Select one of the following:
    
Call All Numbers Together: All your call agents are called simultaneously. Tap the dropdown to select how long callers wait before reaching your voicemail. Call Numbers In Order: All your call agents are called in the order you choose. Tap the dropdown to select how long calls ring before forwarding to the next number.    Tap Save.

source_documents.title: Facebook Ads: Giving Wix Permissions for Facebook Ads
source_documents.content:
Facebook Ads: Giving Wix Permissions for Facebook Ads
When you set up your Facebook Ads account with Wix, we ask for some necessary permissions to access your Facebook Business page. This is so Wix's smart algorithm can track and analyze data and optimize your campaign regularly. If you see an error when connecting your Facebook account, Wix may not have the right permissions.Before you begin:Make sure you've set up your site work with Facebook Ads. Depending on your goal, you will need to follow different set up steps. Learn moreLearn how to:
Give permissions from your Wix account Give page permissions from your Facebook accountGiving Permissions From Your Wix AccountWhen you first set up your Facebook Ads account with Wix, you are asked to grant Wix permissions to access and manage the Facebook Business account where you'll run campaigns.To give permissions from your Wix account:
Go to Facebook Ads in your site dashboard. Click Start Now. Click Connect to Facebook. Follow the instructions in the pop-up link to link your account. Click Choose what you allow to view mandatory permissions.
 
 

 Make sure all the toggles are enabled and checkboxes selected. This is mandatory for Wix's AI to run and maintain your campaign.
Note: You must select every checkbox under Manage your business in order to run a campaign. For all other permissions, you can choose which pages to allow access to (at least one page must be selected.)



 Click OK at the bottom right.If you receive an error message after connecting your Facebook account, it means at least one mandatory permission is missing. Click Manage Permissions to view and approve the missing permissions.
Giving Page Permissions From Your Facebook AccountWhen setting up a campaign, Wix needs permissions for the Facebook Business page where you want to run the ads. If the page doesn't appear in the 'select a page' step it means some permissions are missing. You can allow these permissions in your Facebook account under Business Integrations.To give page permissions from your Facebook account:
Sign in to your Facebook account where you created the relevant Pages. Click the dropdown arrow in the top bar on the right-hand side. Click Settings & Privacy.  Click Settings.
Click Business Integrations on the left side. Select the Active or Removed tab at the top to search for Wix business integrations.
Choose what you want to do:Adjust permission settings
Click View and edit next to the relevant Wix permission. Adjust the settings by checking or unchecking the boxes next to your information. When you're inished click Save.Renew expired permissionsClick Renew next to the business integration to renew the permissions.Note:If at any time you decide to remove mandatory permissions it will disconnect your Facebook account. You must reconnect before editing or starting a new campaign. Any live campaigns will continue running as usual.

source_documents.title: Facebook Ads: Understanding Your Store Campaign Data
source_documents.content:
Facebook Ads: Understanding Your Store Campaign Data
Important:This article is only for campaigns who have selected the 'get more store orders' goal.Your Facebook Ads dashboard provides you with extensive campaign data imported directly from Facebook. For campaigns run with Wix Stores, you will see what purchases and revenue has been attributed to your campaign.How Facebook Decides Which Purchases Come From a CampaignFacebook uses an attribution model to determine which customer actions (such as 'add to cart' and purchases) were as a result of your campaign. An attribution model is a rule, or set of rules, that determine how to assign credit for sales and conversions based on online touchpoints.That means if someone sees your ad and goes to your site to make a purchase within 7 days of clicking the ad or within 1 day of viewing it (whichever happened last) that purchase is attributed to your campaign. Circumstances In Which Campaign and Store Order Data Might DifferWhen viewing your campaign from your store orders, you may see a discrepancy between Facebook's data and your purchases list. This gap could be happening due to the following reasons:Facebook counts the total transactions that come from your campaign, including those made in other places on your siteIf a customer visits your site after clicking an ad and makes a payment, it counts as campaign data even if the transaction came from somewhere other than your store. For example, if you own a fitness studio and a customer buys a store product but then also purchases a fitness class on your Bookings page, both transactions show as Facebook Ads dashboard data even though you only sold one store product.Facebook counts purchases based on a specific site 'event'Facebook tracks purchases based on customers completing a certain 'event' or action on your site such as making a purchase and seeing a 'thank you page.' However, if there's an issue after this event, such as a declined payment, the purchase won't appear in your store orders list even though it still counts as campaign data.Facebook provides campaign revenue data in $USD before convertingFacebook reports revenue data from your campaign in US dollars. This data is then converted to your store's local currency. Between conversion and exchange rates, you may see a slight gap between your dashboard data and store orders list.How Cookie Banners Affect Your Campaign DataIf you've activated the cookie consent banner it could affect your campaign data. Facebook Ads with Wix uses a Facebook Pixel placed on your site to track visitors and optimize ads. However, if a customer does not consent to the cookie banner (thus not consenting to the Facebook Pixel tracking) your Facebook Ads campaign won't be able to see or collect any data from them. Your campaign is affected in two main ways if a user does not consent to the cookie banner:
Missing campaign data: any actions the user performs on your site, including purchasing a store product, won't be attributed to your campaign (though you will still see the purchase in your store purchases). Unavailable optimizations: some audience optimizations run by Wix's AI algorithm won't be available (such as audience retargeting) as it uses data from the Facebook Pixel to serve ads to audiences who have previously visited or taken actions on your site.Learn how to manage the settings of your cookie banner here.

source_documents.title: Receiving Your Payouts from Wix Payments
source_documents.content:
Receiving Your Payouts from Wix Payments
Payouts are funds transferred from Wix Payments to your bank account.Important:
To receive payouts, your Wix Payments account must be successfully verified. In order to receive payouts to your bank account, your account status must be Active.  Payouts are only made once there's an available balance of at least $1.Payout stagesEach payment from your customer goes through 3 stages before it reaches your bank account. These are:
Processing payment: After your customer makes a successful payment, the payment is processed. Processing usually takes 2-5 business days and is comprised of 2 parts, which happen simultaneously:
    
The settlement period, which usually takes 1-2 days, but can take longer depending on your customer’s payment method. At the same time that the payment is settling, it also goes through a pending period in Wix Payments. The pending period usually lasts between 2-5 business days, and exists to protect your business, your customers and Wix Payments from fraudulent activity.   Scheduled payout: The payment is added to your next scheduled daily, weekly or monthly payout.
Note: If you have more than one payment method active in your Wix Payments account, your payouts may be grouped by payment method. Learn more about working with grouped payment methods. Sent payout: The payout has been sent from Wix Payments and should arrive in your bank account within 3 - 5 business days. Factors such as the day-of-the-week, the currency, or bank holidays will decide the arrival date of your payout.See how payouts are calculatedA payout is the sum of all credits (funds coming in) minus all debits (funds going out).The calculation takes into account the following: 
Credits:
    
Payments: Funds from payments accepted through Wix Payments. Funds Added: Funds you added to cover a negative balance for a given payment method in your Wix Payments account. Funds Transfer: Funds transferred from Wix to your Wix Payments account. Refund Reversal: Any refunds that have been cancelled. Chargeback Reversal: Any chargebacks that have been cancelled. (When applicable) Reserve Released: If there are funds released from reserve, they're added to your next payout.   Debits:

Refunds: Any refunds made to your customers.  Refund Reversal Fee: The fee for processing the reversal transaction. Chargebacks: Any chargebacks called by your customer's card issuer. Chargeback Fee: The fee for processing a chargeback transaction. Chargeback Reversal Fee: The fee for processing a chargeback reversal transaction. (When applicable) Reserve Held: The portion of the payout that stays in reserve is deducted from the amount.  If the resulting sum (credit - debit) is a positive number, the amount is paid out to your bank account, and the payout status switches from Scheduled to Sent.Payout schedulesThere are three payout schedules you can choose from, depending on the needs of your business: 
Daily: Payouts are sent every day, including transactions that were made before the daily cut-off time*. Any transactions received after that time will be included in the next day's payout.  Weekly: Payouts are sent every Monday. You can change this to any other day of the week through your account settings.   Monthly: Payouts are sent on the 1st of every month. You can change this to any other day of the month through your account settings. In months with less than 29 days, payouts are sent on the last day of the month.* About the payout cut-off time: Depending on your region, Wix Payments sends payouts every day at the following time:
US: 6AM EST. Europe: 6AM GMT.  You can choose and change your payout schedule at any time from your Wix Payments account settings. Whichever schedule you select will apply to all your Wix Payments payment methods.Show me how
Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard. Click Manage next to Wix Payments.
 Click Go to Dashboard. Click Account Settings on the left. Scroll down to Payout Settings. Select the checkbox next to the relevant option:
    
Daily Weekly

Use the drop-down menu to select a day.    Monthly

Use the drop-down menu to select a day.      Click Save. Receiving your first payoutYour first payout can only be scheduled once your Wix Payments account is successfully verified. After receiving your first payment, it's available for payout within an average of 7 days. Once the payout is sent, it takes an average of 3-5 business days for the payout to reach your bank account. Learn more about receiving your payouts.Viewing your payoutsView information about previous and upcoming payouts, as well as detailed information about each payment.
Go to Payouts in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant payout to view details. Tip:You can still access your Wix Payments dashboard, even if your Wix Payments account has been disconnected.Grouped payment methodsIf you have grouped payment methods in your Wix Payments account, both your scheduled payouts and sent payouts are organized according to their group. As a result, you have several payouts scheduled or sent on the same date. Learn more about working with grouped payment methods.Tip:By hovering over the overview date, you can see a breakdown of which payouts are due on that date.Reserve FundsIn some cases, Wix Payments needs to hold a portion of each payout for a set amount of time. This is known as a reserve. Keeping a percentage of your payouts in reserve protects you and Wix Payments from financial risk and covers any potential chargebacks or refunds. Once the funds in reserve become available, we automatically include them in a future payout.There are two kinds of reserves Wix can hold:
Rolling reserve: This is the most common type of reserve. A rolling reserve is when a percent of each payout is held for a set number of days before being released in the next available payout. Rolling reserves are held from each payout on an ongoing basis. One-time reserve: This is a specific amount of money held from your available balance one time for a set number of days, then released in the next available payout. If your Wix Payments account is subject to a rolling reserve, you're notified by email of a change in your payout policy. A one-time reserve does not affect your payout policy. Payouts on HoldPayouts are placed on hold if there is an issue blocking your payout. Once the issue has been identified and resolved, the payout will be added to your next scheduled payout. Learn more about payouts on hold.

source_documents.title: Removing Deleted Sites, Old URLs, or Files From Search Results
source_documents.content:
Removing Deleted Sites, Old URLs, or Files From Search Results
Search engines crawl and index content from every page that you publish, with the exception of pages that you prevented search engines from indexing, pages that are password protected.Just as it takes search engines time to crawl and index a new website, it also takes time for them to recognize that a website or old URLs have changed or are no longer available. This can happen if you deleted a page, image, or file from your site, or if you edited the URL of one of your pages. The process of removing pages and files from search results and how long it takes depends entirely on the individual search engines. This also applies to images appearing in Google Images search results.Speeding up the removal processIf you verified your site with Google or Bing, you can submit a request to speed up the removal of pages that you don't want in their search results.Learn how to manually request removals using:
Google Search Console Bing Webmaster ToolsIf you did not verify your site with Google and Bing, you need to wait for them to remove the pages. If you've created a new site and the URLs from the old site are still appearing in search results, you should submit your sitemap to Google and other relevant search engines. This can help speed up both the indexing of your new site and the removal of old site URLs from search results.  Note:If you have recently upgraded your site and connected your own domain, Wix automatically redirects any traffic to your free Wix URL to your new domain. When search engines crawl your site, they detect your newly connected domain and remove the free Wix URL from search results. Learn more about updating the free Wix URL in search results
