Once you submit them, the Branded App by Wix submissions team will get notified and upload the screenshots to Store Listings on your behalf.Make sure your screenshots meet the Apple and Google requirements:
Apple: Requires 3 images for the 3 different device types (sizes 6.5, 5.5, and 12.9). Google: Requires specifications for an app icon, feature graphic, and phone screenshots. 
Learn more about Apple and Google requirements.We are always working to update and improve our products and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: CMS: Setting Up the Selection Tags Input Element and Managing Tags
source_documents.content:
CMS: Setting Up the Selection Tags Input Element and Managing Tags
Give visitors a way to filter the items that appear on your live site or let them submit choices to your collection with the Selection Tags element. In your CMS (Content Management System) collection, you add the Tags field and manage the values associated with each item. If you need to apply changes to a tag value, the changes automatically apply to every item using the tag, so you don't have to manually edit them everywhere in your collection. In this article, learn more about: 
Using the Selection Tags input element to filter content on your live site Using the Selection Tags input element to collect content from site visitors Managing Tags in your CMS collectionUsing the Selection Tags input element to filter content on your live siteConnect the Selection Tags input element to the same dataset that connects to a repeater or gallery. Then set the element to filter content and choose which collection field's values you want to show as filter options in the Selection Tags element. When visitors click these filter options in the element, the repeater or gallery only displays items that have a matching field value. You can also apply advanced filtering conditions to choose an operator that controls how the filter is applied (e.g. Is any of, Equals any of, Includes any). Any filters or sorts you apply to the dataset also apply to the connected elements. This means you can add filters to the dataset to exclude items from appearing and add sorts to control their order. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Add the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Go to the page or section where you want visitors to filter content by tags.  Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Selection Tags.  Click and drag the relevant Selection Tags element onto the page.   
Connect the Selection Tags element to the CMS:
    
Click the Connect to CMS icon  on the Selection Tags element.  Select Filter content in the Connect Selection Tags panel on the right.  Click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select the same dataset that connects to the elements (e.g. repeater, gallery, table) that you want visitors to filter.  Click the Filter content by drop-down and choose the field that visitors will use to filter the content.
Tip: To add a new field to your collection and use it for filtering content, select Add new field, then enter the field name and select a Text, Number, Tags, or Reference field type. You can add content to the field in your CMS collection later.  (Optional) Click the Condition drop-down and choose an operator that controls how the filter is applied (e.g. Is any of, Equals any of, Includes any).
Note: The conditions vary depending on the connected field type.   
Customize the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Click the Settings icon  to edit the Field title.  Click the Layout icon  to set the text indentation, padding, spacing and alignment.  Click the Design icon  to choose a preset design and customize it further.  Click the Animation icon  to choose and customize an animation effect.  Click the Stretch icon  to set the element to full width.   
Click Preview to test your Selection Tags element. Click Publish if you are ready to make the changes go live. 
Go to your editor. Add the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Go to the page or section where you want visitors to filter content by tags.  Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Selection Tags.  Click and drag the relevant Selection Tags element onto the page.   
Connect the Selection Tags element to the CMS:
    
Click the Connect to CMS icon  on the Selection Tags element.  Select Filter content in the Connect Selection Tags panel on the right.  Click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select the same dataset that connects to the elements (e.g. repeater, gallery, table) that you want visitors to filter.  Click the Filter content by drop-down and choose the field that visitors will use to filter the content.
Tip: To add a new field to your collection and use it for filtering content, select Add new field, then enter the field name and select a Text, Number, Tags, or Reference field type. You can add content to the field in your CMS collection later.  (Optional) Click the Condition drop-down and choose an operator that controls how the filter is applied (e.g. Is any of, Equals any of, Includes any).
Note: The conditions vary depending on the connected field type.   
Customize the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Click the Settings icon  to edit the Field title.  Click the Layout icon  to set the text indentation, padding, spacing and alignment.   
Click the Preview icon  at the top right to test your Selection Tags element.  Click Publish if you are ready to make the changes go live. Using the Selection Tags input element to collect content from site visitorsUse the Selection Tags input element to collect responses from visitors. You can use a collection field for the choices or manage the choices in the element itself. When visitors select an option from the Selection Tags element and press a 'Submit' button, their submission is saved to the relevant field in the collection you choose. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Add the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Go to the page or section where you want visitors to submit their selection.  Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Selection Tags.  Click and drag the relevant Selection Tags element onto the page.   
Connect the Selection Tags element to the CMS collection where you will store the submissions:
    
Click the Connect to CMS icon  on the Selection Tags element.  Connect to a dataset that binds to the collection where you will store the submissions: 
        
If your page already has a dataset:

Click Collect content.  Click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select the relevant dataset. Alternatively, click Add a Dataset to create a new one, then choose the collection to connect, enter the dataset name and click Create.   If your page does not have a dataset: 

Click + Add a Dataset on the right. Then choose the collection to connect, enter the dataset name and click Create.   Click Collect content.      Click the Tag values connect to drop-down and choose the Tags field in which you will store the submissions.
Tip: To add a new field for storing submissions, select Add new field, then enter the field name and click Add.  Set the dataset mode and collection permissions:
        
Click Dataset Settings.  Click the Dataset mode drop-down and select Write. (If necessary) Click the permissions type next to Permissions and select the relevant collection permissions:
            
Collect content: Allow visitors to add content to the collection. Select the relevant options under Who can add content to this collection? and Who can view this content?. Then click Save.  Custom: Set custom permissions to control who can view, add, update, and delete content. You can choose different permissions for item creators, site members, and everyone else. Click the relevant checkboxes next to each role to choose whether visitors with the role can view, add, update, or delete collection content from the live site. Then click Save.   Click Back to Selection Tags at the top of the Dataset Settings panel.     
Click the Connect list items toggle to choose where to manage the choices that appear in the Selection Tags element:
    
Enabled: Use a field from another CMS collection for the choices. Choose a dataset that connects to the collection that has the field you want to use as the choices. Then click the Labels and values connect to drop-down and select the Text or Number field you want to use or select Add new field to create a new field for the choices.  Disabled: Click Manage Choices on the Selection Tags element to create and manage the choices in the element itself, rather than in a CMS collection.   
Customize the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Click the Settings icon  to edit the Field title or require visitors to select a tag when submitting as part of a form.  Click the Layout icon  to set the text indentation, padding, spacing and alignment.  Click the Design icon  to choose a preset design and customize it further.  Click the Animation icon  to choose and customize an animation effect.  Click the Stretch icon  to set the element to full width.    Add a 'Submit' button for visitors to click to submit after they make a selection in the Selection Tags element. 
Click Preview to test your Selection Tags element. Click Publish if you are ready to make the changes go live. 
Go to your editor. Add the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Go to the page or section where you want visitors to submit their selection.  Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Selection Tags.  Click and drag the relevant Selection Tags element onto the page.   
Connect the Selection Tags element to the CMS collection where you will store the submissions:
    
Click the relevant option on the right:
Note: The options vary, based on the number of datasets your page has. 
        
Add a Dataset: Choose the collection in which you will store the submissions, give the dataset a name and click Create. Then select Collect content.  Collect content: Select this option, then click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select a dataset that connects to the collection where you will store the submissions.
Tip: Select Add a Dataset to create and connect a new dataset.    Click the Tag values connects to drop-down and choose the Tags field in which you will store the submissions.
Tip: To add a new field for storing submissions, select Add new field, then enter the field name and click Add.  Set the dataset mode and collection permissions:
        
Click Dataset Settings.  Click the Dataset mode drop-down and select Write. (If necessary) Click the permissions type next to Permissions and select the relevant collection permissions:
            
Collect content: Allow visitors to add content to the collection. Select the relevant options under Who can add content to this collection? and Who can view this content?. Then click Save. Custom: Set custom permissions to control who can view, add, update, and delete content. You can choose different permissions for item creators, site members, and everyone else. Click the relevant checkboxes next to each role to choose whether visitors with the role can view, add, update, or delete collection content from the live site. Then click Save.   Click Back to Selection Tags element at the top of the Dataset Settings panel.     
Click the Connect list items toggle to choose where to manage the choices that appear in the Selection Tags element:
    
Enabled: Use a field from another CMS collection for the choices. Choose a dataset that connects to the collection that has the field you want to use for the choices. Then click the Labels and values connect to drop-down and select the Text or Number field you want to use.
Tip: Select Add new field to create a new field for the choices that you can fill out later.  Disabled: Click Manage Choices on the Selection Tags element to create and manage the choices in the element itself, rather than in a CMS collection.   
Customize the Selection Tags input element: 
    
Click the Settings icon  to edit the Field title or require visitors to select a tag when submitting as part of a form.  Click the Layout icon  to set the text indentation, padding, spacing and alignment.  Click the Design icon  in the Inspector panel on the right to edit the design.    Add a 'Submit' button for visitors to click to submit after they make a selection in the Selection Tags element. 
Click the Preview icon  at the top right to test your Selection Tags element.  Click Publish if you are ready to make the changes go live. Managing Tags in your CMS collectionAfter adding a Tags field type to your collection, you can add the tag values for each item. When adding tag values to an item, a list appears where you can select from your existing list of tag values. If you need to rename, merge, or delete tags, the changes you make to the tags apply to all items and elements on your site where the tags are in use. This lets you manage your tags efficiently, without having to manually apply your changes to them in every item in which they appear. To add and manage tags in your collection: 
Go to CMS in your site's dashboard. Alternatively, you can click CMS  in your editor﻿, then click Your Collections.  Click the relevant collection. Click Manage Fields.  Click + Add Field.  Select Tags and click Choose Field Type.  
Enter a name for the field in the Field name. (Velo only) If necessary, update the Field ID, which is used in the site's code. You cannot update this ID later.  (Optional) Enter help text to include a tooltip in your collection next to the field name. Click Save. Click the Tags field of the relevant item and choose what you want to do:Add a new tag to an item
Enter the name of the tag you want to use.  Press Enter on your keyboard or select + Create {tag name}.  Repeat these steps to add multiple tags for the same item. Select the Tags field for a different item and repeat these steps to add new tag fields to the item. Add existing tags to an item
Click + Add Tag. Select the tags that you want to add to the item from the list of existing tags. 
 Select the Tags field for a different item and repeat these steps to add existing tags to the item.Rename, merge, or delete tagsIf you rename, merge, or delete tags, the changes are applied to the tags everywhere they exist. To manage your tags: 
Click + Add Tag. Select Manage Tags.  Choose what you want to do: 
    
Rename: Change the name of the tag everywhere it is in use. Click the relevant tag, edit the name and press Enter on your keyboard.  Merge: Combine multiple tags into one tag everywhere the tags are in use:
        
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant tag and select Merge.  Select the checkbox next to the tags you want to merge and click Merge. 
 Enter a name for the tags you're combining and press Enter on your keyboard.    Delete: Remove a tag from all the items it's assigned to: 
        
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant tag and select Delete. Click Delete to confirm.      Click Close. NextLearn how to add field validations to make the field a mandatory 'required' field in your collection.

source_documents.title: Connecting Exactly as a Payment Provider
source_documents.content:
Connecting Exactly as a Payment Provider
Accept payments from your customers using Exactly as your payment provider. General Info Supported countries Czech Republic and United KingdomSupported payment methodsCredit / debit cardSupported currenciesEURTransaction feesMay vary. Fees start from .7% + .08 EUR per transactionNotesThe currency used in your Wix account must match the currency in your Exactly account. If the currencies do not match, the transactions may be declined. Learn how to change your currencyManaging your accountFor information on topics such as payout schedules, refunding a customer, chargeback disputes, and more, contact ExactlyIn this article, learn about:
Connecting Exactly Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Connecting Exactly
Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard.
Tip: Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it. Click See More Payment Options. Click See Options next to Third-Party Credit/Debit Card Providers. Click Connect next to Exactly.
Depending on whether you are creating a new Exactly account or have an existing account, follow the instructions:Have an account
Enter your Project ID and Api Key.  Click Connect.Don't have an account
Click Create Exactly account.. Fill in the registration form to create your Exactly account. Wait for an email or chat message from Exactly to get your Project ID and Api Key credentials. Return to the Accept Payments tab (repeat steps 1-5) and follow the steps under Have an account to connect your account.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about accepting payments.How can I tell if a payment method is active?In order to accept online payments, you must connect a payment provider. Once connected, your checkout will be active for your chosen payment method(s).

You need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.Is my currency supported?Be aware that payments will fail If you are using an unsupported currency.
The currency used in your payment provider account must match the currency that you set in your Wix account. If you need to change the currency set in your provider account, please contact your payment provider.If your current payment provider does not support your desired currency, Wix hosts a wide range of alternative payment providers. Learn how to change your payment provider.What is a minimum payment amount?Some payment providers have a minimum payment threshold (e.g. $1.01). Payments below this amount will not be processed.Make sure that all of your products or services are priced over the minimum threshold. This includes discounted items or Pricing Plans. Please contact your payment provider to get the most up-to-date information about their minimum payment threshold. Can I offer recurring payments?To offer recurring payments, you must connect a payment provider that supports recurring payments.How do I get my payouts? Payouts are managed by your payment provider. If your provider is a third-party provider, contact them directly. 
If your provider is Wix Payments, learn about receiving payouts from Wix Payments. My customers' payments are being declined. What can I do?If your customers are experiencing payment failures, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting issues for accepting payments.Why can’t I connect my desired payment provider?If you’re having trouble connecting your payment provider, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting common connection issues.Do I need to upgrade my site to accept payments?Yes. You need to upgrade your site to a plan that supports payments in order to accept payments.

source_documents.title: Displaying Events Using Your Site Colors or Google Colors in the Google Event Calendar App
source_documents.content:
Displaying Events Using Your Site Colors or Google Colors in the Google Event Calendar App
When choosing colors for your Google Event Calendar, you have 2 options; use your site's colors or use the colors that Google chooses for you. Your Google Event Calendar app can host multiple calendars for various purposes.For example, you can add a calendar for events specifically related to teachers and another related to students. The events in each calendar are given specific colors based on the calendar they are aligned to.  In this article, learn how to:
Display your site colors in the Google Event Calendar app Display Google colors in the Google Event Calendar app Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Displaying your site colors in the Google Event Calendar appYou can choose to use your site theme colors for your calendars. Each calendar displays a different color from your main site colors. To display your site colors:
Click the Google Event Calendar app in your Editor.  Click Settings.  Click the Design tab.  Click Events.  Scroll down to Event Colors.  Select Use site theme colors. (Optional) Click the color boxes next to the relevant calendars to adjust the colors. Displaying Google colors in the Google Event Calendar appYou can choose to use the colors from Google's logo in each of your calendars. To display Google colors:
Click the Google Event app in your Editor.  Click Settings.  Click the Design tab.  Click Events.  Scroll down to Event Colors.  Select Use Google Calendar colors.  (Optional) Click the color boxes next to the relevant calendars to adjust the colors. FAQsClick a question below to learn more.How are my site theme colors applied to my calendars?When using site colors, it is the calendars that are colored and not specific events. By default, the app uses a different site theme color for each calendar. Why do my site colors look different? You may notice that your vivid and bright site colors are toned down slightly to make them more accessible.What is a "Primary calendar"?Your primary calendar is the default calendar that is created when you set up a Google account. It serves as the main calendar where you can add, manage, and view your events and appointments. It is often used as the central calendar for organizing your schedule.What events are displayed?When you sync or connect your Google account to your Google Event Calendar app, the app retrieves and displays your primary calendar's events. Any changes or additions you make to your primary calendar in the Google Event Calendar app by Wix are also reflected in your main Google Calendar.

source_documents.title: Selling CBD on Your Wix Site
source_documents.content:
Selling CBD on Your Wix Site
If your business is based in the U.S., you can use Wix to sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products online. Complete our declaration form, connect to a payment provider that works with CBD merchants and start accepting payments from all major credit cards. Before getting started, read the following article and make sure you fully understand the terms for selling CBD products on your site.In this article, learn more about:
What are hemp & hemp-derived products? Requirements to sell CBD on Wix Declaration for selling hemp and/or hemp-derived products Available payment providers Setting up to sell hemp on your site Frequently asked questions (FAQs) Note:As laws and regulations continue to develop and vary significantly from one state to another, we recommend consulting with an attorney before selling hemp or hemp-derived CBD products on your site. It is your responsibility to ensure that your business complies with all applicable regulations and to monitor them regularly. What are hemp & hemp-derived products?As a U.S. merchant, you must comply with federal and state law, as well as FDA and other applicable regulations, defining what hemp-derived CBD products you can legally sell. Important:The sale of hemp and hemp-derived CBD products is subject to a complex set of rules (on federal, state and local levels). You must make sure that the products you sell and the manner in which they are described, marketed and shipped is legal. We highly recommend consulting with an attorney before starting to sell these products.  Federal lawThe U.S. federal law* defines Hemp as the following:The Cannabis Sativa L. plant with no more than 0.3% THC concentration on a dry weight basis. This includes any part of that plant, including the seeds thereof and all derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not.*Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 ("Farm Bill")State lawIn addition to the federal law, states in the U.S. have issued their own regulations or declarations regarding the sale, purchase, possession and consumption of hemp and CBD products. Certain states have no explicit law that either allows or prohibits the retail sales of such products. These laws, declarations and policy statements are separate and unrelated to any laws governing medical use of cannabis and other THC-containing products. As a Wix user, it is your responsibility to be familiar with the regulations relevant to your business. Wix does not support the sale or purchase of hemp and hemp-derived CBD products in the following U.S. states: HawaiiIdahoIowaMississippiNew HampshireSouth DakotaThis means that your business cannot be located in the above states, nor can you ship hemp or hemp-derived CBD products to customers residing there. FDA (Food and Drug Administration) regulationsIn addition to state and federal law, the FDA also governs the sale of hemp and hemp-derived products. We recommend checking the FDA's website on a regular basis for more instructions on selling these products, as well as cosmetics and supplements. Requirements to sell CBD on WixEvery Wix site owner interested in selling hemp and hemp-derived products in the U.S. must comply with the following requirements: 
Your business must be managed in the U.S., from a state where Wix supports the sale of these products. You must read this article and make sure you fully understand the terms for selling hemp and hemp-derived CBD products on your site. You must read, confirm and submit the Declaration for Selling Hemp Products.  You must connect your site to a third-party payment provider that supports the sale of hemp and hemp-derived CBD products.  You must adjust your store's shipping regions only to the states that allow the U.S.e and sale of hemp and hemp-derived CBD products. Declaration for selling hemp productsBefore connecting to a payment provider and selling Hemp products on your site, you're required to read and submit this declaration. The declaration form describes the legal terms for selling hemp and hemp-derived products on Wix. By submitting it, you confirm that your business is located in a U.S. state we can support and that your shipping area is limited to that same list of states. You're also confirming that the products on your site answer Wix's requirements. To access and submit the declaration for selling hemp products on Wix, click here. Available payment providersWix has partnered with third-party payment providers, Square, Bankful, Priority Payments and Evergreen Payments Northwest so you can securely accept payments for hemp and hemp-derived CBD products on your site.  If you haven't yet connected your site to a payment provider, you'll be able to connect Square, Bankful or Evergreen Payments Northwest right after submitting the declaration form. You can either create a new account with Square or connect an existing account if you have one. Tip:If you need your payment provider to support recurring payments, see our list of recurring payment providers. Changing your payment providerIf your site is connected to a provider that doesn't support the sale of hemp and hemp-derived, you'll be able to change it after submitting the declaration form.  Show me howAfter reading and submitting the declaration, you'll be redirected to the Accept Payments tab in your site's dashboard.


Click Connect beside your desired provider.  Click Yes, Switch to confirm your new provider. Connect your account:
    
Have an account:

Enter your credentials Click Sign in.   Don't have an account: Click Create new account and follow the steps to create your account.  Note:When creating an account with a third-party payment provider to sell hemp or hemp-derived CBD products, the application process may take longer than usual. Wix cannot guarantee the approval of your account, which is at the sole discretion of the relevant payment provider.  Wix PaymentsCurrently, Wix Payments does not process payments for hemp or CBD products. If you would like to sell these products on your site and have already connected to Wix Payments, you'll be automatically disconnected once you submit the declaration form. Tip:Alternatively, you can create a new Wix site dedicated to hemp and hemp-derived CBD products. Our stunning ready-made templates can help you get started. Pick a template and customize it to your exact needs: CBD Skin CareCBD Facial OilsCBD Soaps and CandlesSetting up to sell hemp on your siteTo start selling hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products on your site, you need to complete the following steps:
Read this article to check Wix's requirements for selling hemp and hemp-derived CBD products. Click here to go to the dedicated "Sell CBD on Wix" page. Then, do one of the following:
    
Create a new Wix account: Click Get Started. Log in to your Wix account: Click Sign in at the top right.    Follow the steps to submit our declaration form.  Connect your site to a payment method:
    
Click Connect next to the payment methods you want to connect. Select an option:  
Have an account:

Enter your credentials Click Sign in.   Don't have an account: Click Create new account and follow the steps to create your account.  Already connected to a payment provider?Click Change Provider to select a new provider that supports CBD and hemp payments. If you're currently connected to Wix Payments, your account will be automatically closed after submitting the declaration. 
Adjust your store's shipping regions to exclude the states that aren't supported by Wix.
Tip: Learn how to add new products to your store.

        Read and submit the declaration form to start selling hemp and hemp-derived CBD products
    


            Go To Form
      

FAQsTake a look below to find the answers to our most frequently asked questions on selling hemp and hemp-derived products. What does the term "Hemp" mean?Under federal law, constituents derived from hemp means the plant Cannabis sativa L. and any part of that plant, including the seeds thereof and all derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not, with a delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration of not more than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.Can I sell CBD products derived from marijuana?No. As stated in our Declaration for Selling Hemp and CBD Products, you are only allowed to sell hemp-derived CBD products. These products cannot contain more than 0.3 percent of delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) concentration (on a dry weight basis). Additionally, they must not contain any Controlled Substances as defined in Schedule IV of Title 32 United States Code Controlled Substances Act. Can I sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products in my store while also selling other kinds of products?Yes. You can use the same Wix site to sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products alongside other products of any kind, as long as your chosen payment provider allows it in their terms and conditions. If you already have a store that's up and running and would like to add products, you can either add the products there or create a new site. Choose from our CBD templates (see below) or explore the full catalog of 500+ templates created by Wix.
CBD Skin Care CBD Facial Oils CBD Soaps and CandlesNote:As stated in Wix's requirements for selling hemp and hemp-derived products, you must adjust your store's shipping regions to the states supported by Wix. Which Wix Apps can I use while selling hemp and/or hemp-derived products CBD products on my site? You may use any Wix app (e.g. Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, Pay Button) for selling hemp and/or hemp-derived products CBD products.My business is located outside of the United States. Can I sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products using Wix?Wix's solution is designated for users selling hemp and hemp-derived products in the U.S. states that we support. As with any other product you want to sell on Wix, you should check local regulations before actually adding them to your site. If you're located outside of the U.S. and would like to start selling hemp and hemp-derived products, we highly recommend consulting with an attorney to find out what regulations apply to you. Additionally, you must verify with your payment provider that they're able to process payments for hemp and hemp-derived products.  Are Wix site owners responsible for knowing the regulatory aspects of selling hemp and hemp-derived CBD products? If the law changes, will Wix notify its users? Like any other Wix user, you are responsible for your site's content and the products you sell. When using Wix to sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products, you are responsible for understanding the federal, state and local regulations that apply to them. As U.S. laws regarding hemp and CBD products continue to develop, we recommend reviewing them on a regular basis, as well as the FDA's regulation of Cannabis and Cannabis-derived products (Learn More). Wix will not notify users of changes made to these laws. We highly recommend consulting with an attorney before selling these products on your site.Which shipping service can I use to send my hemp or CBD products?You can use any carrier that can legally deliver help and/or hemp-derived CBD products. We recommend contacting the relevant shipping service to check this in advance.  I am currently connected to a payment provider that is not included in the list above. Can I continue using that provider to process my payments?As a Wix user, you are not limited to the specific providers we've partnered with for this solution. As long as your chosen provider is integrated with Wix, and supports the sale of hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products, you may use it to process your payments. It's important to note that many payment providers don't process these transactions, so we highly recommend checking with them in advance.  I've previously created a Wix Payments account that was closed because I sell hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products. Can I now use Wix to sell these products? Yes. If your Wix Payments account was closed due to this particular line of business, you can still use Wix as a platform to sell these products. To get started, read and submit the Declaration for Selling Hemp and Hemp Derived Products. I'm currently using Wix Payments to process my payments. What happens if I decide to start selling CBD using Wix?Wix Payments cannot process any transactions related to hemp and/or hemp-derived CBD products. For this reason, we'll disconnect and close your Wix Payments account once you submit the declaration form.  Any credit remaining in your Wix Payments account will be paid out according to your current payout cycle, as long as our compliance team can confirm that these funds aren't associated to the sale of restricted or prohibited products. If your Wix payments account was closed due to the sale of restricted or prohibited goods / services, any credit remaining in your account has been or may be refunded to the credit card owner (your customer).Checking Wix Payments' Restricted and Prohibited Businesses list,  I see CBD in the 'prohibited' section. However, this article states that Wix does support CBD in this solution. What does it mean?  The Wix Payments Restricted and Prohibited Businesses list is applicable to those who want to use   Wix Payments as their payment provider. You can still use Wix as a platform, only with a different payment provider that can support the sale of hemp and hemp-derived CBD products.  To get started, read and submit the Declaration for Selling Hemp and Hemp Derived Products and connect to one of the suggested providers that processes CBD transactions.

source_documents.title: Troubleshooting Google Analytics
source_documents.content:
Troubleshooting Google Analytics
Adding a Google Analytics Tracking ID to your Wix site lets you track the number of visitors to your site, where they come from, how long they stay, what keywords they use to find your site, and more. If you're experiencing issues using Google Analytics, try the following troubleshooting steps:Step 1 | Make sure your domain is connected to Wix correctlyYou can check your domain connection using Wix Domain Assistant.Step 2 | Make sure the property ID is correctly formattedYou can track information in Google Analytics about your site visitors using a Google Analytics 4 (GA4) property (G-XXXXXXXXXX).If you're not sure if your property ID is correctly formatted, follow these steps to get your Google Analytics property ID and check the format. Note: From July 1, 2023, Universal Analytics (UA) properties will stop collecting data. If you previously connected a UA property to your site, you should upgrade to a Google Analytics 4 (GA4) property.Step 3 | Make sure you haven't added the HTML elementCheck to make sure you haven't added Google Analytics using the HTML tool.
Learn MoreStep 4 | Make sure you haven't added Google Analytics multiple timesCheck that you haven't added Google Analytics to both Google Tag Manager and Marketing Integrations. If you've added it in multiple locations, remove it from one of the locations to allow Google Analytics to work properly. Step 5 | Use DebugView to check your Google Analytics connectionAfter adding your Google Analytics (GA4) tracking code to your Wix site, it may take some time before you see statistics in your Google Analytics account.If you are no longer receiving data in Google Analytics, you can use Google's DebugView to troubleshoot connection issues. DebugView shows you the events that Analytics collects in real time.Learn more about using DebugViewStep 6 | Check if you have a cookie banner on your siteWhen you add the cookie banner to your site, it automatically disables the usage of non-essential cookies and scripts until your visitor provides consent. Learn MoreAs a result, Google Analytics will only collect information after a visitor approves using the relevant cookies. Note about Google Analytics and cookie banners:
Using a cookie banner on your site can reduce the site traffic recorded by GA4. This is because some visitors might not give their consent to be tracked. For this reason, it is normal if you see a drop in your Google Analytics numbers.  Due to recent regulations that apply to Google, if you don't have a cookie banner on your site and a site visitor comes from a country that requires consent (e.g. those covered by GDPR) no data is sent to Google Analytics. Google only tracks sessions when visitors give explicit consent. As you know your target audience best, use this information to make an informed decision about whether to add a cookie banner.Important:
You should make sure that your use of Google Analytics is compliant with local data protection regulations. Learn more about Google Analytics and the GDPR By using this service, you are engaging directly with a third-party service provider. We recommend reviewing the service provider's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use prior to your use of such third-party service. You acknowledge that we are not liable for any loss or damage resulting from your use of such third-party service, including any liability arising from any personal data exchanged between you and such third-party.

Enterprise Solution: About Domains
From the enterprise dashboard, you can manage all the domains for your sites. Transfer or connect an existing domain or, if you need a new domain URL, you can get one straight from your dashboard. Learn more about Wix Studio for enterprise or contact our sales team.Transfer a domainTransfer your domain so that Wix becomes your domain host. Once the transfer is complete, your domain's contact information, DNS settings, and registration payments are all managed from within your Wix Studio for enterprise account. Domain transfers can take up to 7 days to complete. If you want your domain to link to your site in a shorter timeframe, you can connect your domain to Wix first.Connect a domainConnect a domain you already own to Wix by changing its name servers. With this connection method, Wix hosts your DNS, while your domain remains registered with its current host.To connect your domain, you need to update the DNS records in your domain host account (usually the company you bought your domain from). Wix Studio for enterprise provides a step-by-step outline to help you. Once the domain has been connected, it can take up to 48 hours for your domain's new DNS records to propagate and your site to appear worldwide.Get a new domainGet a domain from Wix to give your site a personalized, unique web address. This makes it easier for visitors to find your site by providing a distinct online space for your company and brand.The Wix Studio enterprise solution provides a complimentary domain voucher every time you upgrade a site. Use this voucher to get your desired domain.Assign a domainOnce you've transferred, connected or purchased a new domain, you can assign it to any site in your Wix Studio or enterprise account. You can assign a domain to a site that has no assigned domains. Alternatively, you can reassign a domain as the new primary domain for a given site.

source_documents.title: SSO: Troubleshooting and Error Codes for IT Admin
source_documents.content:
SSO: Troubleshooting and Error Codes for IT Admin
View the following list of error codes that the end user may report to you if they experience an error using Single Sign-On (SSO). This list includes a description of the root cause of each error.SSO authentication allows the use of a single ID and password to quickly and securely log in to any of several related, yet independent, online platforms. Learn more about SSO settings.Error Code:Description:8020Failed to acquire ID token from code.8021A user is trying to log in to an account using SSO with their employee email, but they already have an account associated with this email.8022The user is trying to log in with SSO to an account that has no Open ID authentication method configured in authentication settings.8023The user is trying to log in with SSO using a federated authentication ID, which does not exist in the account authentication settings.8024SSO user doesn't exist. In SSO for clients, users (clients) must already exist as SSO users when they attempt to log in with SSO. We identify users by their external user id (their ID in IdP) and the SSO ID. This error is returned when such a user doesn't exist.8025The user of the SSO account (such as VP where JIT provisioning is set to false) doesn't exist.8026An existing user is trying to log in to an account they don't belong to.8027SSO IdP authorization request has failed.

source_documents.title: Transferring Your Wix Domain Away from Wix
source_documents.content:
Transferring Your Wix Domain Away from Wix
You can transfer a domain purchased from Wix to another domain host. When you transfer your domain away from Wix, your domain's contact information, DNS settings, and renewal payments are all managed in your new provider's account.Before you begin:We recommend keeping your domain with Wix as your host. If you transfer your domain away, your Wix site is disconnected, and Wix is no longer able to assist with managing your domain. Transferring your Wix domain away from WixTransfer your domain away from Wix to have your domain settings, billing and support managed outside of Wix.To transfer your domain:
Go to Domains in your Wix account. Click the Domain Actions icon  next to the relevant domain. Select Transfer away from Wix.
After reviewing the info about transferring your domain, click Transfer Domain.  Click I Still Want to Transfer. We’ll send a transfer authorization code (EPP code) to your domain's registrant contact email address.  Once you get the code, follow the instructions from your new domain host to transfer your domain. Tip:Once your new domain host enters the EPP code on their end to initiate the transfer, you can use whois.com to confirm it was initiated. Go to whois.com to check the status. Search for your domain, then check the Status field, which should show "pending transfer" if the transfer has been initiated. FAQsClick below for answers to common questions about transferring a domain away from Wix.What are ICANN's rules about domain transfers?ICANN oversees the domain name system. According to their transfer rules:
You cannot transfer a domain within 60 days of purchase. Changing your registrant contact information locks your domain from transfer for 60 days. Transferring your domain locks it from being able to transfer again for 60 days. How long does it take to transfer a domain?It can take up to 7 days for the domain transfer to complete.After the transfer, will I pay the same price for my domain renewal?Future domain renewals will be subject to the pricing of your new domain host.Who do I contact about the status of my domain transfer?Wix is unable to track the status of your transfer once it's been initiated. Please contact the receiving domain host for updates on your transfer. Can I transfer a Wix domain to Network Solutions?If transferring to Network Solutions, let them know you are transferring a Wix domain. They should provide you with a form to fill out.Can I transfer a .co.uk Wix domain away from Wix?Yes. Learn more about transferring a .co.uk domain away from Wix.Can I transfer an expired Wix domain?Yes, it is possible to transfer an expired Wix domain, as long as the domain is still in the Grace Period.  Will my business email work after transferring?No. You need to add the MX records again after the transfer in order for the business email to work.

source_documents.title: Enterprise Solution: Adding and Setting Up Salesforce Integration
source_documents.content:
Enterprise Solution: Adding and Setting Up Salesforce Integration
Connect your Wix Studio for enterprise account to your Salesforce account so you always have the most up-to-date information. Using our automations, you can send data like store orders and form submissions to Salesforce, as soon as they're captured in Wix.Note:Wix integrates with Salesforce using API version 61.0. For the most up-to-date information on Salesforce's API capabilities, please consult their documentation.Learn more about Wix Studio for enterprise or contact our sales team.Step 1 | Add and connect SalesforceContact your enterprise success manager to connect Salesforce to your Wix Studio for enterprise account. When connecting your Salesforce account, you are providing permissions for Wix to access your spreadsheet data. You can remove permissions at any time from your Salesforce account.Already connected to Salesforce? Skip ahead to Step 2 | Create an automation.To connect your Wix Studio enterprise solution site to Salesforce:
Go to Manage Apps in the relevant site's dashboard. Click Salesforce.  Click Connect. 
Log in to your Salesforce account. Step 2 | Create an automationOnce you have connected your Salesforce account, you can now create an automation with Salesforce as the action. To create an automation:
Go to Automations in your site's dashboard. Click + New Automation.  Click + Start from Scratch. Give your automation a title and choose the relevant app under Trigger:
    
Wix Forms Wix Stores Wix Bookings Wix Events   Set up the trigger based on the app you selected.Step 3 | Map data from the trigger to Salesforce Next, you need to match the data from your chosen trigger to the relevant Salesforce entity and fields. This ensures the data from Wix gets to the right place on Salesforce.For example, if your trigger is a new store order, you will need to match the customer's data to the relevant entity fields in Salesforce.To map data from the trigger to Salesforce: 
Scroll down to Action and select Update Salesforce. Select the relevant entity from the Select which entity to update in Salesforce drop-down.  Click Map Fields.  Choose the relevant pieces of Wix data under Data from trigger, so the right Salesforce fields get updated. Click Save.Step 4 | Activate automation Click Activate to make your automation live. Now, every time the automation is triggered (e.g. whenever a new store order is placed), the data you mapped from Wix will be updated in the relevant Salesforce fields. For example, if you created an automation with a form submission trigger, every time a site visitor fills in that form, their submission details are sent to the relevant Salesforce entity and fields. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about the Wix Studio for enterprise Salesforce integration. I can't connect to Salesforce with Single Sign-On (SSO), how do I resolve this issue?If you are having issues with SSO, there may be an issue with Wix servers being blocked from Salesforce servers. You can resolve this by whitelisting the relevant Wix server IP addresses. To whitelist the relevant Wix server IP addresses:
Go to your enterprise dashboard. Hover over Settings in the left sidebar. Select IP Allowlisting. Click Create Rule. Enter a name for the rule. Click the Add URLs drop-down. Choose the relevant URLs from your connected sites. Enter each of the following IP addresses in the IP address field under Allowed IP addresses, and click Add each time:
    
64.7.220.0/24 64.95.157.0/24 70.42.116.0/24 70.42.119.0/24 185.230.60.0/22 199.15.160.0/22 91.199.119.0/24 65.38.108.0/24 3.219.52.190/32 3.234.195.187/32 23.23.59.232/32 44.199.164.16/32 3.90.122.42/32 54.147.198.201/32 34.235.216.255/32 52.203.188.4/32 35.167.2.215/32 54.212.48.139/32 35.84.122.228/32 100.20.131.234/32 34.252.5.25/32 54.170.22.1/32 34.248.203.220/32 46.137.24.202/32   Click Create once you have entered all the IP addresses above. Do Salesforce automations count towards my automations quota?Yes, this automation counts towards your automations quota. What is a Salesforce entity? A Salesforce entity is a contact, lead, account or order, whose data fields you can update (e.g. first name, last name, email address). What is a Salesforce required field? These are the fields you must map when updating your records. The required fields are based on each of your Salesforce entities. Why can't I see some of my Salesforce fields while mapping them?There are a number of reasons why your Salesforce fields might not be showing in Wix:
Read-only fields: If you set a Salesforce field to read-only, it cannot be updated through the automation. Wix will only show the Salesforce fields that can be updated.  New fields: It may take some time for your newly created Salesforce fields to appear. Please allow up to 24 hours these fields to appear in Wix. What happens if I delete a field in my Wix Form being mapped to Salesforce? The automation stays active and data will continue to be transferred to Salesforce – just without the field you deleted. Having said that, any previous data from the deleted field will still appear on Salesforce.   What happens if I rename a field in the Wix form mapped to Salesforce?Renaming a field does not impact the automation, as the mapping is based on the ID of the field, not its name. How do I disconnect the Salesforce integration?You can disconnect the Salesforce integration at any time, which also disables any automations that send data to Salesforce.
To disconnect the Salesforce integration:
Go to Manage Apps in the relevant site's dashboard. Click Salesforce.  Click Disconnect at the top.  Click Disconnect to confirm.

source_documents.title: Wix Inbox: Working with Site Collaborators
source_documents.content:
Wix Inbox: Working with Site Collaborators
As site owner, you can invite collaborators to work on different aspects of your site. Share the responsibility of managing your inbox by assigning inbox permissions to your collaborators, allowing them to view and answer messages.Collaborators with inbox permissions can enable notifications so they're alerted to all incoming messages. They can also set up personal profiles so that outgoing messages include their individual signatures.In this article, learn more about:
Inviting collaborators to work in your inbox Enabling email notifications for collaborators Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Note:Anyone you've assigned the Admin or Back Office Manager role has access to your inbox, as well as some roles for integrated Wix apps (e.g. Customer Relations Manager, Front Desk Staff), and custom roles with added Wix Inbox permissions. Learn more about roles and permissions.Inviting collaborators to work in your inboxInvite collaborators to view and respond to messages in your inbox. Each collaborator will be able to create a personal profile, giving communications a personal touch. Customers will receive messages with a name and personalized signature attached.To invite collaborators:
Go to Inbox in your site's dashboard. Click the Settings drop-down at the top right. Click Profile & collaborators. Click + Invite People next to Inbox collaborators. Enter the email address of a person you'd like to add.
Note: This will assign them the role of Back Office Manager by default. You can edit their role after you add them. Click Send Invite. Click Done. (Optional) Repeat these steps for any other team members you'd like to add. What's next?Each team member you've added will be able to edit their profile in the Profile & collaborators tab when they log in.Enabling email notifications for collaboratorsIf you'd like collaborators to be automatically notified of all incoming messages, enable email notifications. You can enable or disable email notifications separately for each individual.If notifications are enabled for a collaborator, this collaborator will have the ability to manage their own notification settings (including disabling notifications).To enable email notifications:
Go to Inbox in your site's dashboard. Click the Settings drop-down at the top right. Click Profile & collaborators. Under Inbox collaborators, click the Email notifications toggle next to a collaborator to enable email notifications.
Note: If you don't see the relevant collaborator on this list, it means they don't have Wix Inbox permissions. Go to Roles & Permissions to manage your roles. (Optional) Click Set Permissions to edit the team member's role.
Click Save Changes at the top right.Note:The Inbox collaborators section is only visible to site owners.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about working with site collaborators:What can my site collaborators do?Your collaborators can access and work in different parts of your site depending on the roles and permissions you've granted them.For example, you could have a collaborator working on your site design who has no need to access your inbox, and a collaborator working in your inbox who has no need to access your site pages.Learn more about roles and permissions.What if I want a collaborator to work in my inbox but I don't want to assign the Back Office Manager role?The Back Office Manager role is assigned by default if you add a collaborator to your inbox. You can remove this role and create a custom role if you'd like a collaborator to be able to carry out specific activities in specific parts of your site.Follow these steps to create a custom role. Make sure you select Message via Inbox & Chat (under Customer Management) if you'd like to include these permissions.How do I ensure my collaborators have set up their inbox profiles?Each collaborator has access to their own inbox profile. As site owner, you do not have access to these individual profiles.Share any email signature guidance necessary and advise each team member that they will be able to edit their profile when they log in.Access more information for site collaborators that you can share with your team.

source_documents.title: Wix Logo: Using the Wix Business Card Maker
source_documents.content:
Wix Logo: Using the Wix Business Card Maker
Elevate your brand with the Wix Business Card Maker, which allows you to create professional business cards that match your brand. This tool helps you maintain a consistent and polished look for your business, making it easier to leave a lasting impression on clients and partners.For example, if you run a freelance graphic design business, you can use the Business Card Maker to design cards that reflect your style and creativity, ensuring potential clients remember you.Step 1 | Select a business card templateChoose a template from our range of professional business card designs. You can also preview the template in a larger popup window for a more detailed view of the card's design.Before you begin:
This is not your business card's final design. You can further customize it later. You can change your order's shipping destination by clicking the flag icon at the top right.
To select a business card template:
Go to the Business Card Maker. Choose what to do next:
    
Hover over a template and click Preview to view the template. Click View All Templates to view all the templates we offer.   Hover over a template and click Customize to select it. Add your business details.
Note: You can add more details later when customizing your card. Click Save & Continue. Click Customize below your chosen business card design.Step 2 | Design your business cardAfter choosing your card's template, you can start designing it from the business card editor. From this editor you can customize the card's text, image, color and more.You may also want to change an element's location. You can reposition elements by dragging and dropping, or arrange any overlapping elements using the toolbar above your card design which will appear when clicking on the element. Edit the other side of the card by clicking Switch to Front / Switch to Back.
Click an option below to learn how to customize it:Text
Select the relevant text on your card or click Add Text Box on the left. Customize the text using the following options:
    
Edit Text: Type to replace the existing text. Font: Select a font from the dropdown menu. Opacity & Color: Click the color box to change the text's color and drag the slider to adjust its transparency. Font Size: Drag the slider to increase or decrease the size of the text. Letter Spacing: Drag the slider to adjust the space between letters.   Shape
Click Add Shape on the left or click the existing shape on your template. Choose from a square or circle shape. Customize your shape using the following options:
    
Shape Opacity & Color: Click the color box to change the shape's color and drag the slider to adjust its transparency. Border Width: Drag the slider to adjust the shape's border width. Border Opacity & Color: Click the color box to change the shape's border color and drag the slider to adjust its transparency.

  Vector Art
Click Add Vector Art on the left or click the existing vector art on your template. Search for and select the vector art you like. Click Add to Template. Drag and drop the vector art to its position and resize using the grip handles. Customize your vector art using the options on the left:
    
Image Opacity: Drag the slider to adjust the vector art's transparency. Image Colors: Click Change Colors. Then click the relevant color box to change the vector art's color(s).   (Optional) Edit the other side of the card by clicking Switch to Back / Switch to Front and repeating steps 1 to 5.
Image
Click Add Image on the left or click the existing image on your template. (If uploading an image) Click the relevant image in the Media Manager and click Add to Template. Customize your image using the options on the left:
    
Image Opacity: Drag the slider on the left to adjust the transparency of the image.   (Optional) Edit the other side of the card by clicking Switch to Back / Switch to Front and repeating steps 1 to 3.
Background
Click Change Background on the left. Click the color box to change the card's background color. Drag the slider to adjust the color's opacity. (Optional) Edit the other side of the card by clicking Switch to Back / Switch to Front and repeating steps 1 and 2.
Once you finish customizing your design click Done on the top right to choose your paper type and card quantity.Step 3 | Choose your paper type and quantityAfter customizing your business card it's time to choose your card's paper type. From here you can also choose the quantity of cards you want to order.To choose your paper type and quantity:
Click the Paper Type drop-down menu and select the paper thickness and finish you want. Click the Quantity drop-down menu and select how many cards you want to order (100, 250, or 500 cards). Click Add to Cart.Step 4 | Complete Your OrderAfter choosing your paper type and card quantity you can finalize your order and submit your purchase.To complete your order:
Click the Cart  icon in the top right corner. Click Continue to Checkout. Add your shipping details. Click Save & Continue. Add your payment details. Click Submit Purchase.Step 5 | Check your order statusOnce you have completed your order you can check your order's status and track your business cards directly from the Business Cards Maker.To check your order status:
Go to the Business Cards Maker. Click Order History at the top. Click View items next to the relevant order. Click Track Order under Tracking Number.FAQsClick a question below to learn more. Can I preview the business card template before customizing it?Yes, you can preview the template in a larger popup window by hovering over the template and clicking Preview. This allows you to see the card's design in more detail before making your selection.How many business cards can I order at once?You can choose to order 100, 250, or 500 cards. Select the quantity from the drop-down menu after choosing your paper type.Can I cancel my business card order or report damages?Orders are fulfilled by Order a Print. You can cancel an order within the first 24 hours by contacting them. Damaged or defective orders need to be reported within seven days of the delivery date to Order a Print via email: support@orderaprint.com, and not Wix. Order a Print will investigate and send a replacement at their discretion. Can I edit my business card after placing the order?Once an order is placed, you can't edit it. If you need changes, cancel the order within the first 24 hours and create a new card with the required adjustments.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Using the Members Area in Wix Blog
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Using the Members Area in Wix Blog
Build a thriving community with the Wix Blog Members Area, where your members can follow posts, subscribe for updates, and manage their notifications. Plus, they can create and customize their own profile pages, giving your blog a more interactive and social feel. Whether you're aiming to build a dedicated readership or spark meaningful conversations, the Members Area is an ideal tool for encouraging community engagement on your blog.About the member pages in the blogThe Members Area in Wix Blog is a dedicated space where site members can personalize their experience and engage with the community. It offers features like customizable profile pages, where members can edit their personal information and manage their activity, including posts and comments. Member profile pageEvery person that signs up to your site as a member, gets their own Profile page. With the Members Area installed on your site, your site members can view other members' profiles. Once they are on their Profile page, they can see the member's public blog activities (posts they've written, comments they've made, etc.).Public member pagesAs the Members Area is considered to be a community, some parts of a members profile are public, which means they can be viewed by any site visitor. These include:
Profile Blog Posts Blog Comments Blog LikesPrivate member pagesCertain pages in the Members Area are private, meaning only the member who owns the page can view them. These private pages are not accessible to other members, even when they visit someone else's profile. Unlike public pages, which can be seen by the entire community, private pages are designed to protect individual members' privacy and keep their personal content hidden from others. Private member pages include:My DraftsMy AccountNotificationsSettingsAdding the Members AreaYou can add the Members Area from the Wix App Market. Some site templates already come with the Members Area pre-installed, which means it is already available to use in your site. If you do not have a Members Area installed in your site, you can follow the steps below to add it.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Add Apps  on the left side of the editor. Enter "Members Area" in the search bar. Select the Wix Members Area app. Click Add to Site.
Click App Market  on the left side of the Studio Editor. Click App Market. Enter "Members Area" or "Wix Members Area" in the search bar.  Select the Wix Members Area app. Click Add to Site.TroubleshootingYou might experience an issue where you cannot see particular members on the Members page. This could be for the following reasons:The member was approved, but hasn't logged inOnce you approve a site visitor as a member, they are invited to log in to your site. Their member profile is only visible after they log in for the first time. The member accepted invite, but hasn't logged inYou sent an invitation, but the person hasn't logged in since they received it. This member will appear on the member's page only after they sign in for the first time. The member hasn't joined the communityBesides logging in, members need to join your community with a public profile to appear on the Members page. The community is an opt-in feature that allows your members to decide whether other members can view their information.

Wix Studio: Accessing Product Betas
Enroll in Product Betas to experience new Wix features before they're released. When joining a product beta, you should identify and report bugs, provide feedback and help determine improvements needed before the product is released. We may ask you to join a performance review to share your experience with our developers and product managers.Note:Currently, product betas are available in English only and for Wix sites that you are an owner of. Keep in mind that the betas are still in development and you may not have the same seamless experience that you have with other Wix products.In this article, learn how to:
Join the Beta Program Use product betas in your current projects Share your feedback on product betasJoin the Beta ProgramJoin the Beta Program and gain access to try out new Wix features before they're released.To join the Beta Program:
Go to your Wix Studio workspace. Click the News Center icon  at the top right and select Betas.  Click Join Beta Program on the top right. Click Join.Using product betas in projectsOnce you've joined, you can access the available product betas and try them out in Wix sites that you're an owner of. Product betas are a way for you to experience Wix features before they're released. Some of these features may end up being rolled back or available to Wix users at a later time.To use a product beta:
Go to your Wix Studio workspace. Click the News Center icon  at the top right and select Betas. Browse the list and click on the product beta you'd like to try out. Follow the steps on the left under Steps.Sharing feedback on product betasMake a difference and share your feedback in the Wix Studio Community Forum on any betas you've used in your Wix sites. This is important as it helps us improve our products for you and all our users before they're released.To share your feedback:
Go to your Wix Studio workspace. Click the News Center icon  at the top right and select Betas. Click on the product beta you'd like to leave feedback for. Click Leave Feedback. Enter your feedback about the beta in the Wix Studio Community Forum.

source_documents.title: Wix Studio: Receiving Revenue Share
source_documents.content:
Wix Studio: Receiving Revenue Share
Important:Currently, revenue share payments are not issued to banks located in Russia and Pakistan.As a Wix Partner, you can earn revenue share through the sale of various Wix plans and from transactions processed through Wix Payments on your clients' eligible sites. Once you start earning revenue share, you can track your payouts and invoices in the Payouts tab of your Wix Studio workspace.In this article, learn more about:
Qualifying for revenue share Connecting a payout method Receiving payouts for revenue share Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Qualifying for revenue shareIn 2024, all Wix Partners can earn revenue share through the sale of eligible Wix plans and from transactions processed through Wix Payments on their clients' eligible sites.Earning revenue share on Wix plansEarn revenue share for the sale of specific Wix plans to clients in 2024. Check out the table to see how revenue share is calculated for Wix plans.PlansWix Partners (all levels)Wix LegendWix Premium yearly, 2 year, or 3 year plans0%20%Wix Studio yearly, 2 year, or 3 year plans20%30%Branded App by Wix50%50%Email Marketing50%50%Enterprise solution50%50%Logo50%50%Retail POS plan50%50%Hopp - Link in Bio20%20%Business Email5%5%Facebook or Google Ads5%5%To qualify for revenue share on Wix plans:
You must comply with the Wix Partner Program Terms of Use. You must be the first owner of the site, even if you no longer have access to it. The site must have an active Premium or Studio plan, either yearly or longer. Revenue share is not applicable on monthly plans, except for Google Ads and Facebook Ads. The site has completed the 14-day trial period. Plans bought on sale (non-seasonal/personal) are not eligible for revenue share. Official Wix.com sales are eligible for revenue share, but coupon codes like TAKE10 from public resources are not. For the enterprise solution, you must refer the client to Wix to be eligible for revenue share. Learn more about selling Wix Studio enterprise solution for revenue share.Earning revenue share on client salesAs a Wix Partner, you can earn revenue share from transactions processed through Wix Payments on your clients' eligible sites between January 10, 2024 and January 31, 2025. Revenue share on client sales is calculated daily, based on the total daily sales generated by your clients' sites, including both online sales and sales made through Wix Retail POS. Once your clients' sales qualify for revenue share, you can track your earnings in the Client sales tab. Check out the table and example below to see how revenue share from client sales is calculated.Total Daily SalesRevenue Share %Potential Yearly EarningsLess than or equal to $20000.05%Up to $365 a yearMore than $20000.10%UnlimitedExample earnings from client sales:
On February 1st, a partner had 2 client sites that collectively generated a total of $1,500 in sales through Wix Payments. The partner's revenue share for this day would be: $0.75, calculated as 0.05% of $1,500. On February 2nd, the partner added 2 more sites, and all 4 sites generated a total of $20,000 in sales through Wix Payments. The partner's revenue share for this day would be: $20, calculated as 0.10% of $20,000.To qualify for revenue share on client sales:
You must comply with the Wix Partner Program Terms of Use. You must be the first owner of the site, even if you no longer have access to it. The site must have an active Premium plan or Studio plan, either yearly or longer (unless defined otherwise by Wix). The site has completed the 14-day trial period. The site must process payments through Wix Payments in the available countries and currencies. Earnings are displayed and paid out in US dollars only. The site must generate a minimum of $1 in sales per day to be eligible. If sales fall below $1 on a specific day, revenue share will not be applicable for that day.Connecting a payout methodTo start earning revenue share, you need to connect a payout method in the Revenue Share tab of your Wix Studio workspace.Note:Only workspace owners and co-owners can view and manage the Revenue Share tab. Learn more about managing the roles and permissions of your teammates.To connect a payment method:
Go to Revenue Share in your Wix Studio workspace. Click Connect Payout Method at the top right. Click Continue. Add your contact info and click Next. Add your payout method details and click Next. Tip:Click Back if you need to edit your payment details. You can always edit your details by clicking Payout Settings in the Revenue Share tab.Receiving payouts for revenue shareYour revenue share earnings from plans, client sales, and Marketplace template sales are combined. Once your total earnings reach $200, a payout is scheduled 30 days after the end of that month.For example, if you meet the $200 threshold in January, your payout will be scheduled for the end of February. If you don’t meet the threshold, your earnings will roll over to the next month. Learn more about tracking your payouts.Notes:
Revenue share payouts are calculated based on the price of the plan, excluding the VAT. For Wix Studio enterprise plans, revenue share payouts are issued once Wix receives full payment from the client, with a net 90-day cycle.FAQsClick on a question below to learn more about revenue share.What qualifies as the first owner of a site? The first owner of the site is the one that initiated its creation from their Wix Studio workspace. When you click Create New Site in your Wix Studio workspace, you become the first owner of the site, regardless of whether you later transfer ownership to a client.What is the difference between Legend level and non-Legend level Partners in revenue share eligibility?Partners at Legend level enjoy access to revenue share on all participating plans and higher revenue share percentages on specific plans:
Wix Premium yearly, 2 year, or 3 year plans: Legend level partners earn 20% revenue share, while non-Legend level partners do not. Wix Studio yearly, 2 year, or 3 year plans: Legend level partners earn 30% revenue share, whereas non-Legend level partners earn 20% in 2024.Do all plans qualify for revenue share?To qualify for revenue share, a site must have an active Premium or studio plan, either yearly or longer (unless defined otherwise by Wix). For Partners who aren't legends, the plan must be purchased in 2024.How is revenue share calculated for client sales?Revenue share on client sales is calculated daily across all of the Partner's sites based on the net amount generated and processed through Wix Payments. This includes online sales and sales made with Wix Retail POS.The net amount refers to the total sales generated by your clients' sites, factoring in deductions such as applicable fees, charges, chargebacks, refunds, etc. If refunds or chargebacks occur after payout, this will be corrected in the next payout.There are two tiers for revenue share:
Clients' daily sales generated less than or equal to $2000: You qualify for a revenue share of 0.05% on the net total from client sales for the day. If the total sales for a given day are equal to or less than $2000, your revenue share for that day would be calculated at 0.05%. Clients' daily sales generated more than $2000: You can earn a higher revenue share of 0.10% on the net total from client sales for the day. No annual earning cap; earnings are unlimited if the total daily sales exceed $2000.How often are revenue share earnings updated?Revenue share earnings from client sales are updated once every 24 hours. On Wix plans, earnings are posted up to 30 days after the purchase date.How often are revenue share earnings paid out?Your revenue share earnings from client sales and plans are invoiced together. To qualify for a payout, your total earnings from both plans and client sales must reach a minimum of $200. Once you meet this threshold, the payout cycle is net 30 days for revenue share earnings.Note: The payout cycle on revenue share for enterprise is net 90 days.Can I earn revenue share from my client's existing Wix plans?No. You have to be the first owner to be eligible to earn.Is there a limit to the number of sites I can onboard to earn from?No. There's no limit.

source_documents.title: Site Members: Adding and Customizing the Members List Element
source_documents.content:
Site Members: Adding and Customizing the Members List Element
Add the Members List element to showcase your site members. You can add this element to any site page, making it your own by adjusting the layout, refining the design, and personalizing member badges.You decide if this list is visible to all site visitors or just your logged-in members. In this article, learn how to:
Add the Members List element Adjust the layout Design the Members List Making the Members List public Personalizing how badges look on the listCan't click on members in your live site?Clicking a member on the Members List leads to their profile – unless that page / tab doesn't exist on your site. You can quickly add it from the Pages panel. Adding the Members List elementHead over to the Add Elements panel to add the Members List element. You can show the element anywhere on your site, whether it's a page in your Members Area or a site page that is visible to all visitors. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Community. Drag the Members List element onto your page. 
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Members. Drag the Members List element onto the page.Adjusting the layout of the Members List elementChoose from a Cards or List layout for the Members List. Then, customize the chosen layout to your needs, deciding how member profile pictures should look.   Wix EditorStudio Editor
Select the Members List element. Click Settings. Click Layout. Select the layout you like best; Cards or List. Choose a shape for your members' profile pictures; Circle or Square.
Select the Members List element. Click Settings. Click Layout. Select the layout you like best; Cards or List. Choose a shape for your members' profile pictures; Circle or Square.Designing the Members List elementMake your Members List complement your site's design by customizing the fonts, buttons, colors, background, borders, and more.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Select the Members List element. Click Settings. Click Design. Customize the design of this element to make it your own. Click below to learn more about the areas you can design:Text
Member name: Choose a font, font size, and color for your members' names. Following / Followers counters: Choose a font, font size, and color for the counters. Button
Text: Choose a font and font size for your buttons. Opacity and color: Click the color box to select a new color for your buttons. Drag the slider to adjust the color's transparency. Corner radius: Drag the slider to make the buttons more round.  Border color and opacity: Choose a new color for the button borders and drag the slider to adjust the opacity.  Border width: Drag the slider to make the border thinner or thicker. Background & Borders
Show cover photo: Enable the toggle to show each member's cover photo on their card. 
    
Choose default color: Choose a color to appear when a member does not have a cover photo on their profile.  Default cover photo opacity: Drag the slider to change the transparency of the cover photo / default color. Set default cover photo: Choose a cover photo to appear for all members unless they customize it from their own account.    Page background opacity & color: Click the color box to select a new background color for the list. Drag the slider to adjust the color's transparency. Profile background opacity & color: Click the color box to select a new background color for the member cards on the list.
