source_documents.title: Wix Analytics: Managing Alerts and Emails
source_documents.content:
Wix Analytics: Managing Alerts and Emails
Wix Analytics allows you to receive alerts and emails so that you can stay on top of important site data and activity. Using these tools, you can monitor trends and shifts so you can respond quickly to changes, and plan your next steps effectively.In this article, learn more about:
Managing your Analytics alerts Managing your Analytics emails Frequently asked questions (FAQs)How do I access the Alerts and Email Settings page?Go to Analytics Highlights and click the Alerts and email settings icon  at the top right.Managing your Analytics alertsWix Analytics alerts help you to track your site data and business activity. There are two types of alerts:
Alerts by Wix: Default alerts that we send you automatically if there are significant increases or decreases in your daily or weekly site sessions and total sales.  Custom alerts: You can create your own alerts that focus on the data you want to monitor.Note:Analytics notifications will only be triggered after your site has generated enough data to run the algorithm.To manage your alerts:
Go to Alerts and Emails Settings in your site's dashboard. Under Alerts, choose what to do:Create a custom alertYou have the option to set up new alerts to stay informed about shifts in your data. For example, you could create an alert to be notified when your total daily sales exceed $1000, or if your daily visitor count falls below 100.
Click + Create New Alert. Set up your alert:
    
Click the Select a stat drop-down and choose from a list of measures grouped by Traffic, Sales, Blog, and People data. In Check every, set the frequency of the alert (daily, weekly or monthly). Choose the relevant option from the If there is drop-down (e.g. More than, Less than).  Enter a threshold in the Number field. For example, set the alert to notify you if your total orders increase by 100 or more.   Click Save.Edit custom alertsEdit your custom alerts to match the ever-changing needs of your business. Whether you want to be notified about a decrease in the number of page views, or an increase in the number of items sold, alerts can be updated as you need.
Click the Edit icon  next to the custom alert you want to edit. Update the conditions that trigger the alert. Click Save. Deactivate alertsYou have the option to disable both the default alerts provided by Wix and any custom alerts you've created. This is a great option if you may want to use the alert again in the future. To deactivate an alert, disable the toggle next to the alert you want to deactivate.
Tip: You can enable the toggle and reactivate the alert at any time.Delete a custom alertDelete custom alerts you no longer need to stay organized and only get notified for what matters most.
Click the Delete icon  next to the custom alert you want to delete. Click Delete.Managing your Analytics emailsWix Analytics emails directly sends you reports you're subscribed to and helps you keep track of your key stats with a monthly highlights email.The Monthly Highlights email includes key stats on your site's performance. The stats you see are based on the type of site you have. For example, if you have a blog you'll see stats based on post views, and if you have a store you'll see sales stats.Note:
You can only get Monthly Highlights if your site is upgraded and received 30+ site visits during the previous month. The Monthly Highlights email is only available for English language sites.To manage your emails:
Go to Alerts and Emails Settings in your site's dashboard. Under Emails, choose what to do:Edit a report subscriptionEdit the subscription settings for a report you're subscribed to. You have the flexibility to adjust how often you receive it and when, and to change the attachment type.
Click the Edit icon  next to the report you want to edit. Update your subscription settings, including the report time period, attachment type, frequency, and delivery time. Click Save.Unsubscribe from a reportUnsubscribe from any report you no longer want to receive by email. You can always go back and re-subscribe to it from the report's page.
Click Unsubscribe next to the report name. Click Unsubscribe again in the window.Deactivate the Monthly Highlights emailYou can choose to stop receiving the Monthly Highlights email if you prefer. Disable the toggle next to Monthly Highlights to stop receiving the email.Tip: You can enable the toggle and start receiving it again at any time.Subscribing to Wix Analytics reports:You can subscribe to any report and customize the report format, time period, frequency, delivery time, and more.FAQsClick a question to learn more about Wix Analytics alerts and emails.Where can I manage all my Wix notifications?You can manage the notifications you receive on your desktop (web browser), dashboard, and email under Notification Preferences in your site's dashboard.You can do the same for notifications on your mobile device through the Wix app or the Wix Studio app. Learn more about managing your site's notification preferences.How does Wix Analytics determine when to send out alert notifications for default alerts?Wix Analytics collects your statistical data over initial periods of 3 months for daily alerts, and 1 year for weekly alerts. This helps to build an algorithm which distinguishes between real statistical fluctuations, random fluctuations, and seasonal behavior.After the initial periods, your statistical data continues to be collected and is compared to previous data to detect significant changes. For example, an unexpected surge in Total Sales on a particular day (unrelated to seasonal events), would be considered a significant change and would result in an alert notification being sent.When do I receive my Monthly Highlights email?You receive the Monthly Highlights email at the beginning of the month. For example, if you had 30+ site visits in March, you will receive the email in the beginning of April.If you recently published a new Wix site, you'll receive the email at the beginning of the following month.Who does the Monthly Highlights email get sent to?With Wix Editor, the email only gets sent to the email address of the site owner. If you're a partner using Wix Studio, you can define who the email gets sent to.Note: In Wix Editor, the email address for the delivery of the Monthly Highlights email cannot be changed.I can't find my Monthly Highlights email. What should I do?If you can't locate your Monthly Highlights email:
Check your email's spam or junk folder. Make sure that your Wix account is set up with the correct email address. You can change your email address here.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Customizing the Design of Your Transparent Videos
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Customizing the Design of Your Transparent Videos
After you've added a transparent video to your site, customize its design to rhyme it in with your site's color palette and visual story. Change the video's colors, enlarge or shrink the video, decide how and when the video plays and stops, and even customize the play button if you choose to display one.In this article, learn more about:
Customizing your video's design Customizing your video's colors Customizing the play buttonCustomizing your video's designPick a cover image for your video which visitors see before the video starts to play. You can choose to add a fade-out effect that applies when the video finishes playing. Flip and rotate videos and place them anywhere you want to fit the design of your site.Click an option below to learn more:Change my video's cover imageViewers see your cover image before the video starts playing. Choose from a preset cover image or add your own.To change your video's cover image:
Click the transparent video in your editor. Click the Design icon . Click the Cover Image icon . Select one of the preset cover images or add your own by clicking the Add icon . Click the Fade out toggle to enable the fade-out effect.
Flip, duplicate and rotate videosTo rotate a video click and drag the Rotate icon  at the top-left of the video. To flip the video, right-click the video and click Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical.

Tip: You can also flip your VideoBox both horizontally and vertically using right-click.Customizing your video's colorsPersonalize your transparent videos with unlimited custom coloring options. Choose from preset color templates or create a custom template specific to your needs.To customize your video's colors:
Click the transparent video in your editor. Click the Design icon . Click the Color icon . Click to enable the Recolor video toggle. Select a color preset, or click the Customize icon on the custom preset and change the colors.Customizing the play buttonIf you set your video to play on click, then a play button is displayed on the video. You can choose the play button you like best from the preset designs, and change the color to suit your transparent video's theme.To customize the play button:
Click the Big Play Button on your video. Click Change Big Play Button. Select a design. Click Customize Design to change the color and opacity:
    
Click the color box(es) to select the colors of your button. Drag the slider to increase or decrease the play button opacity.  Tip:If you don't want to display a play button on your video, set the opacity to 0.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Customizing Your Breadcrumbs Trail
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Customizing Your Breadcrumbs Trail
After adding and setting up your breadcrumbs trail, you can make it your own by customizing it to suit your site's look and theme. Select presets, adjust the layout, and personalize the design to encourage visitors to keep clicking and exploring your site.In this article, learn more about:
Adjusting the layout of the trail Customizing the designImportant:You need to enable Velo Dev Mode on your site in order to add and customize breadcrumbs. Velo allows you to use coding on your site to create custom functionalities and interactions. Learn more about VeloChanging the layout of your breadcrumbs trailAdjust the layout of your breadcrumbs trail to fit your site's alignment. You can change settings such as the separators, spacing, and direction of items. To adjust the trail's layout:
Click the breadcrumbs element in your editor. Click the Layout icon . Adjust the layout using the available options:
    
How are overflow items displayed?: Select how to display items that don't fit on the trail:
        
Show all items: If items don't fit, another line is created on the trail. Collapse items: Items are displayed on one line only. If they don't fit, an ellipsis displays.   Separators: Enable the toggle to show separators between trail items, then choose the icon you want to use: V-shape or Backslash.  Vertical spacing: Drag the slider to change the spacing above and below the items. Horizontal spacing: Drag the slider to change the spacing between the items.  Align items: Choose how items are aligned: Left, Center, or Right.  Display breadcrumbs from: Choose the direction in which the items appear: Left to Right or Right to Left.   Designing your breadcrumbsSelect another trail preset from the available options, or customize it further to create a clean, sophisticated way to display the hierarchy of your pages to visitors. Adjust the look of the whole trail with settings such as spacing, color, and size.To customize the design:
Click the breadcrumbs element in your editor. Click the Design icon . Click Customize Design. Choose what you want to design from the dropdown menu:Background Click Background in the dropdown menu and choose how you want to customize it:
Background Fills: Choose a color for your trail background, and set its opacity. Borders: Add a border to your trail background, and change the color, width and spacing. Corners: Make the corners of the trail background square, or more circular. Shadow: Add and adjust a shadow on your trail to give it a cool 3D effect. Separators
Click Separators from the dropdown menu. Click the Show text toggle to enable separators between trail items. Choose how you want to customize the separator:
    
Themes: Apply one of your saved text themes to the separator. Fonts: Choose a font from the dropdown menu for the separator. Font size: Set how big or small you want the item separator to be. Formatting: Add different formatting options to your separator, such as bold, underline, and strikethrough. Color and Alignment: Choose the colors for your separator, and set the text direction and alignment. Spacing: Make the spacing between the characters and lines bigger or smaller. Shadows: Add a shadow to the separator to give it a cool 3D effect.  ItemsClick Items in the dropdown menu, and use the options to make them look the way you want:
Items state: Select which mode you would like to adjust the items for:
    
Regular: How the items look before a visitor interacts with them. Hover: How the items look when a visitor hovers their cursor over them. Current page: How the item is displayed when it is the page the visitor is currently on.   Background Fills: Choose a color for your items, and set their opacity. Text: Adjust the text for your trail items. You can choose and edit options such as the font, color, and alignment to suit your site's look and theme. Borders: Add and adjust a border on your items. You can change the color, width and spacing to make them stand out on your page. Corners: Make the corners of the trail items square, or more circular. Shadows: Add and adjust a shadow on your items to give them a cool 3D effect. Layout: Adjust the padding around your items to make the space around them smaller or bigger.

source_documents.title: Wix Events: Hiding a Ticket Type
source_documents.content:
Wix Events: Hiding a Ticket Type
You can hide any ticket types (e.g. VIP ticket, early bird ticket) from your site if the ticket is no longer or not yet available.To hide a ticket type:
Go to the Events tab in your site's dashboard. Click Edit on the relevant event. Click the Tickets tab. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant ticket. Select Hide.Tips:
To display a hidden ticket, click the More Actions icon  and select Show. You can also preselect dates when ticket purchases for an event opens and closes (e.g. registration opens a month before the event and closes a day before the event).

source_documents.title: Wix Events: Using Wix Groups to Promote Your Events
source_documents.content:
Wix Events: Using Wix Groups to Promote Your Events
Wix Groups is an app that allows you to create a place for members to post updates, share images and videos, have discussions, and more. It's like having your own social media platform. In this article, learn how to:
Create a group for your event Post your event in your group feedCreating a group for an eventCreate a group from inside the Wix Events dashboard. All the guests who register for your event are automatically invited to join the group.Note:When you use Wix Groups for the first time, 2 pages are added to your site: 
Groups List page: This page is automatically added to your site's menu. It lists all your groups.  Group Page: This is the actual group where you and your guests can post.To create a group for an event:
Go to Events in your site's dashboard. Select the relevant published event or event draft. Click the Features tab. Click Groups. Click Create Group or select an existing group. Set a privacy level:
    
Public: Anyone site visitor can view discussions and images. Event guests are automatically asked to join the group. Private: Only members can join and view this group. Event guests are automatically invited to join the group. If selected, choose who can join:
        
Select Visible or Hidden from the Visibility drop-down.  Choose who has access:
            
Only members approved by admin: You must approve each request Only event participants: Any event participant can join the group       Click Create. Click Done.Next steps:
Customize the design of the group page Go to the Wix Groups dashboard to customize and manage your group. Learn more about Wix Groups.Posting your event in a groupIf you already use Wix Groups, you can post an event in your feed. Guests can click Register Now to sign up for your event.To post an event in your group feed:
Go to your group on your live site. Click to start a new post. (Optional) Write a message. Click +More. Scroll down and select Events. Select the relevant event. Tip: You can search for the event name. Click Embed Now. Click Publish.

source_documents.title: Wix Invoices & Price Quotes: Adding Default Notes
source_documents.content:
Wix Invoices & Price Quotes: Adding Default Notes
Add notes that appear at the bottom of all of your invoices or price quotes. Updates will not be applied to past invoices or price quotes retroactively.To add default notes:
Go to Settings in your site's dashboard. Click Getting paid.  Click Invoices & quotes. Go to the relevant tab: 
    
Invoices

Click the Footer notes drop-down. Enter Notes or Terms.   Price Quotes:

Scroll down to Default note sections. Enter Notes or Terms.    Tip:You can also edit default notes when creating a new invoice or price quote.

source_documents.content:

Publishing your photo album Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Publishing your photo albumReady to go live with your latest photo album? You can publish the album directly from your album editor. To publish your photo album:
Go to Photo Albums in your site's dashboard.  Click Edit next to the relevant album. Click Publish Now at the top right.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about publishing your photo album. What blockers might I face when trying to publish my album?You cannot publish your album if:

You are not the owner of the site (if you are a site collaborator).Can I unpublish an album I no longer need?No, it is not possible to unpublish a photo album. source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Creating a Site Menu with Anchors and Sections for One-Page Sites
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Creating a Site Menu with Anchors and Sections for One-Page Sites
Even though one-page sites cannot have a regular site menu (with tabs that link to different pages), you can create a site menu with anchor and section links instead. You can place anchors and sections wherever you like on your one-page site, and when your visitors click the links on your menu, they are directed to the relevant part of the page.In this article, learn more about:
Adding an anchor to your site menu Adding a section to your site menu Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Adding an anchor to your site menuGuide visitors directly to the content they’re looking for with anchors in your site's menu. You can place multiple anchors within a section, so your visitors can easily access different points of interest. To add an anchor to your menu:
Add an anchor to your site. Drag the anchor to the top of a page section. Change the name of the anchor to something that describes the content (e.g. "About" or "Services"). Repeat steps 1-3 for each anchor on your site. Click Pages and Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click Add Menu Item.  Select Anchor, and on the pop-up, select the relevant anchor under Where on the page?. Click Done. Rename the menu link to something that describes that page content (e.g. "About" or "Services").
Tip: It can be the same anchor name as you previously entered. Repeat steps 5-9 for each anchor.Adding a section to your site menuImprove visitor navigation and content organization with clear sections in your site's menu. To add a section to your menu:
Add a section to your site. Rename the section to something that describes its content (e.g. "Contact Us", or "Our Story"). Repeat steps 1-2 for each section on your site. Click Pages and Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the Add Menu Item.  Select Section, and on the pop-up, select the relevant anchor under Where on the page?. Click Done. Rename the menu link to something that describes that page section (e.g. "Contact Us", or "Our Story"). 
Tip: It can be the same section name as you previously entered. Repeat steps 5-8 for each section.FAQsClick a question below to learn more. What will my anchor look like in the pages panel?You can easily spot it in the pages panel as the icon changes next to the name:

What will my anchor look like in my menu?Your anchor or section link looks like a regular tab on your site menu:

When your visitors click it, they are directed to the anchor / section.

source_documents.title: Enterprise Solution: About the Account Level Monitoring Dashboard
source_documents.content:
Enterprise Solution: About the Account Level Monitoring Dashboard
The account level monitoring dashboard is a powerful tool designed specifically for larger organizations with multiple sites. It offers a comprehensive overview of individual site performance, enabling your team to efficiently monitor and optimize your online presence. Learn more about Wix Studio for enterprise or contact our sales team.Centralized monitoringThe dashboard provides a centralized hub for monitoring the performance of all sites within a Wix Studio for enterprise account. This streamlines the monitoring process and allows your organization to easily track performance metrics across multiple sites, on both desktop and mobile, from a single interface.You can also grant viewing permissions to the relevant people in your organization for increased visibility and interdepartmental communication. Track Core Web Vitals across all of your sitesQuickly and easily track the Core Web Vitals scores for all your organization's sites. Core Web Vitals, include: 
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): An indication of a site's loading time - more specifically, how long it takes for the largest content element in the site's viewport to load. Interaction to Next Paint (INP): An assessment of your site's responsiveness to all click, tap, and keyboard interactions that occur throughout each visit on every page. The final INP value is the longest interaction observed.  Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): A measurement of unexpected movements of elements that change the layout of the page.By tracking these metrics, you can identify areas for improvement and optimize site performance to enhance site visitor satisfaction. Learn more about Core Web Vitals for improved site performance.Detailed reports and insightsThe dashboard also offers detailed reports and insights for each individual site. These reports provide in-depth analysis of performance metrics, highlight areas of concern, and offer actionable recommendations for optimization. Your organization can use these insights to make informed decisions and drive improvements across your entire portfolio of sites.Frequently asked questionsClick a question below to learn more. What are Core Web Vitals?Core Web Vitals are the industry standard for measuring site speed, ranked based on your actual visitors' experiences, and the color-coded system follows Google's benchmarks. The Core Web Vitals displayed in the account level monitoring dashboard include:
Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): An indication of a site's loading time - more specifically, how long it takes for the largest content element in the site's viewport to load. Interaction to Next Paint (INP): An assessment of your site's responsiveness to all click, tap, and keyboard interactions that occur throughout each visit on every page. The final INP value is the longest interaction observed.  Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): A measurement of unexpected movements of elements that change the layout of the page.Learn more about Core Web Vitals for improved site performance.
Sites appear in descending order according to session numbers. For more detailed, site-specific insights, you can click View Breakdown next to the relevant site to explore specific metrics and receive improvement tips. Learn more about optimizing your elements, text, and media for improved site performance.

Who has access to the account level monitoring dashboard?Account admins, co-admins and those with custom roles with the relevant permissions can view the monitoring dashboard.Does my PageSpeed score affect my SEO ranking?Not exactly. Even though site speed is one of the many factors affecting your SEO ranking, only data collected from real user sessions counts. The PageSpeed score you see here is based on a lab test and doesn’t affect your site’s SEO directly. Why are my scores different for desktop and mobile? PageSpeed scores for mobile are often lower than for desktop. That’s because mobile devices have slower processors and take more time to resize texts and images. Lab settings are another reason: Google’s mobile test is on a simulated 3G connection, which is different from the 4G and Wifi connections most visitors use to access your site.

source_documents.title: Enterprise Solution: Managing Access to Your Sites using IP Allowlisting
source_documents.content:
Enterprise Solution: Managing Access to Your Sites using IP Allowlisting
IP allowlisting is a method for restricting access to a URL. It works by checking the Internet Protocol (IP) addresses of visitors against a list of approved IP addresses. If a visitor tries to access a URL from an IP address that is not on the list, they are automatically blocked. This can help prevent unauthorized access to a site's resources.You can use the Wix enterprise solution's IP Allowlisting feature to create rules that limit access to your sites. For example, you can create a rule to allow access only to visitors from your organization's IP addresses. Select which URLs on your account that you want to include in your rule and enter the IP addresses that are allowed to access them. Learn more about Wix Studio for enterprise or contact our sales team.In this article, learn more about:
Creating a rule Editing a rule Deleting a rule Troubleshooting issuesCreating an IP Allowlisting ruleYou can create new IP Allowlisting rules in the Settings section of your enterprise dashboard. Use any of the following formats for your IP addresses:FormatExampleSingle IP address40.77.182.32IP address range40.77.182.32-40.77.182.200Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation40.77.183.32/27Important:A URL can only be used in one rule at a time. You can't create two rules that contain the same URL.To create a rule:
Go to your enterprise dashboard. Hover over Security in the left sidebar. Select IP Allowlisting. Click Create Rule. Enter a name for the rule. Click the Add URLs drop-down.
Select the URLs on your account that you want to include. Enter an IP address under Allowed IP addresses.  (Optional) Add a description to help you remember what the IP address is for. Click Add. Repeat steps 7-10 for all of the IP addresses that you want to add. Click Create.Editing an IP Allowlisting ruleYou can edit an IP Allowlisting rule in the Settings section of your enterprise dashboard. To edit a rule:
Go to your enterprise dashboard. Hover over Security in the left sidebar. Select IP Allowlisting. Hover over the rule that you want to update. Click Edit.
Make your changes to the rule. Click Save.Deleting an IP Allowlisting ruleYou can delete an IP Allowlisting rule in the Settings section of your enterprise dashboard. Important:It is not possible to recover a rule after you delete it. To delete a rule:
Go to your enterprise dashboard. Hover over Security in the left sidebar. Select IP Allowlisting. Click the More Actions icon  beside the rule that you want to delete.  Select Delete.
Click Delete. Troubleshooting IP Allowlisting issuesIf you're experiencing issues when you try to create a rule, try the steps below:Make sure that you haven't used the URL in another ruleA URL can only be used in one rule at a time. You can't create two rules that contain the same URL.If the URL that you want to include in your rule is not available in the list, check if you've already used the URL in another rule. Check the format of your IP addressMake sure that your IP address matches one of the following formats:
Single IP address: e.g. 40.77.182.32 IP address range: e.g. 40.77.182.32-40.77.182.200 Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation: e.g. 40.77.183.32/27If you see a message that says IP address is not valid, make sure that your IP address matches one of these formats.Check your IP address for any spaces or incorrect charactersYou can only use numbers, periods, dashes, and slashes in your IP address. If you see a message that says IP address is not valid, make sure that your IP address does not contain any spaces or incorrect characters. Make sure you haven't used the same IP address more than once in your ruleYou can only use an IP address once in your allowlisting rule. If you see a message that says This IP address is already part of the rule, check the addresses that you have already added to make sure that you're not repeating an IP address.

source_documents.title: Wix Loyalty Program: Adding an Expiration to Your Loyalty Points
source_documents.content:
Wix Loyalty Program: Adding an Expiration to Your Loyalty Points
With Wix's Loyalty Program, you can add an expiration date to your loyalty points, helping to encourage repeat visits and purchases from your customers. This can be great for your business, as it motivates your customers to use their points before they expire, driving more sales and enhancing customer engagement.For example, imagine this scenario: Sarah, a regular customer at your online store, accumulates loyalty points with every purchase. She notices that her points are due to expire at the end of the month, so she returns to your online store to use them, making additional purchases in the process. Add expiration dates to the points in your own loyalty program to boost your business in a similar way.In this article, learn more about:
Enabling and setting up points expiration Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Adding and setting up points expirationAdd points expiration to your Loyalty Program from your site's dashboard.Before you begin:To launch a Loyalty Program, you first need to upgrade your site. To add a points expiration date to your Loyalty Program:
Go to Loyalty Program in your site's dashboard. Click Manage Program. Click the Points and rewards tab. Click the toggle next to Points expiration to set it as active. Select the terms of your loyalty points expiration:
    
Expiration period: Choose how long customers have to redeem points before they expire.  Share of points to expire: Choose the percentage of points that will expire after the expiration period. Send an email reminder: Automatically send an email notification 14 days before your customers' points expire.   Click Save.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about loyalty points expiration.What happens if I make changes to point expiration rules, such as changing the percentage of points to expire?If you edit your points expiration rules, the updated program starts from that date for all customers, and their inactivity period will be calculated from that date onwards.For example, if your customers' expiration date was 1st January 2024 with an inactivity window of 6 months, and you changed the window to 3 months on the 31st December 2023, the new point expiration date for customers would be the 31st March 2024.Why do the last activity date and point expiration date in my dashboard not match?Earning and redeeming points are the only customer actions that count for point expiration. Other actions such as program signups are included under a customer's last activity. These dates do not impact each other, and may appear differently in your dashboard.Does issuing refunds affect points expiration?Refunding points to a customer via your dashboard will not affect their points' expiration date. Only customer actions affect the expiration date.Do expired points affect the Tier program?Points expiration does not affect the Tiers program.

source_documents.title: Asked to Upgrade When You Already Have a Site Plan
source_documents.content:
Asked to Upgrade When You Already Have a Site Plan
Possible reasons why you might be asked to upgrade when you've already purchased a Premium or Studio site plan include:
You have more than one site: Premium or Studio plans are for one site only. You are welcome to have more than one site in your account, however, each site needs to have its own site plan to access premium Wix features, such as connecting a domain or accepting payments.

 You are signed in to the wrong account: Make sure you are signed in to the account which contains your site plan. If you are having trouble finding your account, you can use our account recovery tool. 

 You are trying to use a service not covered by your site plan: Wix offers a range of Premium or Studio site plans. Make sure that you choose a plan that includes all the services that you wish to offer. If you want to take payments on your site, for example, you must upgrade to a plan that allows you to accept payments.

source_documents.title: CMS: Referencing Multiple Items in One Collection Field
source_documents.content:
CMS: Referencing Multiple Items in One Collection Field
A reference field creates a connection between an item in one collection and an item in a different collection. A multiple items reference field is similar to a reference field, except it allows you to reference more than one item from another Collection.Multiple item reference fields create a two-way connection between collections. This means that when you create a multiple-item reference field in collection A that points to collection B, a corresponding multiple-item reference field is automatically created in collection B that points to collection A. For an overview of this process, check out our Ultimate CMS Guide video.To create a multi-reference field:
Go to CMS in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant collection. Click the Add icon  to create a new field. Select Reference or Multi-Reference as the Field Type. Enter a Field Name.  Select which collection you want to reference to under Referenced Collection. Click Save. Tip:After setting up your multiple items reference field, learn how to display content from multiple content collections using reference fields.

source_documents.title: Editor X: Adding and Customizing Chat
source_documents.content:
Editor X: Adding and Customizing Chat
Communicate with your visitors directly by adding a chatbox to your site. Using Wix Chat, visitors can always reach out, whether you're available or offline. You can even initiate a chat with visitors who are currently browsing your site. Learn how to:
Add chat to your site Customize the chatboxAdding Chat to Your SiteYou can add the Wix Chat app to your site directly from the App Market. Once you do, a minimized chat bar appears at the bottom right corner of your Editor. To add chat:
Click the App Market icon  on the top of Editor X. Type "Wix Chat" in the search field and press Enter. Click Wix Chat. Click Add to Site.What's next?Go to your inbox to view and reply to all chat messages. You can also initiate chats with live site visitors to keep them engaged.  Customizing the ChatboxCustomize the chatbox to completely match the site's look and feel. From the Settings panel, you can adjust the automated texts, the layout and the design to your needs. You can even add a pre-chat form to capture leads in case you're not available to talk. To customize the chatbox:
Select the minimized chatbox at the bottom right of your Editor. Click Settings. Using the tabs on the left, customize your chatbox:
    
Settings: Create a pre-chat form and choose which pages should show your chatbox. Display: Control the positioning of your chat on the page and choose how new messages appear to visitors.   Design: Customize the design of the chatbox background, header, messages and border. You can also upload your business logo to add a touch of branding. Texts: Write your own automated text for the chatbox so it speaks your language.

source_documents.title: Google Ads with Wix: FAQs About Your Monthly Subscription, Daily Spend, and Ad Credits
source_documents.content:
Google Ads with Wix: FAQs About Your Monthly Subscription, Daily Spend, and Ad Credits
From the main campaigns page in your Google Ads with Wix dashboard you can view and manage your subscription. You can also adjust your daily spend across all your campaigns and make one-time payments.Click a section below to learn more about your Google Ads with Wix subscription, daily spend, and ad credits.In this article, learn more about:
Your monthly subscription, ad credit, and daily spend Ad credits for live or paused campaigns How your ad spend works Making one-time payments The Google Ads $500 promotional credit Currency questionsYour monthly subscription, ad credit, and daily spendWhat is the difference between a monthly subscription, ad credit, and daily spend?
Monthly subscription: The amount billed monthly (before VAT) as a whole for all campaigns you're running with Google Ads with Wix. The monthly subscription amount is applied directly to your ad credit each month. Ad credit: The total sum of money available to run ads across all your campaigns. Ad credit is only spent on ad link clicks and clicks to CTA buttons. Note: Your ad credit is paid in USD regardless of the currency you pay your subscription in. One-time ad credits: A one-time purchase of extra credits for when you want to promote a specific sale or event, or give a specific campaign(s) a boost and get more clicks.  Daily spend: The amount of money you set for a specific campaign to spend on clicks per day. You can set a different daily spend for each campaign using your ad credit. Your daily spend is optimized to be spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks. The amount will be paid up front, and is not pay-per-click.What does my Google Ads with Wix subscription include?Your Google Ads with Wix subscription includes:
The amount billed monthly (before VAT) as a whole for all campaigns you run with Google Ads with Wix. The amount is applied directly to your ad credit each month.  The Wix fee* and tax.*Wix gets 15% of your payment for running and optimizing your campaign. The remaining 85% goes towards your ad credit which is spent on ad clicks.Does Wix charge a fee?Wix gets 15% of your payment for running and optimizing your campaign, the remaining 85% goes towards your ad spend which is spent on ad clicks. Prices do not include VAT, which is determined based on your billing country.What does my ad credit include?Your ad credit may include your monthly subscription, any rollover ad credit from previous months, as well as any qualifying Google Ads credit applied to your account. If you pay in a supported currency (e.g. EUR, GBP, JPY, USD) the ad credits are in the same currency. For all other currencies, ad credits in your dashboard show as USD.How is my ad credit spent?Google Ads use PPC model of digital advertising. PPC stands for pay-per-click, a system where the advertiser pays a fee each time one of their ads is clicked. Essentially, you're paying for targeted visits to your website (or landing page or app).Therefore, in some cases, the ad credit might not be used if the campaign is not clicked.How do I manage my subscription?You can manage your subscription from the campaigns page of your dashboard. Click Manage Spend & Credits at the top to update your monthly subscription or adjust your daily spend across all campaigns you're running.Ad credits for live or paused campaignsWhat happens to my ad credit if I pause a campaign?You can pause your campaign at any time. As soon as you pause, the following changes happen:
Your ad is no longer shown on Google. Your remaining ad credits stay in your account. If the paused campaign was your last active campaign on the account, auto renew is turned off for the subscription.Note: Any Google Ads credits that have an expiry date may expire while the campaign is paused.Can I use my remaining ad credit for a paused campaign without purchasing a new subscription? Yes. Ad credit is saved in your account. If your subscription expires, you can run a campaign on the remaining ad credit until it is gone. Then the campaign will stop.How your ad spend worksHow do I change the daily spend of my campaign?
From the main campaigns page, click Manage Spend & Credits at the right. View the ad credits remaining in the current billing cycle. Click Adjust Daily Spend to change your daily spend. Enter a new daily spend for the campaign(s) you want to change. If you are running more than one campaign, you can see the total daily spend across all your campaigns.
Note: If you don't have enough for the new daily amount, you can increase your monthly subscription. Click Save to update your daily spend. If you have also increased your subscription, you will go through the checkout process at this step.What happens to my daily spend if it is not fully utilized within the month?As Google uses the PPC (pay-per-click) model, it is possible that the your daily spend will not be fully utilized due to a lack of clicks. If this is the case, your remaining spend will be added to the total ad credits for the following month.How does my daily spend work if I am running multiple campaigns?You pay for one Google Ads with Wix subscription regardless of how many campaigns you run. You can also always buy extra ad credits with a one-time payment that are added on top of your subscription. Your ad credits are used to run your ads.When you choose a daily spend for a new campaign, it's taken from the total 'bucket' of ad credits available for all campaigns in your account. To get more ad credits, Click Manage Spend and Credits in the campaigns page and increase your subscription.How do I view my Google Ads with Wix invoices?All invoices for Wix services can be viewed in the Billing History page of your account. Invoices may include VAT, which is determined based on your billing country.Making one-time paymentsHow do I make a one-time payment?
Click Manage Spend & Credits in the campaigns page. Click Manage Ad Credits. Select Purchase one-time ad credits and choose an amount. Click Purchase Credits.What is the difference between a monthly subscription and a one-time payment?Your monthly subscription is the amount billed monthly for all the campaigns you're running with Google Ads with Wix. The monthly subscription amount is applied directly to the total ad credit each month (ad credit available across all the campaigns).
However, if you want to purchase additional ad credit, you can make a one-time purchase of credits that are added to the total in your account. You can then readjust the daily budget of one or more campaigns as needed. This won’t affect your overall monthly subscription.About the Google Ads $500 Promotional CreditWhat are the requirements for receiving the promotional credit ($500 for USD subscriptions) offer from Google?You are eligible for the ad credit as long as you meet the following conditions: 
You are new to Google advertising. You have not run a Google Ads campaign previously with your site. You have spent $500 USD (or your currency equivalent ) on ad clicks in the first 60 days after launching your campaign.Note: If you have run a campaign in the past with Google Ads, you will not be eligible, even if this is your first campaign with Google Ads with Wix.Is Google's promotional credit offered for different currencies?Yes. Your promotional credit is based on the currency you used to pay for your subscription.Below is a list of what you need to spend on Google to get promotional credit:
USD: Spend 500 USD to get 500 USD EUR: Spend 400 EUR to get 400 EUR GBP: Spend 400 GBP to get 400 GBP JPY: Spend 60,000 JPY to get 60,000 JPY Every other currency: Spend 500 USD to get 500 USD. (e.g. if converting AUD to USD you must spend roughly 725 AUD to reach 500 USD threshold).Can I use Google's promotional credit to cover the renewal of a subscription?Unfortunately, it is not possible to use the credit to cover a subscription renewal. This credit must be used towards your campaign.How long do I have to spend the ad credit after receiving it?You need to spend the ad credit within 60 days of receiving it in your account. After 60 days, the ad credit expires.How is the ad credit applied to my account?After you have spent $500 USD within the first 60 days, Google automatically applies the amount to your available ad credits. You will receive an email about the new credit, as well as a dashboard notification.Why am I not seeing the credit immediately?Purchasing a Google Ads with Wix subscription does not apply the credit immediately. The promotional credit is applied to your account after you spend $500 USD on ad clicks. Then it is applied to your account.Note: Since the credit comes directly from Google, it may take a few days to see the credit applied to your account after you have fulfilled the requirements.Currency questionsWhat if I choose to pay for my subscription in a currency other than USD?You pay for your monthly Google Ads subscription to Wix in the currency of your choice. This is applied to your ad credits that are spent on clicks. If you pay for your subscription in an unsupported currency, your monthly subscription gets converted into US Dollar (USD) to pay Google for the ad credits you spent on clicks.You can find the exact conversion value for the current subscription period next Monthly Subscription on your dashboard.What are the Google Ads supported currencies?The supported currencies that Wix can apply to your ad credits to pay Google are:
US Dollar (USD) Euro (EUR) Great British Pound (GBP) Japanese Yen (JPY)If you pay Wix for your monthly subscription in one of these currencies, it will be applied to your ad credits in that currency.Why was I charged for Google Ads in USD when that isn't my currency?Wix automatically determines your billing currency by geolocation. If you pay for your Google Ads with Wix subscription in an unsupported currency, your subscription is converted into USD ad credits each month to pay Google.This conversion from monthly subscription to ad credits in USD happens when your initial subscription is purchased, and repeats each time the subscription renews.Note: Your Google Ads dashboard also shows your ad credit in USD.

source_documents.title: Renaming Files and Folders in the File Share App
source_documents.content:
Renaming Files and Folders in the File Share App
With the File Share app, you can create a file sharing library where people can exchange ideas and collaborate on projects.You can rename your files and folders at any time on your live site or from your site's dashboard. Add useful names to make them more meaningful to the people in your community.In this article, learn how to rename files or folders:
From your site's dashboard On your live siteRenaming files or folders from your site's dashboard
Go to File Share in your site's dashboard. Click the Show More icon   next to the file or folder you want to rename. Select Rename.
Enter a new name. Click Save.Renaming files or folders on your live site
Go to the File Share app on your live site. Log in using the email address associated with your Wix account. Click the Show More icon   next to the file or folder you want to rename. Select Rename.
Enter a new name. Press Enter on your keyboard.

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Adding an Entrance Animation
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Adding an Entrance Animation
Adding an entrance animation to an element is a great way to draw visitors' attention to it. The animation appears when the element first enters into view, so it instantly catches the eye. There are many types to choose from and customize to your client's exact needs.In this article, learn more about:
Adding an entrance animation Customizing an entrance animation Removing an entrance animationAdding an entrance animationYou can add an entrance animation to specific elements and sections, or the site page as a whole.To add an entrance animation:
Select the relevant element. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Click the Animations and Effects tab . Click + Add under Entrance. Select an animation from the list. 
Tip: Hover over animations to see a preview of how they look.  (Optional) Click Adjust Animation at the bottom to customize settings like direction, delay and duration.Customizing an entrance animationAfter choosing an animation, set it up to behave the way you want. Choose how long the animation lasts, when it starts, its intensity and more. To customize an entrance animation:
Select the relevant element, section or page. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Click the Animations and Effects tab . Click the animation you want to change.  Click Adjust Animation to change its settings:
    
Direction: Decide which direction the animation should come from. 
Tip: Depending on the animation type, you either set the direction in degrees (e.g. 180°) or choose an option from a drop-down (e.g. from left, clockwise).  Duration: Change the length of time of the animation. Delay: Set the amount of time between the page loading and the animation starting.  Easing: Choose how gradually the animation should ease in and/or out.   Note:The available customization options depend on the animation you choose.Removing an entrance animationYou can remove an entrance animation at any time from the Inspector panel. To remove an entrance animation:
Select the relevant element. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Click the Animations and Effects tab . Hover over the animation and click the More Actions icon . Click Remove.

source_documents.title: Wix Chat: Designing Your Chatbox
source_documents.content:
Wix Chat: Designing Your Chatbox
Ensure your chatbox reflects your brand's style and voice by customizing its colors and text. Consider its placement on your site and which pages it'll be displayed on. Make it easy to find and use to encourage visitors to get in touch. From your Editor, you can experiment with the appearance of your chatbox until you find the right fit.In this article, learn more about designing every aspect of your chatbox:
Customizing where and how your chatbox is displayed Designing the look and feel of your chatbox Setting the text your chatbox displaysCustomizing where and how your chatbox is displayedChoose which pages you'd like to display your chatbox on, where on those pages it will appear, and how new messages appear to visitors. Make your chatbox easy to spot to make your business more accessible.To customize your chatbox display:
Click the chatbox in the bottom corner of the Editor. Click Settings.
Click the Display tab. Choose what you want to customize:Position on PageDecide whether you want your chatbox to appear in the bottom left or bottom right of your live site.New Message DisplayChoose how new messages appear to site visitors. Have the full chatbox open automatically when site visitors receive a new message, or show a smaller bubble notification that prompts them to open the chatbox to view a new message.Chat VisibilityChoose where across your live site you want your chatbox to appear. Have it visible on every page of your site or have it visible only on the pages you select.Designing the look and feel of your chatboxFully customize your chatbox's design to match your brand. Give site visitors a cohesive experience by choosing colors and fonts that match the rest of your site. You can also add your logo to the chatbox's header and minimized chat for brand consistency.To design your chatbox:
Click the chatbox in the bottom corner of the Editor. Click Settings.
Click the Design tab. Choose what you want to customize:Business LogoClick the Update Logo icon  to update the business logo that appears in your chatbox heading when the chatbox is expanded.Minimized ChatThe minimized chatbox is how Wix Chat appears on your live site when visitors are not interacting with it. Choose your minimized chat layout, background color, text and icon.

Background & MessagesDesign your chatbox's background as well as how messages appear. Set your background color and pattern, how your Send icon appears and the font of sent and received messages.  Header DesignCustomize your header by choosing whether or not to include your business logo as well as setting your background color and text style.Border StyleCustomize your chatbox's border by setting a corner radius, border width and border color.ChannelsNote: This option will only be available if you've added the WhatsApp channel to your chatbox. Learn more about adding the WhatsApp channel to your chatbox.Choose the color of the chat message icon  at the bottom your chatbox. The WhatsApp icon is predefined and can't be customized.Setting the text your chatbox displaysDecide whether you'd like to display default text or your typical response time in your chatbox. Enter the text you'd like to appear when the chatbox is minimized or you're not available to chat. Give your visitors upfront information about getting in touch with your business.To set your chatbox text:
Click the chatbox in the bottom corner of the Editor. Click Settings.
Click the Texts tab. Choose what you want to customize:When Chat is OpenEdit the text that appears when visitors open the chatbox. Choose the name you'd like to appear in the header when the chatbox is open and set the default text prompting visitors to enter a message (e.g. "Type your message...").Typical Response TimeChoose whether or not to show your typical response time in the header of your chatbox.Note: If you choose to show your typical response time, it only appears during your available chat hours.Minimized Chat TextEdit the text site visitors see when your chatbox is minimized, both when you appear online and available to chat and when you appear offline and unavailable.
Note: This option is only available if you've selected a minimized chat layout that includes text. Go back to the Design tab to update the layout of your minimized chatbox.Offline MessageEdit the message site visitors see when they open chat outside your available chat hours.Tip: You can manage your chat status and online hours from both your dashboard and the Wix app. Learn moreNext steps:You can customize your Wix Chat settings so it works best for your business.

source_documents.title: Wix Logo: Printing Your Logo
source_documents.content:
Wix Logo: Printing Your Logo
Your logo is a great way to share your visual identity and establish your brand. It belongs anywhere your current and potential customers can see it - not just online. Print it on business cards, stationery, or promotional merchandise like pens, mugs, and sweatshirts, via Order a Print. Note:Order a Print takes care of printing and shipping your merchandise, not Wix. Learn how to get help with your order here.In this article, learn more about:
Recommended file types for printing Logo plans with printable files Available products by regionRecommended file types for printingDepending on the Logo Plan you purchase you receive different logo file types. All file types (Standard or SVG) are printable but differ in terms of quality when printed.When printing your logo, the ideal file type to use is an SVG file. An SVG file is an infinitely scalable file that doesn't decrease in quality; no matter how much you expand or shrink it. Since SVG logo files are infinitely scalable, you can use them for any kind of purpose – from mini-magazine ads, up to huge billboards.  Learn moreNotes:
The standard high-resolution files of 5000x5000 pixels (included in the Basic Logo Maker plan) may be suitable in some printing scenarios. PNG files in their original size may also be suitable for printing in some cases. Keep in mind that PNG files decrease in quality when re-sized.Logo plans with printable filesBefore choosing from a Basic, Advanced, Value, Deluxe, or Professional Logo Maker plan, it's important to decide what you want to do with your logo.
The Basic and Value Logo plans come with 8 standard logo files (5000 x 5000 PNG) in color, grayscale and monochrome which are suitable in some printing scenarios. The Advanced, Brand Plus, Unlimited, and Business Logo Maker plans come with infinitely-scaling vector files (SVG files) which are most suitable for printing.Learn more about Wix Logo Maker plans here.Available products by regionYour merchandise order is printed and shipped by Order a Print. The available products vary per region; see the table below for a breakdown. Learn more about Order a Print. Setting your shipping region for the Logo MakerYou can choose where to ship your merchandise to directly from the Logo Maker. Learn moreSetting your shipping region for the Business Cards MakerYou can choose where to ship your merchandise to directly from the Business Card Maker. Learn more

source_documents.title: Wix Member Apps: Sales of Digital Goods & Services Unavailable For iOS Members in the Member Apps
source_documents.content:
Wix Member Apps: Sales of Digital Goods & Services Unavailable For iOS Members in the Member Apps
Due to Apple's In-App Purchase policy, any members using iOS devices will not be able to purchase online goods and services from the Wix Member Apps (Spaces App and Fit by Wix). Instead, they are encouraged to send a message to you (the business owner) to chat about the product or service they're interested in.Important:This policy only affects online goods and services in the mobile apps, not the sale of physical products or services.In this article:
About Apple's policy update How iOS members contact you about digital goods and servicesAbout Apple's policy updateApple's In-App Purchase policy affects the way you sell online goods and services to customers who are using iOS devices. If you sell online products that are consumed on the member apps, you will be affected by this update.A few examples of online goods and services that Apple will not allow members to purchase in-app include:
Online programs/classes (via Zoom, etc.) Buy/renting a video consumed on the app Pricing plans for online subscriptions Digital downloadsNote:The policy does not reject purchases of in-person classes, 1:1 sessions.Learn more about Apple's In-App purchase policy.How iOS members contact you about digital goods and servicesIf a member using an iOS device is interested in speaking to you about a digital good or service you offer, they'll be directed to an inbox message where they can ask for more information and you (the business owner) can decide how to proceed.The new inbox flow:
Members browse your digital goods or services on their member app. To start communication with you, they tap the relevant CTA. Depending on the app, the CTA will say something like 'Join Program' or 'Get Plan.'
Note: Members cannot view prices for your online goods and services at this point.
A message appears explaining that online payments are currently unavailable. Members can tap Send Message to start a chat with you about the digital product or service they're interested in.
Members are directed to their inbox and see a pre-filled message. They can edit the content and tap Send to send the message to the business (you). You receive an Inbox notification in the Wix app. You can view the new message and decide how you want to proceed. It is the responsibility of the site owner (you) to handle communication from this point onward.TipYou can use saved replies to quickly reply to your members for each service you are offering with pre written responses. Learn more
