source_documents.title: Site Performance: Your Site's DOM Order
source_documents.content:
Site Performance: Your Site's DOM Order
Your site's DOM order refers to the reading order of elements on your pages. This order is important for visitors using assistive technologies such as the Tab key or screen readers, as it determines the order in which they can view or interact with these elements.We recommend ensuring that the DOM order matches the visual order of elements on your pages, so every visitor can navigate through your site with ease. As well as improved accessibility, matching the loading order also prevents layout issues on your site.In this article, learn more about:
How DOM impacts your site's performance DOM order on Wix Editor sites DOM order on Studio Editor sitesDOM order and site performanceThe DOM determines the sequence in which elements load on your site. If the DOM order does not match the visual order of elements, it can impact your site's loading.For example, if a button appears at the bottom of a page but is first in the DOM order, it loads before the elements above it. As additional content loads, the page's layout may shift and move around to accommodate the other elements.Furthermore, if a visitor attempts to click that button while the rest of the content loads, they may accidentally select another element and be taken to another page or section.Your site's DOM order should match the visual order of the page, regardless of the reading sequence of the language (left-to-right or right-to-left script) to ensure that it loads correctly, and is a smoother experience for visitors.DOM order on Wix Editor sitesAutomatic DOM order is automatically enabled on your desktop Editor site. This means that any changes you make to the visual order of elements are automatically applied to the DOM order, so you don't need to do anything. When you build a site with the desktop Editor, a mobile version of your site is created. The DOM order of your mobile site is also automatically arranged, and doesn't require any manual changes. Important:The automatic DOM order on desktop Editor sites has been built for left-to-right scripts (e.g. English, Spanish, etc.). If your site uses a right-to-left script such as Arabic or Hebrew, you need to manually re-arrange the DOM order in the Layers panel.Note:Automatic DOM order is only applied to changes on desktop when you save your site.DOM order on Studio Editor sitesAuto DOM order is automatically enabled on sites you  build in the Studio Editor. The order is automatically rearranged when you add, align, and resize elements - so it should stay optimized as you go.You can disable auto DOM on a Studio Editor site and make manual changes if needed. Learn more about DOM order on Studio EditorImportant:
Auto DOM is automatically enabled on sites created in the Studio Editor after the beginning of November 2024. If you created a site before this date, it is not enabled. The automatic DOM order on desktop sites has been built for left-to-right scripts (e.g. English, Spanish, etc.). If your site uses a right-to-left script such as Arabic or Hebrew, you need to manually re-arrange the DOM order in the Layers panel.

source_documents.title: Wix Member Apps: Adding a Podcast to Your Member App
source_documents.content:
Wix Member Apps: Adding a Podcast to Your Member App
Embed a podcast for your members to listen to on the go, directly from their member app. You can add a podcast player to an existing screen or create a dedicated screen for it.Podcasts are pulled in to your site using an RSS link (Really Simple Syndication); a web feed that contains all the information needed to play your podcast. This allows members to access the podcast and its archives, and share episodes with others.Before you begin:Go to the settings section of your podcast hosting platform (for example, Apple Podcasts, Google Podcasts, Spotify, SoundCloud etc.) and copy the RSS link.DashboardWix appWix Studio app
Go to Mobile App in your site's dashboard. Select the relevant tab (e.g. Spaces by Wix app, Branded Mobile App).  Click Edit Mobile App.  Click the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Click Elements on the left.  Scroll through the top menu and click Podcasts. Click the podcast element. Choose what you want to do:
    
Paste your RSS link in the Link to podcast field.  Enable the Show title toggle to display and edit your podcast name. Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Click the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Click General Settings and under Element visibility, choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android, or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.      Click Save & Publish.
﻿Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Mobile App.  (If needed) Switch to editing a different mobile app:
    
Tap the mobile app name at the top. Tap Branded Mobile App or tap the relevant mobile app (e.g. Spaces by Wix app). 
Tip: Go to your site's dashboard on desktop to choose your preferred member app.  
Tap Edit under your site name or the name of your branded app.  Tap the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Tap + Add Element in the relevant location. Scroll through the top menu and tap Podcasts. Tap the podcast element. Choose what you want to do:
    
Paste your RSS link in the Link to podcast field.  Tap the Element Title toggle to show or hide the name of your podcast:
        
Enabled: The title of your podcast appears on your site. Enter the name you want to display. Disabled: The title of your podcast is not displayed.   Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Tap the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Choose which screen and device you want this button to appear on:
        
Visibility: Choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.  Location: Select which screen you want the button displayed on.     Tap Add. 
Go to your site in the Wix Studio app. Tap Mobile App.  (If needed) Switch to editing a different mobile app:
    
Tap the mobile app name at the top. Tap Branded Mobile App or tap the relevant mobile app (e.g. Spaces by Wix app).
Tip: Go to your site's dashboard on desktop to choose your preferred member app.  
Tap Edit under your site name or the name of your branded app.  Tap the Screen drop-down at the top and choose the screen you want to edit.  Tap + Add Element in the relevant location. Scroll through the top menu and tap Podcasts. Tap the podcast element. Choose what you want to do:
    
Paste your RSS link in the Link to podcast field.  Tap the Element Title toggle to show or hide the name of your podcast:
        
Enabled: The title of your podcast appears on your site. Enter the name you want to display. Disabled: The title of your podcast is not displayed.   Margins: Drag the Margins sliders to adjust the padding for the button(s).
Note: Tap the Edit individually icon to separately adjust the margins.  General Settings: Choose which screen and device you want this button to appear on:
        
Visibility: Choose which devices to show this button on: All, Android or iOS.
Note: You can show or hide elements of your site depending on what operating system your members are using on their mobile devices. Your elements are visible on all operating systems by default, but you can decide what to show on iOS, Android, or both.  Location: Select which screen you want the button displayed on.     Tap Add.

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Adding and Customizing Tabs
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Adding and Customizing Tabs
Use the tabs element to organize and group related content on a page. This element displays multiple sections of content in a compact manner, making it easy for your client's site visitors to find the information they need. In this article, learn how to:
Add the tabs element Manage the tabs Design the tabs Choose a default tab Adjust the layoutAdding the tabs element to a pageAdd as many tab elements as needed to organize the site content. After choosing a preset and dragging it onto the page, you can then customize the content and add elements. To add tabs:
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Layout Tools. Click Tabs. Select a design and drag it onto the page. Customize the content of the tabs:
    
Click the Tabs element you just added. Click Manage Tabs. Select the tab you want to work on.  Edit the tab's content: 
        
Add more elements. Edit existing elements. Adjust the grid to the desired layout.    Managing tabsUse the Manage Tabs panel to add, duplicate, rename or delete tabs. This panel also allows you to navigate between tabs to preview and edit them as needed.  To manage tabs:
Click the tabs element. Click Manage Tabs. Hover over the relevant tab and click the More Actions icon . Choose what you want to do with the tab: Rename, Delete or Duplicate.Want to add a blank tab?Click Add Tab at the bottom of the panel.Designing tabsCustomize the tabs element so it matches the style of the page. You can design the tab menu, the tabs themselves, and the container that displays the content.Tip:You can design the tabs for 3 different states: Regular, Hover and Selected.To design the tabs:
Click the tabs element.  Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Click the Design tab . Choose the part you want to design from the drop-down:
    
Tab container: This container shows the tab menu. Tabs: These are the tabs appearing on the menu. Select the state you want to customize (Regular, Hover, or Selected). Container: This is the container that shows the content of each tab.   Use the available design options:
    
Background fills: Apply a color, gradient or image background. You can add multiple background layers and adjust their opacity.  Borders: Add borders to create a contrast against the site page. Choose a design and color, and set the width. Corners: Choose how you want to corners to look. You can adjust each corner differently, and make them rounder or more square. Shadows: Add shadows for a cool 3D effect. You can set the size, visibility, angle, and more to give it more impact. Layout: Adjust the padding to make it larger or smaller. You can enable or disable the Lock icon  to adjust each side separately, or make them match. Text: Style and format the tab names appearing on the menu. You can change the font, size, color and more.   Note:The available options depend on the part you choose to design (i.e. Tabs container, Tabs or Container). Choosing a default tabThe default tab the tab that is automatically opened on the live site. You can change it to whichever should appear first for your client's content and site needs. Tip:In the Manage Tabs panel, you can see a checkmark icon next to the current default tab.
To set the default tab:
Click the tabs element. Click Manage Tabs. Hover over the relevant tab and click the More Actions icon . Click Set as default.Adjusting the tab layoutCustomize the layout, spacing and padding of tabs element. If there are a large amount of tabs, you can also decide how to display them in the menu (Scroll or Wrap). To adjust the tab layout:
Click the tabs element. Click the Layout icon . Adjust the layout using the available options:
    
Tab distribution: Decide how much the tab menu should stretch:
        
Default: The menu does not stretch to fit the width of the element. You can then align the tabs to the left, center, or right. Stretch: The menu stretches to fit the width of the element. You can align the text on the menu to the left, center, or right.   Space between tabs: Drag the slider to change the spacing between the tabs on the menu. Space between tabs & container: Change the space between the menu and the container that shows the content of each tab. Horizontal padding: Adjust the padding on the left and right of the menu tabs. Vertical padding: Adjust the padding on the top and bottom of the menu tabs. Overflow tabs: Select how to display to display tabs that don't fit in the menu:
        
Scroll: Site visitors can scroll through the menu to see more tabs. Wrap: Another row is added to fit the other tabs. You can then use the slider to adjust the space between the rows.   Tab direction: Display tabs on the menu from left to right, or vice versa.

source_documents.title: Using Pinterest Rich Pins with Your Wix Site
source_documents.content:
Using Pinterest Rich Pins with Your Wix Site
Rich Pins are Pinterest pins which show additional info when you view them on Pinterest. They are generally used for:
Product pages: These pins may include the product name, price, and availability. Blog posts: These pins may include the post's title, author, and a brief description. Recipes: These pins may include the ingredients and basic directions.This info is taken from the metadata included with the pinned page. Wix automatically adds this metadata for your Wix Stores product pages and Wix Blog posts, so it automatically appears when you pin a post to Pinterest. You can view it under the page type's SEO Settings.For any other page on your Wix site (including Recipe pages), you'll need to add the metadata to the page manually as additional meta tags. Tip:Make sure to check Pinterest's guidelines on how this metadata should be written.To add additional meta tags to a page:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant page. Click SEO basics. Click the Advanced SEO tab. Click + Add New Tag under Meta Tags. Add your meta tag code in the HTML Code field.  Click Apply.  
Go to your editor. Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant page. Click SEO Basics. Click the Advanced SEO tab. Click + Add New Tag under Meta Tags. Add your meta tag code in the HTML Code field.  Click Apply.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: About Social Sharing
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: About Social Sharing
You want to control how your web pages look when they are shared on social networks. Having great images, titles and descriptions for each page of your site makes your business look professional and increases the chances that people will come to your site. Wix automatically adds Social Share meta tags (known as open graph or og tags) to your pages so that search engines and social networks display them properly. You can customize the text and image that display when you share your site's pages on social networks.Tip:You can also customize your page's Twitter Settings to display a different text and image for pages that you share on Twitter. To change your social share settings:
Click the Pages icon  on the left side of the Editor. Click the relevant page. Click the Show More icon . Click Social Share to change your social share settings:
    
Click Upload Image to add an image. Click the Change icon  to replace the image Click the Delete icon  to remove the image.  Add a title under What's the page's og:title (title on social media)?. Add a description under What's the page's og:description (description on social media)?.    Click Twitter Settings to change your Twitter share settings:
    
Click Upload Image to add an image. Click the Change icon  to replace the image Click the Delete icon  to remove the image.  Choose the card size under What size card do you want to display on Twitter?. Add a title under What's the page's twitter:title (title on Twitter)?. Add a description under What's the page's twitter:description (description on Twitter)?.  Tip:For best results, upload an image that is at least 600 x 315 pixels. Learn More.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Adding Embeds and Custom Elements to Your Mobile Site
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Adding Embeds and Custom Elements to Your Mobile Site Use embeds and custom elements to display content such as external URLs, widgets, and animation on your site.In this article, learn more about:  Embeds and elements brought over from your desktop site Adding embeds and widgets to your mobile site Important information about iFrames Important information about custom elementsEmbeds carried over from your desktop siteCustom elements and embeds that you have added to your desktop site may be displayed differently on your mobile site.This is because certain iFrames are designed for specific screen sizes, and may not fit or align correctly on mobile devices.If your element isn't displayed properly on the mobile version of your site, we recommend hiding the desktop version, and re-adding a mobile-friendly alternative from the Add panel in the mobile editor (see below).Adding embeds and custom elements to your mobile siteAdd an embed, widget, or custom element to your mobile site to display relevant, fun, or interesting content. You can use them to add apps, sites, and even animations to your site.Important:Elements added from the mobile editor are mobile-only. This means they are not displayed on the desktop version of your site.To add an embed or custom element to your mobile site: Click Add on the left side your mobile editor. Click Embed Code. Click the relevant element to add it to your page: Embed HTML: Enter code from external servers to display widget and apps on your mobile site. Embed a site: Paste or type a URL to display external websites on your page. Custom element: Display whatever you would like on your site using snippets of code. Enter the relevant details for your widget.Note:If you are adding a custom element to your site, you must choose a source. You may also be able to add attributes to your element. Important information about iFramesWhen embedding code or a URL in an iFrame, keep the following guidelines in mind to ensure they are displayed properly on your site.  Always make sure the code you are embedding is up to date and HTML5 compatible. Most browsers don't display pages and scripts properly if they were written using older versions of HTML.  There is no character limit of the HTML and Embed a Site elements.  Your code must contain HTTPS and not HTTP.  HTML documents are described by HTML tags. HTML tags normally come in pairs like

and

. The first tag in a pair is the start tag; the second tag is the end tag. This format of the tags is crucial for maintaining the structure of the page you are trying to embed. Some sites have security policies that forbid them from being embedded on external platforms such as Wix. As a result, they won't appear in your iFrame after pasting their URL. This is controlled by the site's external coding, and it is not possible to bypass this within Wix.Important information about custom elementsFor security reasons, the custom element is rendered inside an iFrame inside the editor and in Preview mode. This might affect the layout of the component, so we recommend going to your published site to see how it is displayed on your live site. You can also use Release Candidates as a live site preview.  For security reasons, to use the custom element, you must upgrade your site with a premium plan, connect a domain, and have no ads on it. Make sure that your code contains HTTPS, not HTTP, or it will not be displayed on your live site. JavaScript code contains the core elements of the page, but the design settings and other complex functionalities might be stored separately. Therefore, some elements may not function or look the same if the relevant elements aren’t included within the main JS code, for example the CSS and other JS files.  Always make sure the code is up to date and HTML5 compatible. Most browsers don't display pages and scripts properly if they were written using older versions of JS or HTML.  SEO can be defined separately using Velo API.  The performance depends on the implementation of the custom element itself. The custom element code must be hosted by you if you are not using Velo.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Password Protecting a Specific Page of Your Site
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Password Protecting a Specific Page of Your Site
Limit the access to a specific site page by password protecting it. Visitors who navigate to a protected page are prompted to enter the password. This allows you to share your exclusive content on your own terms.In this article, learn more about:
Adding password protection to a page Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Important:If you choose to password protect a page, this also prevents search engines from crawling and indexing that page. This means that password protected pages do not appear in search results.Adding password protection to a pageHead over to the Page Settings panel to add a password to a site page. Once you publish this change, you can send the password to anyone who needs it.To password protect a page:
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant page. Click Settings.  Click the Permissions tab. Select Password holders.  Enter your chosen password for the page.  Press the Enter key on your keyboard.Tip:Make sure to send the password to visitors that you want to access the page.FAQsSelect a question to learn more about password protected pages.When should I add password protection to a page?Password protection can be used for a variety of needs. Some common examples include party / event invitations, small business updates, and contact information.Can I password protect my entire site?Yes, you can password protect your entire site with a single password. Can I password protect my site's homepage?Absolutely. However, you should be aware that adding a password to your homepage restricts access to the rest of the site – unless someone has a direct link to other site pages.Is code affected by password protection?Any code you have added with Velo by Wix to a password protected page, or the public folder, can still be viewed using the browser developer tools.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Renaming a Page
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Renaming a Page
Rename your pages so you can easily recognize them in the Pages panel. The new name that you select is automatically updated on all menus that display the page. To rename a page:
Click Pages  on the left side of the Editor. Click the relevant page. Click the Show More icon . Click Rename . Enter the new page name. Click DoneImportant:As your site menu displays your page names, changing the name of a page also changes the text on your site's menu.If you would like to update the page URL, follow the steps here.

If you would like to see a "Back" button added to product pages in Wix Stores, you can vote for it here.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is hugely appreciated.

Wix Editor Request: Superscript or Subscript Text

Open the relevant page in the Editor. Add a separate text element for your superscript / subscript text, and enter the text you want. Adjust the size of the text. Position the text box so it appears as subscript or superscript. Group the text boxes together so they act as a single element. We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is hugely appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Multilingual: Customizing Your Site Menu per Language
source_documents.content:
Wix Multilingual: Customizing Your Site Menu per Language
Customize your site menu per language so your site visitors see content relevant for their demographic. You can also reorder items or hide some of them per language. Doing so may improve your site's SEO by matching search queries in different languages. In this article, learn how to:
Translate your site menu Change the order of menu items per language Show or hide menu items per language Get answers to Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Translating your site menuTranslate your site menu so visitors can browse in their own language, making your site more inclusive. For example, translating "Emergency Services" to "Services d'Urgence" for French visitors ensures they can quickly find critical help. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Select your menu type and follow the steps: Regular menu
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant menu item.  Select the relevant option to choose how you want to translate the menu item: 
    
Edit name: Manually translate the item name, enter your translation, and click Done. Auto-translate name: Translate the name automatically.   Repeat for the rest of your menu items and languages.Advanced menu
Select your menu. Click Edit Translation. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant menu item.  Select Rename page.  Enter your translation. Click Done. Repeat steps 3-6 for the rest of your menu items.
Go to your editor. Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  on the relevant page. Select the relevant option to choose how you want to translate the menu item: 
    
Edit name: Manually translate the item name, enter your translation, and click Done. Auto-translate name: Translate the name automatically.   Repeat for the rest of your menu items and languages.Changing the order of menu items per languageCustomize your site menu for each language so visitors see the most relevant content. For example, a French version of your site might prioritize "Women's Clothing," while the German one may show "Men's Clothing" first. Changing the order in one language doesn't affect others.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. (If you have a regular menu) Convert your menu to an advanced menu.  Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Select your menu. Click Edit Translation. Click and drag menu items to change their order.
Go to your editor. Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Click Edit Translation. Click and drag menu items to change their order.Showing or hiding menu items per languageShow or hide menu items for each language to promote different content to different site visitors. For example, you might display "Local Events" on the Spanish site and hide it on the English site. Adjusting visibility in one language doesn't affect others.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Select your menu type and follow the steps: Regular menu
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant menu item.  Choose the relevant option: Hide from menu or Show in menu.  Repeat steps 2-3 for the rest of your menu items.Advanced menu
Select your menu. Click Edit Translation. Decide what you want to do:
    
Remove an item: 

Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant item. Click Hide from menu.   Add an item: 

Click + Add Menu Item at the bottom of the panel. Select the item type you want to add to your menu:
            
Site Pages: Add site pages as menu items. Link: Add a link to your menu. You can link to external sites, documents, and more. Section: Add a page section as an item to your menu.  Anchor: Add a link to a page anchor on your menu.  Submenu title: Add a drop-down submenu to your menu. Once you add the title, you can drag and drop menu items to be displayed in the submenu. Mega menu: Add a container that's displayed when visitors hover over the item in the menu. You can change the layout and design of the container and add elements.      
Go to your editor. Click the Switch Languages panel at the top of the editor.
Select the relevant language. Select your menu.  Click Edit Translation. Choose what you want to do:
    
Remove from menu: Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant item and select Remove from menu. Add to menu: Click + Add Item and select the type of menu item you want to add. The options differ depending on which type of item you add.   FAQsClick a question below to learn more about customizing your site menu per language.How can I reset the translation and order of my menu items? You can re-add the menu by clicking Add Elements  on the left side of your editor and selecting a menu. Will my menu's design, font and colors change when I translate it? No. The design remains similar, only the text changes. Why can't I see the menu items from my main language on my secondary language site version? If you can't see the menu items from your main language on your secondary language site version, it might be because you've created a custom menu in the past. You can easily re-add the menu by clicking Add Elements  on the left side of your editor and selecting a menu. Then, you can connect different items for each language.Can I hide a menu item for a specific language?Yes, you can hide a menu item from your menu in a specific language, but keep in mind that it will still be accessible from your other site versions and via a direct link.Can I translate the "More" button in my menu?Currently, it is not possible to translate the 'More' menu item, which appears when your menu is not wide enough to fit all the items in it.You can remove the 'More' menu item by doing one of the following:
Rename the 'More' menu item with a title that is not language-specific (such as three dots). Stretch the menu to display all site pages. Add a menu folder and move the additional pages to this folder. You can translate the folder name.How can I order my menu item for the sites that have both RTL and LTR languages?To re-order your menu items for sites with both RTL and LTR languages, you need to manually drag and drop the items into your preferred order.Can I translate my site menu from the translation manager on my site dashboard? Translating the site menu is available only in your editor. However, you can access the site menu translation mode via the shortcut section in the left panel of the translation manager.

source_documents.title: Wix Photo Albums Store: No Longer Available
source_documents.content:
Wix Photo Albums Store: No Longer Available
As of February 2023, the support of Wix Photo Albums Store has been discontinued. If you already have Photo Albums Store on your site, you can continue to use it as normal.Click a question below to learn more:I have never had Photo Albums Store on my site. Can I add it?No. The support of Photo Albums Store has been discontinued, so as of February 2023 it cannot be added to any sites that didn't have Photo Albums Store enabled before this date.Note: This change applies on a site level, not an account level. If you have multiple sites within an account, you may have Photo Albums Store on some sites and not on others.I have the Photo Albums Store on my site. Can I continue to use it?Yes. If you have Photo Albums Store on your site, you can continue to use it the same way. You can still add new albums, manage your store and accept orders.Order a Print will remain responsible for fulfilling and shipping orders as normal. If you have questions/concerns around the order status or quality of your prints, contact Order a Print directly:Website: https://www.orderaprint.com/wix-photo-albumsEmail: support@orderaprint.comI have the Photo Albums Store on my site. Can I continue to withdraw my earnings?You can continue to withdraw earnings as normal.Learn more about withdrawing earnings in the Wix Photo Albums Store.I have the Photo Albums Store on my site. Can I still receive support for my store?Yes, our Customer Care team is available to answer any questions you have around your Photo Albums Store.Learn more about contacting Wix Customer Care.

Note: If your question relates to the shipping or printing of merchandise, contact Order a Print directly:Website: https://www.orderaprint.com/wix-photo-albumsEmail: support@orderaprint.comIf I delete the Photo Albums Store from my site, what happens to my images?Your uploaded images will remain in the Media Manager in the Site Files folder, without a watermark.What can I use to sell my photos instead of Photo Albums Store?You can add Wix Stores to your site and connect it to Printful to sell your photos.

Wix Stores allows you to sell a variety of product types and control the delivery of customers' orders.My Photo Albums Store isn't working properly. Will it be fixed?As of February 2023, the support of Photo Albums Store has been discontinued. We cannot guarantee that we'll able to fix issues that might occur in the use of Photo Albums Store.

source_documents.content:
Transferring a .co.uk Domain Away from Wix
Wix domains with a .co.uk suffix require a change of the IPS tag name in order to transfer them away from Wix. This process does not involve an authorization code (EPP code) like with other domain transfers.Before you begin:You need an IPS tag to submit a transfer request for .co.uk domains. Contact your new domain provider to get the IPS tag before starting the transfer process.To transfer your domain away from Wix:
Go to Domains in your Wix account. Click the Domain Actions icon  next to the relevant domain. Click Transfer away from Wix. Click Transfer Domain after reviewing the important details of the process. Enter your new provider's IPS tag and click Continue. Click Submit Request to confirm your transfer.What's next?You don't need to do anything else in your Wix account. Your new domain provider can provide the next steps. Once the process is complete, the domain transfer will be finalized within 7 days.

source_documents.title: Wix Blocks: A Quick Tour
source_documents.content:
Wix Blocks: A Quick Tour
Before you begin:Wix Blocks is an advanced feature. To learn more about how to create a Wix Blocks app, go to the Blocks section in WixDocs.Welcome aboard – it's great to have you here!The Blocks Editor is where you create apps for Wix sites.Blocks apps can be anything from simple widget layouts to full-fledged interactive web components, complete with APIs and code files – the sky is the limit.Let's get started with a quick tour of the basics. You can then dive straight into the Blocks app workflow and start building apps, or try out our Blocks tutorial.Build amazing widgets for Wix sitesWix Blocks offers you all the tools you need to design professional widgets that site builders (yourself included!) can add to any site. It comes with powerful layout and design tools to help you make your widgets responsive, precise, and beautiful. Responsive from the ground upBlocks widgets are fully responsive when added to any Wix site, adapting elegantly to any viewport or layout.Limitless customization out of the boxIn Blocks, you compose your widget out of standard Wix site elements, like text boxes, images and buttons. They all come with tons of built-in customization options. When site creators add your widget to their site, all those options are still available, allowing them to adjust almost anything and make your widget perfect for their needs.Give site builders a tailored editing experienceYour widget's configuration settings control how site builders interact with the widget in the Editors, for example, which widget elements can be selected or removed, and the buttons available in each action bar.You can even build your own custom panels for the Editors using the Panel Builder, to let site builders easily adjust your widget's settings, layout, design, and more. Turbocharge your widget with Velo codeVelo's full-stack development platform empowers you to rapidly build, manage and deploy professional apps. Add custom functionality and interactions using Velo's APIs, use your own tools, and enjoy serverless coding in both the frontend and backend, all in an open, extendable platform.Let Wix sites interact with your widgetExposing your own API allows site builders to smoothly integrate your widget into their site, by manipulating the widget's props, calling its public functions, and reacting to its events.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Adding Notes to Your Posts
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Adding Notes to Your Posts
You can add notes to your blog posts in the post composer in your site's dashboard. Notes are a great way to leave reminders for yourself or your blog's authors for changes that the post may need. For example, you can leave a note on a post when multiple authors are working to create a post together. In this article, learn more about:
Adding a note Using mentions in a note Responding to a note Resolving a note Editing a note Deleting a noteAdding a note to a postAny writer or editor with access to your blog can write notes on your posts. You can also add as many notes as you want to a post. To add a note:
Go to Blog in your dashboard.  Select the post that you want to add a note to. Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Enter your note in the bottom right of the notes panel.
Tip: Use the "@" symbol with a writer's name to mention them on the post, e.g. "@Jay Cee". Learn more about mentions Click Add. Using mentions in a noteYou can mention writers or editors in your notes so that they receive a notification about your comment. Anyone who has access to a post can use mentions.Note:It's only possible to mention writers with Editor permissions or writers who are the owner of the post. To use mentions:
Go to Blog in your dashboard.  Select the post that you want to add a mention to.  Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Add a new note or edit an existing note. Type the @ symbol followed by the name of the person you want to mention, e.g. "@Jay Cee". 
Click Save.Responding to a noteWhen someone mentions you in a note on a post, you'll receive an email notification. You can go to the post that contains the note by clicking View Note. To respond to a note:
Click View Note in the email notification. Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Click Reply under the note you want to respond to.  Enter your response. Click Reply.Resolving a noteWhen you or your collaborators are finished with a note, you can resolve it. For example, if an editor tagged you in note to replace an image in a post, you can resolve the comment after you replace the image. Resolved notes are moved to the Resolved tab and are no longer visible on the Open tab. To resolve a note:
Go to Blog in your dashboard.  Select the post with the note that you want to resolve. Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Click the Mark as Resolved icon .Tip:To see notes that were previously resolved, click the drop-down menu under Notes and select Resolved. You can also click the More Actions icon  beside previously resolved notes to re-open or delete them. Editing a noteYou can edit your post's notes if you need to change something. For example, if you realize that you mentioned the wrong person on a note, you can edit the note and mention the right person instead. To edit a note:
Go to Blog in your dashboard.  Select the post with the note that you want to edit. Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Click the More actions icon  beside the note.  Select Edit. 
Make your changes to the note. Click Save.Deleting a noteYou can delete notes if you no longer need them. For example, if you decide there are too many notes on a post, you can delete some of them to leave only the most important notes. Important:It's not possible to recover a note after you delete it.To delete a note:
Go to Blog in your dashboard.  Select the post with the note that you want to delete. Click Notes in the top right corner of the post.
Click the More actions icon  beside the note. Select Delete.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Offering Services at Multiple Locations
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Offering Services at Multiple Locations
Offer your services at multiple business locations to provide your clients and staff more choices and flexibility. You can create appointments and classes that occur at more than one location or create separate services for each branch. Important:For services that require resources, make sure you add the relevant resource types, and their amount, to each of your locations to ensure a smooth experience for your clients and staff. Learn more about adding resources to your services at different locations. Notes:
When clients book services, the emails go to the email address connected to the default business location.  Your dashboard's time zone doesn't change if you have multiple locations. Only the time zone for your default location appears on your site. In this article, learn more about:
Adding business locations to your site Changing staff members' available locations Adding more locations to an appointment or class Offering courses at multiple locations Displaying services by location Removing a business location from your siteAdding business locations to your siteAs your business expands, add new locations to the Business Info section of your site. Keep your clients in the loop with easy access to the updated location details. They can then select the most convenient location to book their services.To add business locations to your site:
Go to Business Info in your site's dashboard. Scroll down to the Location and contact info section. If you have not already done so, enter the details of your first location:
    
Enter your business address. (Optional) Enter a Location name, for example, 'Our newest location'. (Optional) Enter an Address description, for example, "Enter from the side door beside the elevators". Enter contact info relevant for this location.
Note: Your default location will be set to your default time zone. For additional locations select a new time zone from the Time zone drop-down. Learn more about displaying times zones.   Click Save.  Click Add New Location.
Enter the details of your new location. Repeat steps 3 - 5 to create any additional locations. Click Save.Changing staff members' available locationsSet your staff up at multiple locations to offer more convenient options to your clients. Once you have set up the staff availability, you can create or edit appointments for all your locations. Learn about additional factors that can affect appointment availability. Before you begin:Make sure to set your default work hours. To change staff members' available locations:
Go to Staff in your site's dashboard. Hover over the staff member you want to update and click Edit. Scroll down and click the Edit icon  next to the relevant day of the week.
Click the Location drop-down and select the relevant location where your staff member works on that day. Click Save.
(Optional) Repeat steps 4-6 to select the relevant locations for each of the staff member's working days. (Optional) Repeat the steps above for all staff members who work from multiple locations. Adding more locations to an appointment or classAs your business grows, you may want to add more locations to your existing services. This is a great way to win new clients and offer more convenience to your existing clients. To add more locations to an appointment or class:
Go to Booking Services in your site's dashboard. Click an existing appointment or class to edit it.  Click Edit under Location. Click Business Location. Select the relevant business addresses from the Choose locations drop-down. 
Click Save. (Optional) Schedule recurring classes at multiple locations by scrolling down to the Schedule section. 
    
Add Sessions (click Save & Continue if prompted). Add the required session details, including the location. (Optional) Click + Save & Add New to schedule additional sessions. Click Save.  Tip:
Click Edit schedule under the Schedule section to edit class details.
Add a one-time session through your Booking calendar.Offering courses at multiple locationsYou can create a course and offer it any one of your locations. You cannot create a single course service to be held at multiple locations.To offer a course at multiple locations, start by creating the course at one location. Then, duplicate the course and set it at a different location. A single course service cannot have sessions in more than one locationTo offer a course at multiple locations:
Go to Booking Services in your site's dashboard. Click an existing course to edit it. Click Edit next to Location in the Locations section. Choose where you want the course to take place: 
    
Business location: Select one of your business addresses. Custom Location: Add a location other than one of your business addresses. For example, an Online session.   Click Save. Click the More Actions icon  next to the course you created above in the Booking Services tab. Click Duplicate. Hover over the class you duplicated and click Edit.
Click Edit next to Location in the Locations section. Choose where you want the second course to take place:
    
Business location: Select one of your business addresses. Custom Location: Choose a location other than one of your business addresses. (Optional) Repeat steps 6 -10 above as necessary, depending on the number of locations you want to include in the course. 
Note: Your clients will have to sign up for each course session at each location.    Click Save.Displaying services by locationIf you choose to include tabs on your Service List, you can display your services by location, instead of by service category. To display services by location: Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Go to your Book Online page:
    
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click Bookings Pages. Click the Book Online page.   Click the Book Online element on your page. Click Settings.  Click the Display tab. Enable the Show title on Service List toggle if you want to include the title (e.g. "Our Services").  Enable the Show tabs on Service List toggle to add the tabs showing your different locations. Select Locations under Use tabs to filter by.

Go to your editor. Go to your Book Online page:
    
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click the Book Online page under Bookings Pages.   Click the Book Online element on your page. Click Settings.  Click the Display tab. Enable the Show title on Service List toggle if you want to include the title (e.g. "Our Services").  Enable the Show tabs on Service List toggle to add the tabs showing your different locations. Select Locations under Use tabs to filter by.Removing a business location from your siteIf you stop offering a service at a location, you can remove it from your site. Any scheduled services at the deleted location won't be affected; so make sure to update the new location or cancel the service from your calendar. Alternatively, you can update all the relevant services from Booking Services on your site's dashboard.Note:You can't delete your default location. However, you can make another location the default, then delete the original default location. To remove a business location from your site:
Go to Business Info in your site's dashboard. Scroll down to the Location and contact info section. Click the More Actions icon  next to the location you want to delete. Click Delete. Click Delete to confirm.

source_documents.title: Wix Groups: An Overview
source_documents.content:
Wix Groups: An Overview
Wix Groups is a great platform to build a community for your members with shared interests. Get members talking about your brand, and to each other, using your group's discussion board. As a group owner, you can post announcements and promote exclusive events for members to join.Ready to get started?Add Wix Groups to your site and set up your group.Create unique groups for your membersCreate unique groups for members who share similar interests. Groups make it easy for you to give your members a place to get the conversation going and encourage them to engage with your business / brand. Choose from pre-existing templates or create one from scratch to create your first group.Build relationships with potential group members Create membership questions for people to answer when they request to join your group. This gives you an opportunity to get to know your members before they join. What's next?When new members join, you can post on your Groups Feed to welcome them and introduce them to the other members.Create a community with your Groups FeedYour Groups Feed lets members easily discover new group content in real-time. Members can also interact with each other and join new groups based on their interests.Promote engagement in your groupUpload a variety of content to generate buzz around a topic by creating and managing posts. For example, you can post business updates and announcements you want members to know about.Organize posts in your group:Assign feed topics to posts in your group to help your members find what they are looking for. Bring group members together with exclusive eventsCreate exclusive events for your group members to get them excited and bring them together. Showcasing events in your group makes it easy for members to sign up and RSVP.

Note: If you accept payment in installments, fees may differ depending on the number of installments.Account activationRequires review by PayU TurkeyNoteCurrently, this payment provider cannot be used with Wix Bookings.Settings in your PayU AccountEnable the following settings to make sure PayU processes orders from your site correctly and notifies you of any new transaction. IPN settingsSign in to your PayU Turkey account.Click Account Management.Click Account Settings.Click the IPN Settings tab.Enter the following URL in the URL field: https://api.paymentsos.com/callbacks/payuturkey/live/notificationsSelect the following fields under Data:SALEDATEREFNOEXTORDERSTATUSIPN_PIDIPN_PNAMEIPN_DATEIPN_TOTALGENERALClick Save Settings.Click the Account Settings tab.Select the following under Notifications:Canceled and returned ordersComplete ordersNotifications settings
Sign in to your PayU Turkey account. Click Account Management. Click Account Settings. Select one of the following options under Notifications: 
    
Email Text & IPN IPN (Instant Payment Notifications)  Note: Do not select the Email Text option as your orders won't be processed correctly.

source_documents.title: Live Site Errors
source_documents.content:
Live Site Errors
Standard HTTP status codes can appear in your browser if there is an error loading your site. Each status code represents a different type of error message. The most common codes are 401, 403, 404, 500 and 502.Click below to learn how to resolve live site errors:
Error 401 (unauthorized) Error 403 (forbidden) Error 404 (not found) Error 500 (internal server error) Error 502 (bad gateway)Tip:If you receive the error message ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT, check your internet connection. Click here to troubleshoot. If you're still unable to view your live site, contact us with the following information:
The specific error you are receiving, including a screenshot of the error. Your Wix username or email address.  Your domain name and site name.  Your Operating System (e.g. macOS Sonoma, Windows 10). The different browsers and browser versions you have tried.
Note: Go to whatismybrowser.com to find out what browser version you are using.  Your geographic location and which Internet Service Provider (ISP) you use.  Which internet security programs are installed on your computer (e.g. antivirus, firewall). Which troubleshooting steps you've already tried.

source_documents.title: Pricing Plans: Managing Purchased Plans in the Wix App
source_documents.content:
Pricing Plans: Managing Purchased Plans in the Wix App
The subscriptions area in the Wix app is the place to manage and keep track of the pricing plans you've sold.Note that any product subscriptions (from Wix Stores) or recurring invoices you've sent to customers (from Wix Invoices) also appear here. In this article, learn more about:
Accessing plans that customers purchased Extending a plan Suspending a plan Reactivating suspended plans Canceling a planAccessing plans that customers purchasedOn the subscription page, you can view each of your subscriptions and see their current status at a glance. To access the subscriptions tab:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Subscriptions. Tap the relevant subscription to view more details such as the subscription status, or to contact your customer. Show me a list of subscription statusesEach subscription you sell has a status to indicate what's been done so far. 
Active: Your customer can use the plan. Pending activation: The plan has a future start date and is not yet active. Suspended: The plan has been temporarily suspended. Canceled: The plan was canceled, and the customer cannot use it. Expired: The plan has ended. Grace Period: Filter for customer whose payment failed for their recurring subscriptions.  Pending Cancelation: The plan can be used by the customer until the end of the billing period they paid for and then will change to "Canceled" status. 
Note: You can undo cancelations for plans with the "Pending cancelation" status. If you undo the cancelation, the status of the plan returns to "Active". Free Trial: The recurring plan has a free trial and is in its free trial period.Extending a planYou can extend the duration of a customer's plan. This can happen, for example, when a customer was sick and wasn't able to make use of the plan. Extending a plan does not charge customers any additional fees.To extend a plan:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Subscriptions.  Tap the relevant subscription you want to extend.  Tap the More Actions icon  at the top.  Tap Extend Subscription.  Tap the Extend this subscription till drop-down and select the relevant date. Tap Save. Tap Yes, extend to confirm.Suspending a planYou can suspend a plan whenever you or your customer need to. This is useful if your customer cannot use their plan temporarily through injury, travel or for other reasons.To suspend a plan:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Subscriptions. Tap the relevant subscription you want to extend. Tap the More Actions icon  at the top. Tap Suspend Subscription. Tap Yes, suspend to confirm.Reactivating suspended plansYou can reactivate a suspended plan at any time. Your customer regains access to the subscription and all associated benefits, and you start collecting upcoming payments again.To reactivate a suspended plan:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Subscriptions. Tap the relevant subscription you want to reactivate. Tap the More Actions icon  at the top. Tap Reactivate.  Tap Yes, reactivate to confirm. Canceling plansIf a customer no longer wants to continue a subscription or you haven't received payment, you can manually cancel a subscription. To cancel a subscription: 
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Subscriptions under Business. Tap the plan you want to cancel. Tap the More Actions icon . Tap Cancel Subscription. Tap Yes, cancel to confirm.Issuing refunds:
To refund a plan with a one-time payment: To issue a refund, contact your payment provider (e.g. PayPal, Stripe). To refund a plan with a recurring payment: When you cancel a recurring payment, the purchased plan and payment will not continue for the next cycle. For example, if you cancel a monthly plan in the middle of January, the plan continues until the end for January, but does not recur in the following months. During January, in this example, the Plan Status will be "Pending Cancelation".

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Adding and Customizing Collapsible Text
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Adding and Customizing Collapsible Text
Collapsible text is a great option if you have a lot of information that you want to display. Parts of the text are hidden, and visitors can view the full text by clicking an expand button, or a link to the full body of text. In this article, learn how to work with collapsible text:
Add collapsible text Adjust the layout Edit the text Design the elementAdding collapsible textDepending on your needs, you can add different styles of collapsible text to the page. Some presets include a button that expands the text on the current page, others show a link that takes visitors to another page to read the full body of text. To add collapsible text:
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the Editor. Click Text. Click Collapsible Text. Drag your chosen text box onto the page.Adjusting the layout of the collapsible textChoose how visitors can read the full body of text. Add a button that opens the full text on the current page, or a link that directs visitors to the full piece.You can also set the alignment, spacing, and number of lines that appear before a visitor needs to click it.To adjust the text's layout:
Click the collapsible text box.  Click the Layout icon . Customize the layout using the options:
    
Choose how the text appears: Choose how the entire text is displayed: 
        
Collapsed: Visitors see a text preview, and they need to click a button or a link to read the full body of text. Show All: The entire text is displayed on the page, not collapsed.   Number of lines displayed: Choose how many lines of text to show before visitors need to click a button to see the rest. Button alignment: Align the button visitors click to read more, to the left, right or center. Spacing between text and button: Increase or decrease the spacing between the text and the button.  Editing the collapsible textAfter adding a collapsible text box, click Change Text to enter the full body of text (up to 120,000 characters). You can also edit the text of the button or link that lets visitors read more.  To enter or edit the text:
Click the collapsible text box. Click Change Text. Type or paste the full text under Change Text. Decide what the button does:
    
Expand: Clicking the button expands the text box on the current page to show the entire text. Link: Clicking the button redirects visitors to another page with the full text. Make sure to choose the destination under Links to.   Enter the text you want to appear on the button(s).Designing the collapsible text boxDesign the collapsible text box to match the page's aesthetic. You can adjust the look of the box itself (e.g. its background color), format the text and customize the button / link leading to the full text. To design the collapsible text box:
Click the collapsible text box. Click the Open Inspector arrow  at the top right of the Editor. Scroll down to Design. Choose an option under What do you want to design?:
    
Text: Customize the box that contains the text (e.g. background color, borders, shadow), as well as the actual text (font, size and more).  Button: Customize the link or button that visitors click to view the full text. You can adjust it on 3 different states – Regular, Hover and Disabled.   Note: Currently, the option to scale text is not available for collapsible text.

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Adding Elements
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Adding Elements
Elements make up the content of the site. They include text, buttons, forms, images and much more. In the Add Elements panel, you can find them all and choose the designs that fit your client's needs.In this article, learn more about:
Adding an element in the Studio Editor Types of elements you can addAdding an elementThe elements in the Add Elements panel are split up into categories and subcategories, making it easier to find what you're looking for. You can also use the search bar to find elements quickly.To add elements:
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the Editor. Click the element category. Click the relevant subcategory. Click an element or drag it onto the page.Types of elementsBrowse through the following categories in the Add Elements panel:
Quick Add: Build more efficiently and quickly using these common elements, rather than searching the Add Elements panel each time for what you need.  Sections: We have tons of beautiful pre-designed page sections to help you get started. These presets were made to look great on all screen sizes. Containers: A container helps you structure content that belongs together. Add and attach elements like videos, text and images to create your layout.  Text: Add different text elements for titles and paragraphs. Layout Tools: Use these tools to show groups of related elements in a responsive layout.   Buttons: Encourage visitors to interact with the site using functional and stunning buttons. Menu & Search: Add a variety of menus to help visitors navigate around the site. You can also add a search bar from here. Media: Add images, videos and music to bring the site to life. Decorative: Decorate the site with these beautifully designed elements. Contact & Forms: Let visitors contact the site owner and collect responses in a submissions table. You can also add a Google Maps element from here. Embed & Social: Embed code, external sites or Lottie animations. You can also add a social bar from here with links to the client's social accounts.   Input: Using these CMS (Content Management System) elements, you can create your own forms or allow visitors to filter the site's content.  Blog: Create a stunning blog and grow an online community. Store: Set up an online store to sell products. Bookings: Add a bookings system to let clients book and pay for services. Events: Create and manage online or in-person events.  Members: Allow visitors to become members and access their private account on the site. Multilingual: Localize the site for multiple languages and regions.  CMS: Manage your site more efficiently by creating and storing content in collections.

source_documents.title: Understanding Preset Markups for Your Site's Pages
source_documents.content:
Understanding Preset Markups for Your Site's Pages
Important:
Structured data markup is an advanced topic. Wix Customer Care cannot help you with any changes to your markup or submissions of it. However, if you experience any errors, you can check out our structured data markup troubleshooting help. Need help from an SEO expert? You can hire an SEO professional from the Wix Marketplace. Structured data markup gives search engines detailed information about your page. You can add structured data markup to your site's pages to help improve your website's search results and ranking.By default, Wix adds preset markups to some of your site's pages when you create them. These are Wix Stores product pages, Wix Bookings services pages, Wix Blog posts, Wix Forum posts, and Wix Events pages. Search engines like Google can also use markup to create rich results like article previews, product previews, and FAQs for your page's search results.Note:Adding structured data markup to your site's pages does not guarantee that search engines will create rich results for them. In this article, learn more about:
Preset markup basics Managing your preset markups Types of preset markups for your site's pagesPreset markup basicsThe preset markups that Wix creates for your site's pages use SEO best practices to give search engines optimized information about your pages. These preset markups also use variables to create dynamic code. Variables are pieces of text that represent a value, or text that's a placeholder for a value.Using variables, you can include information that varies from page to page based on the actual content of the page. For example, the preset markup for Wix Stores product pages uses a number of placeholder variables including:
Product Name Product Description Product Brand Product PriceThe actual information that is used for these placeholder variables depends on the product information that is on each page. This means that the preset markup is automatically customized for each of your pages and creates unique rich results for every product.Managing your preset markupsYou can view and manage your preset markups in the Structured data markup section of a page type's SEO Settings.To manage your preset markups: 
Go to your SEO Dashboard. Select Go to SEO Settings under Tools and settings. Select the page type that you want to edit.  Note: It's not possible to customize the default markup for your Main Pages. You can customize markup for individual pages in the Edit by Page section or in your editor.  Click Edit beside Structured data markup. Choose what you want to do:Preview or switch a preset markup
Click Preview Preset beside the markup you want to preview, or Switch Preset for pages that have multiple preset markup options.

Include or exclude a preset markup
Click the Show/Hide icon  beside the markup you want to include or exclude.
Create a custom markupYou can create a custom markup by duplicating a preset markup and editing it. 
Click Preview Preset beside the markup you want to create a custom markup from.
 Click Convert to custom markup. Enter a name for the markup.  Edit your markup under Write your markup in JSON-LD format. Click Apply.Create a new custom markup
Click + Add New Markup. Enter a name for the markup.  Add your new markup under Write your markup in JSON-LD format. Click Apply.Edit or remove a custom markup
Click Edit beside any custom markup you want to edit. Click the Remove icon  beside any custom markup you want to remove. Tip:You can have up to 5 markups per SEO Setting (including the preset markup).Types of preset markups for your site's pagesWix automatically creates preset markups for your Wix Stores product pages, Wix Bookings services pages, Wix Blog posts, Wix Forum posts, and Wix Events pages.Click a heading below to learn more about the different types of preset markups for your site's pages.Wix Stores product pagesWhen you create a Wix Stores product page, Wix automatically creates a Product preset markup for it. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the product page. This preset markup tells search engines that the page includes a product and helps them include relevant information for the product in search results.For example, the markup can help Google provide rich results that include information such as price, description, brand, availability, and product images.Click Preview Preset under Structured data markup on the Products page of your SEO Settings to see an example of what a rich result using this preset markup looks like. Wix Blog postsWhen you create a Wix Blog post, Wix automatically creates a Blog preset markup for it. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the blog post.There are three preset markups for blog posts:
Article (Blog Posting) Markup - This is the default preset markup Article (News Article) Markup Article MarkupEach of these preset markups tell search engines that the page includes a certain type of blog content and helps them include relevant information in search results.For example, the Article (Blog Posting) Markup can help Google provide rich results that include information such as the post's author, category, published date, and headline. Click Switch Preset under Structured data markup on the Blog Posts page of your SEO Settings to change to a different preset markup or to see an example of a rich result using that preset markup.
Wix Bookings services pagesWhen you create a Wix Bookings services page, Wix automatically creates a Course preset markup for it. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the services page.This preset markup tells search engines that the page includes a course and helps them include relevant information in search results.For example, the markup can help Google provide rich results that include information such as the service's type, name, description, and provider.Click Preview Preset under Structured data markup on the Booking Services page of your SEO Settings to see an example of what a rich result using this preset markup looks like.
Wix Forum postsWhen you create a Wix Forum post, Wix automatically creates a Questions and Answers markup for it. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the forum post.This preset markup tells search engines that the page includes questions and answers and helps them include relevant information in search results.For example, the markup can help Google provide rich results that include information such as the post's title, author, content, and published date.Click Preview Preset under Structured data markup on the Forum Posts page of your SEO Settings to see an example of what a rich result using this preset markup looks like.Wix Events pagesWhen you create a Wix Events page, Wix automatically creates an Event preset markup for it. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the event page.This preset markup tells search engines that the page includes an event and helps them include relevant information in search results.For example, the markup can help Google provide rich results that include information such as the event's name, description, start and end dates, and location. Click Preview Preset under Structured data markup on the Events page of your SEO Settings to see an example of what a rich result using this preset markup looks like.Wix PortfolioWhen you create a project or collection in Wix Portfolio, Wix automatically create preset markups for them. All the fields and values are automatically updated in the markup based on the actual content of the page.For your projects and collections, Wix creates an Images preset markup. This preset markup tells search engines that the page includes images so they can be added to the image search engine.Click Preview Preset under Structured data markup on the Portfolio Project or Portfolio Collection page of your SEO Settings to see what this preset markup looks like.

Update Payment Method for Subscriptions in Indian Rupee
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced new regulations for cross-border online payment transactions. As such, Wix subscriptions purchased in Indian Rupee must now be processed through an authorized facilitator of online Payment Aggregator - Cross Border (PA-CB) transactions.Wix has partnered with Razorpay (authorized for PA-CB) to process payments for Wix services.For subscription renewals originally purchased before July 31, 2024, users must update their payment method(s) to ensure uninterrupted Wix services.  If you don't update them, Wix may not be able to process your future payments, and your subscriptions could be canceled.To update your payment method:
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click Update Payment Methods at the top of the page.
Update your payment card details.
Tip: You can re-enter your existing card details, as long as the card is still valid. Click Submit.
Note: Once you have updated your card details, we'll verify your updated payment method with Razorpay.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Adding Images, GIFs, and Videos to Products
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Adding Images, GIFs, and Videos to Products
Add images, GIFs, or videos to your products so customers can see exactly what they're purchasing. In this article, learn how to:
Create effective product images Add images or GIFs Edit and crop images Add alt text to images Display different images for product options Add videosCreating effective product imagesGreat product images can be the difference between making a sale or losing out on one. Since customers can't touch or try your product in person, your images, GIFs, and videos are the key to showing customers what you have to offer. 
Quality: Even your best products may not look enticing if the picture quality is poor. Make sure to create - or have a professional take - high quality images. Using a tripod and correct lighting can make a big difference. What to showcase: Customers love to see multiple images of a product on all sides. It's also helpful to show closeups, for example to show the stitching and material on an article of clothing. Make sure to also show your product in context. For example, not just a close up of earrings by themselves, but show how they look when worn. For many more helpful tips on how to create great product images, click here.Adding images or GIFsWhen creating your images, make sure you pay attention to image ratios (image width vs height). In addition, use crisp and clean images with high pixel resolution.Note:To make sure the images display correctly, follow these recommendations:
Minimum pixel resolution: 3000 x 3000 pixels. Image ratios: 16:9, 3:2, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 2:3, 9:16 For viewing on a mobile device, the recommended image ratio is 1:1 (a square picture).  The Classic Product Page layout supports all image ratios. Other layouts look best with wider images.To add images or GIFs to a product:
Go to Products in your site's dashboard. Click to select a product. Click Add Images. Select images or GIFs from your Media Manager or click Upload Media to add images or GIFs from your computer. Click Add to Page.Editing and cropping imagesAfter you upload an image, you can use the Wix Photo Studio to edit and crop it, right in the Products tab. You can:
Crop images Adjust the brightness, contrast, or saturation  Create transparent images  Change the background color   Add text And more...To access the photo studio in Wix Stores:
Go to Products in your site's dashboard. Click to select a product. Hover over the image you want to edit. Click the Edit icon .

TipTo learn more about what you can do with Wix Photo Studio tools, click here.Adding alt text to imagesImprove your business's SEO by adding alt text to product images.To add alt text:
Go to Products in your site's dashboard. Click to select a product. In the Images & Videos section, click the More Actions icon .  Click Edit Alt Text for Images.  Enter the Alt Text.  (Optional) Click the Copy to all images icon   to apply the same text to all images.

 Click Done.Displaying different images for product optionsHelp customers visualize each of your product options by displaying separate images of each one.Note:You can link images to each option, but not to each variant. To vote for this feature, click here.To link images, GIFs, and video to product options:
Go to Products in your site's dashboard. Select a product with product options. Scroll down to the Product Options section and click Connect Images.

 If you created more than one type of option, select the relevant option.

 Click the Plus icon  next to the first option choice.  Select or upload up to 15 images for each option choice and click Done. Click Apply.Adding product videosProduct videos are the next best thing to experiencing a product in person. They can give customers the confidence they need to make a purchase.Notes:
Acceptable video formats: AVI, MP4, MOV, MPEG  Videos can be up to 50 MB in size. To learn how to sell video content with Wix Video, click here. To add videos to your store products:
Go to Products in your site's dashboard. Select an existing product or click New Product to add a new one. Click Add Videos.

 Select videos from your Media Manager or click Upload Media to add videos. Click Add to page.Want to learn more?Check out the full Wix Learn course on getting started with Wix eCommerce.

source_documents.title: Changing the Language of Your Account and Editor
source_documents.content:
Changing the Language of Your Account and Editor
The language of your dashboard/workspace and site editor is determined by the language of your Wix account. You can change the language of your Wix account by following the steps below.In this article, learn more about:
Changing the language of your account and editor Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Changing the language of your account and editorOnce you change the language of your Wix account, your editor will also be displayed in that language.WixWix Studio
Sign in to your Wix account. Click the user panel at the top right. Click Account Settings. Click the Account language drop-down and select a language.
Sign in to your Wix account. Click the user panel at the top right of your workspace. Click Account Settings. Click the Account language drop-down and select a language.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about languages at Wix.What languages are available?Currently, you can use Wix and Wix Studio, both your account and editor, in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Polish, Italian, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Turkish, Chinese, Thai, Swedish, Norwegian, Dutch, Danish, Czech, Bahasa Indonesia, Vietnamese, and Ukrainian.Note: From January 2024, Hindi will no longer be supported.Does changing the language affect my live site?No. The language you set in your account determines the language of your dashboard/workspace, editor and communications. If you want to change the language of your live site, you need to update the content, or use Wix Multilingual to display your site in more than one language.Do you have website templates on all languages?Currently, we have templates in only some languages. However, as you can customize all aspects of our templates, you can choose a template in another language and just edit the text as needed.Can I use special characters when writing the content for my site?The editors support all languages and special characters that are supported by UTF8, which is a dominant character encoding for the Internet. This includes Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Arabic, Korean, Greek, Russian, Portuguese, and Hebrew, as well as several others.No setup or configuration is required to use these languages, as the editors support whatever language you have installed on your computer's operating system. Simply ensure that your computer supports the language you want, and type wherever text is editable on your site.What languages does the Wix Help Center support?The Wix Help Center is available in English, Dutch, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish and Ukrainian. Learn how to change the language of the Help Center.Wix offers phone support in English, Dutch, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish, and Turkish. Learn more about contacting Wix Customer Care.
