source_documents.title: Editor X: Adding and Managing a Members Area
source_documents.content:
Editor X: Adding and Managing a Members Area
The Members Area is a tool that enables your site members to have their own account on your site, thereby improving the experience you can provide to your users. Members can log in, view members-only pages and access their account settings. Learn MoreWith Editor X, all the Members Area features have been designed to be fully responsive, so that they look great on every screen size!Learn more about:
Adding a Members Area The login bar The signup and login forms Member-exclusive pages Deleting the Members AreaNote:Some Wix apps such as Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, and Wix Blog automatically add the Members Area to your site. However, you can also use a Members Area without these.Adding a Members AreaHead over to the Add panel to add a Members Area to your site. Once you do, we'll add a login bar, basic member pages and signup and login forms to help you get started. Show me how
Click Add  on the top of Editor X. Click Members. Click Add to Site.The Login BarThe Login Bar appears in your site's default master header so members can sign up, log in or out from any page of your site. You can move the element wherever you need and adjust its design and layout. Show me how
Select the login bar on your header. Do the following to customize it:
    
Click Set Up Login Bar to change its text and choose what info to show (profile pic, member's name or both).  Click the Layouts icon  to adjust the icon size and choose an arrangement: Left to Right or Right to Left. Click the Design icon  to design the log in bar for three different states: Regular, Hover and Selected. Learn More  The Signup and Login FormsThere are 2 types of default forms that come with the Members Area: One that lets new members sign up, and another that allows existing members to log in.Click below to learn more about each form:Signup FormThis form is displayed when a site visitor wants to sign up to become a member of your site. They can sign up with their Facebook or Google accounts, or enter an email address and password manually. The fonts and colors appearing on this page are pulled directly from the Theme Manager so it matches your site's design.Using Velo?You can create a custom signup form that opens as a pop-up using lightboxes. 
Login FormThis form is displayed when an existing member wants to log in to your site. Depending on how your members signed up, they can use Facebook, Google or their credentials to log in. The fonts and colors appearing on this page are pulled directly from the Theme Manager so it matches your site's design.
 Member PagesOnce logged in, a member has access to all of the member pages. Each member has a "My Account" page where they can add their personal details. These details are automatically added to your Contacts. Other available member pages depend on the features you have on your site. For example, if you've added a store to your site, members can enjoy a personalized shopping experience with pages like "My Orders", "My Addresses" and "My Wallet".  Tip:From the Pages panel, you can add pages of your own with member-exclusive content. Learn HowDeleting the Members AreaYou can delete your Members Area at any time. This removes all of your member pages, member profiles, and login bar from your site.  Show me how
Click Pages  at the top of Editor X.  Hover over Wix Members Area and click the More Actions icon .  Click Delete Members Area. Click Yes, Delete.

source_documents.title: Editor X: Using Styled Horizontal Menus
source_documents.content:
Editor X: Using Styled Horizontal Menus
Styled Horizontal Menu is an advanced navigation element offered by Editor X, with tons of unique customization options. You can tailor this menu to your exact needs, adjusting the layout and design of every single area. In this article, learn how to:
Add a Styled Horizontal Menu Design the menu Adjust the layout of the menu and submenuAdding a Styled Horizontal MenuChoose a Styled Horizontal Menu that matches your desired look. You can personalize the design to make it more accurate to your needs, and choose which menu to show on this element – it can be an existing menu displayed elsewhere on your site, or a custom one just for this context. To add a Styled Horizontal Menu:
Click Add  at the top of Editor X. Click Menu & Search. Click Styled Horizontal Menus. Drag and drop the relevant menu to the desired location on your page.  (Optional) Create a new menu with custom pages:
    
Click Manage Menu.  Click the drop-down under Which menu is displayed?. Click Manage Site Menus. Click + Add New Menu at the bottom to create the custom menu.   Designing a Styled Horizontal MenuFrom the Inspector panel, you can design every part of your Styled Horizontal Menu - the menu and submenu container, as well as the menu and submenu items. To design the menu:
Click your Styled Horizontal Menu. Click the Inspector icon  at the top of Editor X. Click the Design tab .  Select an option under What do you want to design?:
    
Menu container Menu items Submenu container Submenu items   Use the available options to design your menu. You can:
    
Add layers of background fills and adjust the opacity of each layer. Format and style the text. Add borders to make that area of your menu stand out.  Round the corners of your menu / submenu. Add shadow to accentuate the menu or its items. Adjust the padding around the menu or its items.   Tip:You can design the menu and submenu items for different states - Regular, Hover or Current page (i.e. when the visitor is on a page they see in the menu or submenu).Adjusting the layout of a Styled Horizontal MenuAdjust the layout of your menu and submenu so they look exactly as you want. You can choose how to display menu items that don't fit (Wrap or Scroll) and the way your submenu opens (Flyout or Columns). You can also control the spacing, padding and much more.To adjust the menu's layout:
Click your Styled Horizontal Menu. Click the Layout icon . Choose which area you want to work on: Menu or Submenu. Adjust the layout of the menu and submenu to your needs. Click below to learn more about the available options:Menu layout options
How to display items that don't fit: Choose how to display items that don't fit in the menu container:
    
Wrap: More rows are added to your menu in order to display all items. Scroll:  This option keeps your menu compact, featuring only one row of items. Visitors click the scroll button to see the rest of the menu.   Horizontal / Vertical spacing between items: Drag the sliders to adjust the spacing between menu items. Items fill the whole menu: Enable this toggle to make your items stretch to fill the entire space of the menu container. 
    
(When the toggle is enabled) Align text: Choose how to align the text on your menu items: Left, center or right. (When the toggle is disabled) Align items: Choose how to align the menu items: Left, center or right.    Display items from: Choose whether to show menu items from left to right, or right to left. Item Padding: Drag the sliders to adjust the vertical and horizontal space each item takes up in the menu.Submenu layout options
How do submenus open?: Select how the submenu items appear:
    
Flyout: Your submenu opens in a drop-down list. This is a good option if you only have a few items to display. Columns: Your submenu items are displayed in columns. If you have many items in your submenu, choose this option while defining the number of columns you need.  Depending on what you choose, there are different layout options to adjust:
Flyout:

Spacing between menu & submenu: Drag the slider to adjust the distance between the menu and the submenu. Align submenu: Align the submenu to the left or center. Align text: Align the submenu text to the left, right, or center. Padding: Drag the sliders to adjust the horizontal and vertical space the submenu fills. Spacing between items: Drag the slider to adjust the spacing between submenu items.
   Columns:

Spacing between menu & submenu: Drag the slider to adjust the distance between the menu and the submenu. Stretch submenu: Choose whether to make the submenu match the width of your menu, or stretch it to the full width of the page.  Number of columns: Drag the slider to adjust how many columns are in the submenu. Align columns: Choose to align columns to the left, right, center, or justified. Spacing between columns: Drag the slider to adjust the distance between columns. Align text: Align the submenu text to the left, right, or center. Padding: Drag the sliders to adjust the horizontal and vertical space the submenu fills. Spacing between items: Drag the slider to adjust the spacing between submenu items.

source_documents.title: Facebook Ads: FAQs
source_documents.content:
Facebook Ads: FAQs
This article answers the most frequently asked questions about Facebook Ads with Wix. In this article:
Setting Up Your Facebook Ads with Wix Campaign Understanding Your Campaign Dashboard What to Do While Your Campaign Is Running In-depth Look at the Wix AI Algorithm General QuestionsSetting Up Your Facebook Ads with Wix CampaignWhy should I use Facebook Ads with Wix?Running Facebook campaigns takes a lot of time and effort, and is very hard. That's why we decided to build an automatic tool using advanced data science algorithms that makes it easier. The algorithm runs daily analyses of every change in campaign performance from Facebook and Instagram, combined with the data from your website, creates all live dataset and then uses this data to run unique decision-making models and trend analyses. These in turn create a variety of potential recommended actions and changes. The system then simulates and estimates the effectiveness of each action, and fine-tunes the campaign based on those results. This simulation is used daily to make changes and improve the campaign.We manage all of the following for you:
Setting up the Business Manager and pixel Choosing the best placement to convert audiences Building initial target audiences A/B testing Testing to create optimized variations of Lookalikes Tracking engagement Retargeting Monitoring ad performance daily and making improvements based on data Analyzing results of views, visits and sales to calculate campaign efficiency Continuous maximization of the ad spend to keep costs per sale low and returns high Predicting how changes to the ad will affect the business Tracking conversion paths over time per audienceIn short, Facebook Ads with Wix is built with millions of data samples, fully integrated with Wix Stores, uses advanced Artificial intelligence (data science), works with Facebook and Instagram and is fully automatic. Our model is the best in the world for automatic advertising.What is the full step-by-step process to get my campaign live?Getting your campaign from set up to live is quick and easy, because the Wix AI does most of the work. Here’s how it works:
STEP 1: Getting Started
Once you’re ready to try it out, click “Get Started” in the Welcome Screen. You can also schedule a call with a Wix Expert anytime to get help or sales advice. STEP 2: Choosing a campaign goal You have three options of campaign goal: 'more store orders' for campaigns run with Wix Stores, 'more leads or bookings,' or 'promote a page.' Pick the goal that's right for you. Note: Once you pick a goal, you cannot change it. Step 3: Connecting to Facebook
In the connect page, choose to connect to your Facebook business page. Once you’ve done it, an ad preview will be created. This is based on a number of things like the campaign goal you chose, what products you advertise if you have Wix Stores, Meta pixel, Business Manager and more. Keep in mind that you must be the admin of the Facebook Business page in order to connect it. Follow the prompts that come up. STEP 4: Your Ad Content
Now you’re ready to set up your ad. In the ad content section, you’ll see an ad already set up for you based on information pulled from your site. The smart algorithm does a full analysis of your website and creates the ad. You can change your ad caption and image at any time, but it’s better to leave them as is, so that Wix’s algorithm can run tests to check how effective these are.  STEP 5: Target Audience
Next on the list is finding the right audience. The Wix algorithm will take care of this based on its analysis of what’s best for your business. Feel free to make changes to the gender, age range, interests and geographic location but keep in mind that it’s best to stick to the recommended parameters. That way, Wix AI can fully test out what’s best for your ad and how to automatically redefine your audience. STEP 6: Budget
Set the budget that best suits your business. The more you spend, the better your chances of reaching more people as your ad will be shown more frequently. The result? More site visits and more purchases of products or services. In this step, take note that your campaign is set to run automatically, renewing your subscription on a monthly basis until you cancel. It’s best to let your campaign run for a couple of months so that the smart algorithm has time to get your valuable data and statistics. You can also change your subscription while a campaign is running. Learn More STEP 7: Reviewing Your Ad
Finally, review your ad and make sure it’s ready to launch. Check the budget, audience and creative - you can edit them anytime - and when you’re satisfied, go ahead and launch your campaign.  STEP 8: Your Ad Will Go Live Soon
Once you’ve completed the checkout process, Wix will submit your ad to Facebook for review. This is a relatively quick process and most ads go live within 72 hours. When your ad is live, you’ll be notified immediately. And that’s it. In a few seamless steps, all of which take less than 10 minutes to complete, your campaign can be up and running.How can this campaign help me?Advertising on Facebook is very rewarding with a lower cost per acquisition than any other channel. It’s fast, increases customer attribution, is very targeted, personalized,  and measurable. Plus, Facebook campaigns work on mobile, which means potential customers can see them on any device. But for many businesses who want to use it, setting up, monitoring and optimizing Facebook ad campaigns can be time-consuming and complex. Facebook Ads with Wix takes the hassle of that process by automating every part of it, from ad creation and set up to consistent testing and optimization. With a cost comparatively lower than any other form of online marketing, and a potential audience reach of 3 million people, most businesses find that they cannot afford to keep their brands off Facebook. And with the work done automatically by the Wix AI, the time investment is just as low as the monetary one. Can I set a weekly subscription instead of monthly?Right now, you’re only able to set a monthly subscription for your campaign. The data that the Wix AI gathers to optimize your campaign has to be collected over a period of months, rather than weeks. This is because the algorithm does its best work when data is significant, i.e., when there’s enough of it for the AI to inspect and analyze. The algorithm can then use that data to run unique decision-making models and trend analyses. What are Dynamic Ads?Note: Dynamic ads are only available for campaigns run with Wix Stores.Dynamic ads at first glance, look similar to other ads you may have already seen on Facebook and Instagram. The difference is that rather than displaying just one or some of your online store products at a time, they showcase multiple products within the same template. Using a sophisticated algorithm, these ads automatically understand who to showcase your products to - potential customers who are most likely to buy your products - and which of your items to feature. The algorithm learns from the way your target audience behaves online and then shows them the most relevant products for them. In this way, they’re really effective at driving more traffic to your online store and boosting your sales.Where will my ad appear?Based on your line of business and your visitors’ habits, Wix’s AI algorithm shows your ad to the most relevant potential customers in the most relevant places. The positions and placements in Facebook and Instagram include stories and the main feed.Who will see my ad?The Wix algorithm uses data from your Facebook page, Pixel and campaign to define the right audience for you. In the setup stage of your campaign, you can change the target gender, age range, interests and geographic location. When you’re done, the Wix AI can run tests to redefine your audience, all with the end goal of bringing more paying customers to your site. While your campaign runs, the algorithm will also keep testing your ad with different audiences, including lookalikes (people similar to your current customers), retargets (showing ads to people who have bought from you or interacted with your site) and new audiences who are looking to buy what you sell.How much does it cost to run a Facebook Ad campaign with Wix?Facebook Ads with Wix offers 9 flexible subscription plans starting at $79 (USD). Choose a plan at the monthly subscription that suits your business. As Wix AI learns more about your business, your target audience and gets valuable data from your ad, you’ll get recommendations about how to change your subscription so you get maximum ROAS. Packages are currently available from just $79 to $4999 a month.What percentage/fee does Wix take?The subscription you spend on your ad is broken down into 2 parts. The fee Wix takes is just 15%. This gets you access to the full scope of the Wix AI, from setup to running your campaign, optimization, testing and more. The remaining 85% goes to Facebook to run your ads on their platform.Can I use videos in my ad?You can create video ads if you choose to run classic ads for your campaign. Learn more about the different ad formats as well as image and video best practices for Facebook ads.Are there any limitations to the products I can advertise?The only limitations to what you’re allowed to advertise with Facebook Ads with Wix are those set by Facebook. You can find them here.Can I advertise product categories instead of choosing products?If you're running a campaign with Wix Stores, you can only choose select products you want to show in your ads. This may be available in future. You can vote for it here.Can I change my product images in the ad?If you're running a campaign with WIx Stores it uses products from your online store. This means any product images in your ad, will be the same as those on the product pages of your website. Any time you want to change the images, you should do it from your Wix Store.How long does it take for a new campaign to be reviewed by Facebook and go live?The Facebook review process usually takes around 72 hours. If there is any action to take on your part, we’ll notify you. We’ll also let you know as soon as your campaign goes live.How many campaigns can I run at once?Right now, you can only run 1 Facebook Ads with Wix campaign at a time. If you have multiple online stores or bookings services, and want to run a campaign for each, you’ll need to go through the setup process for each.What is the Meta pixel?The Meta pixel is code that you place on your website. It collects data that helps track and optimize ads, build targeted audiences for future ads, and remarket to people who have already taken some kind of action on your website.I have different products that need to be targeted to different audiences. Can I use 1 campaign to do that?Right now, you can only run 1 campaign per Wix Store or booking service. If you want to advertise products to a very wide target audience, you can still achieve great results because the Wix AI will optimize your campaign - it tests your ad, refines your audience to include new potential customers as well as lookalikes based on who’s bought from you before and retargets existing customers.I want to advertise COVID-19 (coronavirus) related products, but I'm getting an error. What do I do?Currently, it's not possible for any campaigns to run on Facebook if they advertise COVID-19 related products, according to Facebook's advertising policies.This includes products like (but is not limited to):
COVID-19 (coronavirus) testing kits Face masks and face protectors Surgical gloves COVID-19 medication/treatments Anti-coronavirus sanitizers (personal and home-related)Understanding Your Campaign DashboardWhat is ROAS (Return on Ad Spend)?The best way to explain ROAS or return on ad spend is with an example:
If you spent $100 on FB ads and sold $300 worth of products, your ROAS is 300%.  If you spent $100 on FB ads and sold $50 worth of products, your ROAS is 50%.ROAS is not your profit (ROI). This is calculated differently. Using the first example, here’s how to calculate your ROI: If you spent $100 on FB ads and sold $300 worth of products, but made only a $50 profit on each product, your ROI would be calculated as follows:
3 products sold = $150 Your ROAS = 300% Your profit (ROI) = 50%When you use Facebook Ads with Wix, your return on ad spend is automatically calculated for you. Check your campaign dashboard to see how well your campaign is doing, and remember, the Wix AI algorithm is always changing and improving your campaign. This means the results you see show what’s happening in your campaign right now, not what could happen in future. What's the difference between ad clicks and site visits?Ad clicks - as the name implies - is the total number of clicks on your ad. This number includes the same person clicking on your ad multiple times. For example, if Jane sees your ad 3 times and clicks on it 3 times, you have a total of 3 clicks. Site views are counted based on the site visitor's unique digital footprint. They're counted just once per person. So, following from the example above, if Jane visits your site 3 times, it's counted as 1 site visit.What to Do While Your Campaign Is RunningHow often do I need to update my campaign targeting?You should only change your targeting if you want to target different audiences. You don’t need to fine tune your targeting as the Wix AI does it all for you.Can I edit my ad while it’s running?Yes, you can edit your campaign any time - including the ad content, audience and budget. When you set up a new campaign, we recommend giving it 2 months to run before you make any changes, so that Wix’s AI can gather info and learn what works best.Can I pause my campaign and come back to it later?Yes, it is possible to pause your ad campaign. Any remaining ad spend will be saved until the campaign restarts. When you pause, you will be asked whether or not you want to set a resume date. Depending on the monthly subscription, you may have to purchase a new one if your subscription has expired while the campaign is paused. Learn MoreCan I run A/B tests on my ad?You don’t need to run A/B tests on your ad, since Wix’s AI does it for you. It tests your audiences by creating variations of Lookalikes, engagement and remarketing audiences and measures their potential reach and performance, using data from the business’ Facebook Page, pixel and campaign stats.I don’t have time to track campaigns! What do I do?You don’t need to track or optimize your campaign - Wix’s AI does it for you! The AI, which is built on data science principles, effectively runs daily analyses of every change in campaign performance, examines all live data and acts immediately to make the most effective use of the ad spend. It uses this data to run unique decision-making models and trend analyses, which in turn create a variety of potential recommended actions and changes. The system then simulates and estimates the effectiveness of each action, and fine-tunes the campaign based on those results.In-depth Look at the Wix AI AlgorithmAre all products or services sold on FB & Instagram counted as sales by the Wix AI algorithm? No, the algorithm only calculates sales based on products sold by your Facebook Ads with Wix campaign. So if you sold 10 products on Facebook but only 4 were the result of clicks on your Facebook Ads with Wix campaign, only those 4 will be counted. We only count the direct results of FB ads algorithm, nothing else.General QuestionsWhat if my campaign doesn’t perform?It takes time for any Facebook Ads campaign to become profitable. Facebook Ads with Wix consistently monitors the rate of improvement to ensure your campaign does perform, and if it doesn’t, we let you know.As mentioned, campaign success and return on ad spend can take time. We recommend giving the Wix AI at least 2 months to gather data, optimize, test and refine your ad.As long as a campaign continues to run, Wix’s AI has ways of continually improving it to help it reach positive return on ad spend. The smart algorithm will assess the reasons your campaign may not be getting that, and make recommendations of quick and easy fixes, like:
Changing the products displayed in your ad Editing your ad creative Making adjustments to your store or bookings service Redefining your target audienceAt any time, you can also schedule a call with a Wix Expert who can guide you in improving your campaign, and give you advice on how to get more sales.What’s the difference between Facebook Ads and a Facebook Shop?The major difference between Facebook ads and shopping on Facebook is the place you complete the purchase. In the simplest terms, a shop on Facebook is part of the Business Page where shoppers can buy products directly. They can browse a product catalog, see items they want to buy and make payments without leaving the page. Facebook ads work by promoting the products or services you sell through social media, and getting people to your site where they can browse your catalog, add items to their cart and make payment. Right now, Facebook Ads with Wix is the best way to sell your products, because it’s integrated with your site, and all of Wix’s products are available to you, including Email Marketing, abandoned cart automations, secure payment systems and more.If I have a problem, will Wix give me support? Or do I need to contact Facebook?Wix will give you all the support you need to make your Facebook ad work for you. You can contact a Wix Expert anytime to help you fix campaign issues, or give you advice on how to boost sales.Isn’t it better for me to create a Facebook Ad campaign myself?We don’t recommend this option for those with small/medium sized businesses. Creating a campaign on Facebook is something you can do yourself, if you have the knowledge of the platform and the time to continuously monitor and optimize. We know that most business owners - especially those who are already stretched for time - simply don’t have the resources to do it. That’s exactly why the Wix AI was developed, to give you results without a huge investment of time and effort. Our smart engine runs 24/7 on your campaign, creating hundreds of permutations and finding the most effective ones. It refines your audience, runs tests continuously and optimizes based on the data it gets. It’s like having a marketing manager working for you, day and night, doing all of the work so that you have time to focus on your business. Is there a general rule for how long a campaign should be?Avoiding customer fatigue is an important part of advertising on Facebook and Instagram, but with the Wix AI doing all of the monitoring and optimization for you, there’s no need to stop your campaign. What we do recommend is changing your ad creative every 3-4 months. That way, the algorithm has time to learn about your audience, create lookalikes and retarget, and test what works best for you.Will a “marketing in intervals” option be added to FB Ads?There’s no need to market in intervals, because the Wix AI optimizes daily to show your ads to the right audience. If at any time you want to pause your campaign, for example, when you run out of stock, you can do that, and resume your campaign when you’re ready.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: About Bookings Pages
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: About Bookings Pages
Once you add Wix Bookings, certain pages are automatically added to your site. You use these pages to run all aspects of your Booking business; from creating services to managing your schedule each week. You can also customize each of the pages to suit your business and brand. Showcase your services using the Service ListThe service list is where you display the services you offer. Choose whether to display all your services on one page, in different service categories on different pages, or even display a single service on a page.The service list page displays details of your appointments, classes and courses. This includes the service name, price, and duration. Make sure your service list attracts potential clients by customizing the design to suit your business and brand.Share more details about a service using the Service PageService pages provide clients with more in-depth information they need before they book one of your appointments, classes or courses.Decide what information you want to display and how you want to the page to look. Display your service times on the Calendar PageThe Calendar Page is where clients view the availability of your services and select the time slots they want to book. Ensure the information is as clear as possible to make it easy for your clients to book sessions with you.You can customize the design and edit the text for your calendar page in the Editor. Get details you need from clients with the Booking FormThe Booking Form is where clients fill out the information you require before they can book your services.You can customize this form and add extra fields or create different booking forms for different services. This allows you to collect the information you need to provide the best service possible for your clients.You can also personalize the design of the Booking Form to match your site's design. Offer different payment options on the Checkout PageThe Checkout Page is where clients choose how they want to pay for the services (if you enable more than one option) and where they provide their payment details.You can edit the Checkout Page settings in the dashboard. Important:The checkout page only displays for paid services. If your service is free, your clients go straight to the Thank You page from the Booking Form. However, if you have any coupons on your site, clients go to the Checkout page, even for free services or services with offline payments. This is to ensure that clients complete their booking through the Checkout page to enter any available coupons.Allow clients to review orders with the Thank You PageThe Thank You Page is where clients review their order after they complete a booking.You can edit the text and design of the Thank You Page in the Editor. Important:We're in the process of releasing a new version of the Thank You Page (Confirmation page). If your Thank You Page does not look like the one in the image above, click here.

source_documents.title: Changing the Currency in Your Invoice for Wix Services
source_documents.content:
Changing the Currency in Your Invoice for Wix Services
If you move to a new country, any Wix services that you have set to auto-renew will continue to be charged in your previous currency.While there is no direct way to switch currencies, you can use the workarounds in this article to start getting billed in your new location's currency.In this article, learn how to change the currency used to pay for your:
Premium plan Domain Business email Apps Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Changing the currency used to pay for your Premium planYou can perform the following workaround to change the currency used to pay for your Premium plan. The process involves duplicating your site, moving the existing Premium plan there, and in the meantime, upgrading the original site from the new location.Tip:There are a number of steps involved, so it is a good idea to keep this article open as you follow the instructions.To change the currency used to pay for your Premium plan:
Cancel the Premium plan that you want to change:
    
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the plan associated with the relevant site. Click Cancel plan. Click Cancel Now.   Duplicate the site that the plan is assigned to:
    
Go to the dashboard of the site. Click the More Actions icon  and click Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site. Click Duplicate.    Reassign the canceled Premium plan to the duplicate site:
    
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant plan. Click Assign to a Different Site and choose the duplicated site. Click Next. Click Assign.   Upgrade the original site from your new location:
    
Go to the dashboard of the original site. Click Upgrade on the left. Click Select under the Premium plan you want to purchase. Follow the steps to complete the purchase.   Assign your domain back to your original site:
    
Go to Domains ﻿in your Wix account.
Note: If you have more than one domain in your account, select the domain you want to reassign. Scroll down to the Unassigned Domains section. Click the More Actions icon . Click Assign to a Site. Choose a site from the options if there is more than one, then click Next. Click Assign.  Changing the currency used to pay for your domainIn order to update the currency used on your invoice for a domain payment, you need to extend your domain subscription from your new geolocation.To change the currency used to pay for your domain:
Go to Domains ﻿in your Wix account. 
Note: If you have more than one domain in your account, select the domain that was transferred. Click Extend.
Select the registration period. Click Continue. Enter (or edit) your contact information. Click Continue. Select a privacy option: 
    
Private Registration: Your contact details won't appear in the WHOIS domain information records. You can turn the privacy protection option on and off whenever you want. This option carries a small additional fee. Public Registration: Your information always remains public in the WHOIS domain information records. You can only change it to private when manually extending the domain registration.   Click Continue. Select your payment method. Click Submit Purchase.Changing the currency used to pay for your business emailTo change the currency used to pay for your business email subscription, you need to cancel it (i.e. turn off auto-renew), then repurchase from your new location after your current subscription ends.Important:You can only change the currency used to pay for your business email at the end of your subscription period. This means that even if you cancel right now, you must wait for your business email subscription to end before repurchasing.To change the currency used to pay for your business email:
Turn off auto-renewal for your Business email: 
    
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant business email. Click Cancel Business Email. Select the I still want to cancel checkbox. Click Cancel Business Email. This turns off auto-renewal.   (After your subscription ends) Repurchase the business email from your new location:
    
Go to Business Email in your Wix account. Click Get a Business Email next to the relevant domain. (Optional) Click the Add icon + to purchase additional mailboxes. Enter your email prefix(es). Click Continue. Choose which Google Workspace plan you want from the options listed. Choose a business email subscription: Monthly or Yearly. Click Get it. Enter your credit card information. Click Submit Purchase.  Changing the currency used to pay for your AppsTo change the currency used to pay for your App subscriptions, cancel them (i.e. turn off auto-renew) and repurchase from your new location after your subscription ends.Important:You can only change the currency used to pay for your App at the end of the subscription period. This means that even if you cancel right now, you must wait for your subscription to end before repurchasing.To change the currency used to pay for your App subscriptions:
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account.
    
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant app. Click Cancel App. Select Cancel auto renew and click Submit.   (After your subscription ends) Upgrade the App from your new location, in your Editor or your site's dashboard:Upgrade the app from your Editor
Go to the Wix App Market in your Editor:
    
Wix Editor: Click Add Apps  on the left side of the Editor. Editor X: Click App Market  at the top of Editor X.   Select App Market and search for the app. Click Open. Click the Upgrade icon  or select Settings and click Upgrade.
 Select your payment plan. Click Upgrade Now. Enter your payment information. Click Submit Purchase.Upgrade the app from your site's dashboard
Go to Manage Apps in your site's dashboard. Click Upgrade next to the relevant app. Enter your payment information. Click Submit Purchase.FAQsWe are here to help with all your questions. Click a question below to learn more.How does the workaround for changing my currency work?The workaround involves repurchasing (Premium plans, Business emails) or extending (domains) the subscription from your new location. Can Wix change the currency on my past invoices?No, Wix cannot retroactively change an invoice's currency. Any existing invoice's currency cannot be changed. I followed your instructions but I am being billed in USD. Why hasn't my currency updated to match my current location?Some currencies are not supported for payment of Wix services. If your local currency is not available, you'll be charged in US Dollar (USD).

source_documents.title: Connecting a Norwegian (.no) Domain to Your Wix Site
source_documents.content:
Connecting a Norwegian (.no) Domain to Your Wix Site
Once you've upgraded your site, you can connect a .no domain you already own to your Wix site.In most cases, we recommend connecting your domain to Wix via nameservers. With this connection method, Wix hosts your DNS records, which means you can manage them in your Wix account. This way, if you ever need assistance managing your DNS records, Wix Customer Care can help you.Keep the following in mind when you’re preparing to connect your domain:
You will need access to your current domain registrar. New DNS records may take up to 48hrs to fully propagate.Learn how to connect a Domain to the Wix nameservers.Currently, it is not possible to purchase a .no domain from Wix or transfer one to Wix. If this is a feature you would like to see in the future, please Vote for this feature and we'll make sure to keep you updated.

source_documents.title: Connecting SumUp as a Payment Provider
source_documents.content:
Connecting SumUp as a Payment Provider
Connect SumUp as a payment provider to accept credit and debit card payments from your customers. Using SumUp you can accept payments online, or in-person using a POS card reader. 
From March, 2024 an improved SumUp experience for online payments is available to connect. This includes new features, like the ability to issue refunds directly from your Wix dashboard. For existing SumUp users, you can connect the new SumUp integration to join the new experience for online payments. Please note that in-person (POS) payments are not supported with the new experience, so if you wish to continue using your SumUp card reader, keep your current POS connection enabled. General InfoSupported countriesAustria, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Cyprus, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Switzerland and United KingdomSupported payment methodsCredit / debit cards and POS.
Additional payment methods are available in selected locations: iDEAL (Netherlands), Bancontact (Belgium), Boleto (Brazil), P24 (Poland) and EPS (Austria)Accepted currenciesEUR, GBP, CHF, PLN, NOK, BGN, BRLNote: The currency used in your Wix account must match the currency used in your SumUp account. If the currencies do not match, the transactions may be declined. Learn how to change your currencyTransaction feesVary by locationOnline payments from 1.95% per transaction
Card reader transactions from 0.9% per transactionManaging your accountFor information on topics such as payout schedules, refunding a customer, chargeback disputes, and more, visit SumUpIn this article, learn about:
Connecting SumUp for online payments Connecting SumUp for POS Managing SumUp Connecting new SumUp for existing users (online payments) Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Connecting SumUp
Go Accept Payments on your site's dashboard.
Tip: Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it. Click See More Payment Options. Click See Options next to Third-Party Credit / Debit Card Providers. Click Connect next to SumUp.
Depending on whether you are creating a new SumUp account or have an existing one, follow the instructions:Have an account
Enter your API Key. Click Connect.Don't have an account
Click Create SumUp account. Follow the steps to create an account. Return to this window (repeat steps 1-5), and follow the steps under Have an account to connect your SumUp account.Connecting SumUp for POS
Go Accept Payments on your site's dashboard. 
Tip: Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it. Click See More Payment Options. Click See Options next to Point of Sale.
Click Connect next to SumUp. Depending on whether you are creating a new SumUp account or have an existing one, follow the instructions:Have an account
Click Connect.Don't have an account
Click Create SumUp account. Follow the steps to create an account. Return to this window (repeat steps 1-5), and follow the steps under Have an account to connect your SumUp account.Managing SumUp payment methods
Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard. Click Manage next to SumUp. Use the toggles to enable or disable your SumUp payment methods, such as POS payments. Connecting new SumUp experience for existing users
Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard.  Click See More Payment Options. Click See Options next to Third-Party Credit / Debit Card Providers. Click Connect next to SumUp.
Tip: For POS users, make sure the POS payments toggle is enabled in your existing SumUp connection before you switch. Learn how to manage your SumUp payment methods.  Click Yes, Switch in the pop-up. 
Enter your API Key. Click Connect.
Note: For POS users, you'll now have 2 active payment options in your Accept Payments page: 1 for online card payments and 1 for POS payments.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about accepting payments.How can I use SumUp for in-person (POS) payments?With SumUp, you can sell your products from home, at a festival, or anywhere else you choose.
 With SumUp, you can:
Set up a point of sale with SumUp:
    
Selling store products at a POS. Charging clients at a POS (non-Stores).   Obtain a credit card reader that connects, via Bluetooth, to your mobile device. If you have more than one store location, you can choose which location to view when you manage your SumUp account.How can I tell if a payment method is active?In order to accept online payments, you must connect a payment provider. Once connected, your checkout will be active for your chosen payment method(s).

You need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.Is my currency supported?Be aware that payments will fail If you are using an unsupported currency.
The currency used in your payment provider account must match the currency that you set in your Wix account. If you need to change the currency set in your provider account, please contact your payment provider.If your current payment provider does not support your desired currency, Wix hosts a wide range of alternative payment providers. Learn how to change your payment provider.What is a minimum payment amount?Some payment providers have a minimum payment threshold (e.g. $1.01). Payments below this amount will not be processed.Make sure that all of your products or services are priced over the minimum threshold. This includes discounted items or Pricing Plans. Please contact your payment provider to get the most up-to-date information about their minimum payment threshold. Can I offer recurring payments?To offer recurring payments, you must connect a payment provider that supports recurring payments.How do I get my payouts? Payouts are managed by your payment provider. If your provider is a third-party provider, contact them directly. 
If your provider is Wix Payments, learn about receiving payouts from Wix Payments. My customers' payments are being declined. What can I do?If your customers are experiencing payment failures, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting issues for accepting payments.Why can’t I connect my desired payment provider?If you’re having trouble connecting your payment provider, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting common connection issues.Do I need to upgrade my site to accept payments?Yes. You need to upgrade your site to a plan that supports payments in order to accept payments.

source_documents.title: Online Programs: Managing Coupons
source_documents.content:
Online Programs: Managing Coupons
Promote your program sign-ups with coupons. Offer discounts to encourage people to join your paid programs. You can choose to make your coupons apply to all programs or target specific ones to create a focused offer. Before you begin:Make sure to add Online Programs to your site. In this article, learn more about:
Managing coupons Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Managing couponsWix Online Programs offers two types of coupon options to help you promote and reward participants. The first is a fixed monetary discount, such as a $5 discount, which is ideal for attracting new customers. The second is a percentage discount, like 20% off, which is perfect for rewarding existing participants. For both types of coupons, you can set an expiration date and limit usage to one coupon per customer. Additionally, you can control the total number of times each coupon can be used, ensuring you have full control over your promotions.DashboardWix app
Go to Coupons in your site's dashboard. Choose what you want to do next:Create a coupon
Click + New Coupon.  Select the type of coupon you want to offer:
    
$ Discount: Offer a fixed monetary discount amount. % Discount: Offer a percentage discount.   Enter the Coupon code participants need to use the coupon.  Enter the Coupon name for your own records.  Enter the Discount you want to offer. Select the relevant programs from the Apply to drop-down:
    
All Programs: Participants can use the discount for all programs. Specific Program: The discount is available for the programs you choose. Select the relevant program from the Program drop-down.   Select the dates the coupon is valid between.  (Optional) Select the Limit uses checkbox(s) to:
    
 Limit the total number of uses for this coupon: Set the number of times the coupon can be used.  Limit to one use per customer: The same participant can't use the coupon more than once.   Click Create Coupon. Duplicate a couponIf you want to create a new coupon with settings that are similar to a coupon you already have, you can save time by duplicating it and then making changes.
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant coupon. Select Duplicate. Edit the coupon and click Create Coupon.Activate, deactivate or delete a couponYou can deactivate a coupon when you no longer want to offer a particular promotion and then activate it again when the time is right. If you won't need it in the future, you can delete it. 
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant coupon. Select an option:
    
Deactivate / Activate: Select Deactivate so customers can't use it or Activate to make it available. Delete: Select Delete and then click Yes, Delete to confirm.  Tip: By default, the coupon section displays only your active coupons. Tap the drop-down to view coupons with other statuses.Edit a coupon
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant coupon. Select Edit. Change the relevant information. Click Save.Copy coupon code
Hover on the relevant coupon. Click the Copy coupon code icon  to copy the code to your clipboard. 
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Marketing Home Tap Coupons.
Choose what you want to do:Create a $ Discount coupon (e.g. $10 off)
Tap Add a Coupon. Tap $ Discount. Enter the amount that will be taken off the price and tap Next. Enter the coupon code.
Note: This is the code customers enter. Enter the name of the coupon.
Note: Appears in the cart page and dashboard. Tap Next.  Choose which programs the coupon applies to:
    
All programs: Apply the coupon to any program in your store. Specific programs: Limit the coupon to a specific programs only. Tap the relevant program.   Set the coupon's start and end date:
    
Tap the date. Select the start date from the calendar. Enter the end date or tap No end date. Tap Save.   (Optional) Apply limits to the number of times the coupon can be used:
    
Limit number of total uses:

Tap the Limit number of total uses toggle to enable it. Enter the number of times the coupon can be used.   One use per customer: Tap the toggle to enable it.   Tap Done. (Optional) Tap Share to share your new coupon.Create a % Discount coupon (e.g. 10% off)
Tap Add a Coupon. Tap % Discount. Enter the coupon code.
Note: This is the code customers enter. Enter the name of the coupon.
Note: Appears in the cart page and dashboard. Tap Next.  Choose which programs the coupon applies to:
    
All programs: Apply the coupon to any program in your store. Specific programs: Limit the coupon to a specific programs only. Tap the relevant program.   Set the coupon's start and end date:
    
Tap the date. Select the start date from the calendar. Enter the end date or tap No end date. Tap Save.   (Optional) Apply limits to the number of times the coupon can be used:
    
Limit number of total uses:

Tap the Limit number of total uses toggle to enable it. Enter the number of times the coupon can be used.   One use per customer: Tap the toggle to enable it.   Tap Done. (Optional) Tap Share to share your new coupon.Duplicate a couponIf you want to create a new coupon with settings that are similar to a coupon you already have, you can save time by duplicating it and then making changes.
Tap the relevant coupon. Tap the More Actions icon . Tap Duplicate. Edit the coupon and tap Done.Activate, deactivate or delete a couponYou can deactivate a coupon when you no longer want to offer a particular promotion and then activate it again when the time is right. If you won't need it in the future, you can delete it. 
Tap the relevant coupon. Tap the More Actions icon . Select an option:
    
Deactivate / Activate: Tap Deactivate so customers can't use it or Activate to make it available. Delete: Tap Delete and then tap OK to confirm.  Tip: By default, the coupon section displays only your active coupons. Tap the drop-down to view coupons with other statuses.Edit a coupon
Tap the relevant coupon. Change the relevant information. Tap Save.Copy coupon code
Tap the relevant coupon. Tap Copy Code next to Coupon Code.FAQsClick a question below to learn more. Can I create coupons for other products?Yes. You can create coupons for:
Wix Bookings Wix Events Pricing Plans Wix Restaurants Wix StoresCan I use coupons if my site only accepts cash? Yes. You can apply coupons to services purchased with the Manual payment method. Make sure to mark the service as paid to update the number of coupons remaining.Can customers apply coupons to free programs?No. Customers cannot apply coupons to free programs. How do customers use the coupon? Customers can enter a coupon code on checkout in the Enter a coupon code field. Do coupons work for programs paid using pricing plans? No. Customers can't use coupons for programs set up to be paid with pricing plans only.Can I create a bulk of personal coupons?No. The Bulk Coupon Creator app is not available for Wix Online Programs.How can I promote my coupon?Use the Promote link to easily create an email marketing campaign or social post for any of your coupons.To promote your coupon:
Go to Coupons in your site's dashboard. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant coupon. Select Promote.

 Select a promotion option:
    
Send a social post.  Send an email marketing campaign.  Are coupon codes case sensitive?No, coupon codes are not case sensitive. Customers can enter your codes in capital or lowercase letters.  What happens if the discount is more than the program price?Make sure you aren't giving away program for free. Apply the price discount coupon only to program that cost more than the value of the discount. For example, if you create a $10 price discount coupon and a customer applies it to an $8 program, that item will be free.

source_documents.title: Renting Apartments Using Wix Hotels
source_documents.content:
Renting Apartments Using Wix Hotels
Important:This article refers to the original Wix Hotels. If you are using the new Wix Hotels by HotelRunner, which is not yet available to all users, please read the information here. Learn how to check which version of Wix Hotels you are using. Wix Hotels is an all-in-one booking system, allowing you to rent and manage any type of vacation rental, including apartments. There are just a few small adjustments you'll need to make and you're ready to go.Step 1 | Add Wix HotelsWe have some stunning apartment templates for you to choose from. These already come with Wix Hotels installed, but you're welcome to use any template and add Wix Hotels to it.Show me howClick the App Market icon on the left side of the Editor.Type "Wix Hotels" in the search bar and select Wix Hotels from the drop-down menu.Click Add to Site.Click OK.Step 2 | Set Up Your ApartmentLet's start by choosing your property type and adding your apartment. If you have more than one apartment, you can always go back and add more. Click Manage on the Wix Hotels app in the Editor at any time to access the Hotels dashboard. Now, follow the prompts to add your first apartment, enter your property settings and set up payments. For detailed information, follow the steps here.Step 3 | Customize the Wix Hotels App in the EditorThe default settings of the Wix Hotels app are customized for renting hotel rooms. In order to set up the Wix Hotels app for apartment rentals, you'll need to make a few tweaks to the app's display settings. Click Settings on the Wix Hotels app in the Editor and customize it to suit your needs. Show me howIn the Wix Hotels Settings, you can customize your Rooms list, text and design. We'll give you some suggestions on how to edit these settings for renting an apartment. Click the tabs and make the changes below:Rooms list: This is the main list of all the apartments you're renting. If you only have a single apartment, you can select the Single layout.Text: Since a lot of the text refers to "rooms" and "hotels", you can go ahead and edit this text accordingly. Click the drop-down to select a page and make the following changes:Rooms List Page: Edit the title of the Rooms list (by default it says "Our Rooms").Booking Form: Edit the button text and summary labels ("Reserve Your Room" and "Room Type").Confirmation Page: Edit the title ("Your Room is Booked!) and Hotel Details field.Tip: You can edit any text you want, not just the suggestions above.Step 4 | Change the Hotel Page NameIf you are not using a template created specially for apartment rentals, the name of the Hotel page  (and therefore the menu tab) might be "Rooms & Rates" or "Book a Room".  You can easily edit the page/menu name to suit your needs.Show me howClick the Pages drop-down menu at the top left of the Editor. Click the Show More icon next to the page containing the Wix Hotels app (e.g. "Rooms & Rates" or "Book a Room").Click Rename.Enter the name you want to use and click Done.

source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Adding Tables and Polls to a Blog Post
Enhance your Wix Blog posts by adding tables and polls. Tables help you organize information clearly, making it easier for readers to digest complex data. Polls engage your audience by inviting them to share their opinions, increasing interaction on your site.In this article, learn more about:
Adding a poll to a blog post Adding a table to a blog postAdding a poll to a blog postYou can create a poll for your post in the Blog section of your site's dashboard or from the Wix app.To add a poll to a blog postDashboardWix App
Go to Blog in your site's dashboard. Select the post that you want to add media to. Click the Add icon  beside the section where you want to add the poll. Select Poll under Elements. Select the type of poll that you want to create:
    
Text in a list: Creates a poll with a question and a list of clickable answers. Text & main image: Creates a poll with a question, an image, and a list of clickable answers. Images in a grid: Creates a poll with a question and a list of clickable images with answers written on them.   Enter your poll question and the answers that you want your readers to choose from. (Optional) Customize the layout, design, and settings of your poll.Layout
Click Layout. Customize your layout using the options:
    
Question: Enable the toggle to add a main image to your poll. Answers: Select a List or Grid layout for your answers.
 Add an image to each answer: Enable the toggle to add an image to each answer. Poll Direction: Select a left-to-right or right-to-left direction for your poll.   Click Save.Design
Click Design.  Customize the design using the options:
    
Choose a background style: Select a color, gradient, or image background for your poll. Corner Radius: Adjust how rounded the edges of your poll and answers.
   Click Save.Settings
Click Settings. Customize the settings using the options: 
    
Voting: Select who can vote on the poll. You can choose to let everyone reader vote, or let only site members vote.   People can pick multiple answers: Enable the toggle if you want to let people vote more than once.  Results: Select who can see the results of the poll. You can choose to let everyone see the results, let only site members see the results, or make the results only visible to you. Show vote count: Enable the toggle to display the number of votes that visitors have submitted. Show who voted: Enable the toggle to display the names of the site members who voted on the poll.   Click Save.8.  Click Publish.
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Blog under Content & Community. Tap Posts. Select the post that you want to add a poll to. Tap the Add icon  at the bottom.  Tap Poll. Select the type of poll that you want to create:
    
Text in a list: Creates a poll with a question and a list of clickable answers. Text & main image: Creates a poll with a question, an image, and a list of clickable answers. Images in a grid: Creates a poll with a question and a list of clickable images with answers written on them.   Enter your poll question and the answers that you want your readers to choose from. (Optional) Customize the layout and design of your poll.Layout
Tap Layout. Customize your layout using the options: 
    
Add an image to the question: Enable the toggle to add a main image to your poll. Answers: Select a layout: List or Grid. Add an image to each answer: Enable the toggle to add an image to each answer. Poll Direction: Select a left-to-right or right-to-left direction for your poll.   Tap Done.Design
Tap Design.  Select a color or image background for your poll under Choose a background style. Tap Done.11. Tap Create. 12. Tap the Settings icon  to customize the settings of your poll. 
People can pick multiple answers: Enable the toggle if you want to let people vote more than once.  Results: Select who can see the results of the poll. You can choose to let everyone see the results, let only site members see the results, or make the results only visible to you. Show the vote count: Enable the toggle to display the number of votes that visitors have submitted. Show who voted: Enable the toggle to display the names of the site members who voted on the poll.13. Click Save.14. Tap Next.15. Tap Save and publish.Adding a table to a blog postAdd a table to blog posts to help provide more structure to your content, especially if the post has a lot of important information. To add a table:
Go to Blog in your site's dashboard. ﻿Click Edit on the relevant blog post, or Create New Post to write a new one. ﻿Click Add   on the left side. Click Table.  Type the number of columns and rows you want in your table.  Click Create table.  Add the relevant content to each section of the table.  Customize the look of the table and the text:
    
Click Text style to customize the text that appears in the table.  Click the Vertical alignment icon  to choose how you want the text to align.  Click the Background color icon  to change the background color of the table. Click the Border color icon  to change the color of the table border.  Click the Show More icon  to select a specific row or column. 
        
Click the Show More icon  to add or remove rows and columns in the table.      Click Publish.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Understanding Availability for Appointments
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Understanding Availability for Appointments
Understanding what affects your availability for appointments is important for keeping your business running smoothly. Wix Bookings uses your settings and schedules, including existing bookings, to continuously calculate all the available time slots. Since several factors can determine when your clients can book an appointment, it's important to make sure you configure your availability correctly.By recognizing these factors and setting up your availability, your live site can accurately show your business's available appointment times. If you're having trouble setting appointment availability as needed, you can check out the troubleshooting steps that help resolve most issues.What factors affect appointment availabilityHere is a list of the main factors which affect if you or your staff are available to accept appointments. Default business hoursYour default business hours, or your opening hours, determine when your staff are available to take appointments. Once you set your default business hours, you can then customize your staff members' working hours to offer services outside your normal business hours (see below). Learn more about adding your business information, including your default business hours. Staff working hoursThe availability of appointments largely depends on the working hours of your selected staff members. When you create an appointment, you decide who provides the service. Staff hours are based on your default business hours. You can also customize each staff member's hours individually.

Customers can't book an appointment that ends after the relevant staff members' hours. So, for example, if you work until 6:00 PM, and offer a two-hour-long service, clients can't book it at 5:00 PM.

Learn how to set a staff member's available hours.Adding one-time changes to staff hoursYou can set custom hours for your staff, either as one-time or recurring appointments from your Work Schedule dashboard. These custom hours override the default ones and can affect availability, especially if multiple staff members have custom schedules. Making one-time changes can help accommodate your staff's schedules while making sure your business is not affected.Learn more about editing your staff members' working hours.Default work hoursYour default work hours determine the available hours during which clients can book appointments. Make sure to update your default hours so clients know when they can book their appointments. These hours automatically apply to all new staff members.Learn more about setting your default work hours. Blocked timeYou can manually block any day or part of a day in your Wix Bookings calendar for you or for a staff member. The times you block are not available for bookings. This feature is useful for scheduling holiday, personal time off or any other periods you or your staff are unavailable.

Learn how to block time on your calendar.Synced calendarsTo avoid conflicts and double bookings, you and your staff members can sync your personal calendars with the Wix Bookings calendar. Events synced from these personal calendars block off the time on the Wix calendar, preventing clients from booking during these periods. Syncing your calendars helps manage availability and prevents any double bookings from outside commitments.
We recommend you read the important information on how synced calendars work. Appointment time slotsAppointment time slots control how often available hours appear on your calendar. You can set them at specific intervals or based on the duration of a service, plus any time buffers you add between appointments. For example, if you set a time interval at 30 minutes with a 15 minutes time buffer, clients see appointments listed every 45 minutes on your live site (see image below). 
Time intervals allow you to effectively manage your schedule. You can decide if you want all appointments to have the same time interval on the calendar or if the interval should be based on the service duration plus an additional buffer time.
Learn how to set your time slot durations.Time bufferSet a time buffer between sessions to make sure client sessions aren't booked back-to-back, to allow staff to prepare, and to provide necessary breaks. Time buffers also help manage the appointment flow.

For example, if you provide a 1-hour service, you can add a 15 min buffer so if a client books from 9:00 - 10:00, the next available slot will be from 10:15 - 11:15.

Learn how to set a time buffer between sessions.Your booking windowsBooking windows let you set limits on exactly how far in advance and how close to your sessions clients can book. For example, you can prevent clients from booking too far in advance (e.g. more than 2 months before the session). You can also prevent clients from booking last minute (e.g. less than 3 hours before the session starts). Setting these windows helps manage expectations and ensures your schedule stays manageable and predictable.
Learn how to set your booking window.Troubleshooting availability issuesClick an issue below to learn how to resolve it. There are no available time slots on my Calendar page on my live site.If no available time slots appear for one of your services on your site, check to make sure the following:
The service duration does not exceed the staff member's working hours or your default working hours. For example, if a staff member's shift is only 4 hours long and they offer a 6-hour event planning service, clients can't book that service with this staff member. The staff member's location matches the service location. There are no other events in the calendar blocking the availability. These events could be work-related or personal events that the staff member has blocked off in their synced personal .My available time slots are not showing properly.You choose how to display your appointment slots to clients, either based on the service duration or using fixed intervals. You can also add a time buffer between appointments, so your staff have enough preparation time for the next client. 
Offering time slots based on service duration can result in irregular time slots but maximizes the number of bookings you can take in a day.  Offering time slots based on fixed intervals (e.g. every 15 minutes) makes appointments appear more orderly on the calendar but may reduce the total number of bookings you can accomodate in a day. Service duration example:You offer a service lasting 30 minutes with a 10-minute buffer starting from 9:00AM, your available appear as follows: 09:00, 09:40, 10:20... etc. Fixed interval example:You offer a service lasting 30 minutes with a 10-minute buffer, but clients can only book at fixed 30-minute intervals, the available slots would be: 10:00, 10:30, 11:00... etc. In this case, if a client books the available slot at 10:30, the slots at 10:00 and 11:00 won't be bookable with the same staff member due to the session duration and buffer time.My staff member does not appear as available for a specific time slot in the Calendar page.If your staff member does not appear as available for a specific time slot, check if:
The staff member was assigned to that service when you created it. The staff member's working hours are set up incorrectly. The staff member already has a class/course session assigned for that specific time. You offer the appointment in a custom location, and the staff member's availability has not been set up to "All locations".  You made one-time changes to the staff member's availability.
Tip: Manually schedule an appointment and test how it appears on your Booking calendar. Check how soon before and after the appointment you can add another appointment at the same location with the same staff member. You can then delete the test appointment.My staff member has more availability than is displayed, or some time slots are missing for a specific staff member.Check your booking window in Booking Policies for the affected service. Double-check that the staff member's working hours are set up correctly. Also, check if:
The staff member was assigned to that service when you created it. The staff member's working hours are set up incorrectly. The staff member already has a class/course session assigned for that specific time. You offer the appointment in a custom location, and the staff member's availability has not been set up to "All locations".  You made one-time changes to the staff member's availability.My service is not available in a specific location.Make sure the selected staff member's availability is correctly set for the specific location.Adjust the location settings as necessary to reflect the staff member's availability.When clients try to book a session, there's a message saying that "Bookings will open X days before the session starts".Check your booking window in Booking Policies for the affected service. Adjust these settings to align with your preferred booking timeline.Still need help?If the problem persists, contact us, and we will be happy to help.

Wix Bookings: Viewing Your Upcoming Sessions in the Wix App
View your upcoming sessions directly on the Wix App. This helps you stay organized and manage your schedule on the go. For instance, if you run a yoga studio, you can quickly check your class time or see who has signed up, making it easier to prepare and give the best experience to your clients.You can add advanced filters to easily find a session based on the staff member, location, service, or other events on your calendar. You can also manage your pending appointments through your booking calendar.In this article, learn more about:
Viewing your booking calendar in the Wix app Viewing and managing pending appointments in your Wix appViewing the booking calendar in the Wix appAccess your booking calendar in the Wix app to view and manage your sessions. Choose from different views based on your preference, and filter them to quickly find and manage sessions. You can tap any booking to see details like the participant list, time, and date.To view the booking calendar in the Wix appWix appWix Studio app
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Booking Calendar. Tap Calendar.  Tap the Change View icon  at the top right. Choose your Calendar Settings:Calendar viewTap to select your preferred view:

This is a convenient way to book clients in for their next session Day view: See all upcoming sessions for a specific day, including empty time slots. This is useful for scheduling clients or creating new services. 3 day: View sessions over a 3-day period. This is great for scheduling new bookings, especially during busy periods.Advanced filtersTap the filter(s) you want to apply to your calendar:
Note: If you leave the Bookings area, your calendar filters won't be saved.
Staff: Tap the checkbox next to the relevant staff member(s) you want to display, then tap Select.  Location: Tap a location: All locations, Business locations, Custom location, or Client's place, then tap Select.
Note: If you have multiple Business locations, tap the checkbox next to the relevant location(s). Services: If relevant, tap the category and then tap the services you want to filter. Tap Select.
Tip: Tap the All checkbox next to a category to add an entire category. Other events: Tap the checkbox next to the event you want to display: From synced calendar or Blocked time.7. Tap Apply/Clear Filters.
Go to your site in the Wix Studio app. Tap Manage. Tap Booking Calendar. Tap the Change View icon  at the top right. Choose your Calendar Settings:Calendar viewTap to select your view:
Schedule: See all upcoming sessions in order, regardless of time in between them (e.g. sessions on Friday and Monday will appear next to each other if your business is closed on weekends). This is a convenient way to book clients in for their next session Day view: See all upcoming sessions for a specific day, including empty time slots. This is useful for scheduling clients or creating new services. 3 day: View sessions over a 3-day period. This is great for scheduling new bookings, especially during busy periods.Advanced filtersTap the filter(s) you want to apply to your calendar:

Staff: Tap the checkbox next to the relevant staff member(s) you want to display, then tap Select.  Location: Tap a location: All locations, Business locations, Custom location, or Client's place, then tap Select. Note: If you have multiple Business locations, tap the checkbox next to the relevant location(s). Services: If relevant, tap the category and then tap the services you want to filter. Tap Select. Tip: Tap the All checkbox next to a category to add an entire category. Other events: Tap the checkbox next to the event you want to display: From synced calendar or Blocked time.6. Tap Apply/Clear Filters.Viewing and managing pending appointments in your Wix appFor appointments where you enable manual approval, you can manage booking requests directly in the Wix app. A notification appears at the bottom of your booking calendar when a new request comes in. You can tap this notification to approve, decline, or reschedule the requests.Wix appWix Studio app
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Booking Calendar.  Tap Calendar. Tap View on the appointment request notification at the bottom of your screen.   Tap the relevant appointment request. Choose what you want to do:
    
Approve the appointment: Tap Approve to add the appointment to your calendar. Decline the appointment: Tap Decline. If you want to send your client an email, tap the Notify client with an email checkbox to select it. Then tap Decline to confirm. Reschedule the appointment: Tap Reschedule to move the appointment to a different time. Edit the session details and then tap Save.
Tip: Make sure to let your clients know of any schedule changes.

source_documents.title: Wix Groups: About Your Groups Pages
source_documents.content:
Wix Groups: About Your Groups Pages
When adding Wix Groups to your site, you'll find 3 new customizable pages in the editor:
Group Page: Each group has its own dedicated page. Groups: Lists all available groups for visitors to browse and join. Members Area: Site members can customize their profile, connect with others, and manage notifications.In this article, learn about each of these areas and how you can make them your own. The Group PageEach group you create has its own dedicated page, featuring a discussion tab for posts and media, as well as a members tab. You can choose to display member names on profile photos to enhance connections among group members.Customize this page with design adjustments and integrate features like emoji reactions and member badges, promoting community recognition and participation.Tip:Each group page features various tabs such as "About" and "Media." You can create custom tabs, rename existing ones, and link specific events to the group.Groups (Group list)The Groups page displays all the groups on your site and features a feed where members of each group can post updates, share content, and interact within their specific group's context.You can customize this page (e.g. 'News Feed', 'Latest Updates') to match your site's theme with colors and fonts. Organize groups by activity or member count, and add features like a share button to boost member interactions.Create group posts:
You can offer exclusive posts with your content, accessible only to paying members. Categorize posts with topics, monetize exclusive content with a pricing plan, and delete irrelevant posts at any time.The Members AreaWhen you add Wix Groups to your site, a Members Area is also included. This allows group members to have their own accounts, where they can manage personal information and connect with others through their profiles.The Members Area also gives people access to exclusive pages and benefits, such as Wix Events, Wix Bookings, and other Wix apps.FAQsClick a question below to find out more information. How can I organize group content to help members easily find posts of interest?You can use topics to organize posts and help members easily filter and find conversations that interest them.
Can I display my Groups Feed on other pages of my site?Yes. The Groups List Add-On allows you to add a list of your groups to any page of your site, making it easy for visitors to view and join your groups.For example, you can add your groups list to your home page so it's the first thing people see when they visit your site. You can also display your active groups as cards or in a feed for everyone to see.Can members create groups?Yes. You can allow your members to create their own groups straight from the relevant members app. How can I manage notifications for group activities?You and your members can adjust the relevant notification settings to receive updates on posts, comments, reactions, and new member additions,How do I automatically add site visitors to my group?When new people join your site, you can set up an automation that adds them to your group automatically.
