source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Using Containers
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Using Containers
Containers are responsive layout tools that help you streamline and structure site content. You can customize them to complement the site's design, and attach elements such as text, media, and buttons.In this article, learn more about:
Adding containers to a site Designing containers Attaching elements to containers Applying grids to containersAdding containers to a siteGet started by adding a container to suit the client's design and content needs. You can choose from a range of pre-designed and hover containers, or start from scratch with a blank design.To add a container:
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Select Containers. Choose a container style (Empty, Designed, or Hover). Click and drag your chosen container to add it to the page.Designing containersCustomize the container's design to complement the site's aesthetic. You can change the background color, set the radius, and more.To design a container:
Select the relevant container. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Choose how you want to customize the container under Design:
    
Background: Set the background and make it more or less visible:
        
Color: Select from the site's theme colors, or your own custom shade. Gradient: Apply a gradient or linear gradient to the container. You can choose the colors, angles, and more.   Glass effect: Apply a frosted glass effect to the container and set the intensity of the blur. Border: Add a border to the container and use the options to set its size, color, and opacity. Corners: Adjust the radius of the container's corners (in px) to make them more round or square. Shadow: Add and customize a shadow effect on the container.   Attaching elements to containersWhen you place elements inside a container, they are automatically attached. This means you can drag the container and its attached elements as whole, and view them together in the Layers panel.To attach an element to a container:
Click the relevant element. Drag it to its desire position in the container. Drop the element when you see the Attach message.Applying a grid to a containerApply an advanced CSS grid to the container to structure its layout. You can choose the number of rows and columns you want, and set their size using responsive measurements (e.g. fr, Min/max, %)To apply a grid to a container:
Select the relevant container. Click the More Actions icon . Click Apply Advanced CSS Grid. Choose a layout from the 1x1 drop-down.
Tip: Select Other if you want to set your own number of rows and columns.

source_documents.title: Tracking Google Ads Conversions Using Google Tag Manager
source_documents.content:
Tracking Google Ads Conversions Using Google Tag Manager
Google Ads conversion tracking is a way to measure the conversion actions that users take on your Wix site after they click or view your Google ads. For example, a visitor might finalize a purchase after clicking an ad. You can use Google Tag Manager to track your Google Ads conversion actions by setting up variables, triggers, and tags that use the Conversion ID and Label ID of the action you want to track.Important:
If you don't need to set up any special tracking, it's a good idea to use Google Analytics instead, as it captures all essential business events. By using this service, you are engaging directly with a third-party service provider. We recommend reviewing the service provider's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use prior to your use of such third-party service. You acknowledge that we are not liable for any loss or damage resulting from your use of such third-party service, including any liability arising from any personal data exchanged between you and such third-party.Step 1 | Create a conversion action in Google AdsFirst, create a conversion action in your Google Ads account. This gives you the Conversion ID and Conversion label that you need to use in Google Tag Manager to track the action.Before you begin:You need to connect Google Tag Manager to your site before you can set up conversion tracking.Step 2 | Set up your conversion action in Google Tag ManagerNow that you have created a conversion action, set it up in Google Tag Manager. Choose a conversion type and set up the action. You can create an eCommerce conversion, form submission conversion, or click button conversion.Create an eCommerce conversion based on purchaseAfter you've created your conversion action, set up 2 variables in your Google Tag Manager account. Then, create 2 triggers that use these variables so that you can track your conversion action. Finally, you can start tracking the conversion action by creating 2 tags. Note:Wix fires a special collection of business events that cover the recommended by Google conversions. Do not use the Thank You page capturing method to track eCommerce-based conversions. Click the steps below to learn more.a | Create 2 variables
Go to Google Tag Manager. (If required) Select the container that you want to create variables in. Click Variables.  Click New under User-Defined Variables. Enter "dl_transaction_id" as the name for the variable. Click Choose a variable type to begin setup.  Select Data Layer Variable under Page Variables. Enter "ecommerce.purchase.actionField.id" under Data Layer Variable Name. Click Save.  Click New under User-Defined Variables. Enter "dl_conversion_value" as the name for the variable. Click Choose a variable type to begin setup.  Select Data Layer Variable under Page Variables. Enter "ecommerce.purchase.actionField.revenue" under Data Layer Variable Name. Click Save.  b | Create 2 triggers 
Click Triggers. Click New. Enter a name for the trigger. 
Tip: We recommend "tr_pageview" or similar. Click Choose a trigger type to begin setup.  Select Custom Event under Other. Enter "Pageview" under Event name. Click Save. Click New.  Enter a name for the trigger. 
Tip: We recommend "tr_purchase" or similar. Click Choose a trigger type to begin setup.  Select Custom Event under Other. Enter "Purchase" under Event name. Click Save. c | Create 2 tags 
Click Tags. Click New. Enter a name for the tag.
Tip We recommend "conversion_linker" or similar. Click Choose a tag type to begin setup.  Select Conversion Linker. Click Choose a trigger to make this tag fire.  Select tr_pageview.  Click Save. Click New. Enter a name for the tag. 
Tip: We recommend "conversion_tracking" or similar. Click Choose a tag type to begin setup.  Select Google Ads Conversion Tracking. Enter the following information:
    
Conversion ID: Enter your Conversion ID from your Google Ads conversion action. Conversion Label: Enter your Conversion Label ID from your Google Ads conversion action. Conversion Value: Enter "dl_conversion_value". Transaction ID: Enter "dl_transaction_id". Currency Code: Enter your 3-character currency code.   Click Choose a trigger to make this tag fire.  Select tr_purchase. Click Save. Create other types of eCommerce conversions:Other types of eCommerce conversions you can set up are "View product page", "Add to cart", and "Begin checkout". See the FAQ below to learn more.Create a form submission conversionThere are 2 types of events you can capture and track:
Lead event capturing: Triggered when a site visitor submits a form Thank you page capturing: Triggered if a site visitor is redirected to a form's Thank You page after submitting the form.Lead event capturing (recommended)a | Create a variable
Go to Google Tag Manager. Click Variables.  Click New under User-Defined Variables. Enter "dl_event_label" as the name for the variable. Click Choose a variable type to begin setup.  Select Data Layer Variable under Page Variables. Enter "event_label" under Data Layer Variable Name. Click Save.b | Create a trigger
Click Triggers. Click New. Enter a name for the trigger.
Tip: We recommend "tr_form_submit" or similar. Click Choose a trigger type to begin setup.  Select Custom Event under Other. Enter "lead" under Event name. (Optional) If you want to track 2 or more forms separately, select Some Custom Events, dl_event_label contains “your form name”.
Note: You can find your form's name in the form's settings in your Wix site's dashboard.
 Click Save.Thank You page capturinga | Create a Thank You pageCreate a Thank You page that your site visitor will be redirected to after successfully submitting a form.b | Create a trigger
Go to Google Tag Manager. Click Triggers. Click New. Enter a name for the trigger.
Tip: We recommend "tr_form_submit" or similar. Click Choose a trigger type to begin setup.  Select Custom Event under Other. Enter "Pageview" under Event name. Set the URL of the tracked Thank You page:
    
Select Some custom events. Enter the Page URL that contains your Thank You page URL part.   Click Save.Create click button conversionsTrack conversions for when site visitors click phone, e-mail, and WhatsApp buttons.a | Create a variable
Go to Google Tag Manager. Click Variables.  Click New under User-Defined Variables. Enter "dl_element-url" as the name for the variable. Click Choose a variable type to begin setup.  Select Data Layer Variable under Page Variables. Enter "gtm.elementUrl" under Data Layer Variable Name. Click Save. b | Create a trigger
Go to Variables and select Built in variables.
Note: Make sure that all the click variables are selected. Click Triggers. Click New.  Select the Click – Just links trigger. Enter a name for the trigger.
Tip: We recommend "tr_click_email" or similar. Under This trigger fires on enter the value for the relevant use case:
    
Email address: mailto / or email address Telephone number: Tel: / or telephone number WhatsApp: wa.me   FAQsClick a question to learn more about tracking Google Ads conversions.Can I use custom code to track my Google Ads instead?Yes, you can also track Google Ads conversion actions by adding custom code to your site. My site uses a cookie banner - does this affect the tracking in any way?If your site uses a cookie banner, conversions’ data will only be sent to Google if a visitor provides consent and approves using the relevant cookies. However, if you don't have a cookie banner and a site visitor comes from a country that requires consent (e.g. those covered by GDPR) no data is sent to Google. Google only tracks sessions where visitors give explicit consent.Are there other types of eCommerce conversions?Yes, other types of eCommerce conversions you can set up are:
View product page: The custom trigger name is viewContent. Add to cart: The custom trigger name is addToCart. Begin checkout: The custom trigger name is checkout.Note: Variables are not required for any of these conversions.

source_documents.title: Facebook Ads: Wix's Facebook Ads Refund Policy
source_documents.content:
Facebook Ads: Wix's Facebook Ads Refund Policy
Facebook Ads campaigns with Wix are paid with a monthly subscription and payments are non-refundable. If you end your campaign before the month is up, your campaign ends instantly, and auto-renew is turned off.You can restart an ended campaign at any time before your subscription expires by clicking Edit & Restart from your Facebook Ads dashboard. Notes:
Resuming a campaign also turns auto-renew back on.  Any unused ad spend will remain in your account until you resume the campaign. If the subscription expires, you need to purchase a new subscription in order to activate the campaign and use the remaining ad spend. If you don't want your campaign to renew after the current subscription cycle ends you can turn off auto-renewal of your subscription.Additional Information
What's Wix's cut of my purchased premium plan? 
    
Wix gets 15% of your payment, the remaining 85% goes to Facebook. Prices do not include VAT, which is determined based on your billing country.   To prevent rejections from Facebook, make sure your campaign complies with Facebook's Advertising Policies.  If you feel you deserve a refund, contact us and tell us why and we will review your request.

source_documents.title: Dayful by Wix: About Dayful by Wix
source_documents.content:
Dayful by Wix: About Dayful by Wix
Dayful by Wix is an all-in-one business management and scheduling platform. This allows you to run your service business, get booked and get paid, wherever your online presence is. Benefits of Dayful by WixDayful by Wix provides freedom and flexibility to service business owners like you. Get booked and get paid no matter the size or scale of your online presence. Don't need a website? Dayful creates a landing page for your clients to book your services. You can then share links to your services in emails, on social media and through other digital marketing channels.Already have a website? Embed your Dayful by Wix widgets on your existing site and manage your service business from the Dayful dashboard.FAQsHere are some frequently asked questions about Dayful by Wix:How do I get started with Dayful by Wix?First, sign up at Dayful.com to set up your account. Answer a few questions about your business so we can provide the best solution for you. You can then access your Dayful by Wix dashboard and begin adding your staff and services. How do I add my business details?The Business Info section of your dashboard is where you can add or update important details about your business. These include: 

Your business' name, category, logo and description.  Your default location.  Your primary contact info. How do I create a service?The Services tab is where you create or update your services. These include: 
1-on-1 service:
    
Appointments: Services which clients can book during any available time slot during your business hours. Clients can only book when the relevant staff member is available to host the service.   Multiple participants services:
    
Classes: A regular service you run on a recurring basis. Clients can book each session separately. Courses: A one-time service which takes place over days or weeks. Clients book all sessions together.   How do I add staff members?The Staff tab is where you add and update your staff member profiles. Learn more about adding staff members to your Dayful account. You can also:
Set your default staff hours. Customize individual staff hours in their profiles. Invite staff members to sync their personal calendars with their Dayful by Wix calendars. Set up your video conferencing account and provider to offer online services.How do I get paid when clients book my services?The Accept Payments section of the Settings tab is where you connect your payment providers. Learn more about setting up payments on Dayful.
Note: Upgrade to a premium Dayful by Wix plan to accept online payments. Dayful by Wix currently supports the following payment providers, depending on your location:
Stripe Square Paypal Manual paymentsHow do I share my services online?If you don't have a site yet, you can share links to your services in emails or on social media from your dashboard.Learn more about sharing your Dayful by Wix services online. How do I embed my services on my existing website?If you already have your own site, you can generate code to embed your service widgets on your existing web pages.Learn more about embedding your service widgets on your website.

Wix Bookings: Customizing Your Appointment Form

Change the elements that appear in this form and design every part to match your style.To customize your Appointment Form:

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Editing an Existing Order
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Editing an Existing Order
Important:This feature is not available to everyone yet. Edit an existing order for an appointment or product at any time. This allows you to collect updated payments, set custom prices, issue refunds, and more. You can also add or remove products and services, or include tips in the order.In this article, learn more about:
Adding services and products to an existing order Adding a tip or fee to an existing order  Setting a custom price for an existing order item Removing items from an existing order Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)Adding services and products to an existing orderYou can include extra services and products along with the original order at any point—before, during, or after the appointment—based on the actual services and products offered.Note:
This option only applies to appointments. To change the quantity of items in an existing order, edit the quantity next to the relevant item(s). To add services and products to an existing order:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant order. Click More Actions at the top right and select Edit order.  Click Add Item and select Service, Product, or + Add Custom Item.
Choose from the following options:
    
Products and Services: Select the service or product you want to add and click Add to Order.  Custom Item: Enter the Title, Item info and price for your custom Item and click Add to Order.    Finalize the order updates:
    
(Optional) Enter a Reason for editing. Click Update Order at the top right.  (Optional) Select the checkbox if you want to email the customer about changes made to this order.  Click Update Order to confirm.  Adding a tip or fee to an existing orderAdd a tip or an additional fee by editing an existing order. You can include a note to provide a description for the new item.To add tips or fees to an existing order:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Select the relevant order. Click More Actions at the top right and then Edit Order.  Click Add fees & Tips in the Order summary.   Enter a name for the fee or tip. 
Enter the Amount. Click Add. Finalize the order updates:
    
(Optional) Enter a Reason for editing. Click Update Order at the top right.  (Optional) Select the checkbox if you want to email the customer about changes made to this order.  Click Update Order to confirm.  Setting a custom price for an existing order itemYou can adapt the pricing of items in an existing order to meet your client's specific needs by setting a custom price. To set a custom price in an existing order:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Click to select the relevant order. Click More Actions at the top right and then Edit Order.  Click the More Actions icon  next to item price and select Edit price.
Enter the new price and click Apply. Finalize the order updates:
    
(Optional) Enter a Reason for editing. Click Update Order at the top right.  (Optional) Select the checkbox if you want to email the customer about changes made to this order. Click Update Order to confirm.  Removing an item from an existing orderYou can modify an existing order by removing items to adjust the final price. If the order has been partially or fully paid, you can also issue a refund as needed.To remove an item from an existing order:
Go to Orders in your site's dashboard. Click to select the relevant order. Click More Actions at the top right and then Edit Order.  Click the More Actions icon  next to item price and select Remove.
Note: To change the quantity of items in an existing order, you can also edit the quantity next to the relevant item(s). To remove an item, change the quantity to 0.5.  Finalize the order updates:
(Optional) Enter a Reason for editing. Click Update Order at the top right.  (Optional) Select the checkbox if you want to email the customer about changes made to this order. Click Update Order to confirm.What's next?Once you update an order, you're re-directed to see its overview. At this point, you can also choose to collect payment from your client and see the order change timeline below the order. FAQsClick the questions below for answers to common questions about editing existing orders. Do third parties, such as shipping apps or drop shippers, get notified about changes?Third-party apps won't necessarily get updated when you make a change. Go to the relevant third party's dashboard directly to check if they were updated and, if needed, make changes.Why am I having trouble editing a particular order?You cannot edit an order in these cases:
The order wasn't paid for in your business' main currency The order includes a subscription The order was canceled The order was archived The order was partially or fully refunded What happens if I add or delete services from an order, do I need to manually update my Booking calendar?You do not need to manually update your Booking calendar when you edit an order. When you add a service to an order, the session appears on the Booking calendar. If you delete a service from the order, the session disappears from the calendar. Will my 3rd-party invoicing app send a new invoice after I edit an order?Whether a new invoice is created depends on which app you use. We suggest you create a test order and edit it to see if a new invoice is created.

source_documents.title: Wix Multilingual: Exporting and Importing Site Content for Manual Translation
source_documents.content:
Wix Multilingual: Exporting and Importing Site Content for Manual Translation
Export and import your site content for manual translation. By downloading a CSV file, you can send your content to a professional translator. Once the translations are ready, import the translated content back to your site.Before you begin:
Add Wix Multilingual to your site.  Add a secondary language. In this article, learn more about: 
Exporting your site content  Importing your translated content  Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Exporting your site contentBegin by exporting your website's content into a CSV file. You can then send the file to a professional translator to have them translate the text. To export your site content:
Go to Multilingual in your site's dashboard.  Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant language.  Click Export Content.  Click Export Content again to download the CSV file. Importing your translated contentOnce you've completed the translation you can import it to your site. This process involves uploading your saved CSV file to the relevant language in your site languages. For example, if you are translating content from English to French, you need to upload the French content to your site's French language.To import your translated content:
Go to Multilingual in your site's dashboard.  Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant language.  Click Import translations. 
Click Start Now.  Click Upload CSV File.  Select the relevant CSV file.  Click Import Translations. (Optional) Click Review Translations. Review each page and check the status of the translation.
Note: The status should say "Translated".  Click Save when you are finished reviewing.  Publish your site to view the changes live. FAQsClick a question below to learn more:What are the benefits of the import/export process?There are several benefits to importing and exporting your content for translation purposes, but the main benefit overall is that you decide (based on your level of comfort), if you want to translate the content manually yourself, or send it to someone else.Why do I see more than one language in the exported file?Each exported file contains two languages: the first column includes the content in your Source language, this is your original language (you shouldn’t edit this) and the second column (marked Target language) where you can edit the translation in your target language.What can cause the import process to fail?There are several reasons the import process might fail. We recommend checking the following: 
Make sure your file is saved as a CSV. This is the correct format in order for us to properly import the file. Make sure you haven’t made any changes to the “ID” column in the file.I do not see any new translations, what is the reason?The issue is likely caused by one of the following: 
You added the translated content to the wrong language.  Changes to the “ID” column in the CSV file.  The last column "Target Language" is empty. What can I do if my file does not download?If a download didn’t start, press the “Download File” button in the green banner that appears at the top of your screen.Is it possible to override content?Yes, when you import your newly translated content, any fields in the translated language column where you entered content, will override existing content in Wix Multilingual for that specific language.Tip: If you wish not to override a specific piece of content, simply leave the field column empty in the file.Is there any site content that cannot be exported?Yes, the exported content doesn’t include content from non-integrated business solutions and Third-party apps. Learn more about translatable content. Can you export/import more than one target language at a time?No, the export/import process works on a language level. Meaning, you can only export one target language per file.What happens if I have existing translations in my target language?The exported file also contains any existing translations in the target language, if they exist. This means that your CSV file will contain both new and existing translations in your target language.

source_documents.title: Wix Multilingual Request: Translating the Members Area in Multilingual Sites
source_documents.content:
Wix Multilingual Request: Translating the Members Area in Multilingual Sites
Most components in your Members Area are based on system text, which is text that's automatically generated by Wix.If the Editor supports your secondary language, Members Area components with system text are automatically localized. If your secondary language isn't supported, all system text appears in English and cannot be translated. Currently, the only part of your Members Area that can be manually translated is the My Orders page. This page appears only when you have added Wix Stores and Members Area to your site. To learn how to translate the My Orders page, click here.What languages does Wix Editor support?Currently, the Editor is available in: 
English  Spanish Portuguese French German Polish Italian Russian Japanese Korean Turkish Chinese Thai Swedish  Norwegian Dutch Danish Hindi  CzechExamples of system text in Members AreaSome components in your Members Area include automatic text generated by Wix, for example:
Login page Member profile cards My Account page My Wallet pageIf your secondary language is supported by Wix Editor, these components are automatically localized.What content can be translated with Wix Multilingual?See the list of Translatable Content in Wix Multilingual.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

Wix Photo Albums: Editing Your Photo Album
Edit your album at any time. You can customize the album's design, add information about your photos, create new galleries and more.  Note: Make sure to edit your images before you upload them to Photo Albums. Once you've uploaded images to Photo Albums, you cannot edit them. To edit a photo album:

source_documents.content:

source_documents.title: Wix Retail POS: Managing Business Locations
source_documents.content:
Wix Retail POS: Managing Business Locations
If you're business has more than one location, you can choose which branch is connected to your Wix Retail POS tablet. Note:Managing multiple locations is currently available only with Wix Bookings.After making your selection, services provided at that location appear in the services tab at checkout (see FAQ below for more details).FAQsHow can I add a new location or edit the details of an existing location?To make changes, you need to go to your desktop. Learn more about adding and managing multiple locations.What other factors limit which services appear in the Services tab?Besides location, a number of other factors limit which services appear in the Services tab:
Only appointments appear, no classes or courses. Only services that can be purchased per session (i.e. without a plan). Services that you hide from your site appear in the list.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Fulfilling Orders with the ShipBob Fulfillment Service
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Fulfilling Orders with the ShipBob Fulfillment Service
ShipBob is a fulfillment service which stores your products in their warehouses and then packs and ships products to your customers whenever an order comes in. After setup, the fulfillment process runs automatically:
Orders are forwarded from Wix to ShipBob ShipBob fulfills the order and creates a tracking number The tracking number is added to the order  Customers automatically receive shipping confirmation sent from your storeStep 1 | Add the ShipBob appTo get started, go to the Wix App Market and add the ShipBob app. Show me how
Click Add Apps  on the left side of the Editor.
 Start typing ShipBob in the search and click to select it. Click +Add App. Click Allow and Install. If not taken there automatically, access the app in your dashboard:
    
Go to the Manage Apps tab in your site's dashboard.  Click Open next to ShipBob.   Click Connect next to ShipBob.

 Select an option:
    
Log in to your existing ShipBob account:  
        
Enter your email address and password. Click Login.    Create a ShipBob account:

Click here.
  Complete the form. Click Create Account.     Enter a name for the integration between Wix and ShipBob in the Create a new channel field.
 Review permissions and click Yes, Allow. Step 2 | Sync store products with ShipBobBefore you begin:If you created product options, you must enable the Manage pricing and inventory for variants toggle and track variant inventory amounts so that ShipBob can fulfill orders with variants accurately. Learn how to manage inventory for variants.  Note that ShipBob assigns a unique identifier to each variant. You can sync products in the Wix dashboard. You have the option to sync products, orders, and tracking information at this stage, we recommend, however, that you start by syncing your products.  Show me how
If you closed the Wix dashboard tab, reopen it:
    
Go to the Manage Apps tab. Click Open next to the ShipBob app.   Select the Sync New Products checkbox and click Save.

Step 3 | Complete account setupWhen you're ready, complete the account setup process. This includes deleting the demo data that is in ShipBob dashboard, connecting a credit card, and adding some details to your products. Learn more about completing account setup.Step 4 | Set how often you want to sync with ShipBobAfter the initial connection with ShipBob is established, you'll need to sync regularly so that when you add new products or get new orders, ShipBob is informed about the changes. You can set how often you want to sync. If for some reason, you want to stop syncing for a time, you can select the Pause option. Note that you can also sync manually at any time.Show me howTo set up a sync schedule:
In the Wix dashboard, go to the Manage Apps tab.  Click Open next to the ShipBob app.
 In the Wix dashboard, click Sync Schedule.
 Select a sync frequency from the drop-down. Click Save.To sync manually:
In the Wix dashboard, go to the Manage Apps tab.  Click Open next to the ShipBob app.
 Click Sync Now at the top right.Tip:When ShipBob receives orders with products that are not synced to their dashboard, a new product is automatically created.Step 5 | Send inventory to ShipBobNote:Before ShipBob can start fulfilling orders, your products need to physically arrive at one of their warehouses. When you know how and when your products will arrive, you can sync your orders with ShipBob and set a date when they will start fulfilling orders.Next, your store products must be sent to a ShipBob warehouse. Start by selecting which ShipBob warehouse you want to work with - ideally the one closest to your customer base. To learn how to ship your merchandise to ShipBob, check out these resources:
ShipBob Article  ShipBob VideoStep 6 | Sync store orders with ShipBobAfter shipping your products to ShipBob (or, at least, planning how to do so), you should have some idea of when they can start fulfilling your orders. In order for ShipBob to start fulfilling your orders, they need to start receiving store orders that come in. ShipBob offers the option of syncing orders automatically as they come in, or sending them manually. Learn how to sync store orders with ShipBob.  Tip:Don't forget to set a start date when ShipBob will start fulfilling orders (step six below).Step 7 | Set a date for ShipBob to start fulfilling ordersTo make sure orders aren't fulfilled twice (once by you and once by ShipBob) set the date ShipBob will start fulfilling relevant store orders.Show me how
In the Wix dashboard, go to the Manage Apps tab. Click Open next to the ShipBob app. Click Connection Settings. Click the Date icon.
 Select a date. Click OK. Click Save.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Letting Customers Know About Discounts
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Letting Customers Know About Discounts
Spread the word about the discounts you're offering to make sure that all your customers know about them. There's several ways you can promote your discounts that include displaying them in different ways on your site, and by publicizing them in your social media accounts and email campaigns.Placing a banner at the top of your siteYou can place a banner at top of your site highlighting your discount so that everyone sees it when they browse your site.Learn how to create a banner.Adding an image or video stripYou can add a strip to your site with a beautiful image or video background to grab your customers' attention. Attach any content you want to your strip including text and decorative items, and change the scroll effect to make sure nobody misses it.Learn how to add a stripCreating a lightboxAnother option is a pop up lightbox that you set to appear after a customer is on your site for a set period of time. A lightboox is a great way to grab your visitors' attention and showcase your discount. You can add elements to the pop-up message, decide when it's triggered, and choose how visitors close it.Learn how to add a lightboxSharing on social media and emailsSpread the word to your contacts and social media followers by showcasing your discounts on offer in:
Email marketing campaigns Social media marketing posts,  Social media ads such as Facebook Ads.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Migrating from Other eCommerce Platforms to Wix Stores
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Migrating from Other eCommerce Platforms to Wix Stores
The Cart2Cart app helps you migrate to Wix from over 80 eCommerce platforms so you can create your dream store. To check if your platform is supported, click here.You can add the Cart2Cart app to your Wix site for free, but Cart2Cart charges a fee to perform the migration. The exact price is determined by the platform you are transferring from, which elements you choose to migrate, what optional extra services you select and more. You can run a free demo, including migrating a limited number of elements to your Wix store, to see how the Cart2Cart app works.During the migration process, Cart2Cart gives you a preview, where you see an exact price breakdown before you commit to any changes or pay any fees. In addition, you can click here to get a cost estimate from Cart2Cart.Before you begin:
Make sure you added Wix Stores to your site. Learn how To migrate store orders, you must first upgrade to a Premium plan or Studio plan that allows you to accept payments.Step 1 | Add the Cart2Cart app and select an accountTo start the migration process, go to the Wix App Market and add the Cart2Cart app. Then, make sure the email associated with the relevant Wix account is selected. Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click Add Apps   on the left side of the editor. Search for the Cart2Cart app in the search bar. Click Add to Site. Click Agree & Add. Select an option:
    
Sign in to your existing Cart2Cart account. Create a new Cart2Cart account:
        
Click Sign Up. Fill in the required fields.     In the Cart2Cart dashboard, make sure the email associated with the relevant Wix account is selected. Click Source and Target Cart Setup.
Go to your editor. Click App Market  on the left side of the editor. Click App Market. Search for the Cart2Cart app in the search bar. Click Add to Site. Click Agree & Add. Select an option:
    
Sign in to your existing Cart2Cart account. Create a new Cart2Cart account:
        
Click Sign Up. Fill in the required fields.     In the Cart2Cart dashboard, make sure the email associated with the relevant Wix account is selected. Click Source and Target Cart Setup.Tip:If you close the migration tab at any stage, you can access the Cart2Cart dashboard from the Manage Apps tab in your site's dashboard.Step 2 |  Source and target cart setupThroughout the migration process, the store you are migrating from is referred to as the source cart. The target cart is your Wix store. In this step you select both carts and provide the necessary permissions to access the source cart. For example, to migrate from Shopify, you need to provide an API Password.Note:This step is different for each source cart. Refer to the instructions on the right in the Cart2Cart migration screen.Show me howSelect a source cart (i.e. the platform from which you want to migrate). Enter your store's URL (e.g. http://examplestore.yourplatform.com).Enter the information needed to access your platform.Note: Each platform requires different information. For example, Shopify requires an API Password. Follow the instructions on the right of the screen to complete this part of the process.Leave Wix as the selected Target Cart.Click Choose Entities.Step 3 | Select what to migrate and perform a demo migrationYou can migrate (import) different types of data into your Wix store (data available varies by platform). Afterwords, select any available additional migration options.  To select migration options:
Select which of types of data (e.g. products, orders, and coupons) you want to migrate to Wix. 
Note: Imports are limited to 1,000 products and 1,000 orders. (Optional) Select any of the additional options you see displayed (options vary depending on what you selected in step 1):
    
Select the Clear current data on Target Store before Migration to delete data in your Wix store for the entities you are migrating.
Important: This step is irreversible.
E.g. if you import products and select this option, any products already in your Wix dashboard will be deleted. Learn more Select the Skip product thumbnail images migration checkbox. Watch video to learn more Select the Change products quantity to 100 on Target Store ($29). Learn More Perform data mapping: (relevant when importing orders): Orders in each platform have different statuses. Make sure they are classified correctly in your Wix dashboard by matching terms. Learn more   Click Start Free Demo.Once you've selected options, Cart2Cart performs a demo migration. This gives you a chance to preview the migration and check that everything is ok before you make changes and pay Cart2Cart for the process. Step 4 | Check demo migration results and complete the migration
Now that the demo migration is complete, click Check the Results to view your data in your Wix dashboard.



Products can be found in the Wix Store Products tab. Orders can be found in the Wix Orders tab. Coupons can be found in the Wix Coupons tab.   If you're satisfied with the result, select one of the insurance plans or click the skip migration insurance option. Watch a Cart2Cart video on insurance options When you're ready, review the migration price.
Tip: Click the Menu icons to see the price breakdown.

 Pay and complete the migration:
    
Click Add Funds for Full Migration. Enter the required details. Click Buy now.  When the migration is complete, you'll receive an email notification.

source_documents.title: Workflows: Getting Started
source_documents.content:
Workflows: Getting Started
A workflow is a board that displays all of the steps (columns) of a project so you can easily keep track of every phase. Using Workflows, you can manage and prioritize your projects, marketing campaigns, sales funnel or any other process you need to monitor. Ready to get started?Go to Workflows in your site's dashboard to get started. You can also use the search bar at the top of your site's dashboard to search for "workflows".Creating new workflowsWhen creating a new workflow, you can either define your own custom steps or use one of our ready-made templates. Click + New at the top right, then New Workflow to see the template list. If you can't find a template that works for you, simply click Start from Scratch. Tell me moreSales Leads: Covers all the steps of a sales funnel, from getting leads to making the sale. Hiring Process: Covers all the stages of recruiting a potential employee, from reading submitted resumes to onboarding the new hire. Help Desk & IT: Helps in monitoring IT and Help Desk requests.Website Design: Covers the process of building a new website commissioned by a customer, from getting the initial lead to completing the project. Online Store: Keeps track of orders placed in your online store, from payment to delivery. Business Meetings: Helps in managing new leads, from first contact to setting up meetings and follow-ups.Site Members: Covers the different stages of being your site member, from signup to becoming an active member with badges.      Adding steps (columns) to your workflowThe columns of your workflow represent steps in a project, process or flow. Each column contains cards that are associated to the contacts you're working with. This way, you get a visual understanding of where you stand and what needs to be done. You can always create more columns and move cards between the columns. Learn MoreUsing cards in your workflowEach card in your workflow is assigned to one of your site's contacts. Once you've made progress with one of your contacts, move them to the next step by dragging and dropping their card to the relevant column. Learn MoreAutomating your workflowAutomations can help you streamline your workflow in two ways:Moving cards as a trigger: Set an automated response (e.g. send an email, create a task, etc.) for every time you move cards to specific columns in your workflow.Moving cards as a response: Set an automation that moves cards to certain steps of your workflow in response to an action. For example, move a card to the Contacted column right after messaging the relevant person. Learn More

source_documents.title: Google Workspace: Auto Renewal and Payment Issues for Your Business Email
source_documents.content:
Google Workspace: Auto Renewal and Payment Issues for Your Business Email
Auto Renewal Information
When you sign up for a Google Workspace business email service, you are automatically billed for the renewal of the business email subscription on either a monthly or yearly basis depending on the plan purchased, until it is canceled. For yearly business email subscriptions, the renewal payment is attempted up to 30 days before the anniversary of your purchase to ensure that there is no interruption to your business email service. You can see the exact date in Premium Subscriptions. Wix sends notification emails before the renewal of yearly business email subscriptions to enable users to decided whether to continue with the service or not. Please check all mail folders including any spam folders you have. When you no longer want to continue with your Google Workspace business email service, you can stop any further charges by turning off the auto-renewal. To turn off the auto-renewal, follow the instructions here. If you change your mind, you can easily turn the auto-renewal back on prior to the cancellation date.Declined Renewal PaymentThe renewal payment for your Google Workspace business email may have failed due to one of the following reasons:
The payment has been declined by your credit card provider The credit card provided has expired or has insufficient funds The credit card number provided is invalid The credit card provided has not been approved for recurring paymentsImportant:If your renewal payments are declined it is important to resolve the payment issue as soon as possible to prevent any interruption to your business email service.Resolving Declined Payment IssuesTo resolve the payment issue, please update your payment method to complete the payment, by following the instructions here.Alternatively, please contact your bank or credit card company to check why the payment failed.If your Google Workspace business email service has been canceled due to payment problems, you can repurchase by following the instructions here.Important:Once you select a payment cycle it is not possible to change it. If you select a yearly billing cycle, you can not change to a monthly cycle, nor can you to change from a monthly cycle to a yearly billing cycle.

source_documents.title: Requesting a Refund for a Premium or Studio Plan
source_documents.content:
Requesting a Refund for a Premium or Studio Plan
Wix offers a 14-day, money-back guarantee for new Premium or Studio site plans. If you purchased your site plan within the last 14 days, you're eligible for a full refund. Eligibility for a refundThe 14-day refund policy only applies to new Premium or Studio plans. The refund policy does not apply if:
You are requesting a refund for a plan renewal. You are requesting a refund for the upgrade of an existing plan.If you do not meet the requirements for the 14-day refund policy, but you believe you still deserve a refund, contact us and we'll review your request. Request process for a refundCancel your site plan within the first 14 days of purchasing it to receive a full refund. There's no need to submit a request, simply click the button below to choose a plan to cancel. If you're eligible, your payment method will be refunded automatically. Please allow up to 20 business days for your refund to appear on your credit card statement.After canceling, your site plan is immediately deactivated and you can no longer make use of Wix's premium features (e.g., removing Wix ads or connecting your own domain).

         Click to cancel your plan now
    


        Choose plan to cancel
      

Important:Wix is not responsible for any bank charges, commissions or overdrafts. The only way to remove these charges is through direct negotiation with your bank.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about refunds for site plans.Does the 14-day money back period apply for monthly plan subscriptions?Our Premium and Studio plans are offered on a yearly or monthly basis. Both types of plans offer a 14-day money back period.I accidentally purchased the wrong plan. Can I change it?Yes, you can change to a different plan or different subscription period. For example, you can change:
From a Monthly Core plan to Monthly Business plan From a Monthly Business plan to Yearly Business planIf you change to a cheaper plan, you will be credited the difference.Learn more about changing your plan.I purchased my plan in the last few days, what happens to the payment I made?If you cancel your plan within 72 hours of a purchase, it's possible that the transaction will be canceled before the funds have settled. If this is the case, instead of receiving a refund, the original charge(s) will drop away from your account within 20 business days.If you cancel your plan within the first 24 hours, your payment might have been voided and the charges dropped entirely. In this case, the refund does not show in your account.Is it possible to pause or delay the activation of a plan?No, your site plan (or upgrade) begins the moment that you purchase it. It is not possible to delay the activation or pause the service. 
Tip: If you are not ready for your site to be made public, you can add a Coming Soon (landing page) page and hide the rest of your site.Does the refund policy apply to domains and business emails?No, Wix domain purchases are separate from plan purchases. Domain purchases do not have a 14-day money back guarantee. If you feel that you deserve a refund, contact us and we'll review your request.Note: If you no longer wish to keep the domain you purchased, you can cancel your subscription by turning off the auto renewal process. The domain will expire on the next renewal date. I've canceled my site plan, but it is still active. Why is this? In this case, you may have canceled beyond the 14-day money back period. If you've canceled within the first 14 days, the site plan and its benefits are immediately deactivated. 
If you cancel after the initial 14-day period, the automatic renewal is turned off and the plan remains active until the expiration date. What happens to my site when the plan is canceled?Once your plan is deactivated (if canceled within the 14-day refund window) or expires (if canceled after the 14-day refund window), your site is not deleted; it simply returns to the free site version. The free site version includes up to 500MB of storage, up to 500MB bandwidth and displays Wix ads. Your site URL (e.g. www.mystunningwebsite.com) reverts to the free Wix site URL: siteprefix.wixsite.com/siteaddress

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Offering Free Services
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Offering Free Services
Give existing clients a free bonus service or offer visitors a free trial of your services with Wix Bookings and Wix Automations.In this article, learn more about:
Offering free services with Wix Bookings Offering a free trial with Wix AutomationsOffering free services with Wix BookingsWith Wix Bookings you can reward your members with free services as a nice way of saying thank you.To offer members a free service:
Go to Booking Services in your site's dashboard. Click to edit an existing service or click + Add a New Service.  In the Price & Payment section, click the Price type drop-down and select Free.  Finish setting up the service and click Save. Note:You can also offer free classes without requiring clients to book a spot. Offering a free trial with Wix AutomationsNever miss an opportunity to turn a site visitor into a returning client of your business by offering free trials with Wix Automations. To offer visitors a free trial:
Go to Automations in your site's dashboard. Click + New Automation. Click + Start from Scratch.  Under Choose a Trigger, select Wix Bookings from the list. Select the relevant option under Select a trigger, for example, Session ends.  Select the relevant option from the Select which services trigger this automation:

Any: The free trial coupon automation works for all services you offer.  Specific: The free trial coupon automation only applies to specific services you offer, for example your new services that you want to promote. 
        
Click + Select. Select the checkboxes next to all relevant services.  Click OK.      Select the relevant option from the Limit frequency to drop-down. Under Choose an Action, select Add a coupon. In Set Coupon, select one of the following:
    
Unique single-use coupon code: The coupon you select will be duplicated, and random characters will be added to its coupon code to make it unique. Each unique coupon can only be redeemed once. Fixed coupon code: The coupon you select will be added to the automation as is, so that everyone get the same coupon code.   Click + Select under Select a coupon.  Select an existing coupon or click + Create New.  Click OK.  Click Activate.

source_documents.title: Wix Logo: Hiding and Deleting Elements in the Wix Logo Maker
source_documents.content:
Wix Logo: Hiding and Deleting Elements in the Wix Logo Maker
While designing your logo, you may want to visualize it with or without certain elements. You can hide and unhide elements from your logo at anytime to help you settle on a final design. If you want, you can delete them entirely.In this article, learn more about:
Hiding elements in your logo Deleting elements in your logo FAQsHiding elements in your logoYou can hide elements of your logo, so they won't be visible in your final logo files.To hide elements in your logo:
Go to Logo and Brand. Select the logo you would like to edit. Right-click the element in the Logo Maker. Click Hide. Deleting elements in your logoIf you'd prefer not to hide an element, you can choose to delete elements in your logo instead. To delete elements in your logo:
Go to Logo and Brand. Select the logo you would like to edit. Right-click the element in the Logo Maker. Click Delete. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about hiding elements in the Wix Logo Maker.How do I unhide an element?You can unhide an element at any time. Just go to the relevant tab on the left, hover over the element in the Manage panel and click Unhide.How can I hide just a part of an element and not the whole element?Currently, it is not possible to hide a part of an element in the Logo Maker. If this is a feature you would like to see in the future, you can vote for it here.

Shapes are always visible in white, black, monochrome, grayscale and transparent files of the logo. We do not recommend using them to cover parts of the elements in your logo, so please avoid doing the following:
Making an element the same color as the logo background to hide it. Covering elements of a logo with shapes or icons. Overlapping shapes and icons. Moving elements outside the Logo Maker's borders as they will be visible in the final logo files.Can I hide my business name from my logo?It's not possible to hide or delete your business name from your logo.

source_documents.title: Wix Stores: Setting Up a Flat Rate Shipping Rule
source_documents.content:
Wix Stores: Setting Up a Flat Rate Shipping Rule
Important:We're in the process of rolling out new shipping settings. If you have a Create Region button instead of Add Region, then you have the new version. Learn how to set up shipping using the new settings.Set up flat rate shipping to charge the same rate for all purchases delivered to a certain region. Step 1 | Create or Select a Shipping RegionTo start, create the region the shipping rule applies to.Tip:If you already created the shipping region, just select it and move on to step 2. A region can be made of one or more countries. Alternatively, it can be made of one or more regions within a country. You can set up different shipping regions for your store. For example, a merchant might set up 4 shipping rules: a local shipping region for California, a region for the rest of the US, another for Mexico and Canada, and finally one for the rest of the world.Important:
If there is no rule for a region, customers from that region cannot make store purchases. If you previously set up shipping (and tax) in a merchant account (e.g. in PayPal), remove these settings before starting. Can't find a shipping region you need? Contact us to let us know which region is missing. Show me how
Go to the Shipping & fulfillment settings in your site's dashboard. Select an option:
    
Edit a default rule: Click the region you want to set up.
 Create a new rule:
        
Click Add Region. Click +Add destination, start typing a country name and select it.     (Optional) Select specific region(s) within a country (Not all countries have local regions):
    
Click Edit next to the region number.
 Deselect the checkboxes next to the regions or states you don't want the rule to apply to and click Done.
   (Optional) Click the title (e.g. Region 2) and rename it (e.g England & Scotland).
 Click Done or move directly on to the next step.Step 2 | Set Up a Flat Rate Shipping RuleNow that you've selected a region, it's time to set up the Flat Rate rule for that region.  Show me how
Select Flat Rate from the Select how shipping is calculated drop-down.
 Enter a name in the Shipping Option Name field (e.g. Standard Shipping). (Optional) Enter a time in the Est. Delivery Time field. Enter the shipping rate. (Optional) Offer free shipping on orders above a specific price:
    
Click the Offer Free Shipping when customer buys over a certain amount checkbox and enter the amount.
Note: If you create additional shipping services (e.g. priority shipping), this checkbox must be selected and the amount specified to apply to each rule.   Click Add another Delivery Option to add an additional options (e.g. Express Shipping). (Optional) Check the Add a handling fee to every order checkbox and enter the handling fee. Click Save.Step 3 | Offer Local Delivery or Pickup optionsAfter saving your shipping rule, you can select the region again and add local delivery or pickup options. 
Add local delivery Learn how Add store pickup Learn howWant to learn more?Check out the full Wix Learn course on getting started with Wix eCommerce. Skip to the fourth video to learn more about setting up shipping.

Ascend by Wix: Upgrading an Existing Ascend Plan
You can upgrade your existing Ascend Plan to a plan with more features, or a longer subscription period. The upgrade takes effect immediately. For example:
Ascend Basic to Ascend Professional. Ascend Professional to Ascend Unlimited. Ascend Basic to Ascend Unlimited. Monthly Ascend Basic to Yearly Ascend Basic.To upgrade your Ascend Plan:
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the Show More icon  next to the relevant plan. Click Upgrade Ascend. Click Select under the new Ascend Plan. Select the subscription period and click Next. Enter your payment details and click Submit Purchase.Important:Any remaining credit from your old Ascend Plan is deducted from the price of your new upgrade during the purchase process. This credit is deducted after any discounts from a coupon or seasonal sale are applied.

source_documents.title: Automatic Payment Taken from Your Credit Card
source_documents.content:
Automatic Payment Taken from Your Credit Card
To simplify the billing process for you, we offer yearly and monthly subscriptions, which are billed automatically on a monthly, yearly, or multi-year basis depending on your billing cycle. If you have noticed an automatic payment charged to your card, it is likely for the renewal of one of your subscriptions (for example, a site plan, domain, Google Workspace mailbox or app upgrade.You can check your current subscriptions in the Premium Subscriptions section of your Wix account, and you can view invoices for payments made to Wix on the Billing History page. Learn more about viewing your invoices.Note:If you are still unsure what the payment was for, please contact us and we will assist you further.

source_documents.title: Pages Appearing Individually in Search Results
source_documents.content:
Pages Appearing Individually in Search Results
We enable each page of your Wix site to appear in search results so that each page is accessible to site visitors. For example, if a site visitor wants to find out how to contact you, they can type your business name followed by the word "contact" into a search engine. They can then access your contact page immediately via search results, instead of having to access your home page and scroll through your site.Make sure to add unique title tags and meta descriptions to each page to ensure that search engines display them in search results. Your title tags and meta descriptions should be relevant to the content of the page. This will help your potential site visitors understand what the page is about based on the information displayed in search results.Tip:You can prevent search engines from indexing an individual page if you don't want it to appear. Learn more about preventing search engines from indexing your page.

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Setting Your Editing Size
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Setting Your Editing Size
Set the screen size you're most comfortable working with, for each of the page's breakpoints. As every breakpoint represents a range of screen widths, you can choose a default size that always stays the same. This ensures a consistent design experience, no matter where you're logging in from. Tip:You can set an editing size for global sections as well – it automatically applies to every page where the section appears.To set your editing size:
Go to the relevant page and breakpoint in the editor.  Click the current editing size at the top. Enter the new value next to Editing Size. Click Apply. What's next?The canvas instantly changes to the size you set. You can change the editing size again at any time.

source_documents.title: Unassigning a Premium Plan from a Site
source_documents.content:
Unassigning a Premium Plan from a Site
You can unassign a Premium plan from your site at any time. Unassigned plans can be assigned to another site in your account at any time. You can view your plan in the Unassigned Subscriptions section of your Wix account for easy access after you unassign it.If you reassign a Premium plan, the premium features (e.g. connecting a domain, removal of Wix ads) are removed from the original site. In this article, learn more about:
Unassigning a Premium plan Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Unassigning a Premium plan
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant plan.  Click Unassign Plan.
Click Unassign Plan in the pop-up to confirm.Already unassigned your Premium plan?Learn how to assign your plan to another site. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about unassigning a plan from your site.What happens to my domain after I unassign a plan?When you unassign a plan from your site, your primary domain and any redirecting domains will be disconnected. Learn how to assign your domain to a site in your Wix account. What happens to my site data if I unasign a plan?Statistics and data related to email campaigns do not transfer with the email campaigns themselves. In addition, data related to site-specific features (e.g. apps, SEO settings and tracking tools, analytics) does not transfer.Is unassigning a plan the same as canceling it?No, unassigning a plan does not cancel it. Your subscription will remain active until you cancel the plan. Learn more about canceling a site plan..Why can't I unassign my Business Premium plan?Some older plans cannot be unassigned (e.g. legacy Business Premium plans). If you have Business Premium plan, you can assign it to another site in your Wix account instead. Can I assign a Premium plan to a Wix Studio site?Assigning a Premium plan to a site created with Wix Studio requires upgrading to a Wix Studio plan. Learn more about assigning a Premium plan to a Studio site.

source_documents.title: Wix Art Store: Setting Up Wix Art Store to Sell Digital Images
source_documents.content:
Wix Art Store: Setting Up Wix Art Store to Sell Digital Images
Important:Wix Art Store is currently not available to all users. As of October 2022 it is no longer possible to add the Wix Art Store to your site. Alternatively, you can add Wix Stores to your site and connect it to Printful to sell your art.Once you've added Wix Art Store to your site, follow the steps below to start selling digital images.To set up your store to sell digital images:Step 1: Choose the type of images you want to sell (digital or print).Click the Wix Art Store app in the Editor.Click Settings.Click Set Up Store.Click Start Now.Click Sell Digital.Click OK.If your store already sells prints, and you would like to switch to digital image sales:Click the Wix Art Store app in the Editor.Click Settings.Click Set Up Store.Click Change on the bottom of the window.Select Sell Digital Under Choose What You Want to Sell.Step 2: Add the images you want to sell to your gallery.Click the Wix Art Store app in the Editor.Click Manage Media.Click + Add Media  on the top right.Click Image.Select images from your Media Manager or click +Add Images to upload new files from your computer, social platform or file hosting service.Note: This only uploads your images to your Art Store Files. To display your images in the gallery on your site, complete the rest of the steps.Click the Back  tab.Select the images you want to display.Note: You can add a title, description and link for each image, reorder the images or edit the image quality.Click Done.Step 3: Set the pricing for the images.Click Set Pricing.Set which licenses you want to use:License Templates: Click the toggles under My Licenses to enable or disable each license option:Commercial Use: Web and digital use only.Extended Use: Web, digital and print use.Custom License: Click Create License and fill in the information to create a custom license:Enter the name of the license in the License Name field.Enter a description of the license in the Description field.(Optional) Upload your license agreement:Click Upload.Select your license document or click Upload Docs to upload it from your computer.Click Apply.Click Save.Select or deselect the image resolution checkboxes and enter the price for the selected options:Web Ready: Image quality is slightly reduced to allow for quicker web loading.Original File: The image is purchased in its original quality.Click Save.Step 4: Set your payment and general store settings.
Click Manage Store. Click the Payment tab. Click Connect next to the payment method you want to use and follow the instructions provided. Click the Business Info tab. Enter your business's basic info:
    
Business Name: Enter the name of your business. Your Logo: Click the Add icon + and select your logo from the media manager, or click Upload Images to upload a new one, then click Apply. (Optional: Don't have a logo yet? Design your own stunning logo with Wix Logo, here.) Email: Enter the email address you'd like to use for order confirmations.   Set your business's local settings:
    
Language: Select your language. Currency: Select your store's currency. Price Format: Select a currency format. Symbol Alignment: Select where the currency symbol appears.   Click the Email me when I make a sale toggle to enable or disable email notifications:
    
Enabled: You receive an email notification when you make a sale. Disabled: You do not receive an email notification when you make a sale. You can view your transactions on the Orders tab.   Click Save.Notes:
Your customers receive their digital files via email. To troubleshoot email delivery issues, advise your customers to check their spam / junk folders in their inbox, and contact their email provider to ensure they can receive emails from Wix. If this doesn't resolve the issue, contact Customer Care. If you want to sell digital images and prints (e.g. canvases, mugs, phones cases), click here.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Managing Your Staff and Hours Using the Wix App
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Managing Your Staff and Hours Using the Wix App
As your business grows, you can add new staff members and update your staff hours, even while you're on the go. Add, edit, or delete staff members' hours, directly from the Wix App at any time.To allow maximum flexibility, you can also create one-time changes to the regular working hours.In this article, learn more about:
Adding a new staff member Creating custom hours for a staff member Making one-time changes to staff working hours Editing or removing a staff member's hoursAdding a new staff member using the Wix appAs your team grows, you can add new staff members to your site using your mobile device. Their availability is based on your default work hours, unless you create custom working hours. This is a great way to handle admin while you're on the go.To add a new staff member:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down and tap Settings.  Tap Booking Settings.  Tap the Staff tab. Tap + Add New Staff Member. Enter the staff member's details including their Profile Picture, Full Name, Email and Phone.  Tap Save at the top.Creating custom hours for a staff memberYou can create custom hours for specific staff members who work part-time or different shifts. You can then set how often these custom working hours repeat.Note:When you update a staff member's working hours, you create a custom work schedule for them which is separate from your default business hours. You can only revert the staff member back to the default hours manually.To create custom hours for a staff member:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down and tap Settings.  Tap Booking Settings.  Tap the Staff tab. Tap to select an existing staff member. Tap Add Hours next to Working Hours. Tap Continue.  Tap to select the Start Date for the staff member's new work schedule. (Optional) Tap + Set an end date to make the change to the staff member's work schedule temporary. This is useful for maternity leave cover, for example. Tap to select the days the staff member is available to take appointments. Tap to select the Start Time. Tap to select the End Time. Tap to select the location for these hours from the drop-down.  Tap the Repeats drop-down to select how often your staff member works these hours at these locations: Weekly, Every 2 weeks, Every 3 weeks or every 4 weeks.
Note: A summary of the staff member's custom hours appears at the bottom of the screen.  Tap Save at the top.  (Optional) Repeat steps 6-15 to create additional custom work hours for the same staff member. This is useful if you have multiple locations or if the staff member changes location during the day.Making one-time changes to staff working hoursYou can create one-time changes to regular working hours to allow maximum flexibility. This is useful if a staff member has to leave work early, for any reason. It also works great if your staff work irregular shift hours that change from week to week. Note:When you update a staff member's working hours, you create a custom work schedule for them which is separate from your default business hours. You can only revert the staff member back to the default hours manually.To make one-time changes to staff working hours:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Scroll down and tap Settings.  Tap Booking Settings.  Tap the Staff tab. Tap to select an existing staff member. Tap the More Actions icon  next to the relevant day of the week.  Tap Edit.  Tap the relevant option under When do you want to apply these changes?:
    
Now: The change in shift takes effect immediately. This is useful for last-minute changes. Schedule for later: Decide when the change in working hours takes place. This is useful for future planning.
        
Tap to select the Start Date.  Tap + Set end date and choose the appropriate end date.     Tap to select the relevant Start Time and End Time for the one-time change.  Tap to select the relevant location for the one-time change.  Tap Save at the top.  (Optional) Repeat steps 6-11 to create additional one-time custom work hours for the same staff member. This is useful if you have to arrange cover if another staff member is sick for several days. Editing or removing a staff member's hoursAs your business grows, staff may move locations or change shifts entirely. You can edit or remove working hours completely from a staff member profile in the Wix app. Note:When you remove staff member hours, existing scheduled sessions remain on the calendar. You can remove or reassign these sessions manually. To edit or remove a staff member's hours:
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Booking Calendar. Tap the Staff tab. Tap to select an existing staff member. Tap the More Actions icon  next to the relevant day under Working Hours. Choose what you want to do:Edit staff working hours
Tap Edit.  Tap the relevant option under When do you want to apply these changes?:
    
Now: The change in shift takes effect immediately. This is useful for last-minute changes. Schedule for later: Decide when the change in working hours takes place. This is useful for future planning.
        
Tap to select the Start Date.  Tap + Set end date and choose the appropriate end date.     Tap to select the relevant Start Time and End Time for the one-time change.  Tap to select the relevant location for the one-time change.  Tap Save at the top. Remove staff hours
Tap Remove.  Tap Remove to confirm.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Manually Marking a Service as Paid
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Manually Marking a Service as Paid
When clients pay you offline for a service (e.g. cash, check), you can mark their payment manually from the Booking Calendar. You can also set reminders about partial payments for services, assigning a task to yourself or your staff to follow up with the client. In this article, learn more about:
Marking a service as paid Setting reminder tasks for partial paymentsMarking a service as paidWhen clients pay for services in-person, you can mark them as paid from the participants list for the relevant service. To mark a service as paid:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click on the relevant session.  Click Manage next to the Participants List. 
Find the relevant client in the list.  Select the relevant option from the Payment Status drop-down. 
Note: Selecting Paid in person cannot be undone.Note:We are in the process of releasing a new version of the Booking Calendar, so it's not available to everyone yet. Your version may appear slightly different than pictured in this article.Setting reminder tasks for partial paymentsReceived partial payment from your client in person? You can mark it as paid, while creating a task for yourself to follow-up and collect the rest of the payment. To set a reminder task for partial payments:
Go to the Contacts tab in your dashboard.  Click the relevant client. Scroll down the Overview tab to Tasks & reminders. Click Add next to Tasks & Reminders.  Enter your note explaining the partial payment.  Assign the follow-up task to yourself or a staff member.  Click the calendar icon  to set when the follow up reminder appears.  Click Done.  When the client completes payment, you can then mark them as paid in the participants list of the relevant service.
