source_documents.title: Hopp by Wix: An Overview
source_documents.content:
Hopp by Wix: An Overview
Hopp by Wix helps content creators and influencers connect better with their followers. Using our Link in Bio page, provide your followers with easy access to coupon codes, discount links, or any other content you want to share. There are many other tools that you can use individually, or with your Link in Bio page. From your Hopp account, you can shorten long URLs, create a landing page, and set up pre-rolls that show content to followers before reaching the link they clicked.In this article, learn more about:
Hopp by Wix tools  How to get started Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Learn about Hopp by WixLearn more about each feature of Hopp. You can use these tools individually or together with your Link in Bio page and search engine.Link in BioOvercome linking restrictions in social platforms with limitless sharing, by having one source for your links. Your Link in Bio page includes your own search engine, where your audience can search for products and resources by codes that you assign to each item. Add new content at any time. Mention a code in an Instagram post or TikTok caption for your followers to search. Benefits include:
A search engine that indexes all of your content. Build unique actions that can be added to your Link in Bio page such as links to booking a service, product pages and your social media.  A range of page presets to choose from or design your own.Shorten linksUse the link shortening tool to condense your links into a more easily shareable format. Then, customize your shortened URL even further with your brand name. Or trigger a promotion when the link is clicked. Index the URL in your own Link in Bio search engine and track its performance.Instant PagesInstant Pages allow you to create standalone web pages quickly and easily. These pages are perfect for promoting specific events, products, or announcements without the need to update your entire site. By using Instant Pages, you can drive more traffic, increase conversions, and provide a better user experience for your audience.Use Instant Pages to:
Promote important initiatives. Share exclusive deals and content with your VIP customers. Enhance customer interaction at your physical location. Make something fun and personal.Pre-rollsChoose from a set of content or actions to show your visitors before they reach their intended link destination. When a site visitor clicks to get to a target URL, pre-rolls give you the ability to show them specific content first. You have the option to update and change the target URL whenever you want.Your audience will also have the ability to skip the pre-roll and instead be brought directly to their intended link destination. Some ways that you can use pre-rolls for your business:
Show potential customers a backpack in your Wix Store before they view your hiking blog. Show a video of you explaining a product or service before site visitors purchase or book. Show a coupon to your followers before landing on a product page.  How do I get started? 
Go to hopp.co. Click Get Started for Free at the top right. Log in with your Wix account or create a new account.  Choose a name and username for your Link in Bio page and click Create Account. Set up your Link in Bio page.What's next?You are now on the main Hopp dashboard. You can view your own unique Link in Bio URL in the Link in Bio tab. Click Create New to start building out your Hopp page.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about the Hopp tools.How can I upgrade to a Hopp Pro plan?The Hopp Pro plan offers more design and feature options than the Free plan. To upgrade to a Pro plan:
Go to hopp.co and log in.  Click Upgrade on the top right.  Select the type of plan you want to purchase:
    
Monthly: You will be billed once monthly. Yearly: You will be billed once annually. Purchasing a yearly plan will mean you get a discounted price.   Click Upgrade on the bottom right. Enter your card details in the Checkout section. Click Submit Payment at the bottom. Click Get Started to begin using your Pro features.Learn more about managing your Pro plan. I already have a Wix site. Can I create a Link in Bio page from my Wix account?Yes, you can create a Hopp Link in Bio page through your site's dashboard and associate it to Wix. Make sure you have one of the following roles: 
Site Owner Admin Website Manager Website Designer Can I connect my Link in Bio page to my Wix site?Yes, you can integrate your Link in Bio with your Wix site. This allows you to sync contacts and subscribers, as well as manage your site directly from Hopp.
Go to hopp.co and login.  Click Website on the left. Click Create New Site or Connect Existing Site. Can I add more collaborators to my Hopp account?Currently, only the person who created the Hopp account can manage the account. It is not possible to invite additional collaborators.

source_documents.title: Email Marketing: Moving from Another Platform to Wix Email Marketing
source_documents.content:
Email Marketing: Moving from Another Platform to Wix Email Marketing
Easily move from another email marketing platform to Wix Email Marketing and get to know all the great features it has to offer. In this article, learn more about:
Importing your mailing list Growing your mailing list Setting up automatic responsesImporting your mailing listThe first step is to import your mailing list to your Wix account. To do so you should export your mailing list in a CSV format from the platform you're using. You can find instructions for some common platforms below:
Constant Contact Aweber Campaign Monitor Get ResponseNext, import your mailing list to your Wix account so that you can send email campaigns to your subscribers. Make sure to select the Mark as subscribers checkbox when importing.Important:Only set contacts as Subscribers if they've given you permission to do so. Learn more about Wix Email Marketing best practices. Growing your mailing listGrow your mailing list and gain new subscribers by adding a Get Subscribers form to your site. You can customize the design of the form to match your brand and style.Anyone who signs up using the form is automatically added as a Subscriber. To access your list of Subscribers, you can filter your contacts. Tip:Learn more about changing the subscription status of your contacts.Setting up automatic responses with Wix AutomationsIf you set up automatic responses with your previous platform - you can do the same using Wix Automations.For example, you can set up an automation which automatically sends visitors a Thank You email after they submit a contact form, subscribe to your newsletter, or purchase from your store.Note:Emails sent using Wix Automations use Wix Email Marketing but do not count towards your monthly campaign quota.Tip:Learn more about Wix Email Marketing.

Refund Policy for Wix Domains

source_documents.title: Wix Analytics: About the Marketing Overview
source_documents.content:
Wix Analytics: About the Marketing Overview
View all of your business's marketing efforts and see how each activity is performing at a glance with the Wix Analytics Marketing Overview. See both internal marketing efforts with Wix as well as external activities like Facebook Ads or Google Ads, all in one place.The Marketing Overview helps your business by providing a comprehensive and unified view of each marketing activity. Use the data to identify areas of success or improvement as well as to make decisions on how to allocate marketing resources more efficiently.You can find the Marketing Overview page in the Overviews section under Analytics in your site's dashboard.

        View your Marketing Overview
    


        Take me there
      


Marketing Overview sectionsThe Marketing Overview is broken into sections based on the type of marketing activity you want to analyze. The top section summarizes all your traffic categories including both organic and paid traffic. The sections below the traffic summary focus on a specific category such as email marketing, organic search and any paid ad campaign activities you're running.Tips:
Click the date picker drop-down at the top of the Marketing Overview to change the time period that data is pulled from (the default is 30 days). Note that data from the current day is not yet included. Click See full report in a section to see an in-depth report about that marketing activity.Learn more below about each section of the Marketing Overview.Traffic category summaryThe summary at the top of the Marketing Overview allows you to view and compare all your traffic categories over a specific time period.Customize the traffic summary based on what metrics or categories you want to see. Click the Sales drop-down at the top to change the metric to filter traffic by (sales, orders, sessions, conversion rate). You can also change the default categories shown in the summary. Click + Add category at the right to add a new category. You can pick up to five to display at once.Note:If there are no sales in the last 30 days, the summary will display site sessions by traffic category instead. The Sales drop-down will be set to Sessions by default. Tip:A traffic category refers to the broader category where traffic is coming from (e.g. paid traffic vs. organic social traffic). A traffic source is the specific site where traffic came from (e.g. Facebook.com, Google.com).If you want to temporarily show or hide a category in the chart, select or deselect the checkboxes next to the category. Click the platform drop-down under Organic social to further customize the traffic source (Facebook, Instagram, Tik Tok).Note:If you are running any paid campaigns (e.g. Facebook or Google Ads) outside of Wix, you need to add a UTM tracking link for the external campaign so Wix can track the data. Learn more about UTM tracking.
Email marketing campaignsMeasure the performance of your email marketing campaigns with Wix. The top section allows you to see at a glance how all your campaigns have performed over time, including if any sales have been attributed to that campaign.Click the Campaigns by drop-down to order all your campaigns by date, click rate, unique clicks or sales. You can also select a specific campaign to see how it performed.Tip:See which recipients clicked a link in your campaign but didn't purchase and re-target those people. Click Target potential customers under Unique clicks to create a contact segment of these leads specifically. Use this list to target potential customers in future email campaigns.If you want to edit or send a new email marketing campaign, click Create Email Campaign to go to the Email Marketing dashboard.Get a more in-depth look at your email marketing activities as well as definitions for each term in the Wix Analytics Email Marketing reports.Organic searchThe next section of the Marketing Overview shows the top queries people searched on Google where your site appeared in search results. An organic search result as defined by Google is a free listing in Google Search that appears because it is relevant to someone's search terms. The data in this section of the Marketing Overview is powered by Google Search Console.Note:The data on your site's Google search performance is taken from Google Search Console. Performance data from Google isn't available instantly. Some of the more recent data (e.g. in the last 72 hours) may not appear yet. Check the Google last reported data at the bottom of the Organic Search section for the latest. 
Filter your organic search data by:
Top search queries: See which search queries that show your site are getting the most impressions and clicks as well as their click-through-rate (CTR), and average position over time. Search queries by growth: Understand how different queries changed in the past month based on how your audience is searching. The green and red arrows next to each query display how significant the change was.
Note: You may not see 'search queries by growth' if you recently connected to Google Search Console, as the data needs time before a trend is detected. Top pages in search results: View which site pages appear the most in Google Search results as well as how your page ranking changes over time.Learn more about Wix Analytics SEO Reports. What does Google define as a click?Google counts a "click" as any click that takes someone away from any of Google Search's pages to a non-Google Search page. For example, Google counts a click if a visitor clicks your page on the All tab, the Images tab, or any other tab of Google Search. Google also counts a click if a visitor clicks your page in Google Discover on an Android device.Learn more about clicksWhat does Google define as an impression?An "impression" is when a user sees a link to your page in any of Google Search's pages. For example, this could mean they saw it in Google search results or in Google Discover on an Android device. The visitor does not need to click your link for the impression to count.Exactly when Google counts the impression is different in each type search result. On the All tab of Google Search, your page gets an impression as soon as a visitor opens the search results page where your site is listed.  However, on the Images tab of Google Search, more results load infinitely as the visitor scrolls down. In this case, your page may only gets an impression when it's actually visible in the results.Learn more about impressionsPaid ad campaignsThe final section of the Marketing Overview tracks your paid ad campaign activity.This section allows you to track all your paid marketing activities from across the internet in one place. See data from both paid Wix campaigns (e.g. Facebook Ads with Wix or Google Ads with Wix) as well as any external paid campaigns you are running on these and other platforms. To ensure we can track your paid campaign's performance, choose an option below and follow the instructions for connecting your social account. If you are running campaigns outside of Wix, you also need to create a UTM tracking link.I am running paid campaigns with Wix (Facebook Ads & Instagram Ads with Wix, Google Ads with Wix)If you are using Facebook Ads with Wix or Google Ads with Wix, Wix automatically tracks the sales and session data from the paid campaigns to the Marketing Overview. In order to also track the ad spend and cost-per-click directly from Facebook and/or Google, you need to connect the relevant social account.
Hover over the relevant platform (e.g. Google or Facebook) and click Connect.

Tip: You can also access this step by clicking Connected platforms under the Amount spent and CPC section. Follow the prompts to connect your account.I am running paid campaigns outside of WixIf you are running a paid campaign outside of Wix, you need to first complete two steps so we can get the most accurate data.
Connect to Facebook/Google: In order to view the Amount spent and CPC (cost-per-click) for your campaigns, make sure you have connected your relevant social account (Facebook and/or Google).
    
Click Connected platforms under Amount spent and CPC. Click Connect next to the relevant account.
 Follow the prompts to connect your account.   Create a UTM tracking link and add it as the destination URL of your external ad: In order to view the Sales and Sessions measures, you need to create a unique UTM tracking link from Wix and use it as the external ad's destination URL. Without this tracking link, Wix cannot find data from campaigns run outside of Wix.
    
Click Create a UTM tracking link.
 Fill out the relevant information including:
        
Adding your Wix site page URL (the page you want to open when the ad is clicked). Selecting a traffic source (e.g. Facebook, Google, other).
Note: If you select Facebook or Google, the remaining fields are automatically populated. (Optional) Adding your campaign ID and/or campaign name to get breakdowns by campaign.
Note: You will find this information inside the dashboard of the external platform you are running a campaign on (e.g. Google Ads).
Learn more about UTM tracking links.    Once the information is filled out, a unique tracking link appears at the bottom of the link builder. Click Copy to copy the link. Open the external ad platform (e.g. Google Ads) and paste the new tracking link as the destination URL in your ad.  Once you have connected your Facebook and/or Google account(s) and added a UTM tracking link for external campaigns, you will be able to see all available data at the top of the paid ad campaign section. Note: The data begins from the moment you added the tracking link to the ad.The bottom two sections allow you to filter your campaigns by different measures including Return on Ad Spend, sales, sessions, amount spent, and CPC. You can also see how your campaigns are performing over time.Tip:Filter your campaign performance by platform (e.g. Instagram, Facebook) by selecting an option at the top.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about the Wix Analytics Marketing Overview.What if I am running a paid campaign with Wix as well as outside of Wix? (E.g. Facebook Ads with Wix as well as Facebook Ads on Facebook).You can see the data from both campaigns as long as you follow the necessary steps to sync all the relevant information. Connect your Facebook/Google account(s) to the Marketing Overview to see the amount spent or cost-per-click (CPC) data of all available campaigns.Make sure to also follow the steps above in the "I am running paid campaigns outside of Wix" drop-down to add a UTM tracking link to your other campaigns run outside of Wix. This allows Wix to track the sales and sessions of these campaigns.I can't see data in paid ad campaign section even though I am running paid ads.The four main measures at the top of the paid ad campaign section (sales, sessions, amount spent and CPC) are collected from two different parameters. Depending on which measure is missing, make sure the right information is added:
I can't see Sales and Session data: Make sure have added a unique UTM tracking link from Wix as the external ad's destination URL. Learn how to create a UTM tracking link in the 'Paid ad campaign' section of this article. I can't see Amount spent or CPC data: Make sure you have connected your Facebook/Google account(s) to the Marketing Overview.

source_documents.title: Wix Automations: Creating a Multi-Action Automation
source_documents.content:
Wix Automations: Creating a Multi-Action Automation
This article refers to the previous automation builder.Multi-action automations are automations with a single trigger and multiple actions. These allow you to streamline communication with your site visitors, deliver the right information at the right time, and optimize your business processes.For example, you can create an automation that welcomes members logging in to your site with a chat message and then sends a follow-up email a few days later.To create a multi-action automation:
Create a new automation or edit an existing automation. Scroll down to the bottom of the automation editing screen and click + Add an Action.
Click your chosen action in the Action 2 section. Set up the action using the available options. Click the Timing section to expand it. Click the Choose a time to send this action drop-down to select when this follow-up action should be carried out:
    
Wait between actions: The action is performed after the previous action, after a period of time set by you. Click the up and down arrows to set the number and click the drop-down to choose between days, hours and minutes. Respond Immediately: The action is performed immediately after the previous action.   (Optional) Click + Add an Action and follow steps 3 - 6 to add any additional follow-up actions. Click Activate.Adding actions to existing automationsIf you add new actions to existing automations, these actions will only apply to instances triggered after you save your changes. For every instance already triggered (e.g. form submitted), these new actions will not be performed.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Adding Structured Data Markup to Wix Blog
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Adding Structured Data Markup to Wix Blog
Structured data markup and AMP (Accelerated Mobile Pages) are two methods that Google uses to help display the best search results to users. For example, Google uses markup to help decide which pages are added to some carousels. Google regularly crawls websites to gather information so they can present their users with the best possible search results. Markup helps site owners direct Google to information on your site. Google then may use this information to display rich results in search results. For example, Google may use markup to understand the date a blog post was published and may choose to display that date in search results. Note:
Markup is always enabled and requires a mandatory field, such as an image or logo. Without the field, you may receive notification emails from the Google Search Console to tell you that the mandatory field is missing. Follow the steps below to check the status of the mandatory field.  If markup is enabled and Google finds an error, you receive an email with an error or warning message. This does not mean that your Google ranking will be lowered, it only means that markup was not successfully added to your site. Try correcting the errors listed in the message.To check the status of the mandatory field:
Go to your SEO Dashboard. Select Go to SEO Settings under Tools and settings. Click Blog Posts. Click Edit next to Structured data markup. Note: If you see the message displayed in the image below, you need to update your business information. Make sure you add a logo as this is your mandatory field that is required in order for everything to be set up correctly. 6.  Click Save. Tips:When you’ve published your site with the new markup, you can test it with Google’s Structured Data Testing Tool

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Managing the Participant List for Your Classes
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Managing the Participant List for Your Classes
The Participants list lets you manage your sessions quickly and efficiently from the Booking Calendar. Keep track of who paid for a class session, who attended, who was a no-show, and more.In this article, learn more about: 
Adding or removing participants Marking attendance for a class Moving participants from one class session to another Updating your participants' payment status Contacting your participants Managing your participants' contact cards Viewing responses to custom fields in the Booking form Exporting the participant list for a classTip:You can also mark attendance for classes using the Wix app. Adding and removing class participantsYou can add new participants or edit an existing booking to update the number of people registered to a specific class session. To add or remove class participants:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Depending on what you want to do, follow the steps below: Add new participants
Click + Add Participant at the top right. Enter the participant details:
    
Name: Enter the participant's name.
Note: You can also click + Add Contact to add a new client.  Group of: Enter the total group members associated with the participant who are attending. How do you want to charge your client: Choose from the following options:
        
Charge with an invoice: Email an invoice to the client to get paid online.  Collect payment later: Charge the client at any time from the Manage Participants page or the Orders page in your site's dashboard.  Use client's plan: Redeem the session using the client's package or membership. Note: This option is only available if the client has already purchased a plan.  Use client's plan later: Redeem the session from the client's package or membership after they attend.  Mark as paid: Mark the session as paid (e.g., for clients who pay in person). This cannot be undone.   (Optional) Add to future sessions: Enable the toggle to add the client to future sessions of the class:
        
How often?: Choose the relevant frequency from the drop-down, for example, "Every 2 weeks". For: Choose how many times you want to book the client for the class based on the frequency you selected above. For example, "Every 2 weeks, 4 times". Show sessions: Click to see each of the upcoming class sessions, before confirming. Note: To remove a participant from a specific future session, click the Delete icon next to the relevant class.
     Click Save. You can also click Save & Add Another to save this participant and add another one.Remove participants (without cancellation and no-show fees)
Click the More Actions icon next to the participant you want to remove, then click Remove.  (Optional) Select the Notify participants with an email checkbox and add a message. Click Remove. 
Note: You can issue a refund through the Orders page in your site's dashboard.Remove participants (with cancellation and no-show fees)
Click the More Actions icon next to the participant you want to remove, then click Remove.  (Optional) Select the Apply cancellation fee checkbox to charge a cancellation fee. (Optional) Select the Notify participants with an email checkbox and add a message. Click Remove. 
 (Optional) Edit the cancellation fee.
Note: You cannot charge more than the fee stated in your policy. Click Confirm Fee & Continue. Click Collect Payment and choose how you want to charge the participant.
Note: For more details on collecting payment, see the Updating your participants' payment status section below.Added a waitlist for this class?Your class participant list shows two tabs, one for booked participants and another for those on the waitlist. Marking attendance for a classKeep track of everyone who attends your sessions, and those who can't make it, using the Participants list in your Booking Calendar.To mark attendance for a class session:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Choose who you want to mark attendance for:All participants
Select the Client checkbox at the top left of the list.  Click Check-in Individual participants
Under the Attendance column click the drop-down next to a participant.  Choose the relevant option:
    
Checked-In: The participant booked and came in for the session. No-Show: The participant booked the session but didn't show up. If relevant, you can click Apply a no-show fee to charge the participant for missing the session.
Note: This option is only available for classes that include cancellation and no-show fees in their booking policy.   Tip: Marking attendance regularly allows you to track your attendance statistics over time. Updating your participants' payment statusKeep track of which members have paid for a session using the Participants list in your Booking Calendar. Important:Once you mark a member as "Paid", the change cannot be undone. To update member payment statuses:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Click the Collect Payment drop-down next to the relevant client. Choose how you want to charge your client:Charge with pay linkInstantly request payments from contacts by sharing unique pay link URLs that allow them to make secure online payments.
Click Charge with credit card. Set up your pay link:
    
Link name: Enter a name for your pay link. Price: Enter the amount of money your pay link will charge your customer. (Optional) Description: Enter a description for your pay link. This should clearly summarize the reason for payment. Click Open settings:

(Optional) Set an expiration date: Enable the Set an expiration date toggle. Set a date when the link will expire and cannot be used. (Optional) Customize link: Set a Button color, edit Button text and upload a Link image.  (Optional, multi-payment only) Limit the number of payments: Enable the Limit the number of payments toggle to set the number of times the link can be used before it expires.
Note: On the left you'll see a preview of how your pay link will be displayed.     Click Create Link. Your link has been created. Choose what you want to do:
    
Copy Link: Copy the link to your clipboard. Send via email: Click Send Link to send your pay link to the participant's email.
Note: To send the pay link to a different email, click + Add Contact in the drop-down and enter a new email. QR Code: Click to generate a QR code. Customers can scan this code to access your pay link.  Charge card manuallyWhen you charge with a credit card, you have the option to make a partial payment or charge for the entire order. 
Click Charge with credit card. Choose if you want to charge the full amount or a partial amount:
    
Full payment: Enter the client's credit card details.  Partial payment: 

Select the Charge a custom amount checkbox.  Enter the relevant amount for the partial payment.
Note: The total amount due appears under the custom amount field.  Enter the client's credit card details.      Click Charge. 
Charge with invoiceYou can create invoices to request payment for services or to create a record for you and your clients. When you send the invoice to your client by email or as a link, they can pay for it online using any of your payment methods.
Click Charge with invoice.  Click Create Invoice.  Review the invoice details to make sure they're correct.  Choose what you want to do next:
    
Share Link: Create a shareable link that you can send to your client.
        
Click Copy Link.  Click Done.
Note: when you create the link to the invoice, it automatically marks the invoice as Sent.   Print: Print out a physical copy of the invoice for your offline records.  Collect Payment: Choose from the following options:
        
Charge with credit card: Charge a partial amount or the total value of the invoice.  Record payment: Choose this option to record full or partial payments for the invoice.
            
Enter the Amount received.  Enter the Payment date.  Select the relevant Payment method from the drop-down.  Click Record Payment.     Send via Email: Send the client their invoice via email. 
        
(Optional) Edit the email's subject line and / or message.   Click Send.

    Mark as paidYou can mark clients' class sessions as partially or fully paid. Note: Once you mark a class session as paid, the action cannot be undone.
Click Mark as paid.  Choose what you want to do:
    
Mark as paid: Click Mark as Paid. Mark a custom amount as paid:

Select the Mark a custom amount as paid checkbox.  Enter the amount.  Click Mark as Paid.

    Moving participants from one class session to anotherYou can move a participant to another session within the same class service at any time. The booking's original status, payment preferences and the associated order remain the same, the client just attends a different session of the class service. To move a participant from one class session to another:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant client. Click Reschedule. Click to select the relevant date.  Click to select the relevant session from the list available on that date. (Optional) Click the Notify client with an email checkbox to send email confirmation to the client.  Click Reschedule. Notes: 
If you offer the class sessions in different locations, you can select the relevant location from the drop-down above the calendar. 
 Rescheduling a class session does not affect the payment status. If the session has already been paid for or redeemed (if the client has a pricing plan), the rescheduled session will have the same payment status. If the session is unpaid, you can collect payment or redeem as usual. Contacting your class participantsUpdate your members about changes to an upcoming session or anything else they need to prepare beforehand. To contact your class participants: 
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Depending on who you want to contact, follow the steps below: Contact individual class participants
Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant client.  Click Send Message. Click the Message via drop-down and choose what type of message you want to send:
    
Chat: Send your client a chat message through your site. They can only see these messages when they log in to your site.  Email: Send your client an email using the address they provide when they sign up for your services.  SMS: Send your client an SMS message. You can only send an SMS via your business phone number. 
   Enter your message.  (Optional) Click the relevant icon to add Saved Replies , Payment Requests , Emojis , Attachments  and more. Learn more about replying to messages in Wix Inbox. Click the Send icon .Contact all class participants
Select the Client checkbox at the top to select all of the class participants.  Click Send Email at the top of the session's participant list.  Enter your message.  (Optional) Click the relevant icon to add Saved Replies , Payment Requests , Emojis , Attachments  and more. Learn more about replying to messages in Wix Inbox. Click the Send icon .


Note: If clicking the link doesn't open an email message, you must first define a default mail client. Tip: You can also contact participants using the Wix app.Managing your participants' contact cardsWhenever a new client books a service or interacts with your site (e.g. messages you, buys a product from your store), they're automatically added to your contact list. The contact card is a useful way to manage your clients by adding labels, notes, reminders and attachments like health forms. You can also create an invoice, book an appointment or even start a chat from their contact card. To manage your participants' contact cards:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage.  Click the relevant person's name to open their contact card.  Choose what you want to do next:Edit the client's details, notes, tasks and moreThe Contact Panel may vary depending on your site's features. You can drag the tabs to rearrange their order. Click here to learn more about editing your contacts. Click the Overview tab and choose what you want to edit:
Contact info: Update or edit the client's contact info. Bookings: View a client's upcoming bookings including the time, date, location and payment status of the session. Attachments: Upload and store any important files or documents associated with the client so you can view them any time.  Labels: Keep your contacts organized by adding labels, such as experience level or certifications. Every session a client books also adds a label to their contact card. Learn more about creating and using contact labels. Notes: Add any extra information about the client that you might need to refer to later. Only you see these notes. Tasks: Create and manage tasks for your contact. Set a due date for each task. Loyalty Points: Customers who are site members can redeem loyalty points for rewards. Learn more about managing your customers' loyalty points.  Workflows: Link a client to a workflow so you can track their progress.  Segments: Organize your contacts into segments to target the right people when sending an email campaign or reaching out to your audience. Learn more about creating a segment. Member info: Manage your site members and see details about your site members. You can manage them by add member roles and see their info. Tasks & Reminders: Add tasks for a client and set a completion date. Manage communication with the clientClick the Inbox tab to start a chat, or send an SMS, email, or Booking Service link so they can book their next session.


Tip: You can add Saved Replies , Payment Requests , Emojis , Attachments  and more to your messages. Learn more about sending messages in Wix Inbox. Tip:You can also access your clients' contact cards from your contact list. Viewing responses to custom fields in the Booking formIf you add custom questions to the booking form for a class, you can view client responses by clicking on their name on the list. Learn more about viewing Booking Form responses. Exporting the participant list for a classYou can export the participant list from your classes, so you can open it in Excel, share it using Google Docs, or print it out.Important:Exported files are in English only, even if your account is set to another other language.To export the participant list for a class:
Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant class in your calendar. Click Manage. Click the Export icon  in the top right, under + Add Participant. Choose what you want to export:
    
All: Export the entire participant list for the class. Filtered: Export a filtered version of the participant list for the class. For example, you can filter by unpaid payment status.  Selected: Export only the selected participants.   Click Export.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings Request: Offering Appointment Waitlists
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings Request: Offering Appointment Waitlists
Currently, it is not possible to offer a waitlist for your appointment slots. By offering an appointment waitlist, clients could join when their desired spot is unavailable, and you can contact them directly once a spot opens up or offer them an alternative appointment slot.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings Request: Setting Separate Video Conferencing Availability
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings Request: Setting Separate Video Conferencing Availability
Currently, it is not possible to add separate availability for video conferencing appointments only. For example, businesses offering consultation services both physically and virtually on different days or hours, cannot set separate availability settings for each.Workaround:You can add virtual meetings as an additional location and set the staff hours accordingly. We do not recommend this option for businesses with multiple physical locations, as it may complicate scheduling management and reporting.We are always working to update and improve our products, and your feedback is greatly appreciated.

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: The Essential Checklist for Beauty Business Owners
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: The Essential Checklist for Beauty Business Owners
Wix Bookings is a versatile online scheduling platform tailored to meet the needs of beauty industry professionals (e.g. beauty and nail salons, spas, skin and hair therapy clinics). Manage your bookings and staff, streamline your day-to-day operations, and offer great customer service. This allows you to spend more time focusing on your business and your clients, and less time on administrative tasks.Build and grow your online presence
Beauty templates - Wix Bookings features a range of custom templates designed for beauty businesses: Hair, Makeup & Cosmetics, Wellness and more. AI site builder - By answering a few short questions, the Wix AI website builder creates a site tailored to your beauty business, and your specific needs. Link in Bio - Make a free “Link in Bio” page that reflects your brand's look & feel, and use it on your social channels to drive schedule bookings. Members app - Make scheduling appointments and managing bookings easier for your clients with the Spaces by Wix members app. Branded app - Get your own branded app on the app store with a paid branded app.Set up your business for successAllow clients to book services anytime, anywhere with customizable, responsive booking pages. Boost sales by enabling multi-service appointments, and by offering dynamic pricing. Simplify staff management with features like customizable working hours, calendar syncing, and staff permissions. 
Online Bookings - Let your clients book appointments at any time and from anywhere using your customized booking pages. Multi-service - Grow sales by allowing clients to book multiservice appointments.  Booking policies - Set a booking and cancellation policy for each service separately. This allows you to keep your most in-demand services as fully booked as possible. You can also set your appointment bookings as "request to book". Resources - Create resources like rooms, stations, or chairs and assign them to services that require them so they also get booked when clients make their appointments. Multi-location - Add and manage all of your business locations. Dynamic pricing per staff - Set different pricing for each staff member. Conferencing link - Let every staff member connect their own video conferencing accounts. Optimize your online and in-person payments with Wix BookingsSimplify your payment processes with Wix Bookings. Offer flexible options like Afterpay and streamline in-person transactions with our POS solutions. Simplify invoicing, request payments with pay links, offer convenient methods like Credit Card on file, and more.Get paid online
Online payments - Let your clients book and pay in advance on your website with Wix Payments.  Wix also supports a variety of payment providers, based on your preferences and location.  Afterpay - Allow customers to pay in installments with Afterpay.Get paid in person, or after the service
Retail POS - Make your phone a point of sale, so clients can accept payment for services that have already been booked.  Mobile POS - Use your phone as a point-of-sale (POS). CC on file - Save clients' credit card details and charge for future bookings in a more convenient way. Charge manually with cc details - Accept payments by typing in the customers' credit card details. This works great for accepting bookings over the phone. Pay links - Instantly request payments from contacts by sharing unique pay link URLs that allow them to make secure online payments. Share pay links via email, social media, SMS, and other channels. You can also create and send QR codes as pay links. Invoices - Create and send professional invoices in seconds. Simply email or text your invoice so your clients can make payment.Limit no shows by charging deposits
Charge deposits - If you prefer not to charge your clients the full service fee upfront, you can accept an initial deposit fee at the time of booking, and receive the rest in person or with an automation to complete the payment after the service is provided.Streamline your day-to-day business managementManage staff, schedules, appointments, and more from anywhere. Stay organized by blocking holiday hours, tracking attendance, and managing meeting notes.Manage your staff members
Set up your staff members - Add your staff to your site, and give them different roles and permissions so they can handle their clients and bookings. Working hours - Set the working hours of each employee and create an easy-to-manage work schedule. Sync staff members' personal calendars - Allow staff members to sync their personal calendars with your site's Booking Calendar to keep your availability as up-to-date as possible. Holiday mode - You can block off hours for yourself or for staff members on your Wix Bookings calendar. During those blocked time slots, customers will not be able to book appointments. Payroll management - Set pay rates for your staff and calculate gross pay for payroll. Choose from a flat rate per service, per participant, or a percentage rate based on total session price.Manage your bookings
Calendar - With one click, easily view all your service details, and quickly review each employee's upcoming schedule to check their availability. Choose the view that is most convenient for you by using the various filters in the Booking Calendar. Attendance management - Using the Bookings calendar, you can keep track of who pays and who attends services at your business. You can also cancel sessions and issue refunds if needed.  Meeting notes - Whether you want to jot down information about an upcoming booking or keep track of what happened in a service you already provided, you can easily add a note to your appointments and classes. This is great for creating rapport with regular clients. Booking list - Use the Booking List in your site's dashboard to track and review all booking activity on the site. You can also add different filters and search parameters to review past, present and future bookings. Wix app - Run your business from your mobile device while you're on-the-go. The Wix app allows you to keep track of your business from anywhere, including: scheduling services, processing payments, marketing, form management & analytics.Get booked from anywhereSet up the way you share your services on social media using the Booking Channels tab in your site's dashboard.
Add Instagram and Facebook 'Book' buttons. Get booked directly from Google search with Reserve With Google. Attract more clients by integrating ClassPass with your Bookings business.  Shareable links - Create shareable links to your service pages, memberships, and packages, to make it easier for your clients to book your services.Maximize sales and boost revenue with eCommerce toolsExpand your online sales with Wix's eCommerce tools. From products to memberships, Wix Stores offers essential features like cart functionality and digital gift cards, helping you boost revenue and customer satisfaction.
Manage your online store selling services & products - Integrating Wix Stores with your Bookings site gives you all the tools you need to create a sleek, professional online store and grow your eCommerce business. Cart - Clients can add multiple services and products to their cart before checking out. Gift cards - Boost business by offering digital gift cards on your site. Pricing plans & Memberships - Increase customer loyalty by offering your clients memberships and packages using Wix Pricing Plans. Clients enjoy reduced rates, and you benefit from a more predictable income stream. Classes & courses - Take your business to the next level and offer beauty classes and courses. You can offer live online or in-person classes & courses or pre-recorded services using Online Programs. Upsell & Cross-sell - Upsell products in client’s checkout with Reconvert (3rd party app).Improve your branding and reach with a range of marketing toolsEnhance your brand visibility and attract more customers with Wix's diverse marketing tools, including SEO optimization, blogging, email campaigns, and social media advertising.SEO and Content marketing
SEO - Optimize your site ranking in search engine results by using Wix SEO tools. Blog - Build your brand by creating a blog, let your clients like, comment, and follow blog posts.Email marketingEmail marketing - Use Wix Email Marketing to create, send and manage professional email marketing campaigns.Social media & advertising
Social post - Easily create and customize your post for Social Media Marketing, and quickly share it with your audience on your selected social channels (available on desktop & mobile).  Google Ads - Google Ads with Wix allows you to create a campaign directly from your site's dashboard. Facebook & Instagram ads - Create a dynamic ad campaign on Facebook and Instagram with Facebook Ads with Wix.Branding
Logo maker - Create a unique brand logo in minutes with our AI logo generator. Business card maker - Create a professional business card with the Wix Business Card Maker. Get your personalized design delivered anywhere in the world. QR code generator - Create custom QR codes for free, and use them to drive online traffic to your site, share useful information and increase your sales. Landing page builder - Create effective landing pages that generate traffic, leads and sales for your product launches, promotions and other business needs.Additional marketing tools
Coupons - Offer your clients discount coupons to promote loyalty and increase bookings. Send SMS marketing campaigns with Omnisend (3rd party app).Offer a seamless client experienceAutomatically create client profiles, send client notifications, and save notes and client data all in one place.
CRM - Streamline your customer relationship management and communication with our range of CRM tools. You can also review your appointment, sales & activity history with individual clients.  Attach contracts, documents, or other files. Import contact lists. Wix Inbox - Communicate with your clients, reply to messages from your website chat, app, or business email all from one place. Forms - Quickly select a template or build your custom form from scratch. Send legal waivers, intake forms & surveys to your customers and their responses will be automatically saved.Notifications
Email reminders - Make sure clients know exactly when their sessions are taking place.  SMS reminders - Reduce no-shows with SMS reminders to help keep your business as fully booked as possible. Automations
Bookings automations - Automations can help you to stay in touch with your clients and make sure they come back for more sessions, pay for their sessions, and more, for example:
    
Auto Reminder for “It's time for your next haircut”. Automatically Send Payment Requests to Clients.   SMS advanced automations with Omnisend (3rd party app). WhatsApp automations with WhatsApp notifications by MKP (3rd party app).Loyalty programs
Loyalty programs - Offer your returning site members rewards by creating a loyalty program.Make informed business decisions with reports and analyticsGain insights about your site and make smart business decisions with Wix Analytics reports. Choose how to view your data, customize your reports to focus on data that interests you, and create new custom reports from scratch.
Sales reports - Your sales reports by Wix Analytics help you to analyze all the payments that go through your site. Bookings - Discover helpful data in Wix Bookings Analytics Reports, such as how your bookings have increased over time, your most popular services, and who your top clients are. Bookings and Staff Reports allow you to review your business performance over time.  View data about every booking you've received within a set date range. View data on staff members and the sessions they are running within a selected time period. Marketing & SEO - The Wix Analytics Marketing reports give you an in-depth look at how your marketing efforts are impacting your business. Traffic reports - With Wix Analytics traffic reports, you can find out how visitors find and navigate around your site. Behavior - Wix Analytics Behavior reports show you how people are navigating through your site and what actions they are taking. Stores - Keep track of product inventory, and see what your highest selling products are, including any product variants.  Memberships & Pricing plans allow you to generate more reliable revenue and foster customer loyalty. Accounting - View all financial figures you need for your bookkeeping.Stay on top of your accounting with third-party integrationsAutomate your accounting with several third-party integrations and Wix Bookings. 
Connect to QB with Quickbooks app (3rd party app). Connect to Xero with Xero app (3rd party app).

source_documents.title: Wix Bookings: Uninstalling Zoom
source_documents.content:
Wix Bookings: Uninstalling Zoom
As your needs change, you may wish to switch your video conferencing (VC) service provider from Zoom to another app such as Google Meet or Skype. Important:If you disconnect your main VC account, VC links won't appear for any sessions, even if your staff have their own individual VC accounts.To uninstall the Zoom app:

 Select the shape of your gallery images, and change the overall layout of your gallery.

source_documents.title: Wix Groups: Creating Subscription Based Posts
source_documents.content:
Wix Groups: Creating Subscription Based Posts
Monetize your group by creating exclusive content for members with active pricing plans. For example, offer a series of post-based tutorials visible only to paying members. When people see one of these exclusive posts, they'll see an "Exclusive Post" label at the top. People who are members and have that specific pricing plan will be able to read it. If they're not members, they'll see a "Subscribe Now" button.Before you begin:
Make sure you add Pricing Plans to your site. Connect a payment method to get paid for your subscription plans. In this article, learn more about: 
Creating subscription based posts Converting an existing post to a subscription-based post Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Creating subscription based postsWant to create exclusive content that's only available to paying members? Give extra value to paying group members by composing subscription-based posts. Comprise posts that have a high-quality, unique content which your audience finds beneficial. For example, tutorials, exclusive videos, downloadable resources, and more.DashboardWix app
Go to Groups in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant group. Click Posts. Click Create Post. Write your post.  Click Monetize at the top left.
Choose the relevant option:
    
Create a new pricing plan: Click +Create Plan and set up your new plan. Connect an existing pricing: Enable the toggle next to the relevant plan.   Click Post at the top right.
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Groups. Tap Manage Posts.  Tap + Create a Post. Tap the relevant group. Write your post.  Tap the Monetize icon . Tap Connect next to the relevant Pricing Plan.  Tap Done.  Tap Post. Converting an existing post to a subscription-based postIf you already have a post that you'd like to make exclusive, you can turn it into a subscription post. Non-subscribers can see the pricing plan cost to access the exclusive post. They can also view the content type (e.g., images, videos, files), reactions, and comments.DashboardWix app
Go to Groups in your site's dashboard. Click the relevant group. Click Posts. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant post.
Click Connect Pricing Plan.  Choose the relevant option:
    
Create a new pricing plan: Click +Create New Plan and set up your new plan. Connect an existing pricing plan: Enable the toggle next to the relevant plan.   Click Done.
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Groups. Tap Manage Posts.  Tap the More Actions icon  next to the relevant post. Tap Edit. Tap the Monetize icon . Tap Connect next to the relevant Pricing Plan. Tap Done. Tap Update.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about subscription-based posts.Can I connect multiple pricing plans to one subscription post?Yes. You can connect as many pricing plans as you want to a post.Can members create subscription-based posts?No. Only group admins can create subscription-based posts.How can I manage my pricing plans?You can manage your pricing plans from your site's dashboard. Go to the Pricing Plans section to create, edit, or delete plans as needed. Ensure your plans are clearly described so members know what they are subscribing to.Can I track which members have subscribed to my exclusive content?Yes, you can view all your group members in your site's dashboard. You can also track your subscribers to see who has subscribed to which plans.Can I see analytics for my exclusive posts?Yes, you can view group analytics to see how your exclusive posts are performing. You can also check your Pricing Plans analytics reports. Use these insights to improve your content strategy.

source_documents.title: Wix Pro Gallery Request: Keeping the Title and Description When Replacing an Image
source_documents.content:
Wix Pro Gallery Request: Keeping the Title and Description When Replacing an Image
Currently, replacing an image in Pro Gallery deletes the previous image and adds a new image without retaining the title and description. source_documents.title: Wix Restaurants Request: Adding a Cutlery Option to Online Orders
source_documents.content:
Wix Restaurants Request: Adding a Cutlery Option to Online Orders
Currently, it is not possible to automatically add a cutlery option to all online orders so that customers can indicate that they do not need you to include cutlery with their order. As a workaround, you can add cutlery as a deselection option to each dish. source_documents.title: Wix Restaurants: Adding Modifiers
source_documents.content:
Wix Restaurants: Adding Modifiers
Let customers personalize their orders with modifier groups. Modifiers allow you to add options to menu items, like toppings on a pizza or dressing for a salad. Decide on the number of modifiers customers can choose and determine if a selection is required.Before you begin:Make sure you have the new online ordering app installed to add modifiers to your menu.In this article, learn more about:
Adding modifiers to a menu item Examples of common modifier combinations Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)Adding modifiers to a menu itemOrganize your menu modifiers into groups to make customization simple for your customers. Set limits, decide which options are free, and add extra charges for premium choices. Use these groups across your menu for easy management.Before you begin:Plan your modifiers in advance. List the groups, their contents, and related dishes. For example, outline pizza toppings, their prices, and how many customers can add.To add modifiers to a menu item:
Go to Menus (New) in your site's dashboard. Click Manage next to the relevant menu. Click on a menu item or add a new one. Click the Modifiers tab. Click + Add Modifier Group. Choose the relevant option:
    
Select an existing modifier group. Then, click Add to Item and Save. Create a new modifier group:
        
Click + New Modifier Group. Enter a modifier group name (e.g. "Dips" or "Toppings"). Add the first choice under Modifiers (e.g. "Salsa" or "Mushrooms"). (Optional) Enter a price (e.g. $0.5). (Optional) Click the checkbox under Preselect to set default modifiers for customers. (Optional) Click + Add Modifier to add more modifiers.     Decide if customers are required to make a selection under Modifier group settings:
    
Optional: Customers can place the order without making a selection. Set the minimum and maximum number of modifiers that customers can add. Required: Customers need to select 1 or more options to proceed with their order. Set the minimum and maximum number of modifiers that customers can add.   Click Save & Add.
Note: Once you create a modifier group, you can add it to any menu item and don't need to create it again. Click Save. (Optional) Click + New modifier group to create additional modifier groups. Examples of common modifiers settingsWe collected some of the most common scenarios for which you'd want to use modifiers. Search for the combination or setting you would need. The selection is optionalYou can make a modifier group optional if you want to leave it open for the customer to decide. In some cases, customers may not need to customize the menu item they chose.  How many options can customers choose?The required modifier group settingsHow it looks liveUnlimited selectionOptionalMinimum: NoneMaximum: No limitJust 1Optional
Minimum: None
Maximum: 1Up to 2Optional Minimum: None Maximum: 2The selection is requiredYou can make a modifier group required if it's necessary for the customer to state their preference(s). How many options can customers choose?The required modifier group settingsHow it looks liveUnlimited selectionMandatory
Minimum: 1
Maximum: No limitJust 1Mandatory
Minimum: 1
Maximum: 1Specific number (e.g. 2)Mandatory
Minimum: 2
Maximum: 2Range of selection (e.g. 4) Mandatory
Minimum: 1
Maximum: 4FAQsClick a question below to learn more about modifiers.How many modifier groups can I add?You can add up to 20 modifier groups, and up to 25 modifiers in each group. Once you create a modifier group, you can use it for any menu item.Tip: If you have over 10 modifiers in a group, we recommend setting the maximum selection to up to 10. This ensures all modifiers appear on the page.Can I mark a modifier as 'out of stock'?Yes. You can mark individual modifiers as 'out of stock.' When you do, the modifier is grayed out on your menu and customers cannot select it.
Go to Manage Items in your site's dashboard. Click the Modifiers tab.  Click the Stock drop-down next to the relevant modifier and select Out of stock.
How do modifiers look on my menu?Modifiers allow your customers to choose various options from your menu's offerings by presenting them with grouped lists of selection.You can set the modifiers so customers only choose 1 of the options (e.g. degree of doneness, Vegan friendly, etc.) This adds an instruction saying, "Choose one" next to the modifier name ("Crispiness Level" in the screenshot below).You can also allow customers to select multiple options (e.g. toppings on a pizza, side dishes). If you limit the selection amount, the relevant instruction automatically appears, for example "Choose up to X", or "Choose between X - Y".Tip: If you mark a modifier group as required, customers see an asterisk (*) next to the selection.Will modifiers be shown on my menu? Modifiers are exclusive to the online ordering app and will not be visible on the menus app.

source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Editing and Customizing Images
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Editing and Customizing Images
Once you add images to a site, you can use a wide range of options to customize and edit them. Adjust image sizes, crop them and set their focal points so the relevant areas are always displayed, regardless of the screen size.You can also edit with Photo Studio, and add watermarks for copyright protection. In this article, learn how to:
Choose the image's fit mode Crop an image Set the focal point Mask the image with a shape Edit an image with Photo Studio Add a watermark for copyright protectionTip:Keep an image visible as visitors scroll up and down the page by setting its position to Pinned or Sticky. Choosing the image's fit modeIn the Studio Editor, every image has a bounding box that acts like a responsive container. These are the blue edges that you see around the image. You can choose how the image is displayed within the bounding box (e.g. Fill, Fit).To choose the image's fit mode:
Select the relevant image.  Click the Settings icon .  Select an option from the Display mode drop-down:Fill bounding boxThe image fills the bounding box so there aren't any empty areas, while still maintaining its original aspect ratio.If the image aspect ratio doesn't match the bounding box proportions, parts of the image are cropped out in the process. For example, when fitting a rectangular image into a square, the sides are cropped to fit that shape.  Fit to bounding boxThe entire image is shown inside the bounding box. If the image aspect ratio doesn't match the bounding box proportions, the image shrinks so it's fully displayed.The image is centered inside the box, which may create empty spaces like in the example below:Keep image ratioThe image width is fixed to the bounding box, while the height adjusts automatically to match the image's original aspect ratio.  This is a great option for non-symmetrical layouts where you want to show images in different heights, like in the Repeater below:   Note: This option is not available for stretched images. If you want to select this option, unstretch the image first.Working with breakpoints:The display mode you choose for the image applies to all breakpoints. Cropping an imageYou can choose how an image is cropped for each breakpoint. This allows you to further customize the image to suit your specifications, and provide an ideal experience for visitors on all devices.To crop an image:
Click the relevant breakpoint at the top of the Studio Editor. Select the image. Click the Crop icon . Customize the crop to your needs. Click Apply.Tip:If you want to uncrop your image, you can reset it by clicking the Settings icon , then Reset Image.Setting the image focal pointYou can choose the image focal point for each breakpoint. This allows you to select which part of the image is visible when it's resized for different breakpoints on different screen sizes. Tip:Whenever a dominant face is detected, we automatically set it as the focal point of the image, however, you can change or adjust the focal point as needed. To set the image focal point:
Click the relevant breakpoint at the top of the editor. Select the image. Click the Focal Point icon . Select the area of the image that you want to remain visible when it's resized.Masking an image with a shapeImage masks allow you to easily crop images into different shapes, giving you the flexibility to fit them seamlessly into the design. Choose from thousands of unique designs or upload your own SVG file. To mask an image:
Select the relevant image. Click the Mask icon . Choose the shape you want:
    
Explore the different shapes available in the panel. Click the Add icon  to browse through more designs or upload your own file.    (Optional) Make the image fit the shape's original aspect ratio by clicking Reset to shape's ratio
Note: This might resize the image.Changed your mind?Click the square shape at the top of the panel. This removes any mask previously applied to the image.Editing an image with Wix Photo StudioUse the Wix Photo Studio to create beautiful images without leaving the Editor. The Photo Studio allows you to customize images that you've already uploaded and saves the newly edited version to the Media Manager.There are a variety of editing options available, such as filters, rotation, and overlays, so you can revamp any image on the spot. Tip:You can also edit images directly from the Media Manager by clicking Crop & Edit under the thumbnail image.To edit an image:
Select the relevant image in the Editor. Click the Settings icon . Click Adjust. (In the Photo Studio) Edit the image using the available options. Click Save.What's next?The newly edited version is automatically replaced on all breakpoints, as the Wix Photo Studio makes changes to the image source. However, changes done on the canvas (to the image design or crop) still only apply to the current breakpoint. Adding a watermark for copyright protectionProtect images on the site by adding watermark text in the Photo Studio. The text can be designed and customized to suit your client, and cannot be removed from the file if downloaded.To add a watermark to an image:
Select the image in the Editor. Click the Settings icon . Click Adjust. (In the Photo Studio) Click Text under Add An Element. Browse the text styles and click to add one to the image. Type your watermark message. (Optional) Click Design to customize the text. Click Save.
