source_documents.title: Studio Editor: Creating Sticky Elements and Sections
source_documents.content:
Studio Editor: Creating Sticky Elements and Sections
Make a section or an element stick to the page as visitors scroll up and down. When the element or section reaches the visitor's viewport, it sticks to the top, bottom or both. You can set the offset, which is the distance from the top or bottom. 
Go to our Wix Studio Academy to check out additional Wix Studio webinars, tutorials, and courses.In this article, learn more about:
Making an element or section sticky Removing the sticky position Useful tutorialsDid you know?You can add a header scroll effect to change the way it looks as visitors scroll up and down. For example, make the header change colors on scroll, or move it out of the way to help visitors focus on the page.Applying the sticky position to an element or section
Select the relevant section or element. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Scroll down to Position. Select Sticky from the Position type drop-down. Choose where the section/element sticks to: Top, Bottom, or Bottom and top. (Optional) Enter an offset value to create space above or below.Note about the DOM order:By default, the page's DOM order, including the section order, is automatically organized. If you want a "sticky" section to appear above others in the DOM, right-click the section, select Arrange and Bring to Front.Removing the sticky positionYou can always revert elements and sections back to the default position. This means they no longer stick to the screen when reaching the viewport, they stay in their position.To remove the sticky position:
Select the relevant section or element. Click the Open Inspector icon  at the top right of the editor.
Scroll down to Position. Select Default from the Position type drop-down.Useful tutorialsThere are so many interesting effects you can create with sticky elements and sections. Check out these videos from the Wix Studio Academy and explore your options:
How we built the Wix Studio homepage Create a sticky sidebar with no code Create a half sticky, half scrolling design Add motion and depth will scroll, animations and interactions

source_documents.title: Wix Apps: Optimizing Your Instagram Feed App
source_documents.content:
Wix Apps: Optimizing Your Instagram Feed App
With the Wix Instagram Feed app, you can do much more than just display images. You can also leverage features such as, boosting likes and comments, seamlessly adding Instagram videos, and managing links within your feed. This all helps to create a more interactive and polished experience for your visitors.In this article, learn more about:
Boosting engagement Using videos on your feed Deleting linksBoosting engagementThe Instagram Feed app by Wix is a powerful tool to drive engagement directly from your website. Displaying your feed helps visitors interact with your Instagram posts, leading to increased likes, comments, and followers. You can enhance this engagement by ensuring your posts have compelling visuals, engaging captions, and consistent updates. To encourage user interaction, make it easy for site visitors to like your posts and follow your Instagram account directly from your site.When your site visitors click on an image in your Instagram Feed app, a pop-up appears. Visitors can click the pop-up image or username to go to your Instagram. There, they can like or comment on the image or follow you.Using videos on your feedWith the new features of Wix’s Instagram Feed app, you can seamlessly display Instagram videos on your site. Videos are a great way to capture attention and convey more engaging content compared to static images. Once connected, your Instagram videos will automatically appear in your feed, alongside images, giving your website a dynamic, multimedia presence. This not only boosts engagement but also helps create a visually appealing, interactive experience for your visitors. Learn how to add videos on InstagramNote:
If can take some time for your video to appear in your Instagram Feed gallery after you post it. It is not currently possibly to display Reels in the Instagram Feed app. Vote for this featureDeleting links in your Instagram FeedYou can delete any links that you no longer need from your Instagram Feed posts at any time. You can delete links from your desktop or your mobile device. Important:
Links that you added through the Instagram Feed app on your site must be deleted from your site.  Links that you added through the Instagram app on your mobile device must be deleted from your mobile device.DesktopMobile Device
Click the Instagram feed app in your Editor. Click Manage Links. Click to select the relevant post. Click the More Actions icon  on the relevant link. Click Delete. Click Yes, Delete. Click Done.
Open the Instagram app on your mobile device. Go to your profile. Select the post that you want to edit.  Tap the menu in the top right corner. Select Edit. Delete the link from the caption.  Tap X to save.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Adding Profile Pages for Your Blog Writers
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Adding Profile Pages for Your Blog Writers
When you add Wix Blog to your site, you can choose to also add a Member's Area if you don't already have one. A Member's Area lets your site members access features including the ability to login, create a public profile, and comment on blog posts. Learn more about the Member's AreaYou can also use a Member's Area to create dedicated profile pages for your Blog Writers to help your readers get to know them. You can customize the information that's displayed on the profile pages such as name, bio, image, and recent posts that they've written.Before you start, you need to:
Add Wix Blog to your site Add a Member's Area if your site doesn't have oneStep 1 | Select who has profile pagesYou can choose to let only site members who you have set as Blog Writers or as managed writers have profile pages on your site, or let every member have a profile page. Select your preferred option in the Member Pages settings on your site's Editor. To select who has profile pages:
Go to Member Pages in your Editor.Wix Editor | Show me how
Click Pages ﻿ on the left side of the Editor. ﻿Click Member Pages.﻿ Editor X | Show me how
Click Pages ﻿ at the top of Editor X. ﻿Click Profile under Wix Members Area.2.  Click the More Actions icon  next to Profile.3.  Click Settings.4.  Under Members' Profiles, select who has profile pages:
Only Blog Writers: Your Blog Writers have profiles, but your site members do not.  Blog Writers and Members: Both writers and site members have profiles. 5.  Click Publish, or save your site. Step 2 | Customize your Blog Writers' profilesEach profile page for your Blog Writers can include information such as their display name, title, an About section, and any recent posts that they have written. You can customize your own profile on your live site or your dashboard, and customize the profiles of your writers in your dashboard. Learn how to customize:Blog Writers' profiles from your dashboard
Go to Blog in your site's dashboard. Click Writers. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant writer.  Select Edit. 
 Customize the writer's profile image under Profile picture.
    
Click the Add Image icon  to add a profile picture for the writer, or  Click the Replace icon  to change an existing image. Click the Delete icon  to remove an existing image.   Enter the writer's name under Name.  Click Add Cover Image to add a background image that's displayed at the top of the writer's profile. Scroll down to Additional Info.  (Optional) Add a first name, last name, email address, and phone number for the writer.
Note: By default, these are not displayed on the profile page. Click the Visibility icon  beside any field to make the field visible on the profile. Enter information about the writer in the text box under About.  Customize the URL of the writer's profile under Profile Link. Click Save. Your own profile from your live site
Go to your Profile page on your live site. Log in with the email address associated with your Wix account. Click your profile image and select an image from your computer to update it. Click Edit Profile.  Customize the name that's shown on your profile under Display Name. Click Update Info.  Click the About text box. Enter information about yourself in the text box.  Click Publish. Publish your site to view the changes.  Want to change how your profile looks?
Go to your site's Editor to customize the layout of your profile pages.  If you need to add extra information that's not covered by the existing fields, you can add your own custom fields.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Customizing Your Blog Text (Fonts and Color)
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Customizing Your Blog Text (Fonts and Color)
You can customize text styles, such as fonts style, size, and color, that suit your blog's style. This helps you create a unique and consistent look that matches your brand, making your blog more engaging for your readers.For example, if you run a travel blog, you can use vibrant colors and playful fonts to convey a sense of adventure and excitement, making your content more appealing to your audience.In this article learn more about:
Customizing default text styles for posts in blog feeds Customizing default text styles for the Post page (single post view) Customizing text styles within a specific post Customizing default text styles for blog feedsYour blog feed displays a list of posts (either all posts or specific ones that you choose) and allows readers to scroll through and select the post they want to read. Make sure to choose a text style that's easy to read when scrolling.To set default text style for your feeds:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Go to your Blog page:
    
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click Blog Pages. Click your Blog page under Blog Pages.   Click the Blog element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click Posts. Click the tabs to choose which feed you want to design:
    
All Posts feed: This is your main post feed. It displays all of your posts or specific posts that you've selected. You can customize the colors and fonts of the text, choose the color of the text on hover, and adjust the overlay (the semi-transparent background). Category feed: This feed shows a list of all your blog categories. Select the colors and fonts of the text, choose what color the text appears on hover and customize the borders and backgrounds.  
Go to your editor. Go to your Blog page:
    
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click your Blog page under Blog Pages.   Click the Blog element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click Posts. Click the tabs to choose which feed you want to design:
    
All Posts feed: This is your main post feed. It displays all of your posts or specific posts that you've selected. You can customize the colors and fonts of the text, choose the color of the text on hover, and adjust the overlay (the semi-transparent background). Category Feed: This feed shows a list of all your blog categories. Select the colors and fonts of the text, choose what color the text appears on hover and customize the borders and backgrounds.  Customizing a default text style for the Post pageThe Post page displays the full blog post. It's a dynamic page, meaning the design remains the same, no matter what post you open. Make sure to choose a font that's easily readable for longer paragraphs of text. The text style you set here applies to all of your blog posts, unless you override it while writing the post itself.To set a default text style for your Post page:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Go to your Post page:
    
Click Pages & Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click Blog Pages. Click Post.   Click the Post Page element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click Text Style & Color. Adjust the colors and fonts of the paragraph (main body) and heading text.
Go to your editor. Go to your Post page:
    
Click Pages  on the left side of the editor. Click Post under Blog Pages.   Click the Blog Post element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click Text Style & Color. Adjust the colors and fonts of the paragraph (main body) and heading text.Customizing text styles within a specific postBy default, your posts use the text styles that you set for the Blog Feeds and Post page. However, you can override these settings for a specific post, or for a specific paragraph or word within a post. This is useful if you want to highlight a specific phrase or section.To set the text style within a post:
Go to Blog in your site's dashboard. Click + Create New Post or click an existing post. Highlight the text you want to style. Customize the text using the options in the text editing toolbar.

source_documents.title: Wix Blog: Customizing Your Blog Feed
source_documents.content:
Wix Blog: Customizing Your Blog Feed
Welcome your readers to a captivating blog feed where they can scan through your latest posts and select the ones they want to read. Offer them the convenience of choosing by category, allowing them to zero in on their preferred topics. Customize both the blog and category feeds to match your site's design, providing a consistent and appealing visitor experience.In this article:
Choosing what info to show on your feed Changing the layout of your feed Customizing the design of your feedNote:This article refers to customizing your blog feed. You can also customize the post page that which readers see when they open a specific post.Choosing what info to show on your feedCustomize what information your readers see in the blog or category feeds. Decide whether to provide more context, such as estimated reading time or author name, or opt for a more streamlined look by hiding any extra details.To choose what info you want to show:
Click the Blog page in your Editor.   Click Settings. Click the Display tab. Select or deselect the checkboxes to show or hide info on the feed. (Editor X only) Enable the Category labels toggle to display your categories at the top of the feed.  (Editor only) Click Blog Menu to choose what appears on the menu:
    
Click the Show Blog Menu toggle to show or hide the menu at the top of the feed:
        
Enabled: Select or deselect the checkboxes to choose what info you want to show on the menu. Disabled: The menu does not appear at the top of the feed.     Click Social Sharing to choose which social icons you want to show.
    
Click the Enabled Social Sharing toggle to show or hide the social icons:
        
Enabled: Select or deselect the checkboxes to choose which icons you want to show on the feed. Disabled: The social icons do not appear on the feed.    Changing the layout of your feedCustomize the arrangement of your posts in the feed to perfectly suit your vision. Choose from a variety of options, including post and image size, placement, and loading style, to create a visually stunning and cohesive blog.Tip:You can have a different layout for each of your feeds. For example, you might choose a Side-by-Side style for your All Posts feed and the Editorial layout for your category feed.To change the layout of your feed:
Click the Blog page in your Editor. Click Settings. Click the Layout tab. Click the tabs at the top to choose which feed you want to customize:
    
All Posts Feed: This is your main blog feed which displays all of your posts. Category Feed: This feed displays your blog categories so visitors can choose a specific topic.   Select a preset layout under Choose a layout. Customize the layout further using the options available.Note:Each layout has its own customization options. Click the available layouts to see what options are available. Customizing the design of your feedTailor the colors and fonts on your feed to align with your site and brand. The design options vary based on the selected layout, so take the time to review the available options and select the one that best suits your needs.To customize the design of your feed:
Click the Blog page in your Editor. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Choose what element you want to design and customize it using the options available:
    
Blog Menu: Select the colors and fonts used in the menu at the top of your blog feed. Posts: Select the colors and fonts used in the main blog feed and category feed. Category Label: Select the colors, fonts and style of the category label which appears on the blog post to show what category it belongs to. This option is only available if you enabled Category Label in the Display settings. Buttons & Margins: Select the colors used on the buttons (e.g., the Login button) and the background area of the blog feed. Video Settings: Set how you want videos in your blog feed to play. You can choose when they start to play, whether they play with or without sound and the playback speed.  Want to learn more?Check out the full course in Wix Learn on building your blog. Skip to the second video to learn more about creating and designing your blog.

Wix Bookings: Creating View-Only Services
View-only services let you offer appointments, classes or courses without requiring users to book in advance. This is useful when you have a large venue and don't need to know who is attending your service ahead of time (e.g. free yoga session in the park).DashboardWix appStudio app
Go to Booking Services in your site's dashboard. Click + Add a New Service. Scroll to the type of service you want create: Appointment, Class or Course  Choose what you want to do:
    
Click Edit below the relevant service template. Click + Start from Scratch to use a blank template.    Complete the form to create your service. Scroll down and click the Booking preferences section. Disable the Online bookings toggle to create a view-only service.
Click Save.
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Booking Services. Tap + Create New Service at the bottom.  Choose the relevant service type: Appointment or Class 
Note: To create a course, go to your site's dashboard from a desktop computer.  Complete the form to create your service. Scroll down to the Advanced Settings section. Disable the Accept online booking toggle to create a view-only service.
Tap Save at the top.

Note: To create a course, go to your site's dashboard from a desktop computer.  Complete the form to create your service. Scroll down to the Advanced Settings section. Disable the Accept online booking toggle to create a view-only service.
Tap Save at the top.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Anchors and In-Page Menus on Your Mobile Site
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Anchors and In-Page Menus on Your Mobile Site
Wix automatically builds a mobile version of your site with the same elements and content you add from the desktop editor. Anchors are a helpful way to mark and direct visitors to important information. They are automatically copied to, and are available from the mobile editor, but they do not have some of the functions available on the desktop version of your site.In this article, learn more about:
Anchors on your mobile site In-page menus on your mobile siteAnchors on mobileIn order to keep your site for mobile optimized, anchors you have added from desktop may be hidden from your mobile site.If you can not find an anchor in the mobile Editor, you can check the Hidden panel and re-add it. To find and re-add an anchor:
Click Hidden on Mobile  on the left side of your mobile editor. Click the Show next to the anchor.Important:Anchors are not visible on your live site. They are only visible on the editor. However, if you have hidden an anchor on your mobile site, you can not add it to a site menu.In-page menus on mobileIn-page menus are floating menus that you can use to link anchors and sections. In-page menus not visible on your mobile site, and can not be re-added.However, you can link to anchors and sections on your mobile site by adding them as an item to a site menu. The anchor and section must be linked to a site menu from the desktop editor in order for it to show on your mobile site.To add an anchor / section to your site menu:
Go to your editor. Click Pages and Menu  on the left side of the editor. Click the Add Menu Item on the bottom of the panel. Click Section or anchor on the menu on the left. Use the dropdown menus to select the page and anchor / section you'd like to add to the menu. Click Done. Type the item name into the field. Click Done.Want to see in-page menus available on mobile sites?You can vote for it with our Feature Request. Vote for in-page menus on mobile

source_documents.title: Wix Pro Gallery: An Overview
source_documents.content:
Wix Pro Gallery: An Overview
With the Wix Pro Gallery you can display videos, images and text all in one beautiful multimedia gallery. Your gallery is responsive, meaning no matter what device your visitors use, your gallery adjusts automatically to their screens.It's perfect for photographers and creatives alike, with built-in image protection to keep your content safe. You can even upload content on the go directly from the Wix app.The gallery is fully customizable, allowing you to perfect your gallery's layout and design for desktop and mobile users. You also have access to general and advanced settings. These allow you to engage your visitors with social share options, increase site traffic with SEO settings, and connect your gallery to a dataset.Ready to get started?Learn how to add and set up a Wix Pro Gallery.Prepare your Pro Gallery for desktopAfter you've added the Wix Pro Gallery to your site, you can start customizing your gallery's layout and design for visitors viewing your site on a desktop device. Choose from a variety of fully customizable and predesigned layouts, and personalize your gallery's design to match your brand.Optimize your Pro Gallery for mobileOptimize your Pro Gallery for visitors viewing your site on mobile. The layout of your Pro Gallery is responsive, and automatically adjusts to fit your visitor's mobile device. You can customize the layout and design, so that it looks just the way you want it to on mobile.Let visitors take a closer look at imagesSet your images to open in a pop-up window (Expand Mode) when clicked. You can also customize the look and behavior of this pop-up. Choose what information is shown, allow visitors to zoom in on details with a magnifying glass, adjust the background and icon colors, and more.Learn more about customizing the Expand ModeManage your Pro Gallery on the goUsing the Wix app, you can manage all your Pro Galleries on the go. Quickly and easily add and remove media from your gallery, reorder and rename media, share your gallery with others via social networks, and much more.Learn more about managing your gallery on the Wix appIncrease visitor engagement through social sharingGenerate traffic back to your site and increase engagement by allowing visitors to like and share their favorite gallery items to their social networks. Your visitors can share their favorites via Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Pinterest and email.Learn more about enabling social sharing from your galleryBoost your gallery's reach with SEOWorking with your site's SEO Settings for your Pro Gallery can help it rank higher in search engine results and drive traffic to your site. Adding alt text to your gallery items also helps search engines understand and rank your gallery and its content.Learn more about SEO for your Pro GalleryConnect your Pro Gallery to the CMS Create and store your media in a collection with the CMS (Content Management System) to help you manage the content you display on your Pro Gallery. Then, connect your collection to your Pro Gallery and display multiple items from your collection at once. Learn more about displaying collection content in a gallery

source_documents.content:
Wix Studio: Requesting a Feature
Stay in the loop with all the exciting developments on the horizon through our dedicated Wix Product Roadmap page. Dive into the world of Wix product categories and the upcoming enhancements, explore feature requests that are in the pipeline – complete with their estimated timeframes – and even share your own feature requests.Explore the latest additions and get a sneak peek at what's about to launch. Click Vote to cast in your vote for the features we're collecting votes for, or Follow to stay updated on features we're currently working on. You can use the sort and filter tools to refine your search by the most popular requests, features you're following, ETA and more.To request a feature:
Go to Discover in your Wix Studio workspace. Click the News Center icon  at the top right and select Wix Product Roadmap. Click Request a Feature on the top right. Select the Wix product you are requesting the feature for. Enter a description of the feature you are requesting, including how it works and what it will do. Enter a description of how the feature will impact your business. Click Send.What's next?Our team reviews every feature request we receive and then carefully assesses how they align with our product roadmap for potential development. In the meantime, check out our Wix Product Roadmap page to stay updated on the latest developments. You can also head over to our Wix Studio Community Discord to share your vision for the future of Wix Studio and engage with others.

Roles & Permissions: Changing a Collaborator's Role
Different roles give collaborators access to different parts of your site and dashboard. You can update a collaborator's role as their responsibilities change over time.In this article, learn how to:
Checking a collaborator's role Changing a collaborator's role Removing a collaborator from your site Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Checking a collaborator's roleIf you're not sure what role your collaborator has, or what they can access, you can check it on the Roles & Permissions page. To check a collaborator's role:

Check the role in the Role column and hover over it to learn more.Changing a collaborator's roleYou have full control over your collaborators' roles. You can change them at any time according to your needs or add an additional role.To change a collaborator's role:
Go to Roles & Permissions in your site's dashboard. Click the More Actions  icon next to the relevant collaborator. Click Change Role.
Select or deselect the relevant roles. Click Save.Removing a collaborator from your siteRemove a collaborator's access, so they can no longer log in or make any changes to your site and dashboard.To remove a collaborator's access:
Go to Roles & Permissions in your site's dashboard. Click the More Actions  icon next to the relevant collaborator. Click Remove.
Click Remove to confirm.FAQsClick a question below to learn more about changing collaborator roles.Can collaborators remove other collaborators?Collaborators with management-level roles can remove other collaborators, but only if they have the same permissions as the role they are removing. How do I remove myself as a collaborator on a site?If you no longer wish to contribute to a site, you can remove yourself as a collaborator.How can I learn more about the different collaborator roles?Learn more about the predefined collaborator roles or how to create your own custom role.

source_documents.title: Wix Payments: The Difference Between Account Types
source_documents.content:
Wix Payments: The Difference Between Account Types
While setting up your Wix Payments account, you're asked to select an account type depending on how you do business. Usually, this can be either an individual or a business account. There may be other account types available with specific requirements for your region, such as a sole proprietor in the United Kingdom, or a partnership in Austria.  Selecting the correct account type will help you to manage your Wix Payments account in the best way for your business. In this article, learn about:
Individual accounts Business accounts Regional account types Differences between the account types Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Individual accountsChoose this account type if you're doing business as an individual. We recommend this option if you don't have an EIN or a relevant company registration ID. If you're a sole proprietor in the United Kingdom or Italy, read below for regional differences. Payouts are sent to your personal bank account. While registering your details, make sure that the name in your Wix Payments account matches the bank account holder's name. For example, if you've created a Wix Payments account under Lisa Harrison but the associated bank account is listed as "Lisa's Cupcakes", the transfer will fail.Before creating a Wix Payments individual account, make sure you meet the following requirements: 
Acceptable identification: A valid (non-expired) driver's license, government issued ID card or passport. Address: You need to provide a physical address. PO boxes are not accepted. Business description: Include a brief description of your business, stating the type of products or services you sell and their prices. For more information, see our best practices for merchants. Bank account details: The name of the bank account holder needs to match the personal details provided for the Wix Payments account. Please note that only a personal bank account can be used.Business accountsChoose this account type if you're doing business as a company (Partnership / LLC / Corporation / NGO*).Payouts are sent to your business bank account. Before creating a Wix Payments business account, make sure you meet the following requirements: 
Business documents: Your business must have an EIN or the relevant company registration ID for your country. Business details must be exactly as they appear on the company registration document Company address: You need to provide a physical address. PO boxes are not accepted. Bank account details: The details of the bank account holder need to match the business details provided during set up. Your bank account must be a business account registered under your company's name.
Note: If you register a personal bank account, transfers will fail. Account representative: You'll need to add at least one business owner or account representative with a significant role in managing the business. All business owners and account representatives will need to provide a valid photo ID and have it verified (driver's license, government issued ID card, or passport).Using a "Doing Business As" alias?
Choose the account type that matches your bank account. For example, if your bank account is an individual account, you should create an individual Wix Payments account as well.  After your account is approved, add your DBA name in your statement descriptor so your bank recognizes the payouts. Regional account typesYou may see alternative account options when setting up your Wix Payments account. Currently, regional differences apply to the following locations / account types:
Sole proprietor (United Kingdom): UK sole proprietors are required to submit a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) number when setting up their Wix Payments account. Acceptable ID, business bank account details and a physical address are also required.  Sole proprietor (Italy): Sole proprietors in Italy are required to submit a codice fiscale number when setting up their Wix Payments account. Acceptable ID, bank account details and a physical address are also required.  Sole proprietor (Switzerland): Sole proprietors in Switzerland may submit a BID / UID number when setting up their Wix Payments account. Acceptable ID, bank account details and a physical address are also required. Partnership / Association (Germany): Partnerships or associations in Germany may submit a Handelsregisternummer when setting up their Wix Payments account. Business bank account details and a physical address are also required. Partnership (Austria): Partnerships in Austria may submit a Firmenbuchnummer number when setting up their Wix Payments account. Business bank account details and a physical address are also required. Association (Austria): Associations in Austria may submit a Zentrales Vereinregister Zahl number when setting up their Wix Payments account. Business bank account details and a physical address are also required.Account differencesCheck the table below to understand the main differences between each account type.RequirementsIndividual AccountBusiness AccountItaly Sole ProprietorUK Sole ProprietorSwitzerland Sole ProprietorGermany Partnership / AssociationAustria Partnership / AssociationMinimum age of 18 yrsYesYesYesYesYesYesYesPersonal documentsYesYesYesYesYesNoNoBusiness documentsNoYesYesYesYes, if availableYes, if availableYes, if availablePersonal bank accountYesNoYes (Or Business)NoYes (Or Business)NoNoBusiness bank accountNoYesYes (Or personal)YesYes (Or personal)YesYesPhysical addressYesYesYesYesYesYesYesPremium or Studio site planYesYesYesYesYesYesYesCompany registration / EINNoYesYesYesYesYesYesBusiness descriptionYesYesYesYesYesYesYesAccount representativeNoYesNoYesNoYesYesOn occasion, we may require additional information and / or documentation to verify your account. If this applies to your account, we will contact you.FAQsClick the questions below to learn more about setting up a Wix Payments account.I'm the sole proprietor in the UK. Which account type should I choose?UK Sole proprietors are required to submit a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) number as well as a business bank account when setting up their Wix Payments account. 
If you haven't registered for a UTR, or possess only a personal bank account, you can choose an Individual account instead. I have a partnership in the UK. What business registration number am I required to submit?Partnerships in the United Kingdom should supply a UTR number as their business registration number. I'm a sole proprietor in Italy. Which bank account type should I choose?Italian Sole proprietors can submit either a personal or a business bank account. They must also submit a codice fiscale. My NGO is an unregistered charity. Can I use Wix Payments?If your non-governmental organization doesn't have an EIN or any other company registration ID, it is not possible to create a business account. Wix does not support unregistered charities in compliance with our prohibited products and services. As an alternative, you can check other payment providers available in your region to see if they support your NGO type. How should I upload documents to Wix Payments?To send your documents successfully, follow our guidelines for uploading documents to Wix Payments. What happens if my account information doesn't match my documents?The information you include in your account set up must match the documents you provided. If not, the verification will fail and your payouts are put on hold.

source_documents.title: Wix Editor: Important Information About the Flash Editor
source_documents.content:
Wix Editor: Important Information About the Flash Editor
At the beginning of 2021, Adobe ended support of Flash technology. This affects all websites built with this technology, including the Flash site you've created on Wix. Any sites built on Flash have been deleted, and visitors aren't able to access them anymore. Additionally, the Flash editor is no longer supported. Click an option below to learn more about this change and what it means for your Flash site. Can I bring my Flash site back online?The sites have been removed from Wix. This means that they have been completely deleted, and cannot be restored.You can build a new site with the Wix Editor. The new editor offers better performance for your visitors and tons of new design features, layout options and business apps.Depending on your needs, you can:
Create a new HTML site using a pre-designed template Create a new HTML site from scratchCan I use the Flash Editor?No. Since the beginning of 2021, you are no longer able to access the Flash editor at all, including the dashboard of Flash sites. Do visitors still have access to my Flash site?Flash was disabled on all browsers. This means that visitors cannot view the Flash site that you created with Wix.Can I still see files from my Flash site in the Media Manager?No. At the beginning of 2021, your site's files were removed from Wix. Tip: After creating a new Wix site, you can easily upload all of your files in one go.

source_documents.title: Wix Pro Gallery: Enabling and Customizing a Load More Button
source_documents.content:
Wix Pro Gallery: Enabling and Customizing a Load More Button
Add a Load More button to your gallery to minimize the amount of content facing your site visitors when they access your site. You can then choose if you want to allow visitors to load all images in one click, or section by section. You can customize the button's text, font, color, and more to complement the rest of your site's design.Note:You can only add a Load More button to layouts that have a vertical scroll. You can't add a Load More button to the Thumbnails, Slider, Slide show, and Columns layouts.In this article, learn more about: 
Enabling a Load More button Customizing a Load More button Resolving Load More button issuesEnabling a Load More buttonAdd a Load More button to your gallery to allow visitors to load all images in one click, or section by section. Each section is the same size as the original gallery, meaning if your original gallery view shows four images, each subsequent section a visitor loads will display four images.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click the Pro Gallery element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Layout tab. Click Customize Layout. Enable the Load More button toggle. Select an option under How many more images load:

All images: All images load. One more section: The next section of the gallery loads.  
Go to your editor. Click the Pro Gallery element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Layout tab. Click Customize Layout. Enable the Load More button toggle. Select an option under How many more images load:

All images: All images load. One more section: The next section of the gallery loads.  Customizing a Load More buttonPersonalize your Load More button's text, font, color, and more to fit the rest of your site's design.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Go to your editor. Click the Pro Gallery element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click the Buttons tab. Customize the Load More button using the following options:
    
Button text: Click the Button text field to change the text that appears on the button. Font style & color: Click the drop-down to adjust the button's font, text size, and more. Click the color box to select a color. Button color & opacity: Drag the slider to change the button's transparency and click the color box to select its color. Border width & color: Drag the slider to change the button's border width and click the color box to change the border's color. Corner radius: Drag the slider to make the button's corners rounder.  
Go to your editor. Click the Pro Gallery element on your page. Click Settings. Click the Design tab. Click the Buttons tab. Customize the Load More button using the following options:
    
Button text: Click the Button text field to change the text that appears on the button. Font style & color: Click the drop-down to adjust the button's font, text size, and more. Click the color box to select a color. Button color & opacity: Drag the slider to change the button's transparency and click the color box to select its color. Border width & color: Drag the slider to change the button's border width and click the color box to change the border's color. Corner radius: Drag the slider to make the button's corners rounder.  Tip:If you only see 1 row of images, simply drag the bottom handle of the gallery to increase its size.Resolving Load More button issues for Pro Galleries built on the Wix EditorSome issues may arise in certain layouts when the Load More button is enabled on galleries built on the Wix Editor. Depending on the issue you're experiencing, there are various solutions available.If you have built your Pro Gallery on the Studio Editor, follow our Studio-specific guidelines to resolve any issues related to responsiveness.Click an option below to learn how to resolve common issues with the Load More button on the Wix Editor:Images of different height are cut when the Load More button is set to open "One more section"The gallery section size remains the same across all screen sizes, meaning that some images may be cut if they are of different heights. There are a few ways to resolve this issue:Solutions: 
Apply a layout where all images are the same height (e.g. Bricks, Grid with images set to Crop). Set the Load More button to open All images. Disable the Load More button.Last row of images is cut when the gallery is set to full-width (Grid layout)Across all screen sizes, the height of the gallery with a Grid layout stays the same, while the width changes according to the window / screen size. This means, images become smaller on smaller screen sizes and images on the last row may be cut.Solutions: 
Disable the Load More button or disable the full-width mode. Stretch the Pro Gallery to full width and set its margins to 0px. (If you display text on your gallery) Set the Info position to be Left or Right.Images at the bottom of the next section are cut (Masonry and Collage layout)In galleries with the Masonry or Collage layout, the images at the bottom of the next section are cut when you set the Load More button to open "One more section".Solution: Set the Load More button to display All images or disable the Load More button.

If this is a feature you would like to see in the future, you can vote for it here.

source_documents.title: Wix Pro Gallery: SEO for Your Pro Gallery
source_documents.content:
Wix Pro Gallery: SEO for Your Pro Gallery
The Wix Pro Gallery allows you to showcase your images, videos, and text all in one stunning multimedia gallery.Wix automatically adds SEO settings to your site so search engines and social networks can crawl and index your gallery in search results. These settings are added to each of your galleries by default and are based on your site's information and best practices for SEO.Adding alt text to and working with your site's SEO Settings for your Pro Gallery can help it rank higher in search engine results and drive traffic to your site.In this article, learn more about:
Adding alt text to gallery items Editing the SEO Settings for a Wix Pro Gallery Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Adding alt text to gallery itemsAlt text is a type of descriptive text you can add to images. Search engine bots can't read images and use the alt text to understand what the images are about. Make sure your alt text describes the item accurately while also integrating your site’s keywords.To add alt text to gallery items:
Click the gallery in your editor. Click Manage Media. Select the relevant gallery item. Click the Alt Text field on the right and type your description. Click Done. Publish your site.Editing the SEO Settings for your Wix Pro GalleryYour site's SEO Settings are a great tool to save time by applying the same SEO logic to all galleries at the same time. Instead of editing each gallery's individual settings, you can customize the settings that apply to all your galleries. This way, you can create a systematic SEO strategy much more quickly.For example, you can use SEO Settings to manage the information that's included in the title tags of your gallery pages. To edit the SEO Settings for the Wix Pro Gallery:
Go to your SEO in your site's dashboard. Select Go to SEO Settings under Tools and settings. Click Pro Galleries.  Customize your SEO settings. FAQsClick a question below to learn more about SEO for your Wix Pro Gallery.What happens if I don't add alt text to my gallery items?If you don't add alt text to a gallery item, the alt text is automatically taken from the Title ﻿field. If your gallery item does not have a title, the alt text is automatically taken from the Description ﻿field.My gallery is connected to the CMS. Where can I find the Alt Text field?If you connected your gallery to the CMS, you have two options for your alt text: 
Use the Media Gallery field: If you connected your gallery to a Media Gallery field, click the field in your collection and select Manage media to add text to each item.  Use a text field: If you connected your gallery to image or video fields, you can create another text field for your alt text in your collection. Then add the alt text you want to use for each item in your alt text field. Learn more about displaying collection content in a gallery. Can I change the URL of an individual image?Currently, the URLs of individual images in the Wix Pro Gallery are generated automatically. It is not possible to change them. If this is something you'd like to see in the future, you can vote for that feature.

Important:This article is about the New Wix Restaurants Orders app.Add a service fee to online orders in your Wix Restaurant site. Cover operational costs and state regulation fees. You can add the service fee as a percentage or fixed amount of the total order, and add sales tax if applicable. You can also set the service fee to apply to orders above a certain amount and based on how you fulfill that order. Customers will see every service fee in their order summary during checkout. The fee will get a separate line in the price breakdown and receipts.To add a service fee:
Go to Service Fees in your site's dashboard. Click + New Service Fee. Add your service fee details and set the conditions: 
    
Service name: Add a name for your service fee. Amount: Enter your service fee. It can be a fixed amount ($) or a percentage (%).
Note: Customers will see the service fee name and amount during checkout. (Optional) Add sales tax: Click the checkbox to add sales tax to this service fee and select a tax group. Apply based on fulfillment types: Choose to apply on pickup orders, delivery orders, or both. Apply based on subtotal: Choose what orders to apply the service fee to:
        
Set minimum: Orders placed above the amount you set will be charged this service fee. Set range: Orders between a minimum and maximum amount will be charged this service fee.   Click Save.

source_documents.title: Adding and Setting Up the Wix Hit Counter App
source_documents.content:
Adding and Setting Up the Wix Hit Counter App
Show your visitors how many people are visiting your site with the Wix Hit Counter app. Your counter updates your site traffic in real-time, and you can choose to show all site visits, or visits from unique visitors. You can choose if you want the counter to appear on one page, or on all your site's pages, and you can customize the counter to match your site's appearance.Step 1 | Add the Wix Hit Counter to your siteAdd the free Wix Hit Counter app to your site from the Wix App Market inside the Editor.To add the counter to your site:Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Add Apps   on the left side of the editor. Search for the Wix Hit Counter app in the search bar. Click Add to Site.
Click App Market  on the left side of the editor. Search for the Wix Hit Counter app in the search bar. Click Add to Site.Step 2 | Change your counter settingsChoose the number your counter starts at, and if the counter shows all visits or unique visitors.To change your counter settings:
Click the counter in your editor. Click Settings. Click the Settings tab.
Set up your counter using the options:
    
Counter starts at: Enter a number between 1 and 9999. The counter starts at this number. Important: You can only set the start number once. Count: Select which hits the counter should count:
        
All hits: Every visit to your site is counted. Unique visitors: Visitors are counted only once, no matter how many times they visit your site.    Step 3 | Customize your counterChoose your counter's layout and design, and add an animation to draw your visitors attention.
In Design, you can change the digit font and color, background color, and corner radius. In Animation, you can select different animations for your counter and digits. To customize your counter:
Click the counter in your editor. Click Settings Click to expand steps to customize your layout, design, and animation:Change the layout
Click the Layouts tab. Select a layout style for your counter, with different spacing and border options.Customize the design
Click the Design tab. Use the design options to customize the digits' font and color, the background, the separators, and the corners of the counter.Set up an animation
Click the Animations tab. Select an animation for your counter and customize it. Choose if you want all the digits to be animated at the same time or separately. FAQsClick a question below to learn more.How do I use the Wix Hit Counter app to track visits on a specific page only?To track the hits on a specific page, add the counter to that page of your site in your editor.How do I use the Wix Hit Counter to track visits on all of my site pages?To track hits on all of your site's pages, you'll need to set the Wix Hit Counter app to show on all pages.Wix Editor:
Right-click the app in the editor. Enable the Show on All Pages toggle.Studio Editor:In order to show an element on all pages in the Studio Editor, you need to attach it to a Global Section, which you can then set to show on all of your site's pages. Learn how to use Global Sections in the Studio Editor.

source_documents.title: CMS: Adding and Setting Up a Ratings Display Element
source_documents.content:
CMS: Adding and Setting Up a Ratings Display Element
Add a ratings display element to your site to showcase user feedback and build trust with your audience. After adding and customizing the ratings display element, you connect it to your CMS (Content Management System) collection and choose which Number fields to use for the rating values and total ratings. Need to collect ratings from visitors?Add and set up the ratings input element, which allows visitors to click to rate your products, features, services and more. Before you begin:
Make sure to add the CMS to your site or enable coding if you haven't already.  Make sure you have a CMS collection that stores your ratings. Step 1 | Add and set up the ratings display elementAdd the ratings display element to your page and customize its settings, layout, and design.Wix EditorStudio Editor
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Ratings. Click and drag the Ratings Input element of your choice onto the page. 
Click Settings on the ratings display element and click the relevant tab to choose what is shown when there are ratings and when there are no ratings: 
    
Ratings: Choose what you want to show when there are ratings: 
        
Show the rating value: Enable the toggle to show the rating value as a number in addition to the rating icons.  Show the number of ratings: Enable the toggle to show the total number of rankings.  Ratings text label: Enter the text that appears next to the ratings (e.g. "Recommend it").    No Ratings: Click the No Ratings tab and choose what displays when the element loads and there are no ratings: Nothing, Icons, or Placeholder text  
Click the Layout icon  to adjust the size, spacing, value placement, alignment and text direction.  Click the Design icon  to choose a preset design. Then click Customize Design to adjust the design further. 
Click Add Elements  on the left side of the editor. Click Input. Click Rating Display under Display. Click and drag the Rating Display element of your choice onto the page. 
Click Settings on the ratings display element and click the relevant tab to choose what is shown when there are ratings and when there are no ratings: 
    
Ratings: Choose what you want to show when there are ratings: 
        
Show the rating value: Enable the toggle to show the rating value as a number in addition to the rating icons.  Show the number of ratings: Enable the toggle to show the total number of rankings.  Ratings text label: Enter the text that appears next to the ratings (e.g. "Recommend it").    No Ratings: Click the No Ratings tab and choose what displays when the element loads and there are no ratings: Nothing, Icons, or Placeholder text  
Click the Layout icon  to adjust the size, spacing, value placement, alignment and text direction. Click the Design icon  in the Inspector panel to customize the design.Step 2 | Connect the ratings display to the CMSConnect the ratings display element to a dataset that binds to your CMS collection that stores the rankings. You can connect the rating values and the number of ratings to a Number field type or a Reference field. Wix EditorStudio Editor
In your editor, click the ratings display element.  Click the Connect to CMS icon  . Click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select an existing dataset that connects to your collection. Alternatively, select Add a Dataset, then choose the collection you want to connect, give the dataset a name and click Create. Click the Rating value connects to drop-down and select the Number field that contains the rating values you want to display.
Tip: Select Add new field to add a Number field to your collection that will store the rating values.  Click the Number of ratings connects to drop-down and select a Number field that contains the total number of ratings. 
Tip: Select Add new field to add a Number field to your collection that will store the number of ratings. 
Set the dataset mode and collection permissions:
    
Click Dataset Settings.  Click the Dataset mode drop-down and select Read or Read & Write.  (If necessary) Click the permissions type next to Collection Permissions and set up the permissions that determine who can view, add, delete, and update the collection content. Click Save once you're done setting the permissions.   
In your editor, click the ratings display element.  Click the Connect to CMS icon  . Click the Choose a dataset drop-down and select an existing dataset that connects to your collection. Alternatively, select Add a Dataset, then choose the collection you want to connect, give the dataset a name and click Create. Click the Rating value connects to drop-down and select the Number field that contains the rating values you want to display.
Tip: Select Add new field to add a Number field to your collection that will store the rating values.  Click the Number of ratings connects to drop-down and select a Number field that contains the total number of ratings. 
Tip: Select Add new field to add a Number field to your collection that will store the number of ratings. 
Set the dataset mode and collection permissions:
    
Click Dataset Settings.  Click the Dataset mode drop-down and select Read or Read & Write.  (If necessary) Click the permissions type next to Collection Permissions and set up the permissions that determine who can view, add, delete, and update the collection content. Click Save once you're done setting the permissions.   FAQsClick below for answers to common questions about displaying ratings on your site. Can I use Velo to capture and display ratings?Absolutely. View a Velo tutorial on capturing and displaying ratings using the ratings input element and the ratings display element. What type of field can I connect the ratings display element to?You can connect the ratings display element to the Number field type and Reference fields. How can I let visitors rate my features, products and services? Use the ratings input element to let visitors click to rate areas of your site. Their ratings are stored in a Number field type in your CMS collection. What are the dataset modes I can use with the ratings display element?The dataset mode determines what actions can be done between the connected elements and your collection. In the dataset you connect to your ratings display element, you can use the following dataset modes: 
Read: Elements on your page can read and display content from your collection. Site visitors cannot modify the content in your collection.  Read & Write: Elements on your page can read and display content from your collection. Visitors can interact with user input elements and a submit button to add or edit content in your collection. Are there any 3rd party apps I can add to handle ratings and reviews? Yes. As an alternative to the ratings input element, you can install the Kudobuzz Review app.

What can I do?If your customers are experiencing payment failures, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting issues for accepting payments.Why can’t I connect my desired payment provider?If you’re having trouble connecting your payment provider, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting common connection issues.

source_documents.title: Creating a Privacy Policy
source_documents.content:
Creating a Privacy Policy
As concerns about the protection of personal information are increasing worldwide, it is important that businesses, both small and large, implement and provide their site visitors with a comprehensive privacy policy.What is a privacy policy?A privacy policy is a statement that discloses some or all of the ways a website collects, uses, discloses, and manages the data of its visitors and customers. It fulfills a legal requirement to protect a visitor or client's privacy.Countries have their own laws with different requirements per jurisdiction regarding the use of privacy policies. Make sure you are following the legislation relevant to your activities and location. Important:The explanations and information provided herein are only general explanations, information and samples. You should not rely on this article as legal advice or as recommendations regarding what you should actually do. We recommend that you seek legal advice to help you understand and to assist you in the creation of your privacy policy. Information to add to your policyThere are multiple aspects of privacy law that all website owners must comply with when handling personal information. Below is a list of topics you should consider when implementing a privacy policy for your website.What type of information do you collect?Clarify the type of personal information you collect from your site visitors, such as email, name, IP addresses, billing details, social security number, etc. Collected information may be provided by the visitors and users of your website or collected automatically through monitory tools.See example We receive, collect and store any information you enter on our website or provide us in any other way. In addition, we collect the Internet protocol (IP) address used to connect your computer to the Internet; login; e-mail address; password; computer and connection information and purchase history. We may use software tools to measure and collect session information, including page response times, length of visits to certain pages, page interaction information, and methods used to browse away from the page. We also collect personally identifiable information (including name, email, password, communications); payment details (including credit card information), comments, feedback, product reviews, recommendations, and personal profile.How do you collect information?In this section you should explain your processes in collecting your site visitors' personal information. For example, when your client sends you a message through a contact form, when they purchase a product in your store, or when they subscribe to your newsletter.See exampleWhen you conduct a transaction on our website, as part of the process, we collect personal information you give us such as your name, address and email address. Your personal information will be used for the specific reasons stated above only.Why do you collect such personal information?This section should explain why you collect your site visitors' personal information (PI). For example, you might collect email addresses for your marketing campaigns, or their addresses for shipping purposes. See exampleWe collect such Non-personal and Personal Information for the following purposes:
To provide and operate the Services; To provide our Users with ongoing customer assistance and technical support; To be able to contact our Visitors and Users with general or personalized service-related notices and promotional messages; To create aggregated statistical data and other aggregated and/or inferred Non-personal Information, which we or our business partners may use to provide and improve our respective services;  To comply with any applicable laws and regulations.How do you store, use, share and disclose your site visitors' personal information?Your privacy policy must detail how you store and use your site visitors' personal information that you've collected. You should also inform your site visitors of the website if, when and how such information is shared with third-party services and/or with legal enforcement agencies, according to relevant local regulations.See exampleOur company is hosted on the Wix.com platform. Wix.com provides us with the online platform that allows us to sell our products and services to you. Your data may be stored through Wix.com’s data storage, databases and the general Wix.com applications. They store your data on secure servers behind a firewall.  All direct payment gateways offered by Wix.com and used by our company adhere to the standards set by PCI-DSS as managed by the PCI Security Standards Council, which is a joint effort of brands like Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover. PCI-DSS requirements help ensure the secure handling of credit card information by our store and its service providers.How do you communicate with your site visitors?If applicable, you should explain your means of communication (e.g. email, text message, etc.,) and for what purposes (e.g. marketing campaigns, promotions, updates, etc.). Explain exactly how you contact your site visitors by using personal information collected on your website and how they can opt out of receiving such messages.See exampleWe may contact you to notify you regarding your account, to troubleshoot problems with your account, to resolve a dispute, to collect fees or monies owed, to poll your opinions through surveys or questionnaires, to send updates about our company, or as otherwise necessary to contact you to enforce our User Agreement, applicable national laws, and any agreement we may have with you. For these purposes we may contact you via email, telephone, text messages, and postal mail.How do you use cookies and other tracking tools?If your website tracks personal information through the use of cookies, for example, you must make this clear to your site visitors. Be clear about what tracking tools (e.g. cookies, flash cookies, web beacons, etc.,) your website employs, what personal information they gather and why they are being used.It's important to note that third-party services, such as Google Analytics or other applications offered through the Wix App Market, placing cookies or utilizing other tracking technologies through Wix´s services, may have their own policies regarding how they collect and store information. As these are external services, such practices are not covered by the Wix Privacy Policy.View which cookies are stored on your site visitors' computer. How can your site visitors withdraw their consent?You must explain how your site visitors can withdraw their consent for collection of personal information, as well as how they can delete or change the collected information.See exampleIf you don’t want us to process your data anymore, please contact us at [your email] or send us mail to: [your physical mailing address].Privacy policy updatesWe recommend that you inform your users about your ability to change or update your site's privacy policy.See exampleWe reserve the right to modify this privacy policy at any time, so please review it frequently. Changes and clarifications will take effect immediately upon their posting on the website. If we make material changes to this policy, we will notify you here that it has been updated, so that you are aware of what information we collect, how we use it, and under what circumstances, if any, we use and/or disclose it. Questions and your contact informationProvide valid addresses/channels in order for your users or site visitors to be able to contact you. See exampleIf you would like to: access, correct, amend or delete any personal information we have about you, you are invited to contact us at [your email] or send us mail to: [your physical mailing address].Note:Once you've created your privacy policy, we recommend you add it to your site's footer.

source_documents.title: Editor X: About Stack
source_documents.content:
Editor X: About Stack
Stacking is a helpful tool in responsive design – without it, elements placed above and below each other could overlap on smaller screens. When you stack elements, it puts them inside a flex container with margins you can control. Show me how to create a Stack
Click the first element of your Stack. Hold down the Shift key and select all other elements that should be stacked. Click Stack.Working with breakpoints:Stacking and unstacking elements affect your site on all breakpoints. Learn more about changes that apply to all breakpointsMaintaining a responsive layoutResponsive websites often contain elements that resize and change position depending on screen size. This can cause them to overlap, or the spacing between them might change on smaller viewports. Stack puts your elements in a container that automatically adjusts to different screen sizes, so you can maintain a responsive layout. This is an example of what happens to elements that ARE NOT stacked when the screen resizes:Tip:When placing elements in a Stack, the flex container becomes their parent element. Head over to the Layers panel  to see the relationship between all elements. Customizing the flex containerStacking creates a flex container around your elements, which ensures that they always stay in the right spacing and order. The container is transparent by default, but you can design it to match your style, setting the fill color, borders, corners and shadow. Controling the spacing between elementsElements in a Stack are separated by vertical margins. To see the strips indicating the current margins, hover over or select the Stack. Double-click on elements inside the Stack and move them around to change the spacing between them.  Another option is making all margins equal in height from the Inspector panel, entering a value (px or %) next to Item spacing. Tip:From the same panel, you can also align all Stack elements in a certain direction: left, center, right or justify.

source_documents.title: Facebook Ads: Issues Syncing Your Products or Ad Caption With the Live Ad
source_documents.content:
Facebook Ads: Issues Syncing Your Products or Ad Caption With the Live Ad
If you've made edits to your ad campaign's products, ad caption or description and notice that your live ad isn't updated try the steps below:Products aren't updatingFor campaigns run with Wix Stores, if you've made changes to your store products and see the product list hasn't updated, try these steps:Step 1 | Edit your campaign and remove 1-2 products
Go to Facebook Ads in your site's dashboard. Click Edit Campaign. Navigate to the products section and remove one or two of your store products (you will add them back in later). Click Save.Step 2 | Check that your campaign is not in reviewIf your campaign is currently in review, the products and caption won't update until the campaign is approved. Learn more about campaigns in review.Step 3 | Try Facebook's Debugger tool
Go to Facebook's Debugger tool and log in using your Facebook credentials.  Paste your site URL and click Debug. Click Scrape Again. Check your Facebook Ads dashboard in 30 minutes to see if the campaign is now live with the updated products (missing the 1-2 you removed in Step 1).Step 4 | Add back the products you removed and try the Debugger tool again 
Return to the Facebook Ads dashboard and click Edit Campaign. Add back in the products you previously removed for testing. Go back to Facebook's Debugger tool and scrape the site again. In 30 minutes, check your Facebook Ads dashboard to see if your campaign is now updated with all the products.Ad caption and description are not updatingIf your caption and/or ad description aren't updated, try the following steps:Step 1 | Add spaces after your caption
Go to Facebook Ads in your site's dashboard. Click Edit Campaign. Go to the caption and insert two spaces at the end of the caption. Click Save.Step 2 | Check that your campaign is not in reviewIf your campaign is currently in review, the caption won't update until the campaign is approved. Learn more about campaigns in review.Step 3 | Try Facebook's Debugger tool
Go to Facebook's Debugger tool and log in using your Facebook credentials.  Paste your site URL and click Debug. Click Scrape Again. Check your Facebook Ads dashboard in 30 minutes to see if the campaign is now live with the updated caption.Still not working?If the issue persists, submit a ticket with a screenshot of the problem and the steps you've taken so far to fix it and we will investigate the matter further.

source_documents.content:
Gemini for Google Workspace: An Overview
Use Gemini, Google's AI-powered assistant, to help you write documents, design slideshows, write and summarize emails, organize projects, and much more. Gemini integrates seamlessly with your Google Workspace apps, including Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Chat.Gemini is available as an additional subscription service to existing business email users. The Gemini add-on license is connected to your Google Workspace business email account.Try Gemini free for 30 daysWhen you purchase a Gemini subscription, we won't charge you for the first 30 days. If you cancel your subscription within this period, the service will be canceled immediately and you won't be charged. The 30-day free trial only applies to the initial purchase of a Gemini for Google Workspace plan.Choose a plan that's right for youThere are 2 plans available to purchase to suit businesses of all sizes. Plans are available on a monthly or yearly subscription for anyone with an active Google Workspace business email account.You can view and purchase plans by going to the Business Email and Add-ons page from your site dashboard.Important:Currently it is only possible to purchase one Gemini license.Note:The Enterprise Gemini plan is available as an add-on for 'Standard' or 'Plus' Google Workspace plans only. If you have a 'Starter' plan, you can upgrade your business email plan to purchase Enterprise for Gemini. Learn more about upgrading your Google Workspace plan.Plan featuresBusiness and Enterprise plans offer an AI-powered assistant for teams of all sizes. With both plans you'll get access to Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Slides, Sheets, and Meet. Enterprise-grade security and privacy comes as standard.The Enterprise plan also includes advanced meetings with translated captions in 15+ languages, and full access and usage of Gemini.  Note:Gemini is an English-only tool for Google Workspace accounts set to English. You can purchase a license in all locations where Google Workspace is available, but you'll need to set your language to English to use Gemini. Learn how to change your Google Workspace account to English.Manage your Gemini licenseTo start using Gemini after you've purchased a license, you'll need to assign the license to a business email user first. You can assign and unassign licenses from the Business Email and Add-ons page on your site's dashboard. If you want to purchase a plan, cancel a plan, or update your payment method, you can go to the Premium Subscriptions section of your Wix account. To assign a license:Before you can start using Gemini, you'll need to assign a license to your business email user. 
Go to Business Email and Add-ons from your site dashboard. Click the More Actions icon  next to the user you want to assign the license to.  Click Assign License.Note: It can take up to 24 hours for a user's license to be assigned. Learn more about assigning Gemini licenses to a user from the Google Help Center.To unassign a license:
Go to Business Email and Add-ons from your site dashboard. Click the More Actions icon  next to the user you want to unassign the license from.  Click Unassign Gemini.To update your payment information:
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to your Gemini license. Click Update payment method.  Update your credit card details. Click Submit.To cancel a license:
Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon  next to your Gemini license. Click Cancel Subscription. Important:When you cancel your subscription, your plan will remain active until the end of your billing cycle. You can continue to use Gemini until this time.

source_documents.title: Improving Your Ranking in Bing Search Results
source_documents.content:
Improving Your Ranking in Bing Search Results
Search engines like Bing crawl and index each page on your site individually. When someone enters a search term, Bing tries to understand their intent and gives them the most relevant results for their query.The rank of your page in those results can depend on factors like the age of your site, the quality of your content, how relevant the content is to certain keywords, and how accessible your site is. If you entered your business name, domain name, or keywords into a Bing search box but you can’t find your website, here are some things to consider:Make sure that your site is verifiedVerifying your ownership of your domain on Bing helps to improve your ranking in search results. You can verify your site with Bing Webmaster Tools by adding a meta tag to your Wix site. After you verify your site, Bing will regularly crawl it for changes. However, it's a good idea to resubmit your sitemap to Bing when you publish changes to your site.Check that your site is visible in search resultsAfter you've published your site, you should make sure that you've chosen to let search engines index your pages and show them in search results. If there are certain pages on your site that you don't want to appear in search results, you can choose to prevent search engines from indexing them. Learn how to for:
Editor Editor XUnderstand that getting indexed is different from getting a high rankingJust because Bing crawled and indexed your site, it doesn’t mean that it will rank high in search results. This is especially true if your market is very competitive.Your website may be somewhere in the list of results for your keywords, but it may be on the 10th, 50th, or 100th page. After you complete your SEO Setup Checklist, it's important to keep working on your ranking. Some of the ways you can do this are optimizing your site's content, making your site accessible, and making your site mobile friendly. Optimize your keywordsIf you're not ranking high on Bing for the search terms you're targeting, you may want to adjust your list of keywords. When choosing your keywords, ask yourself, “What would a customer type into Bing when they look for a business like mine?”

Next, take a look at your site and make sure that you've used your keywords as much as possible. It’s important to use your page’s keywords in a natural, unforced way. One way you can do this is by describing the main purpose of your site in different ways. Learn MoreYou can use your keywords in your domain, in your headlines, within the text on your pages, and as alt text in your images. Generate traffic for your site with fresh content and backlinksBing tends to favor sites that are well-written and frequently updated content. Your site's ranking may be affected if your site is low on quality content, duplicates content from others sites, or is mostly ads and redirects.You should try to create fresh content for your site on a regular basis to keep your site up to date. Some of the ways you can do this are by adding a blog for your updates, making an FAQs page that answers popular questions for your target audience, and adding a testimonials page for customer reviews. Learn More

It also helps your ranking if you get links (known as backlinks) to your site from relevant or reputable sites. This improves your online reputation and credibility, increasing your chances of ranking higher.Share your site on social mediaSharing your site on your social media can help improve your ranking in search results. The more your site is shared and reshared, the more likely it is that Bing will consider your content popular and give your site a high ranking. Remember that ranking takes timeIf your site is new, it could take time for it to reach a high ranking. SEO is a long-term strategy and changes rarely happen within days or even weeks. Your site won’t show up in Bing results for your keywords overnight and the more competitive your market, the tougher it will be to rank high. Once you’ve chosen great keywords to target, put fresh content on your website as often as possible. Consider adding new pages, images, or blog articles that incorporate your keywords.

For more tips and ideas about optimizing your site, check out the complete Wix SEO Guide.Want your site to rank higher on Google?Learn more about improving your ranking on Google.
